name: Heroes Walk, 5K & 10k Fun Run Presented By Lithia CDJR and Camp Chevrolet
description:
CHECK IN BEGINS AT 9:00 AM 


Empowering Communities and Fortifying Families to End Veteran Suicide and Strengthen our Heroes to Lead their Communities.

HONOR HEROES - FORTIFY FAMILIES - CELEBRATE FREEDOM

Walk in support of veterans to choose LIFE. The enemy did not have victory in war, and will not win in the day to day battle for our veteran’s lives. Together we can end veteran suicide and fortify families after service. Live life abundantly with a community that hears, sees and recognizes the sacrifices of our HEROES. Family and supporters of our veterans are encouraged to join. Let’s gather in a big way to show the love and support of our veterans and the USA. 

The circle of return from military service to civilian life is a personal and community process. Join a community wide celebration and resources fair as we help veterans and families make the journey back home after service. 

Schedule: 

9 AM Registration Opens and Community Resource Fair

10 AM Opening Ceremonies 

11:00 AM Walk Commences on paths through Riverfront Park.
Those walking with kids are welcome to bring scooters, wagons, bikes or strollers to make your time easier with little ones. 

12 PM Victory Celebration and Closing Ceremony 

1 PM Resource Fair Closes


Heroes Walk brings awareness, solutions, and builds a connected community to end veteran suicide and homelessness by providing resources for wrap around care for the whole veteran and their family or support system. The content and event day will be mindful of the multigenerational crowd. 

Organizations desiring to join the resource community fair or sponsor the event, please email info@heroeshomestead.org.  Services for adults, children, veterans and spouses (including Gold Star families), as well as basic life needs and life enhancement and more are welcome to join.

name: I love the 90s 5k
description:
I love the 90s 5k! 🏃🏽‍♀️ 🏃🏽 

Get ready to groove and run down memory lane at the I Love the 90s 5K, where you can lace up your sneakers & jam to classic 90s tunes!

Join us for the I Love the 90s 5k! Lace up your sneakers and get ready to groove to the best hits of the 90s while running through beautiful Green Lake Park in Seattle, WA. This in-person event is a blast from the past, celebrating all things 90s. Whether you're a fan of grunge, pop, or hip-hop, this 5k is for you! Dress up in your favorite 90s attire and relive the nostalgia with fellow participants. The course will take you around the scenic Green Lake, providing a picturesque backdrop for your run. So grab your friends, put on your Walkman, and let's make some memories together at the I Love the 90s 5k!

 

Questions? Concerns? Email us! General inquiries:  info@run2befit.com

name: It’s A Vibe Run - 5K, 1Mile & Kids Dash
description:
Feel the vibe of the small town Benton City and the energy of a vibrant running community! Whether you're a seasoned runner chasing your next PR or just looking for a fun way to stay active, This run is perfect for runners of all levels.

🏃 Course: Run along Benton City trail with stunning finish. Kids dash will be 2 laps around the Benton City Community park. Soak in the positivity and encouragement from fellow runners and cheer squads.

🏅  Finisher Medals for all Participants: Celebrate your achievement with a medal design of It’s A Vibe.

🍴 Post-Race Goodies: Enjoy refreshments and snacks to refuel after your run.

Aid Station will be at half mile mark of the one mile and the half mark of the 5K.

Why Join Us?
It’s A Vibe race is more than just a run—it's an experience! Embrace the laid-back good vibe, make new friends, and challenge yourself in a supportive and inclusive environment.

Registration Includes

✅ Race day goodies

name: Jack & Jill Downhill Marathon, Half Marathon Washington
description:
New Jack & Jill Course Update
We’re excited to officially confirm the new Jack & Jill Marathon & Half Marathon course.

Thank you for your patience and trust while we worked to secure the best possible course for runners to enjoy and crush their goals.

The updated course keeps the fast, PR-friendly experience Jack & Jill is known for — with fresh scenery and an improved race-day flow.

Course Highlights
• Point-to-point course
• Net downhill: 1,300 feet
• Boston Qualifier eligible — no 5-minute downhill penalty
• Run through the iconic tunnel
• New scenic views including Lake Keecheles

Jack & Jill continues to be one of the fastest and most enjoyable marathon and half marathon experiences in the Pacific Northwest.

Race-Day Experience
• Professionally timed by Laurell (formerly Brooksee)
• Live tracking, mile splits, and printed finisher cards
• Abbott World Marathon Majors Age Group Ranking — Tokyo 2027
• Our Super Pacers leading you to your best time

Looking for a different date?
The Downhill Super Series now offers three weekends and three fast courses:

• Jack & Jill Marathon & Half — 1,300’ net downhill
• Super Hyak Marathon & Half — just under 1,500’ net downhill
• Cascade Express Marathon & Half — just under 1,500’ net downhill

Choose the weekend that fits your race calendar best.

We can’t wait to welcome you to the new Jack & Jill course.

name: Jasper Mountain Trail Fest 2026
description:
2026 Jasper Mountain Trail Fest Video

Jasper Mountain Trail Fest is a fundraising event that benefits Jasper Mountain Reserve, an environmental 501(c)3 non-profit organization to improve and enhance wildlife habitats for rare and endangered flora and fauna native to the Blue Mountains in the Southeast corner of Washington State. Come and enjoy the beautiful natural scenery with the knowledge that your signup funds will benefit the conservation of the reserve.

 

For 2026, we are offering four unique race options:

1) Our classic (sixth annual!) 4-person relay race, 52.4 miles total distance
2) Solo Half marathon, 13.1 miles with 2,570 feet of elevation gain
3) Solo Full marathon, 26.2 miles with 5,140 feet of elevation gain
4) Solo 7k Family Run (4.4 miles) with minimal elevation gain

 

Price increases are on  April 15, 2026, May 17, 2026, and June 13, 2026. Sign up by May 31, 2026 to guarantee you receive a race t-shirt and medal! (we have a few extras for late registrants on a first come-first serve basis). Contact info@jaspermountainreserve.org with any questions.

 

All races take place on the following single track trails (click on each for details):

Red Loop (3.3 miles)
Green Loop (4.4 miles)
Black Loop (5.4 miles)

 

Reserve Information and Accommodations

The start and finish line is at 933 Payne Hollow Road, Dayton, WA 99328. Type "Jasper Mountain Reserve" into Google or Apple Maps and follow online directions.

Come and camp with us on our beautiful campground direct on the race course. On-site camping guarantees a stress-free morning. Suggested arrival is during daylight a day or two days prior to the race. Suggested departure is the day after the race. There will be an informal welcome reception and short presentation about the race in the Start/Finish area, commencing at around 8:00PM on the evening prior to the race. BIB-pickup, starting at 6pm the evening prior to the race is STRONGLY encouraged. Parking and campsites, close to the start/finish line, is included in the race fee.

Campsites for racers are within Jasper Mountain Reserve. As this is a nature reserve, loud noises, including car engines, power generators, high volume loudspeakers etc. are strictly forbidden. Dogs must be on leash at all times. Camp-fires are only allowed at one designated area (please familiarize yourself with WA State and Columbia County seasonal camp fire restrictions). Bring your own food, water, and (battery) power sources (Jasper Mountain Reserve is off the grid, meaning there is no water or electricity). Portable sanitary facilities will be provided. As there is no garbage and recycling collection service please collect all trash and take it with you when you depart.

 

Accommodation options are also available just a short drive from the race! Choose from hotels and Airbnbs in nearby Dayton (11 miles from the event), Waitsburg (16 miles), or Walla Walla (37 miles).

 

Relay Race Details (Start Time 7:00AM):

Relay teams consist of 4 people sharing one assigned bib with an adjustable belt that can be exchanged between team members. Each racer signs up individually and can choose one of the following options:
1) No Team (the race organizers will assign you to a team)
2) Join an Existing Team
3) Create a New Team

 

All teams start together with the 1st runner of each team running the red loop at the same time. Once completed, the 1st runner passes the bib to the 2nd team member who will complete the green loop. Once completed, the 2nd team member passes the bib to the 3rd team member who will complete the black loop. Once completed, the 3rd team member passes on the bib to the 4th team member who will run the red loop, followed by the 1st team member who will run the green loop, followed by the 2nd team member who will run the black loop and so on, until all 4 team members each have completed all three loops. Race timing will provide results for entire teams as well as individual times (splits) on each separate trail loop.

 

All three loops combined are exactly 13.1 miles, the distance of a half marathon. The relay race is expected to take 10-12 hours. Due to the rugged terrain which includes steep downhills, headlamps are mandatory for any runners after 8:00PM.

 

Half Marathon and Full Marathon Details (Start Time 7:00AM)

Calling all Ultra Trail Runners! Our new course is crafted specifically for the adventurous spirit of the ultra trail community. The half marathon is the perfect choice for those eager to test their limits or begin their journey toward ultra distances. description:
2026 Jasper Mountain Trail Fest Video

All races take place on the following single track trails (click on each for details):

Red Loop (3.3 miles)
Green Loop (4.4 miles)
Black Loop (5.4 miles)

 

Reserve Information and Accommodations

The start and finish line is at 933 Payne Hollow Road, Dayton, WA 99328. Type "Jasper Mountain Reserve" into Google or Apple Maps and follow online directions.

Come and camp with us on our beautiful campground direct on the race course. On-site camping guarantees a stress-free morning. Suggested arrival is during daylight a day or two days prior to the race. Suggested departure is the day after the race. There will be an informal welcome reception and short presentation about the race in the Start/Finish area, commencing at around 8:00PM on the evening prior to the race. BIB-pickup, starting at 6pm the evening prior to the race is STRONGLY encouraged. Parking and campsites, close to the start/finish line, is included in the race fee.

Campsites for racers are within Jasper Mountain Reserve. As this is a nature reserve, loud noises, including car engines, power generators, high volume loudspeakers etc. are strictly forbidden. Dogs must be on leash at all times. Camp-fires are only allowed at one designated area (please familiarize yourself with WA State and Columbia County seasonal camp fire restrictions). Bring your own food, water, and (battery) power sources (Jasper Mountain Reserve is off the grid, meaning there is no water or electricity). Portable sanitary facilities will be provided. As there is no garbage and recycling collection service please collect all trash and take it with you when you depart.

 

Accommodation options are also available just a short drive from the race! Choose from hotels and Airbnbs in nearby Dayton (11 miles from the event), Waitsburg (16 miles), or Walla Walla (37 miles).

2) Join an Existing Team
3) Create a New Team

Once completed, the 2nd team member passes the bib to the 3rd team member who will complete the black loop. Once completed, the 3rd team member passes on the bib to the 4th team member who will run the red loop, followed by the 1st team member who will run the green loop, followed by the 2nd team member who will run the black loop and so on, until all 4 team members each have completed all three loops. Race timing will provide results for entire teams as well as individual times (splits) on each separate trail loop.

 

All three loops combined are exactly 13.1 miles, the distance of a half marathon. The relay race is expected to take 10-12 hours. Due to the rugged terrain which includes steep downhills, headlamps are mandatory for any runners after 8:00PM.

name: Jefferson Healthcare RHODY RUN
description:
Jefferson Healthcare Rhody Run
Sunday, May 17, 2026

Race Location
The Rhody Run will take place at Fort Worden State Park, Port Townsend, Washington.
Additional parking and shuttle service will be available from the Jefferson County Fairgrounds (4907 Landes St, Port Townsend, WA 98368).

About the Event
The Jefferson Healthcare Rhody Run is organized and produced by the Port Townsend Marathon Association, a charitable non-profit organization dedicated to fostering and encouraging runners of all ages—both in the school system and in the community at large. Nearly all aspects of this event are made possible by volunteers, and proceeds from the Rhody Run are returned directly to the community in the form of funding support for school sports programs and youth-oriented nonprofit organizations.

Our goal is to produce a race where all runners—champion and beginner alike—feel that it is their race. We strive to live up to our long-standing motto:
“The Run That Cares for the Runner.”

Courses
12K & 5K courses
Updated 2026 course maps are available on the registration page.
 
Parking & Transportation (Important)
Parking at Fort Worden requires a valid Washington State Parks Discover Pass.

Parking at Fort Worden is limited.
Additional parking is available at the Jefferson County Fairgrounds.
Shuttle service will be provided between the Fairgrounds and Fort Worden:

Morning Shuttles: 7:30 AM – 8:45 AM
Return: 10:45 AM – 12:00 PM
The Fairgrounds are approximately ½ mile from Fort Worden, and participants may choose to walk to the start area.
There is no public transit service on Sunday.

Packet Pickup
Friday & Saturday, May 15–16: Jefferson Healthcare (location and times TBA)
Race Day Pickup: Parade Grounds at Fort Worden
 
Awards & Championships
Custom Port Townsend Foundry medals will be awarded to the top three (3) finishers in each USATF 5-year age group for men and women in the 12K:

Under 14, 15–19, 20–24, 25–29, 30–34, 35–39, 40–44, 45–49, 50–54, 55–59, 60–64, 65–69, 70–74, 75–79, 80–84, 85–89, 90–94, 95–100

USATF Road Championship Designation
The 2026 Jefferson Healthcare Rhody Run has been designated by Pacific Northwest Track & Field as a Road Championship event for members of the Pacific Northwest Association of USATF in both the Open and Masters divisions (5-year increments beginning at 40+).

Runners must be current PNTF/USATF members prior to race day to be eligible for championship awards and prize money.
A runner’s age on race day determines division placement.
Prize Money

Open Division:
Top three (3) PNTF/USATF finishers (male and female) who place in the top five overall:
$300 / $200 / $100
Masters Divisions (40+):
First PNTF/USATF finisher in each 5-year age group who places in the top five of the Masters division:
$100

For championship eligibility questions, contact pntf@wolfenet.com.

name: July 4th Run 5K/10K/13.1 SEATTLE
description:
Run Free. Run Proud.
Celebrate America’s independence with the July 4th Freedom Run — where every stride honors liberty, courage, and the spirit of freedom.
Whether you walk, jog, or race your heart out, come together to move for what unites us all.

Overview:
Run will sell-out QUICK! We will close off waves the moment they fill up. If waves are sold out, you can sign-up for the virtual run option or wait list.
This is a smaller, private group run with a cap per wave.
All paces and ages (under 18 with guardian) are welcome - Run or Walk!  
There's no equipment or setup, this is a pure run with our coordinators to support you in a warm, stress-free setting!
When you sign-up, we give you the support you need to help you achieve your goals and fitness. We also invite you to be part of our local run clubs that supports your fitness journey. 
Timing:
- Timing is Optional: You may track your time on an app (Strava, RunKeeper, Nike Run, etc) and submit your times with our easy form to be posted online. Or you can ask our coordinators to help keep track of your time. 
- No timing chips (This is a stress free run to support you in achieving your goals)!
What You Get (Swag Bag):
- Running T-Shirt (Shipped to the address you register with - US only)
- Finisher's Towel or Giveaway
- Finisher's Medal! 
- Digital Training Pack 
- Online Results & Certificate of Completion
- Invitation to Join one of our Local Running Clubs
- We now have Technical Running Shirts (Optional). These lightweight, moisture wicking shirts can be upgraded for just $5 more. 
Packet Pickup:
No hassle of picking up packets required!
-Swag shipped direct to your address (Please make sure you provide your full, correct US mailing address including apartment number and check spelling)
- Race bibs are provided on race day
When will I get my Swag?
You will get your shirt at your mailing address the week of your race.
Race Updates:
We will email you a final update the Wednesday before the race with final details and course maps.
Do you accept last minute registrations? (For those signing up 2 weeks before the race)
Yes, but please note that it takes time for us to ship your shirt. Your shirt will likely arrive after the run. You can wear any shirt you find appropriate to run the race! 
 
Wave Times: (Email Us Your Desired Wave Time: info@thebestraces.com)
(Waves filled on a First Come, First Serve Basis)
Wave A: 7:30AM
Wave B: 8:00AM
Wave C: 8:30AM
Late runners can run upon arrival (Please note our coordinators stay 3 hours after the first wave)
Are there any other Questions we missed?
https://www.thebestraces.com/faq/
Virtual Run Option:
- Our Virtual Run uniquely offers a Training Pack with Digital Tools to support your run. 
Virtual runs can be done any time and place of your choosing using any tracking device (optional). After you finish, you can submit your results to info@thebestraces.com to receive your medal! 
Race Bundle:
Sign-up for more races and get a discount! 

Sponsorships & Promoting your Business:

If you're looking to become a sponsor, we'd love showcase your business!
https://www.thebestraces.com/events
 

Team Glo Volunteers:

If you're interested in helping put on runs for the Community and helping people achieve their goals, we invite you to join our team of volunteers, fill out the form here: https://www.thebestraces.com/volunteer-form/
 

Be part of the Journey!

Our Charity Initiatives. Find out more @ www.thebestracesjourney.com
Keep running. Every mile you log after the race, we'll donate $1 to one of the charities we work with! (Note that Fundraising is Optional)

name: K is for Kindness 5 K and 1K Run
description:
K is for Kindness is a 5K and 1K fun run to benefit Spectrum Studios and Empower Center for Growth.  

The Tri-Cities only nonprofit for young adults on the autism spectrum who have aged out of school—creating opportunities, connections, enrichment and growth.

Empower Center for Growth is a welcoming community hub dedicated to individuals who are looking for a place to connect, learn, and grow. It’s a space to hang out with new friends, take creative and life-skills classes, and discover new interests in a supportive, inclusive environment. Whether you want to explore art, cooking, technology, or personal development, Empower Center for Growth is here to help you build confidence, friendships, and lifelong skills.

name: Kaci Edelbrock Memorial 5K Run/Walk
description:
The idea behind this race was to bring the community together, be outside and run/walk in memory of Kaci. Kaci herself never stopped! She was such a spirited girl that was constantly on the go trying to keep up with her older brothers and their friends.

The Big Heart Big Smile Foundation was created in memory of Kaci Edelbrock, a six year old who passed away in 2018.  The Kaci 5K invites all families to run/walk with babies in strollers and dogs on leashes.

Kaci would have wanted everyone to be included. All of the money raised for this event goes directly into programs such as, the Kaci Edelbrock Memorial Scholarship, Kaci’s Big Toy Giveaway, Kaci’s Backpack Project, Kaci’s Big Hugs, and Kaci’s Kindness Cards. The race will be held the first Sunday in May in Monroe.

Please visit www.bigheartbigsmile.org for more information

name: L.O.S. - LAST ONE STANDING
description:
Inspiration

L.O.S is more than a race. It is a Phase One Mission - an invitation to train for adversity, define resilience, and find hope, leaving no one behind. L.O.S is an opportunity to maintain your internal line of sight and search for strength within.

Course Description

Starting at sunrise, runners will run a 4 mile route every hour on the hour until there is a last one standing.

Course:

A 4 mile course staged at a staged 1.58 mile dirt track.

name: Lake Meridian Triathlon
description:
Welcome to this Pacific Northwest Favorite Triathlon. Lake Meridian includes Olympic, Sprint, and Super Sprint individual events and a Sprint & Olympic Relay for teams of 2 or 3.  All athletes will receive a free T-shirt (if you register on or before August 1st) & finisher medal.  Stick around after your race and enjoy a meal,  the finish line celebration and awards ceremony,  Pint glasses are given to the top 5 finishers of each age group in the Sprint & Olympic - top 3 in the Super Sprint. 

Lake Meridian Park is a beautiful, spectator friendly venue. Lots of room for the kids to run around. 

See you in August!

name: Langlauf 10K XC Ski Race
description:
Langlauf is a 10K Cross Country Ski Race that takes place at the Mount Spokane Nordic Ski Center which is the premier Cross Country Ski Area in the Inland Northwest.  The race takes place on the traditional 10K course and has wave starts to accommodate skiers of all abilities and speeds.  Even maybe more epic than the race itself, are the pre and post race amenities that are enjoyed by all racers.  This is the biggest and oldest Cross Country Race in the Pacific Northwest...you don't want to miss it!

Once again, this year we are offering an adaptive skier category. If you are visually impaired or a sit skier you will be able to participate in our Wave start, but at Junction 1 will continue on Linder Road to a turnaround at the Inland gate then back to Brian's and our traditional finish line. Adaptive skiers must register but their guide skier can accompany them for no cost. Guides will need to sign a waiver the morning of the race and do not need to pay to register unless they want to be timed. Guides will be considered a volunteer and be entered in the prize drawing.

name: Last Chance Marathon and Half Marathon
description:
OK, here is your Last Chance to run a 1/2 marathon or full marathon this year! The 1/2 marathon course is an out and back and the full marathon course is the same out and back course two times, starting at Fairhaven Park Pavillion, running the Interurban trail out to Clayton Beach for the full 13.1 miles or 26.2. Course is subject to change if trail conditions mandate.

 

This trail has spectacular views and very few hills, just enough hills to make it interesting, and break up the flat sections. FYI: We have been known to have SNOW this time of the year so plan accordingly. The majority of this trail is covered with a canopy of trees which deflects some of the rain or snow, but this also means it doesn’t heat as fast as an open course would. It can get cold. The majority of the trail is an old railroad bed, very easy to run on gravel surface, with the exception of Arroyos Park. Arroyos Park is a double track trail with a few bridges and a few fun hills. It is a very well maintained set of trails.

 

The bathrooms at Fairhaven Park will be unlocked as well as the warm heated Pavillion.

 

You should plan on being self-sufficient and carrying your own water and aid. The 1st aid station on the course is ~ 3.5 miles into the race off Chuckanut Crest Drive. In the 1/2 marathon you will run by this aid station twice, and 4 times in the full marathon.  There will be an aid station at the turn around which you will access once in the 1/2 marathon and twice in the full marathon. We will also have an aid station at the start/finish so full 1/2 marathoners will have 3 chances to refill their water bottles, about every 3 to 3.5 miles, & marathoners will have 7 chances to refill their water bottles.  We will have water, an electrolyte drink and other snacks at the aid stations.  Usually I put some type of candy like candy corn, gummy bears, bananas, pretzels, typical ultra style foods. You won’t go hungry!
Keep an eye on the website for any changes to the event. Finishers will receive a Last Chance coin/medal similar to the quality of the Woolley Runs coin.  We will provide food at the end like all the NW Ultra Events.  While all your friends are recovering from their hang over and resting up before the evening’s festivities, you’ll be burning calories and ready to PARTY hardy knowing you’ve already burned off that extra beer or two, or three.

In the 1/2 marathon you will run by this aid station twice, and 4 times in the full marathon.  There will be an aid station at the turn around which you will access once in the 1/2 marathon and twice in the full marathon. We will also have an aid station at the start/finish so full 1/2 marathoners will have 3 chances to refill their water bottles, about every 3 to 3.5 miles, & marathoners will have 7 chances to refill their water bottles.  We will have water, an electrolyte drink and other snacks at the aid stations.  Usually I put some type of candy like candy corn, gummy bears, bananas, pretzels, typical ultra style foods. You won’t go hungry!
Keep an eye on the website for any changes to the event. Finishers will receive a Last Chance coin/medal similar to the quality of the Woolley Runs coin.  We will provide food at the end like all the NW Ultra Events.  While all your friends are recovering from their hang over and resting up before the evening’s festivities, you’ll be burning calories and ready to PARTY hardy knowing you’ve already burned off that extra beer or two, or three.

name: Leif to Leif 5k Fun Run/Walk
description:
Join us for the annual running of the Leif to Leif 5k!! We hope you are ready to get some exercise and explore Ballard with us. 

From the heart of Ballard to Shilshole Bay, the Sons of Norway Leif Erikson Lodge is proud to announce our annual 5k! 

5k Fun Run / Walk:

  • Adult (18yr+) - $20 
  • 13-17 yr - $10
  • Child 12 and under - FREE

Check in begins at 8:00am. Race starts around 9am. Top finishers will receive ribbons and prizes, with prizes also being awarded for fun and creative participants!

Stick around after the run and enjoy some Nordic culture in the main hall! We will be treated to live music and other Nordic cultural demonstrations. We will be serving hot food, Scandinavian baked items (cookies, lefse, bløtkake, krumkake), coffee, soda and more. 

Proceeds benefit the Leif Erikson Lodge and the Ballard Senior Center. More info on the Leif Erikson Lodge. 

Limited registration will also be available the morning of the event.

name: Longview Early Edition Rotary Harvest Classic
description:
Longview Early Edition Rotary's Harvest Classic 2026

October 3, 2026

Helping our community since 1980.  

Have fun while running or walking a beautiful course and raise funds and awareness to eliminate hunger in our community.

Race Info​​

The Harvest Classic offers a flat and fast course with scenic views of downtown and Lake Sacajawea. Come set a new PR and have fun while running or walking a beautiful course and raise funds and awareness to eliminate hunger in our community. Both the 5K and 10K are USA Track & Field-certified courses, so you know your PR, or your age group record, American Record or World Record (??!!) will be real. If you don't care about records, just come and have a good time. 


 Participants can use the RaceJoy application to learn about the city's history along the route.  This year we have two special events. 

Event details and schedule. 

​Packet Pick-up

Friday, October 2, 2026 - race packets can be picked-up from 9:30 a.m. to noon at the CAP Help Warehouse at 1526 Commerce Avenue, Longview. Or, you can pick up your packet on Saturday, October 3rd between 7:00 a.m. and 8:00 a.m. at Life Works at 906 New York Street, Longview.

Race Day 

SATURDAY, OCTOBER 3rd, 2026 , AT LIFE WORKS, 906 NEW YORK STREET, LONGVIEW, Washington.

8:20 AM - High School Challenge 5 Kilometer Race (HS Cross Country Team battle for team plaques and individual ribbons.  Teams sign up through Athletic.net: https://www.athletic.net/CrossCountry/meet/253682/info

8:30 AM - 10:30 AM  5 Kilometer (3.1 Miles) and 10 Kilometer (6.2 Miles) Run/Walk.    

9:20 AM – ¼ Mile Pee Wee Fun Run – Free for kids ages 9 and under.  **The Child & Adolescent Clinic will have games and activities for the kids beginning at 8:30 AM** The C&AC is the exclusive sponsor of the Pee Wee Fun Run and is the event organizer. 

​Parking:  There is plenty of parking nearby.  

Race Course. The Harvest Classic begins at the Life Works building at 906 New York Street in Longview.  The course is flat and fast with scenic views of downtown and Lake Sacajawea.

5K - https://www.mapmyrun.com/routes/view/1803585137 

10K - https://www.mapmyrun.com/us/longview-wa/harvest-classic-10k-route-108566341

Timing Equipment​.  Athletic Timing uses Lynx timing equipment. RFID antennas capture your time using disposable chips that are fastened to the back of your racing bib. Take the chips home with you - you will not be asked to return the chips. Wear your bib on the upper chest to maximize the chip reads.

Weather is usually mild. Race time temperatures are likely to range from the low 40s to mid 50s.

Photos. A photographer will be on hand and will post Harvest Classic photos on-line. Please share photos of your run/walk on the Harvest Classic Facebook page.

name: Lookin For A Cure Seattle
description:
"We're "Lookin' For a Cure" in scenic Warren G Magnesun Park! Join A Cure In Sight on Saturday July 18th, 2026 from 8AM-11AM, to walk or run with us. We will be taking steps to find a cure for a rare eye cancer, Ocular Melanoma. Ocular Melanoma is estimated by the American Cancer Society to have roughly 3000 new cases each year nationwide. Bring your friends and family to the race day--all ages welcome to walk or run with us.

Register, become a fund raiser, make a team, grab your friends and family and raise money to support local research with Dr. Stacey and Fred Hutch Cancer Center.  Prizes will be awarded for largest team, largest fundraiser as well as top finishers.

Race Swag

  • Guarantee t-shirt if registered by June 29th.
  • Finisher Medal
  • Food & Drink
  • Aid Station
  • Commemorative Race Bib
  • Free downloadable photos
  • Official finishers time with age group placements

Race day schedule

  • Registration 8AM
  • Race start 9AM
  • Announcements Awards 10AM

Parking

Free parking past the boat launch area, just steps from the start line. If you have an issue on race day, please call 919-885-5264 for directions.

name: Loop the 'Lupe!
description:
Loop The ‘Lupe—The ONLY Obstacle Course Race in Seattle City Limits!

  • Elite Wave: Calling all hardcore racers age 16+! Tackle 45 obstacles (9 per “loop”) in the ultimate 5K challenge. NOTE: Race fast! The two additional obstacles featured in the Elite Wave will be shut down 40 minutes after the start of the event. Elite racers still competing will complete their event on the 7-obstacle Family Wave course. 
  • Family Wave: Want the ninja action without the pressure? Try the 7-obstacle course—perfect for all ages and skill levels!
  • For Everyone (Ages 2–92): Try the 5K run/walk (no obstacles), the Senior Saunter walk (100% flat, no obstacles), or the Youth Dash (once around our 1K 7-obstacle loop with adult supervision)! 
  • Team Up & Save: Grab your crew for big group discounts. The more, the merrier!
  • Race for Good: Your entry supports Our Lady of Guadalupe Church, whose outreach programs help thousands with food, rent, re-entry programs, and more. Top fundraisers win prizes!
  • Go Virtual: Prefer your home turf? Register, get your shirt, and show off your own obstacle course online for a shot at prizes!
  • After-Party: Celebrate with live music, tasty eats, and a beer/cider garden. Stick around for some soccer fun and a penalty kick showdown!
  • Pro Tip: Sign up before May 15 for the best t-shirt selection!

name: Lotus Run
description:
2026 Lotus Run for Mental Health

Our Community has been greatly affected by suicide. The pains stretch deep and wide within our neighborhoods, schools and businesses.

Too many people with mental health challenges feel like this world would be better without them in it— that they are a burden on the world and their loved ones… and that is simply not true!

Through physical wellness, community support, fellowship and with your support, we KNOW we can make a meaningful change in our community, one stride at a time!

So join us in beautiful Lake Stevens, WA on May 31st for a HUGE DAY IN MENTAL HEALTH AWARENESS with a fun and inspiring 10K run, 5k walk/run, or 1 Mile walk/run.

Visit our website for more information and details.

name: Maple Valley Bear Run & Walk 5K
description:
REGISTRATION NOW OPEN!!


$35 for adults; kids 12 and under are FREE, thanks to our sponsors, when you register online by May 31st (a small handling fee will apply for all registrations).  Participants 8 years old and younger must register with and be accompanied by an adult or participant 13 years or older.  

 

SCHEDULE FOR RACE DAY, 6/27/2026

7:30am - 8:30am   Packet pick up and day-of registration*
9:00am                  5K race starts
10:00am                Awards
*Day-of registration (until 8:30am) using your personal mobile device, then come pick up your bib from us! No on-site payments will be accepted.

 

RACE COURSE

5K Run/Walk Race Course map
 

PARKING

Parking will be available at Lake Wilderness Park. We highly encourage carpooling with others. Arrive early so you have enough time before race start!
Please see attached map for specifics. Parking and Race Day Map

 

PRE-RACE PACKET PICK UP

Pre-race packet pick up will be offered at Road Runner Sports in Kent.  Come and get your race bib and t-shirt* before the race.  Grab all of your race day needs when you come in to grab your race bib!  
*T-shirts only guaranteed for those who register by May 31st.
 

CHIP TIMING

Chip timing will be provided by Tortoise and Hare Timing. Disposable chips will be placed on back of bib numbers. 

 

AWARDS 

Awards for both males and females will be given in the following age groups for in person race only.
Age Group Awards will be given based on Chip Time
0-5
6-9
10-12                   
13-15 
16-19 
20-24
25-29               
30-34
35-39               
40-44
45-49 
50-54
55-59               
60-64
65-69
70-74
75-79
80-84
85-89
90-94
95-100
100+
 
 
1st place in each age division wins the coveted Bear Run Bear! 
2nd-3rd place in each age division receive Bear Run Bells
Special awards for top 3 overall men and women will be based on gun time.

 

RACE RESULTS

Official race results will be posted on our website and online at Tortoise & Hare Timing.  Results will be based on chip time (crossing start line to crossing finish line).

 

STROLLERS, DOGS & WATER

We encourage the use of jogging strollers along the trails of this family-friendly 5K!  Out of consideration for other participants, dogs will not be allowed on the course (with the exception of service dogs). We do offer water at the end of the race.

 

GIVING BACK TO THE COMMUNITY 

Proceeds from the Bear Run will benefit Tahoma High School distance running programs administered by the Tahoma Cross Country Running Club.  The funds fill a wide range of needs for our large team of athletes including support for athletes and families who need help with team participation and summer camp fees, multiple scholarships awarded each year, and travel expenses beyond that available from the school district budget.  These kids work hard and run hard all year while maintaining exceptional grade point averages.  They deserve our support!

 

FOR FURTHER INFORMATION

Send email to Katie Leh at mvbearrunwalk@gmail.com

name: Maryhill Wine Run 5k
description:
Like Running or Walking?  Love Wine?  This race is for you! 

Join us on Sunday, June 21, 2026 at 9:00am for an exciting annual event that features the amazing scenery and landscape of Maryhill Winery! For over 25 years Maryhill Winery has crafted wine with passion, patience and balance. So, whether you are looking to run, walk or just enjoy the wine this race is a sure thing for a great time and an incredible experience!  This race is timed and scored by J3 Timing. Results will be posted at www.J3Timing.com. 

Registration Includes:

  • T-shirt:  Super Soft Ring Spun Cotton t-shirt included! 
  • Wine Glass: Shatterproof, Collapsible, and Portable!
  • Finisher Medal: Doubles as a Wine Stopper!
  • Race Bib: Chip timed 5k run/walk
  • Results Posted Online
  • ...and of course, a pour of wine!

name: May the Course be with You 5k
description:
Get ready for a galaxy-sized adventure! May the 4th is more than just a day – it's a celebration of all things Star Wars! 🚀✨

This year, we’re inviting you to channel your inner Jedi (or Sith!) and join us for a FUN-tastic 5K race. Whether you're aiming to out-speed the Millennium Falcon or just looking for a fun day out, this race is for everyone. So, grab your lightsaber, throw on your favorite Star Wars outfit (Yoda ears? Wookiee costume? You name it!), and let's make this event truly legendary. 🏃‍♂️💨💫

Let the Force guide you as you race through the course with your friends. Whether you're a pro or just in it for the fun, the May the Course Be With You 5K promises plenty of laughs, surprises, and of course, a lot of galactic fun! 💥

DID YOU KNOW? May 4th has officially become Star Wars Day, thanks to the famous line “May the Force be with you” from Star Wars: A New Hope (1977). Since then, it's been echoed across films, books, and video games, becoming a day of celebration for fans around the galaxy. 🌌🎉

Ready to race? Don't forget to dress in your best Star Wars gear and bring your A-game – the Force will definitely be with you!

Check out our FAQs for all the details: May the Course Be With You 5K FAQs 🌠

May the course—and the fun—be with you! 🎉

 

Questions? Concerns? Email us! General inquiries:  info@run2befit.com

name: Medal Madness 5K, 10K, & 13.1M at Everett, WA (11)
description:
Race Information
The race starts at 8:30 AM.
Packet pickup starts 30 minutes before the race and ends 10 minutes before the race starts.
All runners must register on RunSignup. 
No on-site registration.

Additional Information
Park at the North Creek Trail.

5K & 10K Course (0.78M)
https://www.mapmyrun.com/routes/view/6634249787 
The course is an out-and-back (1.56M)
The 5K does the out-and-back two times.
The 10K does the out-and-back four times.

Half Marathon Course (1.09M)
https://www.mapmyrun.com/routes/view/6634249965 
The course is an out and back. (2.16M)
Half Marathon does the course six times. 

Course Time Limit
3 hours and 30 minutes.

name: Medical Lake Lions Club- 48th Annual Only Fools Run at Midnight
description:
Welcome to the 48th Annual Only Fools Run at Midnight!  We will continue to offer both live and virtual options this year. 

Our live event will take place on March 28th with a start time of 11:30 pm. 

Runners will once again be able to run the mean streets of Medical Lake at midnight.  We will start at Medical Lake High School and have race monitors throughout the course with our finish line at the Barrel to celebrate our achievements.  They will be open late just for the race.

name: Medical Lake- Trailblazer Triathlon/Duathlon/5K
description:
The Medical Lake Trailblazer Tri/Du/5k is one of the many things to do in Medical Lake on Founders Day weekend. This is an athlete-friendly race with a point-to-point open water swim, bike, and run on paved roads & trails.

Trailblazer Triathlon
A 350m swim, 12.2mi bike ride, and 2.92 mi run starting and ending at Waterfront Park. 

Trailblazer Duathlon
A 1mi run, 12.2mi bike ride, and 2.92 mi run starting and ending at Waterfront Park. 

Trailblazer 5k
A traditional 2.92 mi run around Medical Lake Trail starting and ending at Waterfront Park.

name: Memorial Day Run 5K/10K/13.1 SEATTLE
description:
Honor, Remember, and Run for Freedom This Memorial Day, join us for the Memorial Day Freedom Run - a special event that combines a run with the powerful spirit of remembrance.  Whether you're running solo or with friends and family, this event honors the brave men and women who have sacrificed for our freedom.
Every mile you complete is a tribute to their courage and service.  With scenic routes, motivating challenges, and a community united in purpose, the Memorial Day Freedom Run is more than just a race - it's a meaningful way to pay respect while staying active. 
Sign up today to celebrate freedom, remember our heroes, and run for a cause that matters.  Together, we can make this Memorial Day unforgettable.

Overview:
Run will sell-out QUICK! We will close off waves the moment they fill up. If waves are sold out, you can sign-up for the virtual run option or wait list.
This is a smaller, private group run with a cap per wave.
All paces and ages (under 18 with guardian) are welcome - Run or Walk!  
There's no equipment or setup, this is a pure run with our coordinators to support you in a warm, stress-free setting!
When you sign-up, we give you the support you need to help you achieve your goals and fitness. We also invite you to be part of our local run clubs that supports your fitness journey. 
Timing:
- Timing is Optional: You may track your time on an app (Strava, RunKeeper, Nike Run, etc) and submit your times with our easy form to be posted online. Or you can ask our coordinators to help keep track of your time. 
- No timing chips (This is a stress free run to support you in achieving your goals)!
What You Get (Swag Bag):
- Running T-Shirt (Shipped to the address you register with - US only)
- Finisher's Towel or Giveaway
- Finisher's Medal! 
- Digital Training Pack 
- Online Results & Certificate of Completion
- Invitation to Join one of our Local Running Clubs
- We now have Technical Running Shirts (Optional). These lightweight, moisture wicking shirts can be upgraded for just $5 more. 
Packet Pickup:
No hassle of picking up packets required!
-Swag shipped direct to your address (Please make sure you provide your full, correct US mailing address including apartment number and check spelling)
- Race bibs are provided on race day
When will I get my Swag?
You will get your shirt at your mailing address the week of your race.
Race Updates:
We will email you a final update the Wednesday before the race with final details and course maps.
Do you accept last minute registrations? (For those signing up 2 weeks before the race)
Yes, but please note that it takes time for us to ship your shirt. Your shirt will likely arrive after the run. You can wear any shirt you find appropriate to run the race! 
 
Wave Times: (Email Us Your Desired Wave Time: info@thebestraces.com)

name: Metaline Falls Bigfoot 5K Race & LittleFoot Kids Run
description:
Bigfoot 5k Race - Saturday, June 20, 2026 at 8:00am

Join us at our 6th Annual Bigfoot 5k Race in beautiful Metaline Falls, WA on Saturday, June 20th at 8:00am! The course will take you from downtown Metaline Falls, up and down Lehigh Hill with gorgeous mountain views, past the historic Cutter Theatre, along the beautiful Pend Oreille river, and finish at the town's Busta Park.

After the event, join in at the fun festivities of the Metaline Falls Bigfoot Festival! There will be vendors, food, and entertainment!

A virtual race option is also available and swag will be mailed to you after the race!

Registration fee includes:

  • Long-sleeve tech material shirt
  • Finisher medal
  • Post-Race snacks
  • 1st, 2nd, & 3rd place medals for men's and women's categories

Bigfoot 5k Race Packet Pickup will take place on Friday and Saturday at Busta Park in Metaline Falls. We strongly encourage runners to attend the Friday packet pick-up to make your race morning less stressful. At packet pickup you will be able to retrieve your race bib and your shirt (if applicable).

Race packet pickup times are as follows:

  • Pre-race Packet Pickup: Friday, June 19 from 4:00 - 6:00 pm at Busta Park
  • Race day Packet Pickup: Saturday, June 20 from 6:00 - 7:30 am at Busta Park
     

 

LittleFoot Kids Run - Sunday, June 21, 2026 at 8:00am

Join us at our 1st Annual LittleFoot Kids Run! The race will begin and end at the Cutter Theatre, 302 Park Street, Metaline Falls, WA.

DISTANCE: The distance will be either 1K or 2K (you choose based on your abilities). This is a fun run that is not timed.

AGES: Ages 13 and under welcome and parents can participate with their small kiddos too. Parents don't need to register.

name: Miles for Mamas 5k
description:
🌍 JOIN US FOR THE MILES FOR MAMAS 5K — March 2026!
Virtual + in-person | $45 Entry | First 50 People Get a Free T-shirt | Medals for ALL Finishers

Safe prenatal care shouldn't depend on where you live!

Location: Greenlake Community Center Basketball Courts 

We are excited to announce the Miles for Mamas 5K, supporting the Manyoni Mama Project to bring an ultrasound machine to St. Maria de Mattias Hospital in rural Tanzania. Whether you're nearby or across the country, you can run or walk from wherever you are!

🏃‍♀️ What’s Included with the $45 (non-refundable) REGISTRATION fee

  • FREE T-shirt for the first 50 registered participants (virtual or in-person)
  • Finisher medal for everyone (virtual or in-person)
  • An opportunity to be a part of something BIG

📅 Participation Options:

  • In-Person 5K
  • Virtual 5K
  • Fundraising Challenge


💛Optional Fundraising Challenge

If you choose to participate as a fund raiser:

  • You use your own Venmo, Zelle, or CashApp, etc. to collect donations
  • By March 21, you donate the total amount you collected to the Manyoni Mama Project (via GoFundMe)
    • https://www.gofundme.com/f/manyoni-mama-project
  • You send a screenshot of your total raised to manyonimamaproject@gmail.com
  • Receive a Prize!
    • AND your $45 registration fee refunded


**T-shirts and medals will be available for pick-up on race day**


🌟 Be Part of Something Big
Your participation will help bring an ultrasound machine to a rural community in Tanzania. Giving mothers safer pregnancies and helping families access lifesaving care. 


 Help us spread the word, invite friends, and let’s make this movement for mothers 💛

name: Miles for Meals Kitsap
description:
Miles for Meals is a VIRTUAL endurance event designed to encourage you to MOVE over a 1 week period! You get to choose what type of movement you want to do: General Fitness, Walk, Run, Hike, Bike, Swim, Ski, Snowshoe, Snowboard, Roll, or Row. Either by yourself, or with your team. This year we've also added an option to sign up your furry friends! And your beloved pets will even compete in their own category to win a prize! 

Each registration ($25) buys two meals for home-bound seniors in Kitsap County and all additional proceeds directly benefit Meals on Wheels Kitsap.

Peer-to-peer fundraising is how the majority of funds are raised in our event! You'll again have the ability to create a personal or team fundraising page...and we hope you will!

So what are you waiting for...

How many miles can we move?

How many meals can we give?

Join our private Facebook group for the event to share your photos from you covering your miles and encourage each other throughout the week! PLUS, there will be some optional BONUS challenges you can choose to complete for additional points, and the Facebook group is where you will post your proof of completed challenges.

Also, feel free to post your pics to your own social media pages and use the event hashtag #Miles4MealsKitsap so we can find your posts and give you kudos!

name: Millwood Daze 5k
description:
Community celebration 5k favorite is back!  The Millwood Daze 5k returns this year.  From it's tree-lined start in historic Millwood, its a flat, fast loop course great for runners and walkers.  Join us for the Millwood Daze celebration after the run with a pancake breakfast, street fair with community booths, and a classic car show.

Tee shirts available for purchase to all registrants.  Order by 8/12 to have it by race day.  After that, tee shirt pick up or delivery will be arranged.

name: Mimosa 5K
description:
Join us for a fun summer run/walk through beautiful Downtown Puyallup!
Participants will run or walk along sidewalks and through one of Puyallup’s vibrant neighborhoods, taking in the charm and local flavor along the way.
The event will start and finish at the Lazy Ballerina Wine Bar,
📍 319 S Meridian, Puyallup, WA 98371

After you cross the finish line, stick around and enjoy amazing mimosas and Sunday brunch at the Lazy Ballerina. Looking for a more family-friendly post-race option? Head just up the street to our fantastic partners at Firemind Brewing and CaskCades, where everyone can continue the fun.

Whether you’re running, walking, or strolling, this is the perfect way to kick off a summer Sunday! ☀️👟🍾

Registration includes custom medal, custom race bib and race day snacks.

description: Experience the rugged beauty of Mt. Spokane State Park with three distance options featuring lush singletrack, challenging climbs, and sweeping summit views. All courses start and finish at Selkirk Lodge, delivering a true mountain trail adventure in a stunning alpine setting.

name: National Chocolate Day: Run for Chocolates 5K/10K/13.1 SEATTLE
description:
🍫🏃‍♀️ Ready, Set, Chocolate! 🏃‍♂️🍫
Join Us for the Sweetest Run of the Year – The Chocolate Run!
Lace up your running shoes and bring your sweet tooth—because this isn’t your average race.
It’s a deliciously fun event for all ages and fitness levels!

 

Overview:
Run will sell-out QUICK! We will close off waves the moment they fill up. If waves are sold out, you can sign-up for the virtual run option or wait list.
This is a smaller, private group run with a cap per wave.
All paces and ages (under 18 with guardian) are welcome - Run or Walk!  
There's no equipment or setup, this is a pure run with our coordinators to support you in a warm, stress-free setting!
When you sign-up, we give you the support you need to help you achieve your goals and fitness. We also invite you to be part of our local run clubs that supports your fitness journey. 
Timing:
- Timing is Optional: You may track your time on an app (Strava, RunKeeper, Nike Run, etc) and submit your times with our easy form to be posted online. Or you can ask our coordinators to help keep track of your time. 
- No timing chips (This is a stress free run to support you in achieving your goals)!
What You Get (Swag Bag):
- Running T-Shirt (Shipped to the address you register with - US only)
- Finisher's Towel or Giveaway
- Finisher's Medal! 
- Digital Training Pack 
- Online Results & Certificate of Completion
- Invitation to Join one of our Local Running Clubs
- We now have Technical Running Shirts (Optional). These lightweight, moisture wicking shirts can be upgraded for just $5 more. 
Packet Pickup:
No hassle of picking up packets required!
-Swag shipped direct to your address (Please make sure you provide your full, correct US mailing address including apartment number and check spelling)
- Race bibs are provided on race day
When will I get my Swag?
You will get your shirt at your mailing address the week of your race.
Race Updates:
We will email you a final update the Wednesday before the race with final details and course maps.
Do you accept last minute registrations? (For those signing up 2 weeks before the race)
Yes, but please note that it takes time for us to ship your shirt. Your shirt will likely arrive after the run. You can wear any shirt you find appropriate to run the race! 
 
Wave Times: (Email Us Your Desired Wave Time: info@thebestraces.com)
(Waves filled on a First Come, First Serve Basis)
Wave A: 7:30AM
Wave B: 8:00AM
Wave C: 8:30AM
Late runners can run upon arrival (Please note our coordinators stay 3 hours after the first wave)
Are there any other Questions we missed?
https://www.thebestraces.com/faq/
Virtual Run Option:
- Our Virtual Run uniquely offers a Training Pack with Digital Tools to support your run. 
Virtual runs can be done any time and place of your choosing using any tracking device (optional). After you finish, you can submit your results to info@thebestraces.com to receive your medal! 
Race Bundle:
Sign-up for more races and get a discount! 

Sponsorships & Promoting your Business:

If you're looking to become a sponsor, we'd love showcase your business!
https://www.thebestraces.com/events
 

Team Glo Volunteers:

If you're interested in helping put on runs for the Community and helping people achieve their goals, we invite you to join our team of volunteers, fill out the form here: https://www.thebestraces.com/volunteer-form/
 

Be part of the Journey!

Our Charity Initiatives. Find out more @ www.thebestracesjourney.com
Keep running. Every mile you log after the race, we'll donate $1 to one of the charities we work with! (Note that Fundraising is Optional)

name: Never Say Never Half Marathon & 10K
description:
This race is all about YOU! Every decision we make has YOU in mind. This is a race designed for everyone from first timers to seasoned racers to all of those in-between. It is a picturesque course with one sizable hill around mile 2 followed by flat road for the rest of the 10K and rolling hills for the remainder of the Half Marathon.  
There will be NINE water stations this year. There are six bathroom opportunities, and lots of fans cheering you on along the way. 
We are again partnering with BOX, a nonprofit organization founded by women, dedicated to building connections that support women and girls. In 2021 we donated $4,100 to the Highland School District, in 2022 we donated $2,000 plus products to Davis High School, in 2023 we presented a $3,000 check to Rod’s House plus a ton of period products, and in 2024 we were beyond proud to write an $8,300 to Children's Village. This was our biggest donation by far!!!! This year we are proud to announce we raised $9,000 for Yakima's YWCA!
We are so excited and proud to announce we will be raising money for Nathan's Place. When we started this crazy dream we raised money for Highland High School (unfortunately we did not have a race that year because of smoke) so, because this is our last year putting on the Never Say Never we wanted to again raise money for our hometown. 
Nathan's Place was born just last year!  Some amazing members of our community who noticed that our high school kids have no place to hang out after school dedicated their time and resources to create a gathering place. They have been worked tirelessly to make Nathan's Place more than just a dream. Nathan’s Place is a “safe, inclusive and supportive environment where [6th-12th grade] kids can grow through educational programs, mentorship, and mental wellness support.” Click here to find out more about Nathan’s Place. Your donations this year are going to make the biggest difference yet!
Flying pig trophies will be back again for first, second, and third place women and men runners and walkers for the Half Marathon and the 10K. 
However, if even a 10K doesn’t sound fun come for the Finish Line Celebration Party! This is FREE to attend and welcome to all! Come cheer on the racers, get fabulous grub from Tacos Don Chayo, get refreshed with local beverages from Shorthead, Tieton Cider, and French Canyon Cellars, play yard games, partake in our raffle, and the WHEEL of FUN will be back again for even more prizes!

name: North Olympic Discovery Marathon (5K / 10K/ Half / Full / Relay / Kids Marathon)
description:
The North Olympic Discovery Marathon, Marathon Walk, Marathon Relay and Half Marathon take place on a unique point to point course that incorporates the beautiful Olympic Discovery Trail with stunning views of the Olympic Mountains and a five mile finishing stretch along the shores of the Strait of Juan de Fuca. The 10K,  5K and Kids Marathon are an out-and-back along the shores of the Strait of Juan de Fuca. 

Frequent sightings of seals, eagles, and an array of shore birds are common from the trail. Iconic trestle bridges provide beautiful back drops. Salmon can be seen spawning at the Morse Creek crossing in the fall. The North Olympic Discovery Marathon is truly one of the most beautiful marathon venues anywhere.

This rails to trails course is a wide, hard surface (99% paved) trail. The course is marked at every mile and water stations are located approximately every two miles. Cool June weather can be expected  – average high is 65F, average low is 49F, average mean is 57F.

The race is organized by the Port Angeles Marathon Association – a group of accomplished amateur athletes.

The Marathon is a USATF certified course and a Boston Marathon qualifier.

name: OAT Run
description:
* 50K * Half Marathon * 12K *

The Olympic Adventure Trail Run (OAT Run) is a point-to-point trail 12K and half marathon as well as an out-and-back 50K that traverses Kelly Ridge between the Olympic National Park and the Strait of Juan de Fuca in Washington State, all on single-track trail.  Limit 130 runners per distance.

The OAT Run Experience

OAT Run is for trail runners who enjoy lush green forests filled with moss and ferns, towering evergreens, and spring trailside flowers. Runners will get a stunning view of the Elwha River Valley as they run by the “Living Room”. And if this wasn’t epic enough, get ready to eat, drink, and relax post-race with an amazing view of the Olympic Mountains. The after-party at Extreme Sports Park is a fun atmosphere, and racers will get hot burritos from Little Devil's Lunchbox and cold drinks, a toasty campfire, and door prizes (woot!). There will be a beer garden at the after-party as well, with proceeds to support 4PA, a local non-profit organization. 

What’s included?

name: OHEF Family Fun Run
description:
Oak Harbor Educational Foundation's first Family Fun Run is coming to Windjammer Park on May 30!

We're hosting a fun run for both kids and grown ups with three race lengths: A 5K route, a 1-mile student run and a 1/2-mile student run! The 1/2 mile student run will begin at 9 a.m., followed by the 1-mile student run and then the 5k run.

Sign up with your family and friends for this event along the Oak Harbor waterfront.

For an extra layer of fun, come dressed in your favorite 80s decade attire. 

After the race on May 30, be sure to stop by MOD Pizza and mention Oak Harbor Educational Foundation or order online with the code MODGIVES20.

----------

The mission of the Oak Harbor Educational Foundation (OHEF) is to empower Oak Harbor School District’s students and educators. We create opportunities for students to thrive, receive scholarships for post-secondary education, and enable teachers and schools to provide supportive and innovative learning experiences.

Learn more about OHEF here:
Oak Harbor Educational Foundation

----------

Things to note for the OHEF Fun Run:
* This race is not a chipped timed event.
* Please leave your pets at home.

name: Oktoberfest Fly Away 10K Run & 5K Run/Walk
description:
Register Now for the 7th Annual Fly Away Run

Join us in 2026 for the 7th Annual Fly Away Run, a family-friendly community event featuring both a 5K run/walk and a 10K run. The race will begin in Kenmore and follow a marked course along the Burke-Gilman Trail toward Bothell.

Additional event details, including schedule, packet pickup information, and race-day amenities, will be shared as the event approaches.

The Fly Away Run is part of Kenmore’s Oktoberfest celebration, now in its 3rd year, bringing even more energy and excitement to this annual tradition.

 

2026 Day of Event Schedule - 

The Fly Away Run launches from the Burke-Gilman Trail access point in Kenmore, located at 192 Brewing Co. Lake Trail Taproom & Copperworks Distilling. (7324 NE 175th Street, Kenmore).

Course: Timed, marked out-and-back route on the Burke-Gilman Trail, heading east toward Bothell

 

8:00 AM - 11:00 AM        

8:00 AM | Packet Pickup Begins  
8:45 AM - 9:00 AM | Launch 10K & Kid Run 
9:00 AM - 9:15 AM | 5K Line Up & Run/Walk Begins   
10:15 AM - 11:00 AM | Finisher Awards and Community Celebration

 

Event Details

Giveaway, Medals & More
All registered participants will receive a commemorative medal, and those who register by September 1 are guaranteed an event giveaway. After September 1, giveaways will be available while supplies last.

Giveaway: Guaranteed with registration by September 1; limited quantities thereafter

Medals: Awarded to all registered race participants

Pets Welcome: Leashed pets, pet strollers, or wagons are welcome on the course. Please ensure pets remain on a short leash and that owners clean up after their animals.

Parking: Parking is available on nearby streets and at the Kenmore Park & Ride, which offers crosswalk access at the traffic light for convenient entry to the event.

 

Bib Pick-Up Week of Race:

Wednesday - Thursday @ Bothell Kenmore Chamber Office (10:00 AM - 2:00 PM)
Friday @ launch location 4:00 PM - 7:00 PM
Day of Event 8:00 AM

name: Oktoberfest Run 5K/10K/13.1 SEATTLE
description:
🥨 Lace up, get festive, and earn your Oktoberfest celebration the best way possible — by running for it!

Our delightful 'Oktoberfest Fun Run' is back with a dash of Bavarian spirit. Join this race that's brimming with Gemütlichkeit (friendliness) and fun! 

Overview:
Run will sell-out QUICK! We will close off waves the moment they fill up. If waves are sold out, you can sign-up for the virtual run option or wait list.
This is a smaller, private group run with a cap per wave.
All paces and ages (under 18 with guardian) are welcome - Run or Walk!  
There's no equipment or setup, this is a pure run with our coordinators to support you in a warm, stress-free setting!
When you sign-up, we give you the support you need to help you achieve your goals and fitness. We also invite you to be part of our local run clubs that supports your fitness journey. 
Timing:
- Timing is Optional: You may track your time on an app (Strava, RunKeeper, Nike Run, etc) and submit your times with our easy form to be posted online. Or you can ask our coordinators to help keep track of your time. 
- No timing chips (This is a stress free run to support you in achieving your goals)!
What You Get (Swag Bag):
- Running T-Shirt (Shipped to the address you register with - US only)
- Finisher's Towel or Giveaway
- Finisher's Medal! 
- Digital Training Pack 
- Online Results & Certificate of Completion
- Invitation to Join one of our Local Running Clubs
- We now have Technical Running Shirts (Optional). These lightweight, moisture wicking shirts can be upgraded for just $5 more. 
Packet Pickup:
No hassle of picking up packets required!
-Swag shipped direct to your address (Please make sure you provide your full, correct US mailing address including apartment number and check spelling)
- Race bibs are provided on race day
When will I get my Swag?
You will get your shirt at your mailing address the week of your race.
Race Updates:
We will email you a final update the Wednesday before the race with final details and course maps.
Do you accept last minute registrations? (For those signing up 2 weeks before the race)
Yes, but please note that it takes time for us to ship your shirt. Your shirt will likely arrive after the run. You can wear any shirt you find appropriate to run the race! 
 
Wave Times: (Email Us Your Desired Wave Time: info@thebestraces.com)
(Waves filled on a First Come, First Serve Basis)
Wave A: 7:30AM
Wave B: 8:00AM
Wave C: 8:30AM
Late runners can run upon arrival (Please note our coordinators stay 3 hours after the first wave)
Are there any other Questions we missed?
https://www.thebestraces.com/faq/
Virtual Run Option:
- Our Virtual Run uniquely offers a Training Pack with Digital Tools to support your run. 
Virtual runs can be done any time and place of your choosing using any tracking device (optional). After you finish, you can submit your results to info@thebestraces.com to receive your medal! 
Race Bundle:
Sign-up for more races and get a discount! 

Sponsorships & Promoting your Business:

If you're looking to become a sponsor, we'd love showcase your business!
https://www.thebestraces.com/events
 

Team Glo Volunteers:

If you're interested in helping put on runs for the Community and helping people achieve their goals, we invite you to join our team of volunteers, fill out the form here: https://www.thebestraces.com/volunteer-form/
 

Be part of the Journey!

Our Charity Initiatives. Find out more @ www.thebestracesjourney.com
Keep running. Every mile you log after the race, we'll donate $1 to one of the charities we work with! (Note that Fundraising is Optional)

name: Olympia Lakefair Races - Half Marathon, 8K & 3K
description:
2026 marks the 50th Anniversary of the Olympia Lakefair Races, which include the Jerry Miller Half Marathon, an 8K and a 3K including free entry for Kids 14 and under; taking runners on routes that circle around the town of Olympia and beyond into Tumwater and Thurston County.

Both the 3K and 8K start and finish on 5th Avenue in front of Heritage Park.  They both circle Capitol Lake, with the 8K continuing into Tumwater Historical Park before returning. Both are flat and fast courses. 

The Jerry Miller Half Marathon heads briefly through downtown Olympia, then along the Woodland Trial and Chehalis Western Trail biking paths.  The course continues on rural streets and a short trail and tour of Squaxin Park before heading back along East Bay Drive and running through downtown Olympia to the finish line in front of Heritage Park.  Runners will enjoy tree-lined trails and scenic landscapes while enjoying flat and narrow paved trails throughout.

Once runners have completed the course, there is an awards ceremony with several raffle awards as well as age group award up to 90+ for all three races.  Participants, family and friends can then enjoy festival activities that are held all around Heritage Park including food and beer tents, carnival rides, booths, a parade and more.  

The Valley Athletic Club is proud to be the 2026 Presenting Sponsor.  The Olympia Lakefair Races are brought to you by the Lake Run Organization and the Rotary Club of Olympia, and benefit local public High School Cross Country and Track programs and Rotary Club of Olympia Scholarship and Grant recipients.

See you July 18, 2026!

name: One Step Closer
description:
What do you get when you take Orca Running and mix it with Evergreen Trail!? Welcome to One Step Closer. An exciting summer endurance event created by Orca Running AND Evergreen Trail Runs. Part whale, part trail-and loopy. Held in the one and only Lincoln Park, this race is going to be THE summer endurance event you won’t want to miss.

Course: Loops at Lincoln Park. Amazingly diverse for its size, this race experience has a bit of everything. Runners will take on a 2 mile course loop, and complete the loop as many times as they can during their selected time period: 18 hours, 12 hours, 6 hours, or 3 hours. All runners will finish together at 11:00pm with a finish line party! 

Check out all the details on our website!

NEW for 2026:

Battle of the run clubs: During registration, you will have the opportunity to be part of a “team.” Teams can consist of 2-5 members and The top 3 teams with the most loops at the end of the event will earn a special finishers plaque and ultimate run club (or friend group) bragging rights.

Kid's Loopy Race: Choose from 30 minutes or 1 hour. Kid’s will complete as many loops around the baseball field as they can within their selected time. Kids can take as many breaks as they choose, and the course will run through the snack station for treats as they go (just like the adults). All of the kids will finish together in a special One Step Closer kid’s race celebration. Each Kid’s Race runner will be awarded a One Step Closer medal upon completion.

name: Onion Man Triathlon
description:
Onion Man is a grass roots, affordable, low-key, early season event in beautiful Walla Walla meant to be accessible to all triathletes. This race is for beginners looking to gain experience to elite athletes looking for a competitive, challenging race. Onion Man is also open to team competitors. We wish all of you a safe race and encourage you to get out there and swim hard, ride strong, run fast and most of all, enjoy yourselves!

* The race will have a 300 participant cap! Register early *

The 31st Annual Onion Man Triathlon will be held on SUNDAY, May 17, 2026. The Olympic Distance race held at the base of the Blue Mountains is a 1.5K lake swim, 40K rolling bike, and a 10k honest run. 

BIKE COURSE:  Will be basically the same as the 2024 bike course: Five Mile hill, down Russell Creek Road and back with a short out and back extension on Scenic Loop Road, and back to Bennington Lake.  The only change is that the course will not run through the Walla Walla Community College and instead continue straight on Tausick Way and turn right onto E. Isaacs Ave.  In accordance with USAT rules, bar end plugs are required on all bikes.

Registration includes a short-sleeved Tshirt (if you register before Apr 29), a meal ticket to the post race meal, and 1 free beer from Quirk Brewing in a custom pint glass.  You may also add-on a beer for non-participants for $5.  No day of race registration and no wait list available if race fills. No refunds, transfers and no deferrals.

Onion Man Triathlon race is a USA Triathlon Sanctioned event (Event ID #310427), if you are a USAT member you will need to enter your number on the registration page. If you are not a member you will need to click on one-day license. If you are a USAT member be ready to show your valid Membership Card at packet pick up. Everyone will need to show picture ID as well.

Thank you and let's race !

name: Operation School Bell® 5K Run/Walk - Assistance League® of the Eastside
description:
The Assistance League® of the Eastside strives to serve the immediate, unmet needs of children and adults challenged by hardship or violence, strengthening our community while fostering dignity, confidence, and hope.

We are holding our second annual 5K at Marymoor Park, Redmond on Saturday, June 6th!  Plan to park at Parking Lot K by the tennis courts. The Race starts by Baseball Field #5.  Your participation helps us raise funds for our signature program:

Operation School Bell® supports the belief that new school clothing and essential living needs, and the resulting increase in self-esteem and school attendance, contributes to a strong foundation for a child’s successful educational experience.  Financial hardship can touch any family, often creating barriers to a child’s success in school.   Assistance League of the Eastside’s program Operation School Bell provides funds to students in need, supporting them to shop at their local Fred Meyer stores for essentials like clothing, shoes, books, school supplies, medications, and groceries.  These students are carefully selected by school personnel from the Bellevue, Lake Washington, and Northshore School Districts, ensuring your support reaches those who need it most.  But our impact goes far beyond material goods. Operation School Bell helps children feel confident, fit in with their peers, and have the tools they need to thrive academically. New clothes, a warm coat, or a book of their own — these simple items foster self-esteem and give students the foundation for a brighter future.  For some children, this will be the first time they have had a new pair of shoes, a warm coat, or a book of their very own.  Now, they truly feel like they fit in with the other kids.

We welcome runners, walkers, & joggers from Redmond, Bothell, Kirkland, Bellevue, Woodinville, Kenmore and all other communities!

All participants will receive complimentary:

  • Event T-shirt (only guaranteed if registered by April 30)
  • Finisher's Medal
  • Finish Line drinks and snacks

==> Should you not be able to join us in person or virtually for the Race, you can still order a souvenir T-shirt by 5/01/2026 - select STORE option above.

If you are unable to make our Race after SignUp, we're sorry to miss you but we gratefully appreciate the tax-deductible donation of your registration fee to support Operation School Bell for the 2026-2027 school year!

name: OUTLAST SPOKANE
description:
What Is OUTLAST?

OUTLAST is a 6-hour trail endurance challenge where runners complete a 5K every hour, on the hour. Each lap must be finished within the hour to stay in the event. If you finish early, you rest until the next round. Miss a lap, and you’re out.

Complete all six rounds, and you OUTLAST.

This isn't just about speed — it's about pacing, discipline, and mental grit. Whether you're trying to survive all six or win your division, the challenge is the same: show up each hour, push your limits, and stay in it.

Each course is trail-based, with natural terrain, elevation, and unpredictable conditions. You’ll have time between rounds to recover, refuel, and refocus — but not much.

 

What You Earn:

​4 laps = “Grit Earned” patch
5 laps = “Survivor” patch
6 laps = Premium “OUTLAST” medal

​​All participants receive a premium OUTLAST Tee.

Top male and female with the fastest combined 5K times at each event win the 1st Place OUTLAST award. 

Finishers are ranked on the national leaderboard—and the fastest runner across all OUTLAST 6-hour events will be crowned National Champion and take home $1,000.

The 1st Place Male and Female 6-hour champions from each city will earn a spot in the Outlast Championship, where they’ll compete against the best of the best at the end of the Tour, and the 1st place male and female winners take home $1000 each. (This is separate from the national leaderboard prize money.)

By the end of the tour, the top 100 best times nationally will be invited to also compete in the Outlast Championship.

 

Frequently Asked Questions:

Do I have to run all 6 laps?
Nope. Run as many as you can. If you complete 4 or 5, you'll still earn a patch. Only those who finish all 6 get the OUTLAST medal and leaderboard ranking.

What happens if I don’t finish a lap in time?
You're out. The next lap starts at the top of the next hour, and only those who completed the last lap on time can continue.

How is the race timed?
Each 5K is timed individually. If you complete all 6, your combined time counts toward the local win and national leaderboard.

Are these trail races or road?
Every OUTLAST race is on trail terrain — dirt, rocks, roots, and elevation. Sometimes some pavement and gravel.

Can I walk?
Yes, as long as you finish the 5K within the hour. But some courses are rugged, and time can sneak up on you.

Are there aid stations?
Yes. There will be water, basic hydration, and snacks at the basecamp/loop start. This is a cupless event — bring your own bottle or hydration system.

What should I bring?
Trail shoes, hydration system, layers (weather dependent), fuel between laps, and grit.

Can I setup a tent?
Absolutely, bring your own aid station/tent setup.

Is OUTLAST for beginners?
Yes — if you're mentally tough. You don’t need to be fast, just consistent and ready to suffer a little.

How do I win?
If you finish all 6 laps and have the fastest combined time, you win your division (male/female). Winners are also added to the national leaderboard for a shot at the $1,000 national prize & title.
