name: 4.5 Mile Trail Run at Silver Falls
description:
The time has come to finally change up the Buck Mountain trail run, and we're excited to announce the all-new "4.5 Mile Trail Run at Silver Falls" with an all-new very scenic single-track course and much less elevation gain than the old course. Same start/finish area as we all know and same start time 9am. 16th annual event!

Here's the big change! The course and timing will be open for 6 hours to allow runners to complete as many loops as they desire in that timeframe! Training for an ultra? Here's your opportunity! Only want to run the course once for 4.5 miles and be done? Perfect! Want to run a very fun and scenic Half Marathon? Awesome, run 3 loops and you got it! We are here for you and will time you every lap of the way and post results, individual lap times and pace after every loop is completed. Aid station at the start/finish of each loop on the course. We will have our usual spread of refreshments, food, beer and snacks for after you finish. Come enjoy a day with us at the beautiful and very scenic Silver Falls St. Park and explore some of the back country single track trails that the park has to offer.

All new 4.5 mile loop course! Very scenic trail run on mostly single track trail mixed with a few gravel and paved sections. Elevation gain and loss of around 430 feet total.
Run as many loops as you desire in 6 hours!
- Run 1 loop and be done
- Run 2 loops for 9 Miles
- Run 3 loops for a Half Marathon (13.5 Miles)
- Run 4 loops for 18 Miles
- Run 5 loops for 22.5 Miles
- Run 6 loops for 27 Miles
- Run 7 loops for a 50K (31.5 Miles) and so on…
Aid Station at the start/finish of each loop at mile 4.5
Course will close and timing will be complete at 6 hours!
Start Cutoff Time - 2:30pm 5 ½ Hours
Finish Cutoff Time - 3:00pm 6 Hours

name: Abacela Wine Run 5k
description:
Like Running or Walking?  Love Wine?  This race is for you! 

Join us on Sunday, June 28, 2026 at 9:00am for an exciting annual event that features the amazing scenery and landscape of Abacela Winery! Abacela is a world-class, multi-award-winning winery and viticulture success story. So, whether you are looking to run, walk or just enjoy the wine this race is a sure thing for a great time and an incredible experience!  This race is timed and scored by J3 Timing. Results will be posted at www.J3Timing.com. 

Registration Includes:

  • T-shirt:  Super Soft Ring Spun Cotton t-shirt included! 
  • Wine Glass: Shatterproof, Collapsible, and Portable!
  • Finisher Medal: Doubles as a Wine Stopper!
  • Race Bib: Chip timed 5k run/walk
  • Results Posted Online
  • ...and of course, a pour of wine!

name: Awesome 3000
description:
Welcome to the Awesome 3000! Join us as we return to McCulloch Stadium for another year of this exciting event.

name: Bandwidth 5k  Fun Run
description:
The Bandwidth – 2nd Annual 5K Fun Run
Get ready to lace up your running shoes and turn up the volume! 🎵 The Century High School Marching Band proudly presents the 2nd Annual Bandwidth 5K Fun Run, winding through the beautiful new neighborhoods of South Hillsboro.

This isn’t your average run—along the course, you’ll be energized by multiple live music stations featuring the talented Century High School Marching Band. Every step is set to a soundtrack, from upbeat pep tunes to crowd favorites, making this a run you won’t forget.

Whether you’re a seasoned runner, a casual jogger, or just here for the music and fun, The Bandwidth is all about community spirit, fitness, and supporting the incredible music program at Century High School.

Run. Listen. Support the Band.

name: Beaver Freezer Triathlon and Duathlon
description: The Beaver Freezer Sprint Triathlon is a community event that attracts racers from throughout the Willamette Valley and all over the Northwest. Started in 1993, the Freezer has been the OSU Triathlon Club's annual fundraising event for the past 25+ years. In 2010, the Beaver Freezer became the LARGEST TRIATHLON (with an indoor swim) in the UNITED STATES! Participants' experience varies from first-time triathletes to veterans; age groups range from 16-19 to 60-plus; and there are individual and relay categories available. Participants use a wide variety of equipment and encourage you to "run what ya brung!" We invite you to join the wonderful world of multisport! Come race in this early season sprint triathlon! All abilities are welcome! Must be at least 16 years of age to participate. Currently, e-bikes are not allowed in competition.

name: Bend Marathon and Half
description:
Welcome to the Bend Marathon, Half Marathon, 10k and 5k. With local ownership the 2026 events will be the best mountain town races anywhere. These are spectacularly scenic courses through West Bend emphasizing everything that makes Bend, Oregon great. You'll cruise around neighborhood parks, through ponderosa pine forests, along the mighty Deschutes River, and finish in a beautiful iconic Bend location to a hoppin' afterparty where the music is playing, delicious food is waiting, and you can relax because you just finished your best race ever! Join us for the 11th edition of the Bend Marathon, Half Marathon, 10k and 5k.

name: Best in the West Triathlon Festival
description:
Best in the West Triathlon Festival - Designed by athletes, for athletes!

Nestled in the foothills of the Cascades and fed by the Santiam River, Foster Reservoir offers premier recreation facilities to the outdoor enthusiast and an excellent location for a triathlon festival.

name: Boring Marathon, Half-Boring Half Marathon, Constantly Boring 10K, and Somewhat Boring 5K Race Series
description:
The 13th Annual Boring Marathon, Half-Boring Half-Marathon, Constantly Boring 10K, and Somewhat Boring 5K will take place on Sunday, September 13, 2026. All races start and finish at Boring Station Trailhead Park in downtown Boring, Oregon. Parking will be at Boring Middle School, Naas Elementary School, Boring-Damascus Grange, and the surrounding neighborhood. Please make sure to check out the updated parking map, as we have been able to add almost 100 additional parking spots. As always please respect the neighbors by not blocking driveways or fence openings, fire hydrants, or parking where 'no parking' sings are posted. Please use SE Wally Rd and SE School Ave to reach parking after 6:15 am, as runners will be crossing SE Dee St. The four races are all on the Springwater Trail, out and back, with the marathon being 2-loops of the half marathon course. Both the Half Marathon and Marathon Courses are certified courses and the Marathon Course is once again a Boston Qualifier!

The Boring Marathon Course runs the half marathon course twice and you will get a half marathon split time when you turn for lap 2. The course is USATF Certified Certificate # OR24005JH. 

The Half Boring Half Marathon is an out-and-back on the Springwater Trail from Boring Stations Trailhead Park to Towle Ave and back. This course is now a USATF certified Half Marathon course. Certificate # OR24004JH.

The Constantly Boring 10K, which gets really close to the City of Gresham boundary, but never leaves the Boring area, is just a constantly Boring stroll. This race starts at the same spot as the others and is a short 5k out and back course. This race sold out the fastest in 2025, so register early!

The Somewhat Boring 5K, never really leaves the Boring area so truly is just somewhat Boring, starts at the same spot and is a short out and back course. 

For 2026, as like the last few years we will continue to offer a virtual option for those that would like to earn the Boring Shirt and Medal, but cannot travel to our lovely little city.

Race Entry Limits - Marathon is limited to 100 entries, the Half Marathon to 220 entries, the 10K to 140 entries, the 5K 140 entries, and Virtual (Unlimited).

Packet Pick-up Locations and Times - 
Packet Pickup (Friday before the race - September 11) - Boring Brewing Co. Tasting Room (38250 Pioneer Blvd, Sandy, OR 97055) 5:00 pm to 8:00 pm

Packet Pickup (Saturday before the race - September 12) - Boring Station Trailhead Park (28008 Keller Road Boring, OR 97009) 4:00 pm to 7:00 pm

Packet Pickup (Race day - September 13) - Boring Station Trailhead Park (28008 Keller Road Boring, OR 97009) starting at 5:15 am and until each respective race starts.

Time limit - Walkers are welcome, but because we run part of the race along roads, we need to discontinue aid stations and traffic control after 7 hours. However, we will keep the finish line open and staffed until the last runner/walker comes in and nobody will be disqualified by time. Early starts can be arranged - but are not required - for marathoners or half marathoners who expect to take longer than 6 hours. The early start is at 5:30 am.

Boring Sister City of Dull, Scotland - any resident of Dull, Scotland gets free registration (but you pay the travel)

Awards - All entries prior to August 23, 2026 are guaranteed to receive a shirt in their first size choice. Shirts are not guaranteed after August 30th, but we will do our best to order enough shirts to get everyone a shirt. Everyone will get a medal, including our virtual runners! To help guide a shirt choice, we will only be purchasing unisex cut shirts. We use the A4 Cooling Performance Crew for sizing help. 

Refunds & Deferrals - Unfortunately, we cannot offer refunds once you have registered. Deferrals are offered only in rare circumstances.

There will be NO day of race registration.

Changing races - If you signed up for a race and wish to change to a different race, please contact the race director before August 30th at racedirector@boringmarathon.com. There is no refund for the difference in cost when changing races.

The Boring Marathon, Half Marathon, 10K, and 5K are all USATF certified and insured races.

Packet Pickup (Saturday before the race - September 12) - Boring Station Trailhead Park (28008 Keller Road Boring, OR 97009) 4:00 pm to 7:00 pm

name: Camelback Run
description:
When:
February 28, 2026

Where:
All races will start and finish on or next to the new Phoenix High School track!

See our course maps.

How long:
15k, 5K and Kids' Mile

Why?
This event is a fundraiser to help the Phoenix High School Track and Field team raise money to help pay for meet entry fees, purchase new throwing implements and jumping equipment.

What is the entry fee:
$25 or $20 for club members. As with all SOR events, participants who are 18 and under run free!

Day of race entry fee will be $25.

What is the course like:
15K – This course gives you a chance to run the back roads of Phoenix, take in some amazing sights, and conquer some gnarly hills.

5K – This out-and-back route turns around at the end of Hilsinger road (just before the intersection of Hilsinger and Pioneer).

Kids' Mile - The kids' mile will be run on the track

Where is Packet Pickup:

Bib pick-up and day-of-race registration will be available from 9–10 am on the day of the race. Check-in, start, and finish will all be situated on or near the track.

Awards:

Age division awards are provided by People's Bank. Trophies will be awarded to 1st place age group finishers, medals for 2nd place finishers and ribbons for 3rd place finishers.

*Races are on public roads and trails that ARE NOT closed to cars, pedestrian or cyclist.  Please use caution while on public roadways and paths.

name: CASA of Marion County Superhero Run
description:
Join us for CASA of Marion County's Superhero Run!

Not all superheroes wear capes, some run or walk! Join CASA of Marion County at Salem Riverfront Park for our annual Superhero Run. Kid-friendly and costumes strongly encouraged! Through its volunteers, CASA of Marion County advocates for abused and neglected children in foster care. We are a 501(c)(3) non-profit dedicated to child safety. Proceeds support CASA operations.

name: Cherry City Half Marathon, 10K, 5K & Kids Race
description:
Runners and walkers of all ages and skill levels are invited to enjoy a fun, fast and beautiful course in Salem, Oregon. After the race, be sure to stay and enjoy music and awards, cheer on our kids race runners and enjoy award-winning Oregon wines and craft beer!


Sunday September 13, 2026
Riverfront Park - Salem, OR


Event Start Times:

8:00 am - Half Marathon
8:05 am - 10K
8:10 am - 5K
10:30 am - Kids Run (untimed kids 0.4 mile run or walk)


What's Included:

  • Official Race Shirt
  • Special Finisher Medal
  • An awesome finisher party including live music and award winning Oregon beer wine & cider
  • Overall awards for top three male and female finishers
  • Masters (40+) awards for top three masters male and female finishers in each race distance
  • Age group awards for top three male and female finishers per category (See Below)
  • An amazing day amongst friends, new friends and fellow participants!

 

Key Event Details:

Dogs and strollers are not allowed on the course. If you have little ones interested in being a part of race day, please consider taking part in our untimed kids race (they also receive a bib, shirt and medal)!

All Race Courses are set to end at 12:30 PM. Half Marathon participants, please ensure you are able to complete the event in under 4 hours and 30 minutes (roughly 20:35 pace per mile)

Packet Pickup:

Packet Pickup will take place on Friday (9/11/26) and Saturday (9/12/26).

Friday (9/11/26) - Packet Pickup from 4-8 pm at Willamette Valley Vineyards Salem Hills Tasting Room
(8800 Enchanted Way SE Turner, OR 97392)

All race participants age 21+ are invited to enjoy a complimentary seasonal flight during packet pickup. Stay for dinner and enjoy the beautiful views of wine country. Be sure to bring your ID! Thank you to our Premier Sponsor, Willamette Valley Vineyards!

Saturday (9/12/25) - Packet Pickup from 1-5 pm at Gallagher Fitness Resources
(135 Commercial St NE, Salem, OR 97301)


Pre-Race offerings:

Morning packet pickup, coffee, water and bananas for participants. Gear check available at registration booth.


Post-Race:

Enjoy a complimentary 5-ounce pour from our premier sponsor and exclusive wine provider, Willamette Valley Vineyards, or a 12 oz glass of craft beer or cider.

Enjoy music and a variety of food offerings from local food trucks for purchase after the event as well as awards for overall and age group finishers.

Parking:

Please prioritize using Street Parking in Downtown Salem as well as downtown parking garages. Plan for plenty of time to arrive and get situated prior to the event. The Riverfront park Carousel Parking lot will fill very fast the morning of the event. 


Please plan accordingly! Day-of packet pickup ends at 7:50 am. The race will begin on time at 8:00 am.


Awards:

1st, 2nd, and 3rd place awards will be given for the overall winners, master's winners (age 40+) and the following age groups:

19 and Under
20 - 29
30-39
40-49
50-59
60-69
70+


Introducing the Cherry City Team Competition!

Grab your friends and running buddies and be sure to register as part of a team/group during registration! Along with your individual race results, we will tabulate the race results for teams and will have awards for the top male and female teams for all three race distances!

Are you a part of or lead a local/community Run Club?

We would love to get connected with you! Please email us or send us a direct message on social media telling us about your group to see about specials offers and opportunities!

Our mission is to empower the grassroots running and walking community and be a reliable and favorite race on your yearly training calendar!

 

We Need Volunteers!

Our event doesn’t happen without the support of the incredible community of runners, walkers and just all around great people who are willing to support the event. If you’re unable to participate in the Cherry City Half Marathon and still want to be a part of race day please consider volunteering.

We would love to get connected with you! Please email us or send us a direct message on social media telling us about your group to see about specials offers and opportunities!

Our mission is to empower the grassroots running and walking community and be a reliable and favorite race on your yearly training calendar!

 

We Need Volunteers!

Our event doesn’t happen without the support of the incredible community of runners, walkers and just all around great people who are willing to support the event. If you’re unable to participate in the Cherry City Half Marathon and still want to be a part of race day please consider volunteering.

name: Christmas 5K/10K/Half Marathon in July - Eugene
description:
Celebrate the holiday spirit in the middle of summer at the Christmas in July 5K/10K/Half Marathon! This means Santa is on Vacay!

Come on out and join us at Kiwanis Park in Eugene.This festive race brings all the cheer of the season—without the cold—giving athletes a fun and energetic way to race during the warm summer months.
Whether you’re tackling the 5K, 10K, or Half Marathon, you’ll enjoy a spirited race atmosphere filled with holiday flair, seasonal fun, and motivation from start to finish. Runners and walkers of all levels are welcome to join in the celebration.
All athletes who cross the finish line will receive a custom finisher medal and a spirited, race-themed shirt to commemorate their accomplishment. Awards will be presented to men and women for all three distances to the top finishers in the usual five-year age groups, starting at 10 & Under.
Break out the holiday cheer, lace up your running shoes, and make summer miles merry at the Christmas in July 5K/10K/Half Marathon.

name: Circle the Bay
description:
This challenging course covers 30 kilometers (18.6 miles), from Ferry Road Park in North Bend through Coos Bay’s waterfront finishing back at Ferry Road Park. Run/walk the whole thing yourself or form a 3-person team and make it a run or walk-cheer-athon.  The first leg is relatively flat, the second is moderately rolling, and the third is for your hill lover!  Note, prices listed are for the entire team.

Aid stations close at noon and the finish line closes at 1:00 PM, so plan to finish the walk in 6 1/2 hours, the run in 5 hours.

Water will be available at the exchanges, approximately every 6 miles.

Not into running or walking that far, but want to be involved? Volunteer!

name: Corvallis Fall Festival Run
description:
WELCOME BACK for the 46th installment of this landmark running event for the mid-valley, an old-school 5K & 10K. We are happy to return to OSUs campus this year, the run will take place from the McNary field between 11th and 14th streets. Come for the run, stay for Fall Festival!

The run is presented by Heart of the Valley Runners. Proceeds from the event go back to the community in accordance with the mission of Heart of the Valley Runners -- to encourage and support local running at all levels.

This affordable, family-friendly event presents a welcoming and fun atmosphere for all who want to participate. HOTV Runners members receive a $5 discount on registration for the 5k and 10k through Saturday September 27, 2025. You can join the club as part of your registration and you will receive the discount. 

The 5k and 10k both begin at 9:00am.  The 1k Kids' Fun Run begins at 10:30am, or shortly after the last 5k/10k finishers. 
Day of race registration ($50 for 5k/10k, $20 for ages 18 and under, Free for 1k) begins at 7:00am.

description: If you are looking for a scenic Willamette Valley road race, the Daffodil Run will not disappoint. The 8K run begins eight miles northwest of Junction City at the historic Long Tom Grange. Daffodils surround you as Ferguson Road weaves through the Coast Range’s eastern foothills.

name: Dave's Solstice Run at Blue Lake
description:
Join us on Saturday morning, June 20, 2026 to celebrate the summer solstice with Dave's Solstice Run 5K at Blue Lake.

This event is named after Dave Green, a long-time ORRC member and volunteer. Dave was an active board member, joining in 1981, and becoming president in 1992. Race director for multiple events, including the original Blue Lake Runs, Dave was also the “Treasurer Extraordinaire” and was instrumental in helping the club through some tough times financially in the past. This event epitomizes Dave Green, and his love for low-key, family friendly events.

name: Dragonslayer Fantasy Dash and Strut
description:
Step into your favorite character’s shoes—whether you’re a superhero, anti-hero, villain, knight, princess, or even Sasquatch—and join us for the inaugural Dragonslayer Fantasy Dash & Strut!

This 5K adventure invites you to walk or run through the magical trails of Gabriel Park (PDX). Along the way, you’ll encounter a thrilling Villain Zones for an extra dash of fun and excitement and be welcomed back to the Heroes Village!

Route includes mild inclines, a mixture of gravel and trail pathways, everyone is assured of a beautiful and accessible run, jog, or walk. The route is suitable for all ages and abilities. Leashed dogs and strollers welcome (strollers ensure you have wheels suitable for unpaved trails).

Lace up your sneakers, gather your squad, and head out for a day of fantasy, fitness, and unforgettable shenanigans. Costumes encouraged; laughter guaranteed!

name: Eastern Oregon Half Marathon  / 5k&10k presented by Asher Community Health
description:
Interested in running the oldest half marathon in Oregon?  Come join us for the Eastern Oregon Half Marathon, and race alongside the beautifully scenic John Day River!  You can choose to tackle the full 13.1 miles, or enjoy a shorter race by choosing the 5 or 10k.  Either way, you will be cheered across the finish line by an enthusiastic crowd that gathers to support racers and take in the annual Spray Rodeo and parade.  The scenery, small-town hospitality, and friendly competition are reward enough – but this year’s top men’s and women’s overall half-marathon winners will also receive top-notch belt buckles! In addition to enjoying an old-school race in the gorgeous John Day River Valley, you will also be supporting a great cause.  All profits go to the Spray Rodeo Association, 70% goes to the Spray Community Fund 30% goes to the Spray Rodeo operating fund.

The Course:
The Half Marathon begins 1/4 mile northwest of Service Creek on HWY 19 and follows the scenic John Day River Valley, beginning at 8 AM.  10k will begin at 8:30 AM, 6.2 miles west of Spray on HWY 19.  5k will begin at 9:00 AM, 3.1 miles west of Spray on HWY 19.  Half Marathon Walkers will start at 7AM.  All races finish in the town of Spray, OR.  The surface is paved, with a twelve foot rise in elevation between start and finish.  Participants will run with traffic on the right side of the road.

Notes:
There will be portable restrooms at Service Creek, and at the 10k start. Halfway for the half marathoners   
Liquids will be available at four places along the course and finish line.

Awards:
Awards will be presented to male and female winners in the following age categories for each event:
13 and under, 14-19,   20-29,    30-39,    40-49,    50-59,    60-69, 70-79, and 80 and up

The overall male winner and overall female winner in the half marathon run  will each receive a belt buckle. Plaques for overall in the 5k and 10k overall, and plaques for all age division winners

Awards ceremony will begin promptly at 10:45 a.m.

Race results will be posted on this website within a week after  the race. 

Transportation:
Bus transportation to starting line departs Spray School at 7:00 a.m. sharp for all runners  Runners will be dropped at the start of their event. 5k and 10k runners will get back on the bus after the start of the half marathon and be dropped at each respecting starting line as the bus returns to Spray. Walkers need to arrange a ride to the starting line for the 7am walker start.  If possible do not leave cars at Service Creek.  No return transportation will be provided. 

Food, Beverage, and Other Accommodations:
Showers will be available in the school. Hot water is limited. So, run fast! A fundraiser breakfast is available at the school as well. The fundraiser is for Spray HS athletics. 

 

Other Information:
 The race will be run entirely on the south/river side of the highway. With this being Memorial Weekend and the Spray Rodeo, traffic will be heavy at times.  Please take all precautions.

-The highway will NOT be closed for this race.
-Watch for vehicle traffic at all times.
-We have no desire to ban baby joggers, children on bicycles, or support vehicles from accompanying runners in this event.  This is a family event. However, if there are instances of such vehicles interfering with
runners, both the non-runner and runner will be  asked to leave the race course.
-Race course monitors are authorized to disqualify  anyone acting in an unsafe manner.

name: Eastern Oregon Half Marathon  / 5k&10k presented by Asher Community Health
description:
Interested in running the oldest half marathon in Oregon?  Come join us for the Eastern Oregon Half Marathon, and race alongside the beautifully scenic John Day River!  You can choose to tackle the full 13.1 miles, or enjoy a shorter race by choosing the 5 or 10k.  Either way, you will be cheered across the finish line by an enthusiastic crowd that gathers to support racers and take in the annual Spray Rodeo and parade.  The scenery, small-town hospitality, and friendly competition are reward enough – but this year’s top men’s and women’s overall half-marathon winners will also receive top-notch belt buckles! In addition to enjoying an old-school race in the gorgeous John Day River Valley, you will also be supporting a great cause.  All profits go to the Spray Rodeo Association, 70% goes to the Spray Community Fund 30% goes to the Spray Rodeo operating fund.

The Half Marathon begins 1/4 mile northwest of Service Creek on HWY 19 and follows the scenic John Day River Valley, beginning at 8 AM.  10k will begin at 8:30 AM, 6.2 miles west of Spray on HWY 19.  5k will begin at 9:00 AM, 3.1 miles west of Spray on HWY 19.  Half Marathon Walkers will start at 7AM.  All races finish in the town of Spray, OR.  The surface is paved, with a twelve foot rise in elevation between start and finish.  Participants will run with traffic on the right side of the road.

Notes:
There will be portable restrooms at Service Creek, and at the 10k start. Halfway for the half marathoners

13 and under, 14-19,   20-29,    30-39,    40-49,    50-59,    60-69, 70-79, and 80 and up

The overall male winner and overall female winner in the half marathon run  will each receive a belt buckle. Plaques for overall in the 5k and 10k overall, and plaques for all age division winners

Awards ceremony will begin promptly at 10:45 a.m.

Race results will be posted on this website within a week after  the race.

Bus transportation to starting line departs Spray School at 7:00 a.m. sharp for all runners  Runners will be dropped at the start of their event. 5k and 10k runners will get back on the bus after the start of the half marathon and be dropped at each respecting starting line as the bus returns to Spray. name: Eola Hills "No Hills" 5K/10K
description:
Proceeds from the Eola Hills "No Hills" run will be shared by the Track and field and cross-country programs at Dallas HS and Central HS.

This is a very fun and popular event that is capped at 350 racers.

New for 2026: Race is chip timed and you get a souvenir wine glass.

***IMPORTANT PARKING NOTE*** Parking at the event location fills fast, and parking is NOT be available at the Polk County Fairgrounds. Please carpool if possible. We have overflow parking about 1/4 mile south of Eola in a field.

There will be race day registration (exact cash amount is requested) and we can take credit/debit. Please arrive early to get your information on the roster.

Day of Race 10k=$60, 5k=$55

Check-in on race morning will open at 7:00am. The 10K run will set off from Eola Hills Wine Cellars at 9:00am.  At 9:15am the 5K run/walk will begin. This is a flat, fast, out-and-back course. It is chip-timed this year. Ensure your bib is on your front and visible, especially at the finish. We will pull bib tabs for place and timing verification. After your run enjoy the company of fellow runners and walkers in the wine cellar. You will get  pizza from Yeasty Beasty and a glass of wine, beer, or soda with thanks to Eola Hills.

Following the race end there will be ribbons handed out to the top finishers of each age group for both male and female racers.

 

**We ask that all participants finish their events within 90 minutes of the start time.

The top 3 male and female finishers of each race will receive prizes.  The top 3 in each 10-year age division, male/female, for each race will receive ribbons.

**No dogs are allowed on the course. Strollers are permitted but we ask you please not crowd the front of the start line.

Join us in October to celebrate fall in Central Oregon with a brand new race weekend experience!

name: Forest Grove Lions Club Run & Walk for Sight and Hearing
description:
All levels of runners and walkers encouraged to participate!!
Registration fees includes a long sleeve tee shirt and personalized bib if registered by 11:59 pm on September 17th. 
Online day of event registration (no cash, no check, electronic payment only)

For more information, visit forestgrovelions.org, or contact Race Directors, Sydney, msdaniels@vgmhc.org Or Tom, tomr@johnlscott.com

Forest Grove Lions partner with Pacific University College of Optometry and School of Audiology to support its students and staff. 100% of monies raised by this event are returned to the community to fund scholarships, equipment and assist the Pacific University AMIGOS program. NO PACKET PICK UP AFTER RACE DAY!

name: Gator Grinder Triathlon
description:
The North Lake Physical Therapy Gator Grinder Triathlon is an excellent introduction for the first-time triathlete, as well as a great early season event for the experienced racer.  All proceeds support the Canby Gators Swim Club.  Thank you for your support.

Swim

500-yard (20 lengths, 10 laps) pool swim in a 6-lane, 25-yard pool, with up to 4 swimmers per lane. There will be volunteer lap counters. Drafting is permitted. The swim will be seeded by 500-yard swim-time submissions. Heat assignments will be e-mailed by the Thursday before the race. The first heat will be in the water at 7:30 a.m. Check-in at least one hour before your start.

Bike

The one-loop 12-mile bike course is over the beautiful rolling country roads that surround Canby. A bike helmet is mandatory. Drafting is not legal. Volunteers will manage traffic at intersections, but roads will be open to traffic and cyclists will be responsible for their safety. 

Run

The 3.1-mile run is mostly on roadways with about one-third on a paved walking trail. The course is flat and fast. Water will be available on the course.

Duathlon (run-bike-run) and Aquabike (swim-bike)

Both variations will follow the same segments as the triathlon course.

REGISTRATION

Online registration only. All race communication is done via e-mail. Once registered, you will receive periodic informational emails. Start times will be sent the Thursday before the race.  If you do not receive these emails, please check your junk or spam folders.

CANCELLATION / WAITLIST POLICY

Cancellations by March 31, 2026, will be given a full refund less $10. No refunds will be given after March 31. Entries are non-transferable.  PLEASE NOTE: T-shirts are only guaranteed to entries registered before March 31.

AWARDS

The top 3 male and female individual finishers in each age group will receive ribbons. Additional awards will be awarded to the top overall male and female finishers and the top male and female finishers from Canby, Oregon.  

ENTRY FEE

$75 individual/$130 relay team December 1, 2025 - February 28, 2026. $85 individual/$150 relay March 1- May 6 2026. Registration deadline is May 5th, 2026. No day of race registration. Registration will include a shirt, results, and a great time!  

RACE T-SHIRTS

T-shirts are included in registration for registrations received before March 31. Entries after March 31 may check in with the race director after the race for shirt availability.

PACKET DISTRIBUTION

Packets will be available starting at 6 AM on Saturday, May 9.

Course maps:  Bike  

From pool, turn 

Right onto S. Ivy St.

Right on Township Rd

Left on S. Redwood Rd

Right on 4th

Left on Sequoia Parkway (stop sign)

Right on Walnut (this right turn is about 100 yards or so after turning onto Sequoia Parkway)

Follow Walnut until it T's into 1st Ave.

Right on 1st Av. (which turns into Haines Rd, which turns into New Era Rd.),

from New Era, Right onto Central Point Rd.

Right on Township Rd.

Left on Sequoia Parkway 

Right on SE 13th Ave.

Turn right into the Adult Center parking lot and dismount by the bus stop shelter

 

Run

From Pool parking lot,

Run behind Ackerman Middle School and along walkway on east side of school,

Turn left on SE 13th Ave.

Left on Teakwood

Right on Baker Prairie Trail 

Left on South Molalla Forest Road aka the logging road

Exit left at SE Township Road

Left on S Redwood Street

Left on access rd. back towards Baker Prairie Trail

Right on S Teakwood Street

Right on SE 13th Ave

Right on walkway at east end of Ackerman Middle School and 

Finish on the Ackerman Middle School track.

name: Guardian Group Virtual 5K for Freedom 2026
description:
🏃‍♀️ Virtual 5K for Freedom
Kickoff: January 11 – National Human Trafficking Awareness Day

Join us for a Virtual 5K in support of Guardian Group, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit dedicated to preventing and disrupting the sex trafficking of women and children across the United States.

Run, walk, or roll—on your own time, from anywhere—while standing up for those who cannot.

Your participation helps fuel Guardian Group’s work to:

Identify and disrupt trafficking networks
Protect vulnerable women and children in our communities


Why January 11 Matters?
National Human Trafficking Awareness Day calls us to take action, not just raise awareness. Every step you take sends a message: exploitation has no place in our world.

How It Works
Register for the Virtual 5K
Complete your 3.1 miles on January 11th or after

The Virtual 5K begins on National Human Trafficking Awareness Day and concludes after April—National Child Abuse Prevention Month.


Invite friends and family to join or donate!


Take a Stand. Take a Step.
Together, we can turn movement into momentum—and awareness into action.

Register. Participate. Share.

name: HAGG Lake Triathlon & Multi-Sports Festival
description:
RACE AT THIS HISTORICAL EVENT AND STUNNING VENUE!

Hagg Lake Triathlon – Rich in Beauty, Rich in Tradition!

Come race at the 45th Anniversary of the Annual Hagg Lake Triathlon & Off-road Endurance Sports Festival, one of the oldest and most gorgeous Triathlon courses in the nation! Now offering an Off-Road Triathlon, Half Marathon Trail Run, 5K Trail Run & Camping!

Olympic & Sprint Triathlon, Duathlon & AquaBike & NEW OFF-ROAD SPRINT TRIATHLON, DUATHLON & AQUABIKE, Half Marathon Trail Run, and 5K TRAIL RUN!

The modern sport of triathlon had its modest beginnings with an event held in Mission Bay in San Diego, CA on September 25, 1974. There were 46 athletes that day. Seven years later, Hagg Lake Triathlon became one of six stops on the Bud Light Triathlon Series Tour drawing about 500 athletes, with Dave Scott coming out on top. Today, as one of the nation’s oldest and longest-running triathlon events, Hagg Lake enters its 38th year and it continues to draw upwards of 700+ athletes. Its popularity is rooted in the rich tradition and the exceptional venue, which is one of the most scenic in the country. The Hagg Lake course offers a true test of this terrific sport with its rolling hills on both the bike and run leg portions of the event. Make the Hagg Lake Triathlon & Off-road Endurance Sports Festival one of your summer stops and compete on the course that has seen many of the greats in the sport of triathlon.

name: Helvetia Wine Run 5k
description:
PLEASE BE AWARE THAT THIS EVENT WILL SELL OUT SO PLEASE REGISTER ASAP!

Like Running or Walking?  Love Wine?  This race is for you! 

Join us on Saturday, June 20, 2026 at 8:30am and 10:30am for an exciting annual event that features the amazing scenery and landscape of Helvetia Vineyards & Winery!  Helvetia Vineyards and Winery is located in the foothills of the Tualatin Mountains, the northernmost grape growing area in the Willamette Valley and just 25 minutes from downtown Portland. So, whether you are looking to run, walk or just enjoy the wine, this race is a sure thing for a great time and an incredible experience!  This race is timed and scored by J3 Timing.  Results will be posted at www.J3Timing.com. 

Registration Includes:

  • T-shirt:  Super Soft Ring Spun Cotton t-shirt included! 
  • Wine Glass: Shatterproof, Collapsible, and Portable!
  • Finisher Medal: Doubles as a Wine Stopper!
  • Race Bib: Chip timed 5k run/walk
  • Results Posted Online
  • ...and of course, a pour of wine!

name: Hood to Coast Semper Fi & America's Fund Team
description:
Join our Semper Fi & America's Fund Team for the Hood to Coast Relay and help us raise $20,000 for The Fund.

Our team will be comprised of Team Semper Fi (service members who participate in The Fund's Recovery through Sport program) and Community Athletes (Fundraisers). This partnership will be a unique experience for everyone involved!

The Providence Hood To Coast Relay, located in Oregon, is the most popular and largest running and walking relay race in the world, annually drawing participants from over 40 countries. Known as the Mother of All Relays, the event takes 12-member relay teams 199 miles from the iconic top of Mount Hood to the beaches of the Pacific Ocean. The event has sold-out for 30 straight years and on lottery opening day for 23 consecutive years. 

Fundraising minimum $3,000. Your $3,000 fundraising will cover the costs for a member of Team Semper Fi to participate in the Relay.

Registration cost $225.00 per person

  • As you register for the team a personal fundraising page will be created for you. This page can be customized with pictures and your personal message. 
  • Each team member will receive a Semper Fi & America's Fund running shirt.
  • Each team member is responsible for their own travel to and from the event.
  • The Fund will provide vans that will transport the team during the event.
  • The Hood to Coast Relay takes place on Friday, Aug 27nd through Saturday, August 30. Participants need to arrive in Portland no later than Thursday, Aug 27 and stay until Sunday, Aug 30.

name: Hunger Run - Columbia Pacific Food Bank
description:
A Race to Fight Hunger

Join us for our 7th Annual Hunger Run to help fight food insecurity in Columbia County. 

Starting and ending at the Columbia Pacific Food Bank, the 1-Mile, 5K and 10K run/walk routes will take you through downtown and old town St. Helens. Come early and stick around after your race to check out our info vendors, collect swag, and have a great time. 

Help us hit our goal of 300 participants!! All monies raised stay in our county and support our community partnerships.

Distances vary based on age, with all courses under one mile.

Start the summer right by lighting up the park and experiencing the joy of movement at the Kids Glow Run!

name: Kirk Rd. Krusher / McLean Mile and 5K
description:
Do you enjoy running in charitable events that benefit the local community?  Do you like a challenging road race?  Or do you like an easy stroll?  If you've said yes to any one of these, then our event is one you need to do!  Please join us for the Kirk Rd Krusher 10K and McLean Mile and 5K hosted by Run Oregon, an event for the entire family!  This road race is a FUN run/walk designed to create an environment that promotes physical fitness.  A portion of the proceeds generated from this event will be donated directly to the Weston Food Pantry, the named beneficiary for this inaugural fun run.  This event will be manually timed, our primary goal is to create a fun experience for runners/walkers and raise funds for the local food pantry.

The Weston Food Pantry is open for anyone who is food insecure twice each month.  The Weston Food Pantry helps anyone who comes to the pantry and says that they need food, in December they served 100 families who needed food!  The Weston Food Pantry doesn't care where people live, no one gets turned away.  Typical food includes fruit, vegetables, canned food, dried food, bread, milk, eggs, cheese, butter and a variety of meats.

Run Oregon is a locally based company whose mission is to promote opportunities in local communities to maintain an active lifestyle through organized fitness events.  Run Oregon’s goal is to provide runners, walkers, and joggers with opportunities to maintain their way of life.  Our events are designated to promote physical fitness and give back to the local community through event fundraisers.  

We will accept day of registration for an additional $10 per entrant.

description:
2025 Results are here: https://www.hubertiming.com/results/2025Ladybug 
2024 Results are here: https://www.hubertiming.com/results/2024Ladybug 
2023 Results are here: https://www.hubertiming.com/results/2023Ladybug
2022 Results are here: https://www.hubertiming.com/results/2022LadyBug

Join us for the 15th annual running of this unique and popular 5K/10K race on July 11, 2026! This stroller-friendly event takes runners on a scenic course through the open green spaces and forested paths along the Tualatin River in Tigard's Cook Park and neighboring areas, offering a fun and memorable experience for all participants.

Perks for Participants:
All 5K and 10K finishers will receive a shirt, medal and a race packet filled with goodies to celebrate their accomplishment.

Can’t join us in person?
No problem! Sign up for the virtual race and run your own 5K or 10K course—anywhere, anytime. As a virtual participant, you’ll receive a race bib, a shirt, and a medal to commemorate your achievement. Want to run with friends? Organize a group virtual run, and we’ll promote it on our website so others can join you!

Race Day Details:
To ensure a safe and enjoyable experience for everyone, the start line will remain open for 15 minutes, allowing for a staggered start and plenty of space.

Why We Run:
The best part? Proceeds from this event benefit the Ladybug CDH Foundation, whose mission is to: Raise public awareness about Congenital Diaphragmatic Hernia (CDH), a potentially life-threatening birth defect affecting 1 in 2,500 children annually.
Fund critical medical research.
Provide direct support to families in the Pacific Northwest facing the challenges of CDH.

Survivor/Angel Signs:
We line the sidewalks at Cook Family Park with signs remembering and honoring Angels and Survivors. If you have a CDH Angel or Survivor you would like represented with a sign, please contact us at ladybugcdh@gmail.com. Send us a few sentences about their story and 2-3 photos. We'd love to be able to honor your CDH warrior. 

Don’t wait—register today to lace up your shoes, make a difference, and help us support families impacted by CDH. Together, we can bring hope and make strides for this important cause.

name: Lake Oswego Lake Run
description:
Join us for the 50th Lake Oswego Lake Run this year on May 2, 2026!

 

For 5 decades, runners have gathered in Lake Oswego to tackle the hilly terrain and enjoy the beautiful views. The run has attracted runners of all ages from across the country and is welcoming you to join us this year on Saturday, May 2nd.

 

Beyond a beloved community event and a great way to get out, be active, meet a goal, prepare for a year of races ... Proceeds from the Lake Run support Oregonians in need of stable and affordable housing. By running in the Lake Run, you are doing so much more goodness than just for yourself and the friends/ family you run alongside, you are helping your community. This run is organized by Northwest Housing Alternatives, where we create opportunity through housing and work tirelessly to end homelessness in Clackamas County. Please join us in this endeavor, in this fight for everyone's basic right. Together, we can change lives.

 

Gender Recognition and Inclusion: We believe that everyone has a place in the running community that is respectful, safe, and inclusive. In an effort to support individuals that do not identify as either male or female, we have the categories of non-binary and "Prefer Not to Say." Individuals who select either option will be eligible for the non-binary awards category.

The Lebanon Strawberry Run/Walk 5k & 1 Mile is one of the many family events during the Lebanon's Annual Strawberry Festival. The run precedes the Grand Parade and opens a day highlighted by the serving of the "World's Largest Strawberry Shortcake" free to over 15,000 people. Race entry fees will benefit the East Linn Christian Cross Country and Track & Field teams. Both races follow the parade route through town just prior to the 11:00 AM parade. The 5k is a flat, fast out and back.  The course will be lined with cheering parade spectators for the entire route.  

Race Day Info
Registration Deadline: 1 Mile @ 8:55 AM, 5k @ 9:25 AM
Day of Race Registration Costs: 5k $25 (t-shirt not included), 1 Mile $8
Packet Pickup: 7:30 AM to Race Time
Race Times: 1 Mile 9:00 AM, 5k 9:30 AM
Awards & Raffle: immediately following each race

name: Legacy Estates "All Hills" 7k/3k/1-mile
description:
The Legacy Estates “All Hills” event is the hilly counterpart to our popular Eola Hills “No Hills” race held each November. If Eola is flat, Legacy is not — and that’s exactly the point.

Set on the stunning Legacy Estate Vineyard in the West Salem hills, this inaugural event challenges runners with rolling vineyard roads, sweeping views, and a course designed to test your legs while rewarding you at the top.

🏃‍♂️ Choose Your Distance — or Choose Them All
Racers can register for a 7K, 3K, 1-Mile, or any combination of races thanks to staggered start times.

Want a 10K? Sign up for both the 7K and 3K.
Want to race hard and then cruise with family? Run the 7K or 3K, then join the 1-Mile with the kids.
Enjoy discounted pricing when you bundle races.

⏰ Start Times
7K – 9:00 AM
3K – 10:30 AM
1-Mile – 11:15 AM
Racers must finish their event before the next race begins.

The top 3 male and female finishers in each event will receive awards!

🍷 Course Highlights
All courses run on vineyard roads — NO running between grape rows!
Wine aid station at the top of the hill for 7K and 3K runners, along with Sparkling cider, Water, and Mortal Hydration.

7K runners get to enjoy it twice
Strollers and well-behaved, leashed dogs are welcome

🎁 Runner Swag & Post-Race Fun
Every participant receives:

A custom wine glass and a glass of wine at the finish
A custom buff featuring the course maps and elevation profiles
Hot and cold post-race treats to refuel and celebrate
Small charcuterie plates are prepackaged. One included per registration. Extras at $10 pre-ordered.
Whether you’re chasing elevation, stacking races, or making it a family outing, Legacy Estates “All Hills” is a one-of-a-kind vineyard race experience you won’t want to miss. Come earn your hills — and your wine — in the West Salem hills. 🍷⛰️

*Swag is included in registration up to the final price increase date in March.

Restrooms are available in the form of portable units near packet pickup at the amphitheater.

Parking is available on-site, and a detailed map with locations will be available soon.

name: Longest Day Mile
description:
WHERE:  Phoenix High School Track

WHEN: Sunday, June 21st, 2026

  • 7:00pm- Heat 1  5:45min pace & Under 
  • 7:10pm- Heat 2  5:46 -7min Pace 
  • 7:20pm- Heat 3  7-9min Pace 
  • 7:35pm- Heat 4  9-11min Pace 
  • 7:50pm- Heat 5  11min Pace & Up

COURSE DETAILS:  Four times around the Phoenix High School Track

RACE FEES: $13 online or $15 day of

RACE DAY INFO: Registration 5:45-7pm

AWARDS:  Ribbons for the top 3 places in all age groups. $100 prize for any male who runs sub 4:00 minutes and any female who runs sub 4:40 minutes.

RESTRICTIONS: Absolutely no roller skaters, bicycles, skateboards, baby joggers, dogs, headphones, or unregistered participants

RACE DIRECTOR: Seamus Cowan

name: Longest Night Mile
description:
WHERE:  Phoenix High School Track

WHEN: Monday, December 21st, 2025

  • 6:15pm- Heat 1  5:45min pace & Under 
  • 6:25pm- Heat 2  5:46 -7min Pace 
  • 6:35pm- Heat 3  7-9min Pace 
  • 6:50pm- Heat 4  9-11min Pace 
  • 7:05pm- Heat 5  11min Pace & Up

COURSE DETAILS:  Four times around the Phoenix High School Track

RACE FEES: Option 1: Bring 2-3+ boxes of dry cereal. YES you read that right! The SOU food bank coordinator expressed to us in 2019 that the students are excited when there is cereal in the food bank because there rarely is and when it is there it doesn't last long. So, we thought it would be a fun treat before Christmas to stuff their pantry full of cereal goodness! We also hosted a can food drive at our Turkey Trot for the SOU food bank and a portion of the proceeds went to them as well so don't worry, we made sure they had other food items. 

Option 2: $13 online or $15 day of (cash or check only) which will also be donated to the SOU Student Food Pantry.

RACE DAY INFO: Registration 5-6pm - Bring $15 or 2-3+ boxes of dry cereal and sign waiver to participate.  

AWARDS:  Ribbons for the top 3 places in all age groups. $100 prize for any male who runs sub 4:00 minutes and any female who runs sub 4:40 minutes.

RESTRICTIONS: Absolutely no roller skaters, bicycles, skateboards, baby joggers, dogs, headphones, or unregistered participants

RACE DIRECTORS: Nathan & Shayla Watt

name: Lucky Leprechaun 5k, 10k Run/Walk
description:
Join us for the Lucky Leprechaun Run or Walk through the charming town of Sisters, Oregon! Grab your Green Gear and run, walk, skip or trot this chip timed race!  We will be starting and finishing at Luckey's Woodsman! 

We will have a fun filled IRISH finisher party in the grassy knoll thanks to Luckey's Woodsman and Sisters Meat and Smokehouse.

Lunch specials will be available for purchase from Luckey's Woodsman.

Beanie or scarf included in registration IF you register by 3/1

The SWAG Included with your registration:

Lucky Leprechaun 5k/10k  scarf or beanie :)  (guaranteed only if registered by 3/1)
Finisher medal/Beads
Beer/Seltzer/Sparkling Water
Best Dressed Lucky Leprechaun Contest
Chip timed event - get your results as you finish!
Live Music to do your Irish Jig to!
Race Bib
Fun new tradition
Strollers and dogs are welcome!

Here is all your race details:
EARLY PACKET PICK-UP:
WHEN: FRIDAY MARCH 13th FROM 4:30 P.M.-6:00 P.M. 
SATURDAY MORNING DETAILS: 
START/FINISH PARTY/CHECK IN:Grassy area between Luckey's Woodsman and Sisters Meat and Smokehouse
PARKING: Will be available on the streets.
CHECK-IN: 8:30 a.m.-9:40 a.m.- You can check in and get your goodies Saturday morning. or Friday night at the early packet pick up.
SHIRT, BEANIE OR SCARF: YES! YOU GET A SHIRT (or other cool swag) IF YOU  REGISTER BY 3/1
RACE START TIMES: 
9:45 a.m.-Kids Dash
9:50 a.m.-10k- (RACE COURSE WILL CLOSE AT 11:30 A.M).
10:00 a.m. 5k run- (RACE COURSE WILL CLOSE AT 11:30 A.M.)
10:05 a.m. 5k walk-( RACE COURSE WILL CLOSE AT 11:30 A.M.)
Bathrooms: At Start/Finish area
DOGS:Must be kept on leash and well behaved. If you are running with your dog, please be considerate of other runners around you and leave plenty of space.
FOOD: Great lunch specials will be offered from Luckey's Woodsman!
DRINKS: One free beer or seltzer or non alcoholic drink will be available for all.
COSTUME CONTEST: Get your GREEN GEAR ON! Don't forget about the costume contest!! Fun prizes! Best dressed individual and Best dressed family/team!
THE FASTEST: Awards for the fastest Men/Women in 5k and 10k. 1st, 2nd places.
MUSIC: We will have live music to do your best Irish Jig too!

 

GET READY FOR A GREAT RUN DAY AND MAYBE A FEW SHENANIGANS!
QUESTIONS: EMAIL KELLY AT RUNSISTERSRUN1@GMAIL.COM

name: Mac's Run
description:
Hilly and challenging course with breathtaking ocean views. The race is entirely on paved roads.  

For both courses, runners loop through Shore Acres heading out (south), and run straight back on the return (north).

5K Course Map

10K Course Map

Note that students are $5.00.  Please use the coupon code Student2022 to register.  To avoid credit-card fees, you will not be charged at check-out.  Please bring $5.00 (exact change appreciated) to registration!

Starting Oct 1, 2025, all vehicles require a parking pass (cost is per vehicle, not per runner).  Cost of a day pass is $10 for in-state or $12 for out-of-state.  Daily passes are available at a kiosk near registration with a QR code using your phone.  We are working with the parks to see if we can sell them as part of registration, but details have not been worked out yet.  Annual state park passes are $30 for one year and $50 for two years.  They can be purchased at the gift shop at Shore Acres or on-line.  FYI, the price will double to $60 for an annual pass January 1 and they will no longer issue two-year passes, so if you visit our beautiful state parks, it is cheaper to buy now.

name: Making Waves for Anne
description:
Supporting the Heart of Our Pool
Anne Scholz has dedicated herself to our community, and now we are coming together to give back to her. Join the Sea Lions for a fun-filled competition designed for everyone—from serious swimmers to those who prefer a pool noodle! This special event is a fundraiser to provide direct financial support to Anne and her family following her ALS diagnosis. Whether you’re racing in an aqua belt or cheering from the bleachers, your presence is a powerful message of love and solidarity for a woman who has given us so much.

The Sea Lions Swim Team is proud to host this special event to rally our community, celebrate Anne’s impact, and raise vital funds for her and her family during this challenging time.

Event Highlights
Whether you're a competitive swimmer or just want to make a splash for a good cause, there is a lane for you:

Fun Races: Sprint events for all ages and skill levels.
Community Relays: Team up with friends, family, or teammates for our "Lanes of Love" relays.
Spirit Awards: Prizes for the most enthusiastic participants and biggest fundraisers.
Deck side Support: Not a swimmer? Come cheer from the stands! We will have music, snacks, and a community tribute board for Anne.

Every Lap Counts

100% of all proceeds—including registration fees, concessions, and additional donations—will go directly to Anne and her family to assist with medical expenses and care.

 
How to Join Us
Register to Race: Click the button below to sign up for individual or relay events.
Sponsor a Swimmer: Can't make it? You can still donate to support a specific participant or the event as a whole.
Spread the Word: Share this page with friends, family, and neighbors!

name: Miles for Midwives 2026
description:
THANK YOU VOLUNTEERS, SPONSORS AND PARTICIPANTS FOR AN AMAZING 2025 EVENT!

Miles for Midwives 5k walk/run/roll was at 10am on May 16, 2026 at the beautiful Champoeg State Park, located halfway between Oregon City and Salem. This annual event raises awareness about the impact midwives have on improving outcomes in maternal and infant health and supports two professional midwifery organizations, The American College of Nurse-Midwives Oregon Affiliate and Oregon Midwifery Council. Please join us in celebrating the important work Midwives provide to women, pregnant people, and families by stepping out in support!

Support The Cause

Money raised will go directly to improving maternal health care in Oregon.

All proceeds benefit The Oregon Affiliate of the American College of Nurse-Midwives and the Oregon Midwifery Council. 

Center For Hope & Safety

10% of your registration will go directly to The Center for Hope & Safety, which is a 501(c)(3), independent nonprofit offering safe refuge and support to victims and survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking and human trafficking.

You can learn more about this organization via their website HopeAndSafety.org or via their Facebook / Instagram pages. 

Diaper Drive

One in two families cannot afford diapers.
Please bring new cloth or disposable diapers for donation to local nonprofit diaper banks on the day of the event. Donations will be delivered into The National Diaper Bank Network (NDBN), a national nonprofit established in 2011.

For more information on this important topic, see nationaldiaperbanknetwork.org or track the tag #enddiaperneed. 

Registration

Registration is open from Feb 24th until the start of the race on May 15th at 11pm through this event page on RunSignup.com. 

  • Registrations before May 3rd to receive a souvenir T-shirt and a discounted registration price of $48. T-shirt availability is not guaranteed for registrations after May 3rd.
  • Registrations between May 10th through May 16th do not include a T-shirt but remain discounted at $48 and T-shirt availability is not guaranteed. 
  • Registration starting at 5pm on Friday, May 15th, through race day will be $58 and T-shirt availability is not guaranteed. Sign up early!
  • Registration for ages 16 and under is FREE.

name: Milwaukie Mile
description:
Welcome to the second annual Milwaukie Mile! Our goal is to provide a safe and fast course for all members of the community to race their pace and set a new personal best in the mile! The course runs gently downhill along the Trolley Trail, starting at the Park Avenue Max Station and finishing in Milwaukie Bay Park. The race will be held the morning of Saturday July 12th, 2025.

The race is open to runners, walkers, and families with strollers. Dogs are not allowed to accompany runners, walkers, or volunteers. You can spectate with your dog on a leash, but please stand back from the course when doing so for the safety of the participants. 

***Please note - T-shirt size and availability are not guaranteed for registrations after July 4th.***

 

Awards

All registered participants will receive a Milwaukie Mile T-shirt. The top-3 finishers in the following categories will receive a special award:

  • Non-binary
  • Open Women
  • Open Men
  • 18 and under Girls
  • 18 and under Boys

 

Transportation

The race starts only a few steps from the Park Ave Orange Line Max Station. Participants and spectators are encouraged to use public transportation to travel to the race!  If you must drive to the race, auto users are encouraged to park in Downtown Milwaukie or at the Park Ave park and ride garage

 

Donations

A portion of the race proceeds will be donated to the Milwaukie High School Cross Country team. If you want to make a dedicated donation to the team to support their 2025 season, we will gladly pass 100% of your donation on to the team! Any amount given would be greatly appreciated and thank you for your generosity! Please click the Donate tab above to donate directly. 

 

Sponsorship

The Milwaukie Mile is a small community event which would not be possible without the support of generous sponsors. If you would like to support or sponsor the event in any way, please email Milwaukiemile@gmail.com.

 

Zenner's - For 95 years, Zenner's has been perfecting its craft of quality sausages and smoked meats, prepared from the best local ingredients into products that have become Northwest favorites.

Bliss Esthetics - Nestled in Gladstone, Oregon, Bliss Esthetics is your one-stop getaway for self-care.

SaunaGlo - Located in the heart of downtown Milwaukie, SaunaGlo is a community Nordic sauna and cold contrast lounge. Experience how a magical place can inspire, heal and awaken your spirit and the senses.

 

Volunteers

Milwaukie Mile is supported by some amazing volunteers! They help us with event coordination, athlete safety, and logistics. If you would like to volunteer, please reach out!

name: Monsters & Mimosas 5K - Diamond Lake
description:
Get ready for a spooky-good time at the Monsters & Mimosas 5K, where Halloween fun meets festive celebration! This spirited run invites ghosts, goblins, and costumed creatures of all kinds to hit the course for a frightfully fantastic fall morning.

Join us at Diamond Lake Resort where all race participants will receive a custom finisher medal, a race-themed shirt, and a refreshing mimosa waiting for them at the finish line—because even monsters deserve a little sparkle after a solid run! We'll have juice and water for those under 21.

We’ll also be recognizing top finishers with awards in the usual five-year age groups starting at 10 & under, giving everyone a chance to show off their speed along with their costumes.

Join us for miles, mimosas, and a whole lot of Halloween magic!

name: Newport Celebration Run
description:
Join the Newport Celebration Run on July 4th!

Celebrate Our 12th Anniversary with a Unique and Scenic Running Experience!

Event Highlights:

🌊 Exclusive Run on NOAA Pier: A rare chance to run on the 1,300+ feet NOAA pier, thanks to NOAA's MOC-P.
🏅 Finisher's Medal: For all half marathon, 10k, and 5k finishers.
🍺 Free Beer: (21 and over) Courtesy of Rogue Brewery.
🎟️ Personalized Custom Bibs
⏱️ Professionally Chip-Timed Races

Course Information:

  • Half Marathon: Challenging course with ~1,500 ft elevation gain, featuring ~5.22 miles of pavement, ~5.28 miles of single-track trails, and ~2.6 miles of paved roads.
  • 10k & 5k: Flat, fast courses perfect for setting a personal record.
  • Kids Run: Fun and exciting race for the little ones!

What you'll get:

✔️ Finisher's Medal for all 1/2 Marathon, 10k & 5k finishers
✔️ Personalized custom bib
✔️ Professionally chip-timed
✔️ Beautiful scenic, flat courses
✔️ (1) Beer (21 and over) Courtesy of Rogue Brewery

Why Run with Us?

  • Support a Great Cause: A portion of every registration supports the Rotary Club of Newport.
  • Run Scenic Routes: Enjoy breathtaking views of the Pacific Ocean, Yaquina Bay, and more.
  • Community Spirit: Join a well-supported, friendly event with a vibrant atmosphere.

description: The Newport Harbor Triathlon and 5K is dedicated to promoting a healthy, active lifestyle for athletes of all ages while supporting the growth of youth athletics in our coastal community. description:

name: Oktoberfest Races: 10k run and 5k run/walk
description:
Online registration ends on Saturday, Sept. 20 at noon.

Day of registration, 5k - $45; 10k - $50. Checks or via your phone with QR code.  

The Silverton Runners Club and Oktoberfest are again teaming up to host the Oktoberfest 5k and 10 races. The races have a little something for every type of runner. Track runner? The start and finish is on the Kennedy High School track. Road runner? The course meanders through the hamlet of Mt. Angel. Trail runner? Parts of the course are on gravel. Like it flat? It mostly is. Like hills? We have a couple. Like a good party after? Mt. Angel Oktoberfest! Every finisher will receive a pint glass and a ticket for a complimentary beer at the Oktoberfest. See, we got you all covered! See you there.

What you need to know:

The 10k course will be new this year.

We allow strollers, please line up in the back.

Though we like dogs, please do not bring them to run the races.

There will be day of registration.

If you register for the 10k, please maintain at least a 15:00/mile pace. The course will officially close at 10:30 so our volunteers can enjoy the Oktoberfest activities.

Proceeds from the races go to support the Kennedy, Silverton and Gervais middle & high school track and cross country programs.

Packet pick-up is Sunday (day of race) at the Kennedy High School track, starting at 7:00 AM. Day of registration will be from 7:00am to 8:45am. 

To guarantee a t-shirt, register and purchase your shirt before September 1.

Please note: We will have extra shirts on race day but availability will be limited to what we have on hand.

We can't wait to see you at the races!

1/1/25 to 4/30/25, 5k - $30; 10k - $35

5/1/25 to noon on 9/13/25, 5k - $35; 10k - $40

Day of race, 5k - $45; 10k - $50

Online registration ends on Saturday, Sept. 19 at noon.

There are no refunds.

name: Oregon Tech Twilight Fun Run
description:
The Oregon Tech Twilight Fun Run is hosted by Oregon Tech Wellbeing in collaboration with the Student Veterans Program, and as part of community Memorial Day events, honors all fallen veterans.

Route: The route has been adjusted this year! The Fun Run will begin at Eulalona (formerly known as Kit Carson) Park,  proceeding up the trail that runs parallel to Crater Lake Parkway, to El Dorado, up Daggett, and then right on Bryant Williams Way and around campus. Participants have two route options: 1) complete one full  loop around campus (5k, 3.16 miles) or 2) come directly into Moehl Stadium (a half run, 1.5 miles). Professional timing services will be provided by Athletic Timing who track participants with chipped custom bibs.

Finish: Participants can choose to run through colored chalk at the entrance to the stadium, or have a chalk-free finish experience! Food trucks will be located between the stadium and the Athletics Building, with a closing awards ceremony once the top finishers are recorded. Awards will be given for overall finishers and by age group. 

Registration: Registration fee will allow participants to run/walk the event, get a t-shirt, and receive one free meal ticket to the food trucks. Students and children (up to 18) can participate at no cost, but they DO need to register - be sure to click on the registration for Students and Children to do so. Participants who register the day of the event may not receive a t-shirt, and there will be no cash accepted at Check-in - so be sure to register ahead of time!

Details for Participants: This is a family-friendly environment and walkers and runners alike are welcome; the route is paved throughout. Although we love furry friends, dogs or other pets are not allowed (aside from registered service animals). We will have volunteers placed throughout the route ringing cowbells for encouragement, and Klamath Falls police will also assist in traffic control. Hootie (Oregon Tech's mascot) will be joining us, too!

Volunteer: We are seeking volunteers to assist with event set-up, check-in, t-shirt distribution, route support, and clean-up. Volunteers will receive an event shirt and ticket to the food trucks! If you'd like to volunteer, click "Volunteer" at the bottom of the page below.

If you have any questions please contact Gaylyn Maurer at Gaylyn.Maurer@oit.edu

name: Oregon Tech Twilight Fun Run
description:
The Oregon Tech Twilight Fun Run is hosted by Oregon Tech Wellbeing in collaboration with the Student Veterans Program, and as part of community Memorial Day events, honors all fallen veterans.

Route: The route has been adjusted this year! The Fun Run will begin at Eulalona (formerly known as Kit Carson) Park,  proceeding up the trail that runs parallel to Crater Lake Parkway, to El Dorado, up Daggett, and then right on Bryant Williams Way and around campus. Participants have two route options: 1) complete one full  loop around campus (5k, 3.16 miles) or 2) come directly into Moehl Stadium (a half run, 1.5 miles). Professional timing services will be provided by Athletic Timing who track participants with chipped custom bibs.

Finish: Participants can choose to run through colored chalk at the entrance to the stadium, or have a chalk-free finish experience! Food trucks will be located between the stadium and the Athletics Building, with a closing awards ceremony once the top finishers are recorded. Awards will be given for overall finishers and by age group. 

Registration: Registration fee will allow participants to run/walk the event, get a t-shirt, and receive one free meal ticket to the food trucks. Students and children (up to 18) can participate at no cost, but they DO need to register - be sure to click on the registration for Students and Children to do so. Participants who register the day of the event may not receive a t-shirt, and there will be no cash accepted at Check-in - so be sure to register ahead of time!

Details for Participants: This is a family-friendly environment and walkers and runners alike are welcome; the route is paved throughout. Although we love furry friends, dogs or other pets are not allowed (aside from registered service animals). We will have volunteers placed throughout the route ringing cowbells for encouragement, and Klamath Falls police will also assist in traffic control. Hootie (Oregon Tech's mascot) will be joining us, too!

Volunteer: We are seeking volunteers to assist with event set-up, check-in, t-shirt distribution, route support, and clean-up. Volunteers will receive an event shirt and ticket to the food trucks! If you'd like to volunteer, click "Volunteer" at the bottom of the page below.

If you have any questions please contact Gaylyn Maurer at Gaylyn.Maurer@oit.edu

name: Oregon Trail Game® 5K, 1 Mile & Kid's Fun Run
description:
Included in the registration fee is an “End of the Oregon Trail” event shirt as long as you are signed up before May 1st.

The Oregon Trail® Game 5k presented by Oregon City Schools Foundation is a run based on the 1980’s classic computer game, The Oregon Trail®! Runners are taken on an interactive journey where they’ll make decisions as if they were traveling from Missouri to Oregon. Will you float or ford the river, or die of dysentery along the way? Each decision you make along the trail will determine your ultimate fate. This one-of-a-kind event celebrates Oregon City’s heritage and encourages an active lifestyle and supports our local schools. Grab your pioneer bonnet and get ready to survive the journey

2026 features the 5K, One Mile Walk and Free Kids Run!

In addition to receiving a timed score, runners and walkers will also receive a game score at the end, based on the decisions they make  throughout the game.

Course features include:
• Start and end at the End of the Oregon Trail Interpretive Center
• Run past the iconic 100-year-old Municipal Elevator
• Challenging 223-step run up stairs alongside Singer Hill Falls
• Beautiful views overlooking the Willamette River and Willamette Falls
• Run through the historic McLoughlin neighborhood and past attractions including Carnegie Library, McLoughlin House and Barclay House

The Kids Fun Run will start at 9:30am. It'll be divided into two groups: The younger group will run approximately 100 yards. The older group will run approximately 200 yards. The kids' fun race is untimed.

COURSE:
With an updated race route this year, the Oregon Trail® Game 5K is a fun yet challenging course through historic Oregon City. Get up, get moving, and don't die of a snake bite

description:
Course Description

Experience the unique combination of history, nature, and recreation on a 10K Champoeg Park course through forests, fields, and wetlands. Complete two loops for the 20K course, or three loops for the 30K.

name: ORRC Free Member 5K Run/Walk
description:
♠  ♥  ♣  ♦

Free ORRC Member Poker Run/Walk!

This event is free for ORRC members who pre-register (and $25 for non-members). Everyone in the community is welcome!

Come one, come all! And don't stress about an accurate distance or time! This is just a fun way to spend Labor Day holiday morning. Don't be concerned about how fast or slow you are… the only thing that matters is your poker hand!

 

What is the Poker Run?

The Poker Run/Walk is a 5K course consisting of 3 out-and-back legs all within Greenway Park in Beaverton, starting and finishing at Tractor Park

The event is capped at 150 participants (due to limitations of the bike trail, and limited port-a-pottie!!! (there is only one in the park near the start area, and we are not allowed to bring in any more so... "GO BEFORE YOU GO!")

If you’re not an ORRC member, you can still join the fun for a small registration fee! To find out more about the benefits of ORRC membership – click here ORRC Membership

 

NOTE: There is no day of race registration!

 

Event Start Times:

-7:00 a.m. Registration opens

-7:45 a.m. Start of the 5K Walk

-8:00 a.m. Start of the 5K Run

-The course will close at 10 a.m.

 

Volunteering
We’d love to have you help us put on a great event on Labor Day. If you’re interested in volunteering, please go to the volunteer tab on this page (click here - Volunteer Free Member Run) or email race directors Julia & Tracy Reisinger at info@oregonroadrunnersclub.org.

name: ORRC Hagg Lake Run and Walk
description: This popular recreational mecca boasts big water and bigger vistas.  Scoggins Valley Park and Henry Hagg Lake are the setting for multiple events on Saturday May 10th. Starting at Bobcat Cove, the 10.5 mile run/walk is one full loop around Hagg Lake. The 5K and 10K are out and back.

name: ORRC Vernonia Marathon,  Half Marathon, and Marathon Relay
description: Picture yourself running a beautiful, tree-lined course along the 21 mile Banks-Vernonia State Trail.  Both events feature a gentle 7-mile, 400-foot downhill into Banks.  Hot soup, baked potatoes and hot showers await all runners and walkers. This Boston Marathon qualifier course, USATF Certified, is point-to-point, with 23 miles closed to vehicular traffic. The half marathon course is also USATF Certified.

name: Owyhee Off-Road Challenge
description: Embark on an unforgettable adventure in the heart of the Owyhee High Desert! Join us in Adrian, Oregon—just 54 miles northwest of Boise, Idaho—for the Owyhee Off-Road Challenge, featuring 55k, Half Marathon, 10k, and 5k distances. Immerse yourself in stunning vistas of the Owyhee and Snake River Valleys, rugged peaks, and wide-open spaces, all while enjoying the warm hospitality of the Adrian community. With the friendliest volunteers west of the Rockies, this event promises not only breathtaking scenery but also a welcoming, small-town vibe. All proceeds support the Adrian School District’s track and local youth programs, making every step you take a stride toward a brighter future for our community. Lace up, breathe deep, and take the Challenge!

name: OXFORD Classic Community 5k
description:
Welcome to the 34th Annual Oxford Classic! This meet has become one of Central Oregon’s longest-running and most competitive cross country traditions. Each year it brings together teams from across the region for a high-level mid-season competition. For the first time, we are excited to add a Community 5k — open to everyone who wants to be part of the action!

The Oxford Classic will be held at Drake Park in Bend, Oregon. The course follows a loop through the park along the scenic Deschutes River, featuring a mix of grass and paved pathways. It is flat and fast, with wide stretches designed to accommodate pack racing and plenty of areas for spectators to cheer.

name: PDX Triathlon Festival
description:
Join us for the 43nd Annual PDX Triathlon Festival at Blue Lake Regional Park and kick off the summer racing season. The fun begins on Sunday where athletes compete on our scenic, flat and fast course in either the Super Sprint, Sprint or Olympic Distances. NEW: A 5K on Sunday or try our Paddle Triathlon for those of you who would rather kayak or paddle-board! Relay options are great for friends, family & co-workers!

The Annual PDX/Blue Lake Triathlon was started by the Portland Triathlon Association and Frank Goulard, who is still an active, local Masters Triathlete. He participates in many of our events so come on out and meet the legend, the man who started it all for us here locally!

This weekend festival offers an Olympic and Sprint Distance Triathlon, Duathlon & AquaBike, and a Super Sprint course that offers shorter distances for those new to the sport or just going for pure, raw speed. The Super Sprint is also a great event for our Junior Triathletes!

Recognized by NW triathletes as the “must do” event to open the triathlon season, the PDX Triathlon encompasses two full days of racing (Kids races & Sunset 5k on Saturday & Super Sprint, Sprint & Olympic races on Sunday) including a Sports & Fitness Expo. Triathlon Clubs from across the NW gather to launch the MultiSport season.

The bike courses are flat and fast, with the majority occurring on a section of Marine Dr that is closed to all but local traffic. This makes the course one of the safest and fastest in the region.

PARKING IS INCLUDED WITH REGISTRATION COST.
