name: Portland Bridge Swim
description:
Portland Bridge Swim: Sellwood Bridge to St. Johns Bridge

Sunday July 12, 2026

Ultramarathon-Distance Open Water Event

Hosted by Portland Bridge Swim

 

LOCATION & COURSE:   The course is approximately 11 miles (17 km) on the east side of the Willamette River through downtown Portland, Oregon. The swim will start at Sellwood Riverfront Park (SE 7th Av. & Miller St.) south of the Sellwood Bridge, pass under all 12 of Portland’s bridges on the Willamette River, and finish at Cathedral Park (N. Edison & Pittsburg Av.) west of the St. Johns Bridge. Water temperature is expected to be 66–74 degrees Fahrenheit.


TIDES & START TIME:  High tide on July 12, 2026 is 3:13 am, and low tide is at 12:42 pm. The swim will start at 7:30 am and all swimmers must be out of the water by 3:30 pm.


ELIGIBILITY: This event is open to any swimmer over the age of 18 years old who has completed the eligibility requirements.


ENTRY WEBSITE & REGISTRATION:  To qualify, swimmers must show that they have completed a minimum 5000 m/5500 yd swim faster than 1:40, within 3 years of race day. Only pool swims will be accepted for qualification. Swimmers who cannot complete one mile in open water in 35 minutes should NOT enter. All entries MUST be received by 4:59 pm Pacific time on Sunday, July 5, 2026. Due to organization & safety needs, late or day-of-race entries will not be accepted.


ENTRY LIMITS:  The Portland Bridge Swim is limited to the first 100 entrants. We will maintain a waiting list in case early entrants drop out.


CANCELLATION POLICY:  Swimmers who do not compete, or who do not complete the swim, are not eligible for refunds. If the swim is canceled up to 60 days prior to race day, 50% of entry fees will be refunded. If the swim is canceled less than 60 days prior to race day, no fees will be refunded.


RULES:  

  • SAFETY TOW BUOYS (STBs): All swimmers MUST wear the STB, provided with their swim packets, during their entire portion of the swim. STBs, defined as inflatable buoys tethered to the waist of the swimmer, are permitted in Category I Swimwear events per USMS Rule 303.4.2.E. Swimmers may not use the STBs for flotation assistance.
  • Swimmers must wear the standard latex cap provided in their swim packet. Swimmers must notify race organizers by Friday, July 3, 2026 if the cap cannot be worn. You will need to wear a suitable cap of the color assigned to you for your wave.
  • All drafting is prohibited.  Swimmers must remain 3 meters or more from other swimmers, except when rounding buoys, when overtaking other swimmers when space is not readily available, when unescorted at the start and finish of the swim, and/or when the swimmer's escort craft becomes disabled.  Incidental or accidental incursion into the 3-meter zone of another swimmer shall not be the basis for disqualification.
  • Swimmers may not make deliberate contact with craft, craft operators, and/or physical features on or near the course during the swim.
  • Propulsive devices, such as fins & paddles, and flotation aids, such as pull-buoys, may be allowed at the discretion of the Race Director if an adaptive category is offered for the race. Please contact info@portlandbridgeswim.com before registering if you need to use an adaptive device.
  • Earphones and snorkels are also not allowed. 
  • Motorized watercraft are not permitted as escorts for swimmers. Under no circumstances may a swimmer come in contact with a motorized watercraft. Swimmers who are supported by motorized craft will be disqualified.

QUALIFYING SWIM:  

  • To qualify for individual entry, swimmers must show that they have completed a minimum 5000-meter (5500-yard) swim faster than 1:40, within 3 years of race day.
  • Only pool swims will be accepted for qualification. This qualifying swim does not have to take place in a competition, but registration requires the location of the swim and the signature of an observer. 
  • If you make a mistake in your entry, we will make a good-faith effort to get your correct qualifying swim information. However, swimmers who cannot provide appropriate qualifying time information WILL NOT BE PERMITTED TO SWIM and their entry fee will not be refunded. 

CUT-OFF TIME:  For safety coverage, swimmers on the course who have cleared the Fremont Bridge (approximately 5.5 miles) within 4 hours of race start (note: later waves have less than 4 hours) will be stopped, transported to the race finish, and listed as DNF in the results. Swimmers who have not completed the race within 7 hours of race start will be stopped, transported to the race finish, and listed as DNF in the results.


SAFETY—OUR PRIMARY CONCERN:  Safety boats will monitor the entire course and medical personnel will be on site at the finish. Swimmers are required to have an escort in a non-motorized craft (kayak, stand up paddleboard) in a life vest and equipped with an additional life vest for the swimmer. Each escort will be provided additional mandatory race-specific safety materials. Swimmers MUST wear the brightly-colored swim cap and use the standard tow float provided in their race packet. Swimmers and escorts must follow all announced safety rules without exception.


ESCORTS:  Swimmers are required to have an escort in a non-motorized craft (ie. kayak or paddleboard). Swimmers must provide their own paddler escort and craft. For swimmer safety, motorized watercraft are not permitted to escort swimmers. 


KAYAK RENTALS: A limited number of kayaks, provided by Alder Creek Kayaks, are available for rental as an option at registration.  Kayak rental includes boat, paddle, two life jackets, delivery at the start, and pick-up at the finish. If the escort cannot fit in a standard-size rental kayak, please contact the race organizers to discuss options.


TRANSPORTATION:   A shuttle will be available at the finish to transport swimmers and escorts back to Sellwood Park. With the exception of the rental kayaks above, swimmers are responsible for transporting their kayaks and they may not be taken on the shuttle.


SCHEDULE:  Sunday, July 12, 2026

5:30-7:00 am Check-in at Sellwood Park
6:30 am Pre-race meeting
7:30 am Swim start
11:30 am Individual swimmers who have not reached mile 6 will be stopped & transported to the race finish.
2:00 pm Awards at finish in Cathedral Park
3:30 pm Individual swimmers who have not reached the finish will be stopped & transported to the race finish.

AWARDS:  All finishers will receive a 2026 Portland Bridge Swim medal.  Awards will be presented to overall race winners, and the top 3 finishers in each category. 


RESULTS:  Results will be available after the race, and will be posted at www.portlandbridgeswim.com.  


OREGON SERIES:  Involvement in the Oregon Series TBD.


EVENT WEBSITE:  www.portlandbridgeswim.com


EVENT DIRECTORS:  Daniela Klaz, info@portlandbridgeswim.com

name: Race to Save the Harvest
description:
9th Annual Race to Save the Harvest!

Minto-Brown Island Park


It's hard to believe this family-friendly race has been going and growing for 9 years! Thank you for continuing to support our mission to feed hungry families and reduce food waste.


The 3k out-and-back course, and 5k loop course, will be within Minto-Brown Park along shaded, hard-surface paths. The start and finish lines will be at the south end of Parking Lot 3 near the covered picnic area. Please review the course maps located under the Race Info tab at the top of this webpage.


There will be No Official Timing at this event. Our focus is on providing a safe, fun, family event where you can run, walk, hop, skip, or jump your way through the course with friends and family to support the work and mission of Salem Harvest.


Two options for Packet Pick up (race bib, race shirt, swag, ...) 
Friday, June 26, from 4pm - 6pm at Gallagher Fitness Resources - 135 Commercial Street NE, Salem Oregon
Saturday, June 27, from 8am - 9:15am at Minto-Brown Island Park - 2200 Minto Island Rd SW SE, Salem Oregon - near parking lot 3.


What else to expect at the race?


All funds earned will be used to help Salem Harvest gather fresh produce from local farms that would go to waste and make it available for hungry families in the Willamette Valley. The harvested crops would be left in the fields to rot unless it is saved by quick working volunteers. These fruits and vegetables are perfectly delicious but not usable by growers. So... Salem Harvest volunteers Race to the fields to Save the Harvest and get this unused resource into the community!


Event t-shirts will be included with registrations being made before June 5th. Entry fees increase and shirts won't be available when registering on June 5th or later. Register early to get the best price and the swag you need!


Raffle prizes - Fabulous raffle prizes will be available to win! Each participant will receive one ticket and can choose which prize they would like to win. name: Race to Space
description:
Join us for the 5th Annual Race to Space on May 9, 2026, on Linfield University's Wellness Trail. This is a timed race with 12, 8, 6, 3, and 1-hour options, and an alternate 4-loop relay for teams of 2-4 participants. NEW this year is the Bingo Run! For each lap, runners draw a number. Once you have pulled the three numbers that match what appears on your bib, you have finished the race. Choose from 10, 20, or 30-number races, with the option to continue running after your bingo card is filled. 

Base Camp is located at the start/finish of our approximately 1.5-mile loop trail course, located at 57 Keck Drive, McMinnville, OR.  Profits from the event go to charity.

 

Sign up before December 31 to get the best pricing.

 

Find Your Why

Our event provides runners and walkers with many options because people have different goals and fitness levels. Looking for something short just to get moving or to work back from an injury? Try the one-hour Moon Shot or grab friends and run the relay. Training for a half marathon? The three-hour Mission to Mars will give runners lots of time to get in the mileage. Maybe you're preparing for a marathon or longer. The 6-, 8-, and 12-hour options are for you. If running a marathon or ultra has always been on your bucket list, but you're worried about being too slow or not having enough fitness, the 6-, 8-, and 12-hour races provide a great opportunity to fulfill that dream. 

Want to try your luck and something new at the same time? The Bingo Run gives every runner a chance to win, with a bit of luck, by filling their card first. Every time you complete a lap, draw a number. If that number matches one of the bingo numbers on your bib, you mark off that number. Once your bingo card is filled, you're finished! (though we'll probably let you keep going). Awards will be given to those who fill their card the fastest, measured both in time and the number of draws, so there may be multiple winners. If the competitive aspect doesn't matter to you, maybe this event appeals to you for the uncertainty of how far you will have to run to get a bingo. 

Regardless of your why, the beauty of a loop course is that you only need to finish one lap to be a finisher (unless you're in the relay, then your team needs to complete four loops, or if you're in the Bingo Run, then who knows how far you will have to go). If you have your sights set on running the 26.2 miles of a marathon or longer, but you're just not feeling it on race day, you're never more than 3/4 of a mile from the start/finish. Those rebuilding from an injury or testing themselves with a new distance can bail if needed and still be a finisher.

(Scroll down toward the bottom if you want to know our why)

General Information

The various events start at different times to avoid course congestion.

Starting at 7:00 AM:

Abduction Adventure (12-hour race)

Bingo 30

Starting at 8:00 AM:

Moon Shot (1-hour race) 

Journey to Pluto (8-hour race) 

Bingo 20

Starting at 9:30 AM:

Mission to Mars (3-hour race)

Solar Shuffle (6-hour race)

Bingo 10

Starting at 12 PM (noon):

Space Sprint (4-loop relay, 2-4 runners per team)

 

Pricing (through the end of December)

Moon Shot - 1 hr race - $25.00 

Mission to Mars - 3 hr race - $40.00 

Solar Shuffle - 6 hr race - $50.00 

Journey to Pluto - 8 hr race - $60.00 

Abduction Adventure - 12 hr race - $80

Bingo 10 - $40

Bingo 20 - $60

Bingo 30 - $80

Runners in the timed events who also want to compete in Bingo can do so for an additional $10

Space Sprint - 4 loop relay (2-4 per team) - $60.00 per team 

 

What to Expect on Race Day

Plan to arrive at least 30 minutes prior to your scheduled race to pick up your race bib. Parking is just a few feet from packet pickup and the start/finish. 

 

Course Description

Loop course: Our race will be a ~1.5-mile loop course run at Linfield University’s wellness trail. It is a mostly dirt/bark dust trail. The start/finish and aid station will be located just off SE Lever Street on Wildcat Circle (in Google Maps, it is the parking lot to the SE of the Linfield University Nicholson Library). There are areas for runners to set up their own aid stations or chairs along the course, and vehicle access is very close.

What shoes should I wear? The trail is not very technical, with just a few tree roots; road shoes work best in dry conditions. If conditions are wet and muddy, trail shoes might be a better option.

Oregon's May weather can be unpredictable. For two of the first four years of the event, high temperatures topped 85 degrees. We have yet to have any significant rain at the event, but this is Oregon, so mentally prepare for anything.

The aid station will provide water and an electrolyte drink, as well as a variety of sweet and savory snacks. Special requests will be considered, but runners with specific needs or preferences are encouraged to bring their own food and drink to supplement. Runners are encouraged to bring their own reusable cups to help reduce waste. 

 

Volunteer Information

Not looking to run? We are seeking volunteers for our race! Jobs for volunteers include registration and packet pickup, course monitors, aid station, waste management, and set-up/takedown. Volunteers will get swag and our heartfelt thanks.

 

Swag

Top finishers in each race will earn special awards. All participants will receive a pair of high-quality running socks. If we get enough entries by mid-April, shirts will also be provided. We are always working on securing additional swag for our amazing runners and walkers, so stay tuned and be ready to be surprised!

 

Refund policy

Unfortunately, we will not issue any refunds or transfers should you not be able to run on race day. Costs are incurred prior to race day, and profits will be donated to charity, so we cannot make any exceptions to this policy.

Why are we putting on this race?

Most of the crew you will see working the race are students in an Economics of Running class at Linfield University. The class project is to offer an event that encourages students to put their understanding of economic concepts into action. While our primary why is educational, we're happy to provide fitness opportunities, particularly for the running community. If we're fortunate enough to earn a profit on the event, extra monies go to benefit a local charity.

Space Sprint (4-loop relay, 2-4 runners per team)

 

Pricing (through the end of December)

Moon Shot - 1 hr race - $25.00 

Mission to Mars - 3 hr race - $40.00 

Solar Shuffle - 6 hr race - $50.00 

Journey to Pluto - 8 hr race - $60.00 

Abduction Adventure - 12 hr race - $80

Bingo 10 - $40

Bingo 20 - $60

Bingo 30 - $80

Runners in the timed events who also want to compete in Bingo can do so for an additional $10

Space Sprint - 4 loop relay (2-4 per team) - $60.00 per team 

 

What to Expect on Race Day

Plan to arrive at least 30 minutes prior to your scheduled race to pick up your race bib. Parking is just a few feet from packet pickup and the start/finish. 

 

Course Description

Loop course: Our race will be a ~1.5-mile loop course run at Linfield University’s wellness trail. It is a mostly dirt/bark dust trail. The start/finish and aid station will be located just off SE Lever Street on Wildcat Circle (in Google Maps, it is the parking lot to the SE of the Linfield University Nicholson Library). There are areas for runners to set up their own aid stations or chairs along the course, and vehicle access is very close.

What shoes should I wear? The trail is not very technical, with just a few tree roots; road shoes work best in dry conditions. If conditions are wet and muddy, trail shoes might be a better option.

Oregon's May weather can be unpredictable. For two of the first four years of the event, high temperatures topped 85 degrees. We have yet to have any significant rain at the event, but this is Oregon, so mentally prepare for anything.

The aid station will provide water and an electrolyte drink, as well as a variety of sweet and savory snacks. Special requests will be considered, but runners with specific needs or preferences are encouraged to bring their own food and drink to supplement. Runners are encouraged to bring their own reusable cups to help reduce waste. 

 

Volunteer Information

Not looking to run? We are seeking volunteers for our race! Jobs for volunteers include registration and packet pickup, course monitors, aid station, waste management, and set-up/takedown. Volunteers will get swag and our heartfelt thanks.

 

Swag

Top finishers in each race will earn special awards. All participants will receive a pair of high-quality running socks. If we get enough entries by mid-April, shirts will also be provided. We are always working on securing additional swag for our amazing runners and walkers, so stay tuned and be ready to be surprised!

 

Refund policy

Unfortunately, we will not issue any refunds or transfers should you not be able to run on race day. Costs are incurred prior to race day, and profits will be donated to charity, so we cannot make any exceptions to this policy.

Why are we putting on this race?

Most of the crew you will see working the race are students in an Economics of Running class at Linfield University. The class project is to offer an event that encourages students to put their understanding of economic concepts into action. While our primary why is educational, we're happy to provide fitness opportunities, particularly for the running community. If we're fortunate enough to earn a profit on the event, extra monies go to benefit a local charity.

name: Rogue River Triathlon
description: The Rogue River Triathlon includes a Sprint Distance and a Mini Distance. Both distances begin with a down-river swim in the Rogue River. Next is the run, 3 miles for the Sprint Distance and 1.5 miles for the Mini. The run takes place on a paved Forest Service Road overlooking the beautiful Rogue River. The event ends with the bike ride, 12 miles for the Sprint and 6 miles for the Mini. The bike ride is also on a paved Forest Service Road and boasts views of the Rogue River. There is also an option for a 2-3 person relay.

name: Rose City Mile
description:
Rose City Track Club is proud to present the 9th annual Rose City Mile! Our mission is to provide a fun and accessible opportunity for runners of all ages and abilities to test their fitness. Join us on Saturday, June 13 at Franklin High School in southeast Portland for a track meet like no other.

We believe that everyone has a place in the running community that is respectful, safe, and inclusive. On race day we present awards in men's, women's, and non-binary categories. Participants who select either "Non-Binary" or "Prefer Not to Say" during sign up will be eligible for the non-binary awards category.

Online registration closes at midnight on Thursday, June 11.

Runners will have the option of registering for the Rose City Mile the day of the race for $38.50 (inc. $3.50 fee). Same day registration closes 50 minutes before the first heat in each section.

Sponsorship

Rose City Mile would not happen without the generous support of our sponsors. Our event features 300 competitors of all ages, as well as many spectators cheering them on. We have four tiers of sponsorship available. To learn more, please check out our 2025 sponsor packet or email rosecitymile@rosecitytrack.com.

name: Roseburg to Coos Bay Relay
description:
68-mile, 5 person running team or 24-mile, 4 person walking team.  Staggered start depending on predicted finishing time.  The slowest running teams (or those who want to get more value for money) will start at 6AM.  Runners start a the ADAPT parking lot in Roseburg, walkers start in Laverne Park, Coquille.  The race ends at the Coos History Museum (1210 N. Front St., Coos Bay). 

Who says running is a lonely sport?  Grab four friends and start cheering!  

Proceeds benefit Camp Millennium, dedicated to providing outdoor recreation activities to kids with cancer.

name: Run for a Reason 2026 with Two Daughters Foundation
description:
Run for Two Daughters Foundation at the 2026 Eugene Marathon, raise money to cover your registration costs, and support our mission of providing free peer grief support to young adults across the country!


There's no more iconic place to achieve your running accomplishment than in Track Town USA! You can tackle the full 26.2 miles in the marathon, or sign up for the half marathon or 5k! Whatever you choose, you will be in the company of other Two Daughters Foundation team members and enjoy the beautiful scenery of South Eugene and the University of Oregon.


To run for team Two Daughters Foundation, sign up and fundraise for your spot! The fundraising minimums are listed below. Two Daughters Foundation will send you a registration link once you've achieved your fundraising goal. All profits received by Two Daughters Foundation go towards our charity's mission of providing free grief support to young adults in Oregon and beyond that are navigating the serious illness or loss of a parent or parental figure.

**Note: The deadline to meet the fundraising minimum is March 15, 2026**

All Team Members Receive:

  • FREE registration for the race! As soon as your fundraising goal is met, your registration fee is waived for the race of your choice.
  • An official Two Daughters Foundation T-shirt
  • Fundraising platform and tools, including your own fundraising page and ongoing fundraising support from Two Daughters Foundation staff

Fundraising Minimums:


Marathon: $350

Half Marathon: $250

5k: $150


Once you've achieved your fundraising goal, Two Daughters Foundation will reach out to you with a registration link that will allow you to register at no additional cost to you.

Please note that you will be accountable for covering the remaining amount to meet the fundraising minimum if the fundraising minimum is not met by the fundraising deadline.


Contact info@twodaughtersfoundation.org if you have any questions! We are happy to help you get set up and provide fundraising tips. 


We look forward to running with you!

name: Run for Salem Free Clinics
description:
2025 Race Results are here 

Thank you for supporting Salem Free Clinics, a community non-profit dedicated to providing quality, compassionate healthcare at no cost to the uninsured as an expression of Christ's love. Last year’s race was a huge success with a record amount of participants. This year, we are excited to announce that we will have both an in-person and virtual race option again!

 

Register by July 31st to be guaranteed a free t-shirt (only adult sizes available)!
•    $30 for Early Bird Pricing | $35 starting August 1st
•    $15 registration fee for ages 6-12
•    Ages 5 and below register for free (no t-shirt included)

 

NOTE TO IN-PERSON PARTICIPANTS: At our event, we ask that you keep your furry friends at home. Thank you!

 

NOTE TO VIRTUAL PARTICIPANTS: Run or walk your distance between August 8th and August 15th and keep track of your time to send to Huber Timing if you want it posted. To post your time, follow the instructions in your Welcome Email sent at the race start time on August 8th.

name: Run for the Oaks
description:
Run for the Oaks

This is the 10th annual Run for the Oaks at Left Coast Cellars! The course will predominantly be on gravel roads or off-road with trail and paved road segments. The run will meander throughout the Left Coast Cellars estate and runners will pass oak forests, vineyards, and gardens with spectacular views of the Willamette Valley. This run has been created to raise funds for our Oak Savanna Restoration Project. The goal of the project is to model how ecological integrity can coincide with responsible industry.

Great Event

  • Complimentary wine tasting!
  • Participant T-Shirts
  • Finishers receive a custom wine glass
  • Event professionally chip timed
  • Free Parking
We hope to see you out there!

name: Run Hub Gear Grants 5K, 10-mi, & Pancake Breakfast
description:
The Gear Grants Run features 5K and 10-mile race distances as well as an add-on pancake breakfast afterward.  All funds go to support the Run Hub Gear Grants program.  Run Hub Gear Grants is a 501c3 non-profit that provides grants to Eugene-Springfield area school athletes in need participating in cross country during the fall or track & field in the spring.  The grants allow recipients to purchase essential running/training gear like running shoes and competition spikes or footwear for the season.  Bib pickup is from 7:45-8:45 AM on race day. Both races begin at 9 AM. 

Thanks to our sponsors, all ticket proceeds will go directly to fund gear grants for local student athletes. Event sponsors include: ASICS, Kiva Grocery, Krusteaz, Palace Coffee | Bakery, Rowell Brokaw Architects & Zenith Performance & Wellness.

Both races begin at 9 AM. 

Thanks to our sponsors, all ticket proceeds will go directly to fund gear grants for local student athletes. Event sponsors include: ASICS, Kiva Grocery, Krusteaz, Palace Coffee | Bakery, Rowell Brokaw Architects & Zenith Performance & Wellness.

name: Run Whiskey Run
description:
For more information, visit our website at www.SouthCoastRunningClub.org

Located roughly 20 miles south of Coos Bay, the region’s first single-track trail system is open year-round to mountain bikers, but for the first time ever will be reserved for those of us who shred at running pace. 

We’ll start and finish at the main Whiskey Run Trailhead. 

Our chosen section of Whiskey Run is shaded and sheltered, which means these trails are rolling, smooth, and oh so loamy.

Course options include:

·      1.5 Mile (Shirley Temple)

·      5 Mile (Whiskey Ginger)

·      10 Mile (Double Shot) 

Please note that all courses are 100% trail, so not stroller friendly.

PRICES

Online

$15 Club member (your discount will appear at check-out), Non-member $25. 

Day of race

$20 Club member, Non-member $30

Students: $5.00.  Use the code Student2022 to register.  To avoid credit card charges, students will not be charged at on-line registration.  Please bring $5 (exact change appreciated) to registration!  

START TIMES

-      9am (10 Mile Double Shot)

-      9:30am (5 Mile Whiskey Ginger) 

-      9:45 (1.5 Mile Shirley Temple)

Course support ends at 12 PM.

Day of race registration and packet pick up begins at 8:00 at Whiskey Run Trailhead.

Runners should assemble at the starting line no later than 10 minutes before start time for instructions from the race director.  

Come dressed to run; no space is available for changing/showering.

INFORMATION ABOUT THE AREA

Whiskey Run is located on Oregon’s Adventure Coast. Our costal community offers endless opportunities for beach combing, fishing, crabbing, paddling, hiking, and golfing. And don’t forget about the mountain biking… bring your bike and explore the 30+ miles of premier single track at Whiskey Run.

Come see what attracts so many runners to Oregon’s Adventure Coast.

name: RUN/WALK FOR THE RARE!
description:
Haley's Heroes Foundation presents 7th Annual RUN FOR THE RARE, a 10k, 5k and 1 mile run/walk to support International Batten Disease Awareness Day.  Did you know that Rare is everywhere? Join us as we run on Sunday, June 14, 2026. 1 in 10 people have a rare disease and 50% of those are children. There are more than 7000 known rare diseases and an estimated 350 million people globally diagnosed with a rare disease. YET, 95% of all rare diseases don't have a FDA approved treatment or cure. Let's run (or walk) to change the course of the lives for all those with rare disease. Post pictures at #RUNWALKFORTHERARE!  

The race will start and finish outside of the Pavilion in the North Meadow. Starting time is 10am and all participants should be finished by 1pm.

Cost is $45 for adults and $35 for children and includes the t-shirt.

Registration fee includes  a T-shirt, coupon for wings and fries, coupon for ice cream and a Photo Booth.

June 13 - Early packet pick up is 2pm-4pm at Gallagher's Fitness | 135 Commercial St NE, Salem, OR 97301
June 14 - Packet pick up beginning at 9am at the run

name: Salem Summer Solstice 5/10K
description:
This race is a fundraiser to support McKay HS Cross Country Team!

 

Friday, June 12th, 2026

10k starts at 7:00 pm 
5k starts at 7:10 pm

Starting location: Minto Brown Island Park, parking lot #3 by the pavilion

The 5K and 10K courses are flat courses in a natural setting in a beautiful park. The 5K course is all on paved trails. The 10K course does have a small loop along an open trail and then returns to a paved path again.

Entry fee includes a post-race ice-cream sundae and chip timing by Eclectic Edge Racing with immediate timing results.

Race divisions will be 10-year age groups (1-10, 11-20, 21-30...80-89), and the top three male/female winners will be awarded ribbons.

Important Details:
Restrictions: No rollerblades/skates, skateboards, dogs, or unregistered participants. Baby joggers and strollers are allowed. Walkers are welcome in the 5K. Headphones permitted as long as they allow ambient passthrough noise.

Packet Pickup Begins at 6:00 pm.  Day of Race Registration will end promptly at 6:50 pm & is **all forms of payment accepted** (unless capacity is reached before then). 

All race courses close at 9:00 PM.

Note: Race timing and course monitoring end at 8:30 P.M.
 
Club Member Discounts:
All current members of the Willamette Valley Road Runners Club will save $3.00 on their entry fee.  Join WVRR or renew today!

Aid stations: One water station is provided for both races around mile point 1.25 for the 5k and 4.25 for the 10k.

name: Santiam Canyon River Run
description:
The Santiam Canyon River Run featuring three race distances: 10k Race, 5k Run/Walk, and 3k Run/Walk. It’s designed to cater to a variety of runners, from seasoned athletes to casual enthusiasts. The course is multi-surface, including sections of trail, pavement, and gravel, providing a diverse running experience. The event takes place in the picturesque setting of Stayton, with sections along the Santiam River. Participants will have a unique opportunity to enjoy the lush natural scenery as they push toward the finish line.  Runners can expect a well-organized event with clear markings and enthusiastic support from the community. Whether aiming for a personal best or simply looking to complete the course, the Santiam Canyon River Run is an excellent opportunity for runners to challenge themselves in a scenic environment. This will be a chipped and timed race provided by Athletic Timing. This race is hosted by Santiam Hospital & Clinics Foundation. 

All races will begin and end at Snow Peak Brewing Company. Each finisher will receive a commemorative pint glass along with a coupon for a soda or beer from Snow Peak Brewing Co. Check in will begin at 8:00am for a prompt 9:30am race start.

name: Scandia Run
description: The Scandia Run provides fun for the entire family! Courses weave through the outskirts of Junction City into the beautiful Willamette Valley farmlands! If you’re looking for a flat, fast, road race the USATF certified 5K or 10K is for you! If you want to take your time and enjoy a gorgeous August morning the 4-Mile Walk is a great option. Kiddos can run alongside Vikings in the 400m “Run with the Vikings.” After your race, enjoy Junction City’s world-famous Scandinavian Festival.

name: Shamrock Run
description:
WHERE:  Crater High School, 655 N 3rd St, Central Point, OR 97502

WHEN:  March 21st 

COURSE:  Start and Finish on Crater High School Track. Run out and back on the Bear Creek Greenway. 

To celebrate St Patrick's day, we will be sending each runner home with Shamrock bulbs to plant. Instead of handing out medals, we will have our (now famous) medal photo booth with our photographer ready to take a photo (with your phone) of you wearing a medal and Shamrock props in front of our rainbow backdrop. We'd love to see your best green outfit!

PARKING: Parking is in the student parking lot off of 3rd St next to the gym and football stadium.  Please DO NOT park in faculty parking lots.

FACILITIES:  Bathrooms available.  No showers

STARTING TIMES:  9:00AM 2 mile & 5 mile | 8:45AM the kids Leprechaun Lap  

PACKET PICKUP: 8:00AM-8:50AM DAY OF RACE

RESTRICTIONS:  Absolutely no roller-skaters, bicycles, skateboards, baby joggers, dogs, headphones, or unregistered participants

RACE DIRECTOR:  Suzanne Ray and Chris Mansuetti

name: Sole Sisters 13.1 / 10k / 5k
description:
Lace up, grab your besties, and get ready to shine! The Sole Sisters Half Marathon, 10K, & 5K is back, and we want YOU to be part of the magic. Whether you’re a seasoned marathoner, a weekend jogger, or taking your very first steps into fitness, this is your moment to celebrate strength, sisterhood, and crushing those big goals!

✨ Why You’ll Love It
Experience the ultimate "out and back" course that winds through Wilsonville’s most stunning scenery. You’ll breeze along the scenic Willamette River trails and cruise through charming neighborhood streets with a community of incredible women cheering you on every step of the way.

Your Race, Your Pace: This is a timing-optional event! Want to gun for a PR? We’ll be awarding special prizes to the top three finishers in every age division. Want to take it slow and soak in the vibes? We’re here for it!

 
🎁 The "Sole Sister" Perks
We’re with you from your first training mile to the finish line! Every registration includes:

 

  • The Ultimate Head Start:  Weekly long-distance routes across 15 different locations (starting March 2026!).
  • Training Support: Optional in-person weekly training sessions led by our amazing coaches.
  • VIP Fun: Exclusive events and raffle prizes at Road Runner Sports in Tualatin.
  • The Connection: Weekly emails packed with tips and sisterhood vibes.
  • The Bling: A gorgeous Finisher’s Medal and a personalized race bib to commemorate your achievement.
  • Race Day Fuel: Refreshing healthy food items to help you refuel and celebrate your victory.
  • Optional Style: High-performance Race Tech Tees or Tanks are available for purchase to complete your look!
     

⚠️ Important Details

Personalized Bibs: Register by May 10th to see your name in print on your race bib!


The Fine Print: We have a no-refund policy, but transfers are allowed.


Paws Policy: To keep our course safe and clear, please leave your furry friends at home—this race is for the humans!

Are you ready to find your finish line?

Lace up, grab your besties, and get ready to shine! The Sole Sisters Half Marathon, 10K, & 5K is back, and we want YOU to be part of the magic. Whether you’re a seasoned marathoner, a weekend jogger, or taking your very first steps into fitness, this is your moment to celebrate strength, sisterhood, and crushing those big goals!

✨ Why You’ll Love It
Experience the ultimate "out and back" course that winds through Wilsonville’s most stunning scenery. You’ll breeze along the scenic Willamette River trails and cruise through charming neighborhood streets with a community of incredible women cheering you on every step of the way.

Your Race, Your Pace: This is a timing-optional event! Want to gun for a PR? We’ll be awarding special prizes to the top three finishers in every age division. Want to take it slow and soak in the vibes? We’re here for it!

 
🎁 The "Sole Sister" Perks
We’re with you from your first training mile to the finish line! Every registration includes:

 

  • The Ultimate Head Start:  Weekly long-distance routes across 15 different locations (starting March 2026!).
  • Training Support: Optional in-person weekly training sessions led by our amazing coaches.
  • VIP Fun: Exclusive events and raffle prizes at Road Runner Sports in Tualatin.
  • The Connection: Weekly emails packed with tips and sisterhood vibes.
  • The Bling: A gorgeous Finisher’s Medal and a personalized race bib to commemorate your achievement.
  • Race Day Fuel: Refreshing healthy food items to help you refuel and celebrate your victory.
  • Optional Style: High-performance Race Tech Tees or Tanks are available for purchase to complete your look!
     

⚠️ Important Details

Personalized Bibs: Register by May 10th to see your name in print on your race bib!


The Fine Print: We have a no-refund policy, but transfers are allowed.


Paws Policy: To keep our course safe and clear, please leave your furry friends at home—this race is for the humans!

Are you ready to find your finish line?

name: Southern Oregon Runners Turkey Trot Run
description:
Come to Talent, Oregon for our Thanksgiving run! We will be hosting a food drive for the SOU food bank and a portion of the proceeds will go to SOR Student Runners Programs which include Shoes for Kids (provides shoes to Jr. High and High School athletes who would like to participate in Cross Country and Track but cannot afford proper running shoes), KidsRunFree (provides free entry to all SOR races for kids 18 & under), and XC Project (provides timing support for schools during cross country season).

When - November 26, 2025

Free Turkey Dash Kids Run( 8 and Under)8:00AM| 8 Mile Run 8:15AM|5k Run/Walk 8:30AM|2 Mile Family Run/Walk 8:40AM $20 for members| $25 for non members| Youth 18 and Under are free. Family Pricing available for this event, this is for families and families with extended family in town for the holidays, only.  

Where - Cummins 300 W Valley View Rd, Talent, Oregon 97540

Packet Pick Up - November 25th from 3:30-8pm at Legend Cider Co. Talent Taphouse, 245 W Valley View, Talent, Oregon 97540. Packet pick up is also available from 7-8am on the day of the race. NO IN PERSON REGISTRATION will be offered. 

Participants will receive a custom race bib and finishers medal. No age group awards.

NO DOGS, BIKES, SKATEBOARDS OR SKATES PERMITTED.

*Races are on public roads and trails that ARE NOT closed to cars, pedestrian or cyclist.  Please use caution while on public roadways and paths.

name: Stayton Fun Run
description:
Stayton Fun Run

Since 1983 Stayton has been celebrating fitness and this family tradition on the 4th of July. Both the runs and walk of this annual event will take place on asphalt and cross-country surfaces. The courses are excellent for the competitive runner, fun runner and walker.

The Runs and Walk is being held in conjunction with Stayton’s 4th of July festival. The festival features such activities as a Kid’s and Grand Parade, a community dinner, band concerts, variety show, kid’s games, food booths and a fantastic fireworks display. So, there is much to do after the race is over.

The MOST PATRIOTICALLY DRESSED RUNNER will win a patriotic denali blanket a $130. value 

WHEN: Every JULY 4th, starting at 9:00 a.m. (DAY OF REGISTRATION FOR TIMED RESULTS WILL END @ 8:45 AM) ***8:30am Race Day Scout Flag Ceremony (start your 4th of july off right)***

WHERE: Starts at the Stayton Community Center – 500 W Burnett St. (Off 1st St.). Stayton is 15 miles east of Salem on Highway 22.

FEE: $15.00 per person if you pre-register online (before July 4th). $20.00 per person day of the race (DAY OF REGISTRATION FOR TIMED RESULTS WILL END @ 8:45 AM). Registration begins at 7:30 a.m. at the Stayton Community Center.

INCLUDED: Ribbons to the top male and female finishers in five-year age-groups in the 5k and 10k races; Stay around after the race to see who won the most patriotically dressed!

WHAT’S NOT INCLUDED: High Entry Fees, Fancy Awards

Learn More About The Race: www.StaytonFunRun.com

name: Sunset Bay Trail Runs
description:
Hilly, scenic trail run along the scenic Oregon Coast.  Sunset Bay Trail Runs feature very challenging courses, especially for the longer distances and the views will take what breath you have left away.  Seriously, this race has it all, killer hills through the woods, and an amazing flat cliff section where you'll see sea lions, rocks, the deep blue sea, and if you're very lucky, a passing whale.  This is an amazing, not to be missed course.

Packet pickup and start/finish line is at the gazebo on far south end of Sunset Bay.  Packet pickup is race morning only.  Please come at least 1/2 hour before your race start time.  Sunset State Park is a very gracious host and we want to keep our welcome warm.  Please do not park on the grass!

Half-marathoners must have reached the aid station after the first loop at Cape Arago by 10:45. This is at approximately 6.5 miles. That is an 18:28 minute mile, which is almost a fast walking pace. If you arrive at the aid station after that, we will switch you to the 15K race, no worries, you will still have a great workout and a great time!

There will be water and Gatorade at the start/finish line and plenty of snacks at the finish. There is one aid station for the 15K and 1/2 marathon runners that will have water, gels, and other snacks. The 15K will pass the aid station twice and the 1/2 marathon will pass it 3 times.  While we will have cups available, we encourage runners to carry a bottle to reduce waste.  No littering on course!  Please leave all waste at the aid station or carry it to the finish.  Sunset Bay has been a gracious host for many years and we want to keep it beautiful. 

There are restrooms at 4 miles for the 15 K and 1/2 Marathon participants. The course isn't on the road very much, but it is open to traffic, so be alert.  This is a RRCA sanctioned event.  For safety, NO headphones, rollerblades, skateboards (hey, you're on trails, that's not even possible), bicycles, animals, or jogging strollers are allowed during the race.

Proceeds from the event will be donated to the Marshfield High School Cross Country Team who will be manning the aid stations.  Go Pirates!

Ribbons to top three winners overall and in each age-group.  Farr's Hardware will donate a $50 gift card to a lucky random winner from each race.  We will select a winner during awards.  Must be present to win.

name: Support the Girls 5K Run/Walk Fundraiser for Breast Friends
description:
REGISTRATION WILL OPEN FEBRUARY 10th!!!!

Join us for this exciting fundraising event at Stickmen Brewing in Tualatin! The course is paved and mostly flat - perfect for all abilities and ages! name: SW Hope 5k
description:
We are back again at OES in SW Portland, starting at 9:45 with kids and the 5k to follow at 10:15!

Every spring, multiple Southwest Portland Faith Organizations and Community Partners join hands to meet the need of hunger specifically, by working to supply Neighborhood House’s (https://nhpdx.org/) Free Food Market, the largest west of the Willamette. This joint effort is known as the Southwest Hope Campaign. Since 2016, Missio Church has organized the SW Hope 5k as a culmination of the greater campaign.

What can $1 buy me at a grocery store? One, maybe two, canned goods at the most. For $1, Neighborhood House can buy 4 pounds of food directly from Oregon Food Bank. We quickly realized we could turn a simple canned food drive into a huge tool to empower Neighborhood House and reach hundreds more hungry neighbors.

This is where you come in. We invite you to run with us in our fifth annual SW Hope Feed the Hungry 5K because each $1 we raise together far outweighs it’s worth in canned goods individually.  If we run together, our neighbors here in SW Portland won’t have to experience the insecurity of not knowing where their next meal is coming from.

name: The Homer Races: The Homer Classic 8k race, 2 mile run/walk, and The Homer Parade Mile!
description:
NEW EVENT! The Homer Parade Mile.

Lead the Homer Davenport Community Festival parade! The Homer Parade Mile is Saturday morning, August 1. Runners will "lead" the parade by running the parade route through downtown Silverton, being cheered by the thousands of people lining the parade route.
The start will be on North Water St. near Silverton Middle School and finish just past Roth's Fresh Market on North First St.

Combine The Homer Parade Mile with the Homer's Classic 8k on Sunday to see who is the overall mile/8k winner.

 

Here are the Homer Davenport Community Festival Race options:

 

1 Mile run: Saturday, August 1, 9:45am start time.

Runners ages 0-9, $0     

Runners ages 10-12, $5

Runners over 13, $10

Family price, up to 10 family members, $20

Day of registration ends at 9:15am.

2 Mile run/walk: Sunday, August 3, 9:00am start time.

      $20 until May 1: $25 Mary 1 - July 31 (online registration ends at 5:00pm) : $30 day of race.

8k run: Sunday, August 3, 9:00am start time.

      $20 until May 1: $25 May 1 - July 31(online registration ends at 5:00pm) : $30 day of race.

Do the Duo, 1Mile/8k runs: Run the Mile on Saturday, the 8k on Sunday.

      $30 until May 1, $35 March 1 - July 31 (online registration ends at 5:00pm). No day of race registration for the combined races. 

 

T-shirts, $ 15 extra. Register before July 14 to be guaranteed a shirt.

Race packets are available day of race.

 

The Homer Parade Mile is Saturday morning, August 1. Runners will "lead" the parade by running the parade route through downtown Silverton, being cheered by the thousands of people lining the parade route.
The start will be on North Water St. near Silverton Middle School and finish just past Roth's Fresh Market on North First St.

 

Sunday, August 2,The Homer Classic 8k and 2 mile run/walk start and finish of is Silverton High School, 1456 Pine St., Silverton, OR. There is plenty of parking at the high school.

 

The 8k run features a scenic, flat and fast course running through the Historic Gallon House Bridge, the only covered bridge in Marion County.

 

The races are organized by the Silverton Runners' Club. Proceeds go to support the Silverton, Gervais and Mt. Angel schools' track and cross country programs, scholarships for youth runners to attend running camps, and other local fitness activities.

 

No dogs or motorized vehicles permitted.

name: Timberline Marathon and Half Marathon
description:
Get ready for the most picturesque marathon and half marathon trail running course in the Pacific Northwest! The course completely circles shimmering Timothy Lake on single track trails that are absolutely a runner's dream. This gem is nestled at 3,227 feet in the high Cascades and the views of Mt. Hood across the lake are extraordinary.

Finisher medals and gender specific technical shirts are included with your registration.

The journey begins at the Clackamas Lake Historic Ranger Station and takes runners on a magical course that traverses three rustic bridges over sparkling tributaries that feed the deep blue waters of the lake. The ever changing scenery and terrain create an experience that is unparalleled. The Timberline Marathon and Half Marathon is a must for any runner's calendar!

name: TrackTown Triathlon
description:
Join the University of Oregon Triathlon Team for a fun, welcoming, and beginner-friendly triathlon right here at the UO Rec Center! Whether you’re a experienced triathlete, completely new to the sport, or you’re a young athlete excited to challenge yourself, this event is built just for you.

What to Expect

This race is designed to be accessible, low-pressure, and community-oriented. Distances are intentionally short, the atmosphere is relaxed, and our UO Tri athletes will be on deck to cheer you on, answer questions, and guide you every step of the way. Perfect for:

  • Newcomers wanting a fun introduction to triathlon
  • Youth and teens interested in trying something active and exciting
  • Community members looking for a supportive challenge
  • Families and friends participating together


Race Format

The event takes place entirely within and around the Rec Center facilities, featuring:

Indoor Swim – Safe, supervised laps in the Rec Center pool
Stationary Bike Ride – Timed effort on indoor bikes—your own pace, no traffic!
Outdoor Run – A quick course to finish strong
Each segment is designed to be manageable for all ability levels. No specialized gear or prior triathlon experience required.

 

Race Distances

Triathlon and Triathlon Relay - 300 yd swim, 4 mi bike, 1.5 mi run

Youth Triathlon - 50 yd swim, 2 mi bike, 0.75 mi run

 

Why Race With Us?

  • Friendly, inclusive environment
  • Great way to try a new sport
  • Meet UO student-athletes and local community members
  • Boost confidence and fitness
  • Celebrate crossing a finish line—maybe your first!

Come Tri!
Bring your energy, your curiosity, and maybe a friend or two. Whether this is your first race ever or simply a fun way to stay active, we can’t wait to see you at the Rec Center starting line.

 

What Do I Need to Bring?

  • Clothes you can comfortably swim, bike, and run in
  • Goggles
  • Running shoes

Optional:

  • Swim cap
  • Cycling shoes (SPD cleat)

 

Schedule

Athlete Check-in will be the morning of the race

Waves will begin at 8:30AM and continue until noon

 

USAT Sanctioned Event

This race is sanctioned by USA Triathlon, which means all participants must have a current USAT membership. If you don’t already have one, you will be prompted to purchase it during registration process.

 

We Need Volunteers!

If you or a friend/family member are interested in volunteering, please fill out the form below. We greatly appreciate any help! https://forms.gle/DnvYCcLm2veieUiAA

name: Turtle Trot 5K, 10K, Fun Run and Brunch!
description:
Join us at Willow-Witt Ranch for The Crest’s 7th Annual Turtle Trot—a true trail race with heart (and breakfast)! Choose the 5K or 10K on rolling single-track through meadows, wetlands, oak woodlands, and native conifer forest, or bring the whole family for a joyful Fun Run for all ages. 

Starting at 4,500’ and climbing to nearly 5,000’, the courses feature elevation, varied terrain, and sweeping views of Mount Shasta, Pilot Rock, and Mt. Ashland. The 10K doubles the challenge with a second lap run in reverse, ensuring you experience the views from every angle.

After the finish, stay for what many say is the best part: a communal, made-from-scratch post-race breakfast shared around long tables, followed by a hands-on Western Pond Turtle learning session. Run hard, eat well, linger and learn. All proceeds support The CREST in our mission to connect people and nature.

name: USARA Adventure Race National Championships
description:
For more than 25 years, the annual USARA Adventure Race National Championships have seen some of the best teams from across the nation come together to compete in a non-stop, 30-hour adventure race. Many of these teams have to push the boundaries of human endurance and teamwork just to finish. Winning requires extreme willpower, mastery across disciplines, and sometime a little luck. 

When the race ends, teams come together for an evening meal. We announce the national champions, crown the winners of the national points series, and celebrate the amazing adventure racing community. 

The 2026 race is limited to teams of four in three divisions:  mixed gender, all-women, all-men.  There is not a separate masters division, though the top masters teams from across all divisions will be recognized.

Race check-in will be Thursday, October 22, 2026. The 30-hour race will start Friday morning, October 23, 2026, and end Saturday afternoon, October 24, 2026.

Priority registration opens January 1, 2026. Eligible teams will receive a link by email. Open registration begins February 1, 2026. You can find the most up-to-date information on the event at the USARA website.

REFUND POLICY:

The RunSignUp processing fee will be deducted from any and all refunds.  A racer who withdraws within one week of registering will receive a full refund, less processing fees.  A racer who withdraws more than one week after registering will receive a refund pursuant to the following scale: 


Before 6/1/26:  Entry fee less $50 and RSU processing fee
From 6/1/26 through 7/31/26:  Entry fee less $100 and RSU processing fee
From 8/1/26 through 8/31/25:  Entry fee less $200 and RSU processing fee 
From and after 9/1/26:  No refund


A racer can transfer their entry to another racer at no charge.  Contact nationals@usara.com to request a refund or transfer of entry.

name: 105th Statuto Race
description:
Running strong for 100 years!
The Statuto Race commemorates the creation of the first Italian Constitution (Statuto Albertino) and is a running tradition in San Francisco going back more than 100 years. Join us in 2025 for the 105th running of this iconic race!

Celebrate post-race with brunch!
Following the race, join us for brunch in the SFIAC Ballroom! Runners/walkers and guests welcome. $43.40 per adult. Kids 5-18 years are $22.20 per person (no charge for kids under age 5). You can purchase brunch tickets during registration or on the Store page in the menu bar above. NOTE: For 2026 the bottomless mimosa portion will not be offered, but a cash bar will be available.

First Responders Cup!
This is an opportunity to bring the Italian community together with the City and County of San Francisco's Public Safety & First Responder families while enjoying a little friendly competition. A trophy will be awarded to the first place First Responders finisher. First responders in agencies outside of SF are welcome to participate and should contact us at statutorace@sfiacfoundation.org to be added to the list of teams.

Awards!
• For the 8K run, trophies will be awarded to the first overall male runner, first overall female runner, the first overall SFIAC dues-paying club member, and first overall first responder.
• For the 8K run, medals will be awarded to the 1st, 2nd and 3rd place in the following age groups (male and female divisions): 19 and under, 20 - 29, 30 - 39, 40 - 49, 50 - 59, 60 - 64, 65 - 69, 70 - 74, 75-79, 80-84, 85-90.

name: 10th Antioch Rotary Club Bunny Hop 5K a.k.a. Antioch Rotary BunnyHop "X"
description:
2025 Results!

Please join the Antioch Rotary Bunny Hop 5K on April 4, 2026 (The day before Easter).

Here we go Hopping again!!!

It's Winter and we are less than 2 months away from Easter so the Easter Bunny is starting to train! We would like to invite participants to run like the Hare or pace yourself steady to victory like the Tortoise. Participants will get a Finisher's Medal and are guaranteed a Bunny Hop T-Shirt if you register before Saturday, March 14, 2026.  Registration will be open until Race Day. If you like to be part of community video please  email your picture to rdeloso@yahoo.com.  Like us and see up to date notices on Facebook @AntiochBunnyHop5K

Important Notes:

(1) Packet Pick up will be at Fleet Feet Sports in Brentwood on Friday, April 3rd from 3-7pm. There will also be same-day Packet Pick-up on Saturday, April 4th from 7:15 - 8:25 a.m. Beat the confusion & crowds on Saturday by passing by Fleet Feet Sports on Friday!

(2) This 5K Fun Run is a timed event. Accurate timing is provided by the E-Tag attached on the back of your Race Bib - your time starts when you cross the Start Line Sensor and you finish when you cross the Finish Line Sensor. Race Timing will be provided by Ford Timing. 

All Finishers will receive a BunnyHop 5K Medal. First Place Overall in Men's & Women's will receive a plaque, and a $100 Gift Card. 

Age Group Medals will go to the Top 3 in each of these Age Groups: 9 and under,
10-14, 15-19, 20-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59, 60-69, & 70 and up.

AWARDS CEREMONY will take place after the KIDS KWIK DASH & EASTER EGG HUNT approximately 11:10am

(3) The 5K Course is entirely within Corteva Wetlands Preserve and the surface is mostly gravel and grass paths. Because of this we do not recommend bringing strollers or wagons unless you are prepared to carry these over some barriers and over the uneven terrain.

(4) We love our furry friends too, but we do not advise that you bring dogs to this fun run for safety reasons.

(5) The Bunny Hop Start Line is about 3/4 mile from the Antioch Marina Festival/Parking Area - please plan on a 20–30-minute nature walk! Plan on arriving at the Antioch Marina by 8:00 a.m. - there will be plenty of Parking and Porta Potties. Start Time will be approximately 9:00am

(6) This Race will happen Rain or Shine! 

(7) For Runners of Antioch Unified School District - please arrive at the Antioch Marina by 7:30am to pick up your Race Bibs and GoodyBags - There will be a special area for AUSD-sponsored Runners.

(8) Because of the size of the Event, we will not have a "Bag Drop"

(9) The KIDS KWIK DASH will take place at the Antioch Marina Parking Lot at approximately 10:30am

(10) The Easter Egg Hunt will follow the Kids Kwik Dash

The Rotary Club of Antioch is a non-profit volunteer civic organization servicing the local community for over 75 years. Some of the projects include Girls Empowerment Project, Boys King Conference, Community Beautification, and Assisting Seniors in the Community with home repairs.  The Bunny Hop 5k proceeds will directly go toward scholarships at the local high schools. If you would like to learn more about the Rotary Club of Antioch please visit www.antiochrotary.net

name: 13th Annual Luc's Run
description:
Luc's Run is held annually each spring in historic Tuolumne, California and Virtually Anywhere in the World. Luc's Run is known as one of the premier races in the county.  We are looking at welcoming our local 10K, 2-mile, and Kids Run (ages 10 & under) back to Tuolumne, CA in 2023! And of course welcoming our supporters around the globe through our virtual run where hundreds of enthusiasts from around the world walk and run in support of Luc’s legacy on their own turf with a virtual 1/2 marathon, 10K, 2-mile, and Kids Run (ages 10 & under). Sign up for two events and save 5%, sign up for all three and save 15%! 

On January 28, 2013, Luc, a United States Air Force pilot was on a training mission over the Adriatic Sea off the coast of Italy. During the sortie, Luc was forced to eject from his F-16 and did not survive the ejection.  Luc is survived by family and friends who continue his Legacy through the Major Lucas Gruenther Legacy Foundation.

Major Lucas Gruenther was an incredible human being.  He was an outstanding F-16 fighter pilot, community role model, and a true humanitarian.  He lived his life to the fullest and never took a single day for granted.  Luc is remembered for the way he treated people with wisdom and kindness and was a genuine human being who made a tremendous positive impact.

All proceeds from this race go to the Major Lucas Gruenther Legacy Foundation, an IRS-approved 501(c)(3) non-profit organization.  The purpose of the Major Lucas Gruenther Legacy Foundation is to bestow scholarships to Americans for the advancement of educational goals and self development.

name: 16th Annual BEACHFRONT RUN
description:
Hello Runners & Walkers!

We’re excited to invite you to City Impact's 16th Annual Beachfront Run on Saturday, May 30, 2026, at the beautiful Ventura Promenade.

Enjoy a race course with stunning views of Ventura’s coastline while participating in one of our exciting race options: Half Marathon, 10K, 5K, or the Kids 1K Run. The event will also feature a variety of vendors, lively music, and a festive awards ceremony.

Each participant will receive a custom event shirt and a finisher’s medal. Please note that if you register after March 15th, 2026, we cannot guarantee your preferred shirt size.

Awards will be given to the top 3 finishers in each 10-year age category (10-19, 20-29, etc.), so everyone has a chance to shine!  Whether you’re racing or cheering, this is a perfect event for friends, family, and colleagues to come together and enjoy the day.

All proceeds from the event will benefit City Impact’s programs supporting at-promise youth and families. Your participation makes a difference, and we thank you for your support!        


If you should have any questions, please email info@cityimpact.com or call 805.983.3636 x105.    

Much appreciation,


Vickie Saipale
Development/Event Manager

name: 16th Annual Mardi Gras Madness 5K/10K!
description:
About the Event

Join us on Sunday, March 1, 2026, as the Junior Chamber International of Santa Clarita (JCI) and the Santa Clarita Track Club proudly present the 16th Annual Mardi Gras Madness 5K/10K and Mini Madness 1K — benefiting JCI Santa Clarita and Students Off And Running (SOAR).

SOAR provides local youth ages 14–18 with a fully supported Los Angeles Marathon training experience — completely free for participants and their families — and is an Official Featured Charity of the 2026 Los Angeles Marathon.

What to Expect

Mardi Gras Madness is Santa Clarita’s premier family-friendly run/walk event, offering fun and fitness for all ages! Participants will enjoy a scenic USATF-certified 5K/10K course, chip timing, custom finisher medals, marathon-quality tech shirts, and a vibrant Health & Fitness Expo.

The festivities continue with a beer garden, great food, costume contest, games and giveaways, silent auction, celebrity hosts, and live entertainment. Whether you’re a seasoned runner, a stroller-pusher, or bringing your furry friend, Mardi Gras Madness welcomes everyone!

 
🏃‍♀️ COURSE INFORMATION
The MGM course is a USATF-certified, rolling 5K/10K circuit featuring scenic paseos, bridge overpasses, and sections along the beautiful South Fork River Trail.

Note: The 10K route includes a dirt equestrian trail from Mile 3.25 to Mile 4.85.
 
🎟 EARLY PACKET PICKUP
Skip the lines and pick up your race materials early!

📍 Saturday, February 28 | 10:00 AM – 5:00 PM
Location: Canyon Club Courtyard (rear entrance near H&M), Valencia Town Center

Please bring a valid ID to receive your 2026 - 8 One 8 Beer Garden wristband. No exceptions.

Due to overwhelming demand, onsite registration cannot be guaranteed this year.
 
🕗 RACE DAY SCHEDULE

6:30 – 8:00 AM - Check-In and Pre-Registration
7:25 AM - 1K Warm-Up
7:30 AM - 1K Start
7:55 AM - 5K/10K Warm-Up
8:00 AM - 5K/10K Start
9:30 AM - Awards Ceremony & Prize Drawings
 
🏅 AWARDS
Top 3 Overall Men & Women (5K & 10K)
Top 3 per Age Group:

  • 10 & Under
  • 11–14
  • 15–18
  • 19–29
  • 30–39
  • 40–49
  • 50–59
  • 60+
  • Top 3 Team Finishes
  • All 5K/10K finishers receive a custom medal, t-shirt, and goodie bag!

 
📍 EVENT DETAILS
Date: Sunday, March 1, 2026
Time: 7:00 AM – 12:00 PM
Location: Valencia Town Center, Valencia, CA 91355

Join us on Sunday, March 1, 2026, as the Junior Chamber International of Santa Clarita (JCI) and the Santa Clarita Track Club proudly present the 16th Annual Mardi Gras Madness 5K/10K and Mini Madness 1K — benefiting JCI Santa Clarita and Students Off And Running (SOAR).

SOAR provides local youth ages 14–18 with a fully supported Los Angeles Marathon training experience — completely free for participants and their families — and is an Official Featured Charity of the 2026 Los Angeles Marathon.

What to Expect

Mardi Gras Madness is Santa Clarita’s premier family-friendly run/walk event, offering fun and fitness for all ages! Participants will enjoy a scenic USATF-certified 5K/10K course, chip timing, custom finisher medals, marathon-quality tech shirts, and a vibrant Health & Fitness Expo.

The festivities continue with a beer garden, great food, costume contest, games and giveaways, silent auction, celebrity hosts, and live entertainment. Whether you’re a seasoned runner, a stroller-pusher, or bringing your furry friend, Mardi Gras Madness welcomes everyone!

 
🏃‍♀️ COURSE INFORMATION
The MGM course is a USATF-certified, rolling 5K/10K circuit featuring scenic paseos, bridge overpasses, and sections along the beautiful South Fork River Trail.

Note: The 10K route includes a dirt equestrian trail from Mile 3.25 to Mile 4.85.
 
🎟 EARLY PACKET PICKUP
Skip the lines and pick up your race materials early!

📍 Saturday, February 28 | 10:00 AM – 5:00 PM
Location: Canyon Club Courtyard (rear entrance near H&M), Valencia Town Center

Please bring a valid ID to receive your 2026 - 8 One 8 Beer Garden wristband. No exceptions.

Due to overwhelming demand, onsite registration cannot be guaranteed this year.
 
🕗 RACE DAY SCHEDULE

6:30 – 8:00 AM - Check-In and Pre-Registration
7:25 AM - 1K Warm-Up
7:30 AM - 1K Start
7:55 AM - 5K/10K Warm-Up
8:00 AM - 5K/10K Start
9:30 AM - Awards Ceremony & Prize Drawings
 
🏅 AWARDS
Top 3 Overall Men & Women (5K & 10K)
Top 3 per Age Group:

  • 10 & Under
  • 11–14
  • 15–18
  • 19–29
  • 30–39
  • 40–49
  • 50–59
  • 60+
  • Top 3 Team Finishes
  • All 5K/10K finishers receive a custom medal, t-shirt, and goodie bag!

 
📍 EVENT DETAILS
Date: Sunday, March 1, 2026
Time: 7:00 AM – 12:00 PM
Location: Valencia Town Center, Valencia, CA 91355

name: 16th Annual Reindeer Run/Walk
description:
Save the Date: the 16th Annual Reindeer Run will be here December 5th!

Come one, come all! There is something for everyone at the Reindeer Run. We welcome runners and walkers of every level to American Canyon on December 5th, beginning with pre-race festivities at 8am, and a staggered race start (10K at 9am, 5K at 9:05am for runners and 9:10am for walkers).  

 

This is a fun event for the whole family: kids 6-17 are $30 and youth 5 and under are just $5 and include a finisher's medal and souvenir antlers! Early bird registration begins June 1st, so be ready to register to join in the fun!

 

*This event is contingent upon the requirements of Napa County Health Guidelines. If deemed necessary by the county, all in-person registrations will be switched to a virtual race. 


*Registration fees are non-refundable. Unused race fees are considered a donation to ACParks.

 

Need a race before the Reindeer Run? Be sure to check out these fantastic races on Thanksgiving Morning, November 26th:

Solano Turkey Trot, by Fleet Feet Vacaville

Napa Valley Turkey Chase, by Athletic Feat

description:

name: 2026 Avenue of the Giants Marathon
description:
The race is currently sold out and we are accepting registrations for the waitlist only. Please consider our sister race this fall, the Humboldt Redwoods Marathon. It uses the same course as the Avenue of the Giants Marathon and is produced by the same running club.

The Avenue of the Giants is one of the most beautiful races in the world!  It runs through old growth redwoods and follows a natural creek in the middle of a state park.  Staged on "The Avenue of the Giants" in Humboldt Redwoods State Park, located in rural Northern California. Course is on a paved road that winds gently up hill but is mostly a flat, fast destination race.  With little to distract you, the tall trees inspire the athlete in each of us to be strong.  The course is certified and the marathon is a Boston Qualifying event.

name: 2026 Cal Tri Castaic Lake - 6.20.26
description:
2026 Cal Tri Castaic Lake - 6.20.25

18 EVENT OPTIONS. 6 Olympic distance events (Triathlon, RunBikeRun, SwimBike, SwimRun, 1640 Yard Swim & 10K Run), 6 Sprint distance events (Triathlon, RunBikeRun, SwimBike, SwimRun, 400 yard Swim & 5K Run) and 6 Youth Sprint distance events (Triathlon, RunBikeRun, SwimBike, SwimRun, 400 yard Swim & 5K Run). Triathlon = swim + bike + run. Typically, the swim and run distances are standard but the bike distance varies from race to race. Check out the course maps for more detailed information.

CASTAIC LAKE. 
The 35th annual Castaic Lake Triathlon takes place at scenic Castaic Lake just 20 miles north of Los Angeles. The Castaic Lake Recreation Area, located just north of Santa Clarita, is an 11,200-acre multi-use facility with two lakes, boating, world class fishing, hiking, walking, horseback riding, wake boarding, jet-skiing, camping, picnicking, kayaking, and sailing.  August is a great time to enjoy the water in the high 60s, and a staging area aptly named Paradise Cove. "Tri-cation" Friday night camping available through Castaic Lake.


THE COURSE. 
The swim course is a modified V shape in Paradise Cove at Castaic Lake, with 8 lifeguards in the water on paddleboards.  The bike course then goes out on back roads to limit your interaction with cars.  The bike course does include some U-turns on back roads to allow this, so athletes should slow down at the turn around points.  The run is primarily on the rolling trails overlooking Castaic Lake. 

WHO WE SUPPORT
All proceeds will benefit the Canyon High School Cross Country and Track Teams (we've been doing this for 33 years to support our programs).  

This is a great triathlon for new triathletes.  For years our coaches and athletes have encouraged new triathletes (young and old), and created a welcoming atmosphere of support.  We offer an enjoyable experience for triathletes of all experience levels.  


AIR TEMPERATURE (AVG).
Mid June temperatures are often cooler in the morning, with early morning fog burning off to reach the mid 80s.  Our event will possibly be around 60 degrees.

WATER TEMPERATURE (AVG). 

Water temps in June typically range in the mid to high 60s.  Email updates will be sent out closer to the race with updates. Use the 20% CALTRI2025 discount code at blueseventy. Note: Fusion wetsuits not eligible for discount.

name: 2026 Cayucos Turkey Trot
description:
Thanksgiving Day Family 5k Fun Run / Walk

Check-in and bib pick-up will start Wednesday, November 25th at the Cayucos Pier from 2-4pm.  Each registered participant will have an assigned bib number and Thanksgiving-themed running socks, while supplies last.

On race day, check-in will begin at 7:15am.  We are set to start at 8:30am so be sure to give yourself enough time.  Dogs, strollers, and kiddos on scooters are all welcome.  

All proceeds will equally benefit Cayucos Elementary School and the California Association of Highway Patrolman Widows & Orphans' Trust Fund.

Thank you for your incredible support, and we can’t wait to see on race day!

name: 2026 CVC San Diego Triathlon and San Diego Tri Series 5K
description:
Mark your calendars for event #2 of the San Diego Triathlon Series & the Triple Crown of Triathlon
📅 Sunday, August 16, 2026
📍 Chula Vista, CA – San Diego Bayfront

This Year, We are Back to the Fantastic ONE PARK Venue! Start / Transition/ Finish line/ and Beer Garden all in one place! See the beutiful new landscape and the Gaylord Hotel

Dive into one of San Diego’s most exciting and scenic multisport races of the summer! The CVC San Diego Triathlon & 5K is Event #2 in the prestigious San Diego Triathlon Series and part of the coveted Triple Crown of Triathlon. Whether you're a first-timer or a seasoned competitor, there’s a race here for everyone. 🌊☀️

Set against the calm, warm waters of San Diego Bay, this athlete-friendly race offers flat, fast courses, great for achieving your personal best—and even better for enjoying the beautiful coastal views while you’re at it. After your race, celebrate with friends and family in our on-the-water 🍺Seek Beer Co. - Beer & 🍸Margarita Garden and soak in those post-race vibes!

Race Options
INTERNATIONAL TRIATHLON
1,000 M swim - 38 K (23.3 mi) bike - 10K (6.2 mi) run 
Ages 16 & over

SPRINT TRIATHLON
500 M swim – 19K (11.6 mi) bike – 5K (3.1 mi) run 
Ages 13 & over

SPRINT RELAY
500 M swim - 19K (11.6 mi) bike - 5k run 
Ages 13 & over
SPRINT DUATHLON
1 mile run - 19K (11.6 mi) bike - 5k run 
Ages 13 & over

SPRINT AQUABIKE
500 M swim - 19K (11.6 mi) bike
Ages 13 & over

MINI TRIATHLON
200 M swim – 9K (5.8 mi) bike – 2.4K (1.5 mi) run
Ages 11 & over

ITSY BITSY TRIATHLON
100 M swim – 4K (2.3 mi) bike – 1.2K (.75 mi) run
Kids 7-10

SD Tri Series - Chula Vista 5K (3.1 mi) run

name: 2026 Fear the Spear 5K
description: The Mark Keppel Alliance is a non-profit organization that advocates for Mark Keppel High School and fundraises in order to enhance the students’ education and engagement. Their mission is to raise money to support academics and sports programs that the school district cannot fund. Anyone who wants to do a 5 kilometer run/walk, support the students, and feel the community’s spirit surrounding such an event can do so at the Fear the Spear 5k. All proceeds generated from the run will benefit academics, sports, and the clubs that students participate in at Mark Keppel.  We encourage everyone to be a part of the 5k experience and sign up!

name: 2026 Foothills Strong Run
description:
Join us this Memorial Day for the Foothills Strong Run(formerly Fiesta Days Run), a community-powered event hosted by the YMCA of the Foothills on Monday, May 25, 2026. This meaningful day of movement and remembrance brings neighbors, families, and fitness enthusiasts together to honor resilience while supporting local families recovering from the Eaton Fire.

Participants of all ages and abilities can take part in one of four unique events: the Foothills Fastest 1 Mile, Dog/Human 1 Mile, 5K Walk/Run, and the Family 1 Mile Fun Run. Whether you’re racing for a personal best, walking with friends, or running alongside your four-legged companion, there’s a place for everyone at the starting line.

Presented by USC Verdugo Hills Hospital in partnership with the City of La Cañada Flintridge, this event goes beyond the finish line. Funds raised will provide YMCA memberships through 2026 for families impacted by the Eaton Fire — ensuring access to wellness programs, youth activities, supportive services, and a strong sense of community connection.

Run, walk, and rally together — because our community is strongest when we move forward together. 

Event happens Rain or Shine.  No Refunds.

name: 2026 Granfondo San Diego
description:
San Diego's Favorite Cycling Event! - Voted Best GranFondo in America & Top 10 Best Century Ride in the USA

Welcome to the ultimate celebration of cycling, flavor, and the breathtaking San Diego waterfront! Get ready to embark on an unforgettable journey at the Southern California-Italian fusion extravaganza – our Gran Fondo awaits!
More Than a Century Ride

🚴 Routes: Choose Your Path, Seize Your Glory! Whether you're a seasoned cyclist or a weekend warrior, our event caters to all levels. Pick your challenge from our diverse route options: 101, 60, or 34 miles. As you pedal through the stunning landscapes, know that every mile brings you closer to the full GranFondo experience!

🏅 Swag: Earn Your Medal, Revel in Victory! Cross the finish line triumphantly, and the cheers of the crowd will resonate with your achievement. Your reward? A well-deserved medal, the tangible proof of your cycling prowess. But the celebration doesn't stop there – brace yourself for the Fantastic Finish extravaganza!

🎉 Fantastic Finish Celebration – Unleash the Festivities! Immerse yourself in the post-ride revelry at our Fantastic Finish Celebration! Live music will set the stage for your triumph, and the bike valet ensures your trusty steed is taken care of. Delight your taste buds at the Italian Pasta Fest and quench your thirst at the Seek Beer Co. - Beer Garden – the perfect way to relish your victory!

🌇 SoCal Meets Italy – A Fusion of Culture and Cycling! Picture this: the vibrant energy of Southern California seamlessly blending with the charm of Italy against the backdrop of San Diego's picturesque waterfront. It's a two-day festival that goes beyond cycling – it's an immersion into a world where passion for food, fitness, and community collide.

🏞️ Downtown San Diego – The Perfect Host! Our event unfolds in the heart of beautiful Downtown San Diego. The cityscape adds an urban flair to your cycling adventure, making every turn and twist of the route an exploration of San Diego's charm.

🚵‍♂️ Gran Fondo Highlights: Challenging Routes & Exciting Competitions! Feel the rush as you tackle challenging and inspiring routes that cater to the cyclist in you. Engage in the thrill of timed King and Queen of the Mountain competitions – an opportunity to showcase your climbing prowess. The Bike & Fitness Expo awaits, where you can explore the latest trends and innovations in the cycling world.

🍝 Italian Feast – Savor the Flavorful Finale! Cap off your cycling odyssey with an Italian Feast at the Finish. Indulge in delectable dishes that celebrate the essence of Italy, bringing a delicious conclusion to your GranFondo adventure.
 Presenting Sponsor

🚀 Join Us for an Epic Experience! Are you ready to be part of a cycling spectacle like no other? Embrace the challenge, savor the flavor, and revel in the community spirit at our GranFondo. Secure your spot today and gear up for a weekend of cycling, festivities, and memories that will last a lifetime! 🚴🍝🎉

description:
THE POLAR PLUNGE
Ready to brave the waters for Special Olympics Northern California? Join the Greater Sacramento Area Polar Plunge & Runs, a fun dip, skip or jump into the Bay for a great cause!  Don’t want to get wet? Register as a chicken and you'll be excused from plunging but still qualify for the incentive rewards and other festivities. 
 
THE RUN/WALK
In conjunction with the Polar Plunge, running enthusiasts can enjoy a scenic 5K timed trail run before the Plunge. Awards presented to the top 3 runners in each age category.  Those not ready for a 5K can participate in the One Mile Fun Run/Walk

name: 2026 Humboldt Redwoods Marathon, Half Marathon, 5K
description:
We'll forgive you if you have trouble concentrating on the road ahead of you while running The Humboldt Redwoods Marathon, half or 5K. After all, you'll probably be looking up at the old-growth redwood trees which tower over the course! This race is in Humboldt Redwoods State Park and the Half Marathon follows the second half of the iconic Avenue of the Giants Marathon course.

All courses are USATF Certified. The Marathon is a Boston qualifier. The race starts and finishes at the Dyerville Bridge.
