name: Animal Tracking workshop
description:
ANIMAL TRACKING WORKSHOP AND HIKE 

Saturday, March 7, 7 AM

Uncover the hidden world of wildlife through the art and science of tracking in Anza-Borrego Desert State Park. Learn how to identify, interpret, and appreciate the signs animals leave behind—and how tracking connects us to conservation and community science. This full day event includes a stop at the visitor center, and guided hike.

name: Anime Fan and Fitness Festival
description:
Initial Mile proudly presents to you Anime Fan and Fitness Festival, the festival where anime and fitness collide.

Join us for our second annual Anime Fan and Fitness Festival in Gilroy, CA on Saturday, September 19, 2026 where we will be brining back our Anime Fan and Fitness Festival 5k Run and Walk and will be adding our newest events the Anime Fan and Fitness Festival 10k run and the Little Ninja Dash!

Whether you’re a seasoned runner, a casual jogger, a dedicated fitness enthusiast, a creative cosplayer, or a passionate anime fan, the Anime Fan and Fitness Festival was made just for you. All experience levels are encouraged so gather your friends, family, lace up your shoes, and step into a world where miles meet anime as we bring anime energy to every stride. Cosplay is highly encouraged, so suit up as your favorite character and make this run a true celebration of anime culture! 

After crossing the finish line, stick around at victory village to celebrate, support small businesses, enjoy some local bites, cheer on our local performers and participate in our Fandom Anime Quest where you'll have the opportunity to complete a series of Fandom challenges and earn our Initial Mile Warrior Badge.

10k Run Registration Release Fees:

January - June: $50

July: $60

August - Race Day: $70

5k Run Registration Release Fees:

January - June: $40

July: $50

August - Race Day: $60

Little Ninja Dash Fees:

Registration is FREE but must register your little ninja by July 31 to receive finisher ribbon.

Each Registration Comes With:

  • Official race timing results from SVE Timing.
  • Official race bib.
  • Finisher wooden medal.
  • Option to purchase a finisher t-shirt for additional fee.

name: Anime Fan and Fitness Festival
description:
Initial Mile proudly presents to you Anime Fan and Fitness Festival, the festival where anime and fitness collide.

Join us for our second annual Anime Fan and Fitness Festival in Gilroy, CA on Saturday, September 19, 2026 where we will be brining back our Anime Fan and Fitness Festival 5k Run and Walk and will be adding our newest events the Anime Fan and Fitness Festival 10k run and the Little Ninja Dash!

Whether you’re a seasoned runner, a casual jogger, a dedicated fitness enthusiast, a creative cosplayer, or a passionate anime fan, the Anime Fan and Fitness Festival was made just for you. All experience levels are encouraged so gather your friends, family, lace up your shoes, and step into a world where miles meet anime as we bring anime energy to every stride. Cosplay is highly encouraged, so suit up as your favorite character and make this run a true celebration of anime culture! 

After crossing the finish line, stick around at victory village to celebrate, support small businesses, enjoy some local bites, cheer on our local performers and participate in our Fandom Anime Quest where you'll have the opportunity to complete a series of Fandom challenges and earn our Initial Mile Warrior Badge.

10k Run Registration Release Fees:

January - June: $50

July: $60

August - Race Day: $70

5k Run Registration Release Fees:

January - June: $40

July: $50

August - Race Day: $60

Little Ninja Dash Fees:

Registration is FREE but must register your little ninja by July 31 to receive finisher ribbon.

Each Registration Comes With:

  • Official race timing results from SVE Timing.
  • Official race bib.
  • Finisher wooden medal.
  • Option to purchase a finisher t-shirt for additional fee.

name: Apple City 5k
description:
The inaugural Apple City 5k!

Come run fun easy trails and be a part of the Watsonville community!

Going back to the roots of farming in Watsonville, the Apple City 5k at Pinto Lake County Park is a dedication to agricultural history and life of the Pajaro Valley. 

Participants will experience the scenic meadows and trails of the county park, with gentle trails circling the whole park. 

The kids 1k will go around the soccer fields near the starting/finish line. 

This race is hosted by the Santa Cruz Track Club Fall Race series with 50% of funds going to the Pajaro Valley Education Foundation to support the students of the Pajaro Valley.

name: Apricot Lane Farms Earth Day 5K Fun Run! (Or Walk!)
description:
Join us for a scenic 5K trail run (or walk!) through orchards, rolling hills, and open vistas on our 234-acre regenerative farm in Moorpark. This is an off-road race designed to get you moving in connection with nature while supporting a meaningful cause! Your participation helps fund school bus transportation for Farm Field Trips, making it possible for more local students to access hands-on learning on the farm.

Race Overview

  • 3.1 mile run or walk
  • Scenic course on dirt roads, orchards, and hills
  • Fresh air, farm beauty, and a fun community atmosphere
  • This is a relaxed, welcoming race focused on movement, nature, and local community.
  • All ages welcome

Parking (Included in Race Fee)
Your $150 registration includes parking at Apricot Lane Farms. Please be sure to reserve your parking pass when registering. 

  • All vehicles with a parking pass will park at Apricot Lane Farms.
  • The parking lot opens at 8am. Cars may enter between 8am and 9am. Please arrive during this window of time.
  • For the safety of our runners and guests, the Farm gates will close at 9am.
  • Detailed driving and parking instructions will be emailed a few days before the event.
  • Important: Parking passes are issued per transaction, not per runner. If multiple runners are arriving in the same car, please register them together in one transaction. Carpooling is encouraged! Parking is limited, but runners are not!
  • Important: Please take note that cars parked on the roads immediately outside of our gates may be towed. This is out of our control and we would hate to see it happen!
  • Are guests who aren't coming to run but want to watch, welcome? Yes! Please bring along your cheering squad! Just remember, all vehicles entering the Farm need a parking pass.

Food & Community Gathering
Join us in the garden for food and drinks available for purchase. Plan for a picnic and community gathering with fellow runners, walkers and their cheering squads!
The event will be open from 8:00am until 12:00pm.

Race Day Schedule

  • 8:00-9:00am Parking lot open: Please arrive within this window!
  • 9:00am Farm gates close, for the safety of runners and guests. Latecomers will not be admitted, unfortunately.
  • 8:00-10:00am Race registration and t-shirt distribution.
  • 10:00am Race starts!
  • 8:00am-12:00pm Join us at the Garden Barn to celebrate Earth Day with drinks, food and good vibes! You are also welcome to BYO picnic!

Registration Includes

  • Race entry
  • Support for ALF's Farm Field Trip School Bus Fund
  • A meaningful contribution to local student field trips
  • A run shirt
  • A medal

Why We Run
Many local schools struggle to cover transportation costs for field trips. This event helps fund school bus transportation, giving more students access to outdoor, nature-based learning. Through hands-on farm experiences, students learn what it takes to grow healthy food and develop a deeper appreciation for their local ecosystem. All proceeds from the race will go towards our School Bus Fund!

Sign Up Soon
Space is limited, and this event is expected to fill quickly. We look forward to welcoming you to the Farm for a beautiful morning of movement, community, and purpose!

Important: 
Parking passes are issued per transaction, not per runner. If multiple runners are arriving in the same car, please register them together in one transaction. Please carpool! The more the merrier!

name: Arbor Day Run
description: Tree Fresno presents The Arbor Day Run/Walk in honor of their 40th Anniversary. Starting at the beautiful Clovis Botanical Gardens, runners and walker alike will head out on the Dry Creek Trail in support of transforming the San Joaquin Valley with trees, greenways and beautiful landscapes. After the run or walk, visit the gardens or participate in a live tree planting right there on the run course! Help us celebrate over 55,000 trees planted, and growing.

name: ARMC 5K
description:
Go to https://register.chronotrack.com/r/72258 to register.

 

The Arrowhead Regional Medical Center (ARMC) Foundation is offering this 5K Walk/Run event FREE of charge! Come out and enjoy a healthy day with the community. The ARMC 5K Walk/Run aims to encourage exercise while also promoting the services that San Bernardino County and Arrowhead Regional Medical Center offer to the community.

Packet Pickup

Join us the day before the race on Friday, March 24 and beat the crowds and show up to pick up your bib from 4 p.m. to 8 p.m. at the Frank A. Gonzales Center at 670 Colton Avenue in Colton, CA 92324. Packets can also be picked up the day of the race while supplies last.

The first 700 people to pick up their bib will have their choice of an event shirt. This is first come, first served with no guarantee that we will have your size if you show up late or on race day. After the shirts are taken, we have some stylish drawstring bags (you can choose one of these instead of a shirt if you like).

Registration

Opens at 7 a.m. on race day. The ARMC 5K Starts at 8:30 a.m. The start line will close, and you will not be able to start the Walk/Run if you arrive on site later than 8:15 a.m.

Event Features

There will be many event booths and light refreshments at the event. This is a rain or shine event. 

Course Aid

There will be one water/Gatorade station along the course.

Parking

There is free parking available on the grounds of ARMC and 5K participants may park in any designated slot which is not already clearly marked and reserved for disabled parking or on-duty hospital staff. Most parking lots are unfenced (please note, employee parking lots are fenced with badge in/out access gates). If the entrance gate to a fenced lot is locked in the open position, it is available for general parking that day. If the entrance gate is closed, it is reserved for on-duty hospital staff – please do not attempt to park in such lots.

Pets

Although walking with your dog elsewhere is a terrific idea, the ARMC 5K is definitely NOT a sensible place to bring your pet. Please do not bring your dogs and do not attempt to negotiate the 5K with your pet. We appreciate your consideration in this regard.

This is a rain or shine event.

name: Artesa Wine Run 5k
description:
Like Running or Walking?  Love Wine?  This race is for you! 

Join us on Sunday, March 8, 2026 with start times at 8:30am or 10:30am (you will select your start time during registration) for an exciting annual event that features Artesa Vineyards Winery. Escape to Artesa Winery, just an hour from San Francisco, and enjoy the finest high-end wines, explore Spanish-inspired architecture, and savor tapas that perfectly complement our exceptional selection. Whether you are looking to run, walk or just enjoy the wonderful wine and camaraderie this race is a sure thing for a great time and an incredible experience!  This race is timed and scored by J3 Timing.  Results will be posted at www.J3Timing.com. 

Registration Includes:

  • T-shirt:  Super Soft Ring Spun Cotton t-shirt included! 
  • Wine Glass: Shatterproof, Collapsible, and Portable!
  • Finisher Medal: Doubles as a Wine Stopper!
  • Race Bib: Chip timed 5k run/walk
  • Results Posted Online
  • ...and of course, a pour of wine!*

name: Ascot Hills Challenge 5K
description:
Event proceeds benefit Wilson High School Fire and Police Magnet Cadet Program and Ascot Hills Park.  

​The Los Angeles Unified School District (LAUSD) and The Los Angeles Fire Department (LAFD) have partnered in bringing the very first LAFD fire academy magnet school program to Woodrow Wilson High School in El Sereno, CA, joining the existing LAPD student police cadet program.

 
Join us on the best 3.1 mile trail course in East Los Angeles! 

Our 5K course will challenge all levels of runners, walkers and hikers.  The race is chip-timed for those seeking friendly competition and/or a chance to win a commemorative LAFD challenge coin.

​If you enjoy trail running, walking or hiking, you'll be certain to enjoy this event with spectacular views of Los Angeles, Dodger Stadium and the Hollywood sign, all visible from within the park.

name: Aut2Run for Autism (15K, 5K, 10K, Fun-K, 1 Mile & Virtual Race)
description:
We are excited to welcome you back to an in-person Aut2Run at California State University Channel Islands on Sunday, April 26th, 2026! For those of you who can't experience Aut2Run in-person, but would still like to support Autism Society Ventura County, we will be offering a virtual option for you to participate in. This year is extra special to us as we celebrate Aut2Run's 14th anniversary!

100% of the proceeds from Aut2Run go directly towards fulfilling Autism Society Ventura County's (ASVC) mission to create connections, empowering all with Autism to live fully. ASVC works to promote lifelong access and opportunity for all individuals within the autism spectrum and their families to be fully included members of the community. They achieve this through education, advocacy, a variety of programs, increasing public awareness, and collaboration with other agencies.

ASVC programs are primarily for individuals, families and caregivers who have people in their lives with autism of all ages. We also collaborate with service providers, agency staff, educators and teachers, and professionals who are interested in furthering the mission of ASVC. Their programs are open to any individual, family, or community member impacted by autism. Our Board consists of all dedicated volunteers.

In-Person Race Information: 

10K (1/2 Road & 1/2 Trail) Run - 7:00am Please note, we have a strict course time limit for the 10K. All participants must be able to complete the 10K in 75 minutes (that is a 12 minute per mile pace).  If you do not reach the University Park Entrance (heading back to the South Quad after the trail loop) in 54 minutes, you will be transported to where the 5K joins in at Channel Islands Dr and will receive a DNF (Did Not Finish).
5K Run/Walk - 8:45am
1 Mile Run/Walk - 10:15am
Fun-K - 10:45am This event is for children under age 12 and for adults with special needs and their caregivers. Limited to 300 participants.
15K Hero Run - Participants run both the 10K and 5K events separately. The times from the two races will be combined to give you your 15K results. 

Virtual Race Information & Instructions:
Please choose a local safe route (since this event is virtual you can run​ or walk anywhere you like, we recommend a place that is safe with limited interruptions).
Please follow all local laws, stop at all lights, stop signs and be careful when you cross at any cross walk. ​Please be aware of your surroundings and be cautious as you will not be running or walking on a closed course. We cannot emphasize this enough. 
Maintain, at an absolute minimum, 6ft between you and anyone else not in your household.

Your race packet will be mailed to you the week of the race. 

Tracking your Virtual Race Distance:

Please use a GPS watch or phone with a GPS app (Strava or RunKeeper or two good ones) to track your time and distance. Upon completion you will then add your distance and time onto https://www.aut2run.org/Race/Results/2323#resultSetId-289928;perpage:100 anytime between April 18th and May 1st. Please note, submissions are based on the honor system and there are not awards for the virtual run. 

Packet Pick Up Information:

We highly recommend that all race participants pick up their packets on Saturday!!

Saturday Packet Pickup will help you avoid VERY long lines and reduce anxiety on race morning. The race packet consists of your required race bib, t-shirt, and goodie bag. 

  • Saturday, April 25th 9:00am - 1:00pm at California State University Channel Islands (South Quad)
  • Sunday, April 26th 6:00am - 10:45am at  California State University Channel Islands (South Quad)
    • Please arrive at least 30 minutes prior to your event start time. Expect lines at race morning packet pick up.

For more info on the Aut2Run event go to http://www.aut2run.org/          
For more info on ASVC go to http://www.autismventura.org/

name: Autism on the Run
description:
We are excited to announce Autism on the Run. On April 11th, 2026 at the Park at Riverwalk in Bakersfield, California.  We will have a 10k, 5k, 2k, and family walk.

 

Pricing is $45 a person for 10k, 5k, 2k and includes a shirt and medal

Pricing for Family is $160 and includes 5 medals and 1 swag bag, (no shirts are included with this discount) 

 

April is Autism Awareness Month. Autism refers to a broad range of conditions characterized by challenges with social skills, repetitive behaviors, speech, and nonverbal communication.

 

This event benefits H.E.A.R.T.S. Connection Family Empowerment Center whose mission is to enhance the quality of life for people with special needs through a family-directed resource center that symbolizes professionalism, dignity, compassion, and respect.   For more information contact us at 661-328-9055.  This event will feature vendors, family fun, and raffles.

name: Avalon Benefit 50 Mile/50K Run
description: The Avalon Benefit 50 Mile/50K Run is the oldest Ultra Trail Run in California with the 50 Mile run entering its 44th year.   The 50K joined the party seven years ago and instantly became a California classic in trail running traversing all of the same trails that the older run uses.   Running the Avalon Benefit 50Mile/50K provides you a first rate, up-close and personal experience of one of California's natural jewels in trail running across Catalina Island.   The run begins and ends in Avalon and in between you simply have to run the entire length of the island - and back!  In between you will experience beautiful vistas, tremendous views of the Pacific Ocean, see a bison or two and experience some of the sports great volunteers and aid stations.

name: Awesome 80's Run
description:
Get ready to transport back to the 80s with our Awesome 80s 5K and 10K run! Join fellow enthusiasts dressed in retro gear as classic 80s hits fill the air. Whether you're a seasoned runner or just starting out, our routes cater to all fitness levels.

Cross the finish line to receive your gnarly medal, then stick around for a post-race party blasting classic 80s tunes. Dust off those leg warmers and join us for an unforgettable journey through the sights and sounds of the 80s – it's going to be totally epic!

name: Aztlan XC Classic
description:
Aztlan XC Classic was established in 1976. It has been long due and now we welcome you back. This time, those who have competed at this event are now well into their 50s. You are now coaches, mentors, teachers, parents and even grandparents. Bring your family, team or if you're still challenging yourself then sign up and let’s celebrate our success.

This event exclusively benefits Aztlan Athletics Foundation (AAF). For details about the subsidized running camps, scholarships, and complimentary registrations visit AztlanAthleticsFoundation.org.

This event exclusively benefits Aztlan Athletics Foundation (AAF). For details about the subsidized running camps, scholarships, and complimentary registrations visit AztlanAthleticsFoundation.org.

name: Badwater 267 VR
description:
BADWATER: It’s a frame of mind, a global family of horizon-chasers, and a statement to the world about priorities and preconceived notions of what is possible. Badwater is a way of life! Are you ready to kick off the New Year with an authentic, original Badwater experience?

AdventureCORPS® – the organizers of the iconic worldwide series of Badwater® races – are pleased to offer the BADWATER 267 VR in which competitors virtually and sequentially traverse the routes of all three Badwater® races – the 51-mile Badwater Cape Fear, the 81-mile Badwater Salton Sea, and the 135-mile Badwater 135 – for a total of 267 miles, or 430km. These three events comprise the legendary Badwater Ultra Cup - and Badwater 267 VR! Start off the New Year with this new challenge and lay the ultimate foundation for your best year yet!

During this challenge, you will complete 267 miles (430km) during the month of January. You have 31 days to complete 267 miles and you can do them anywhere you want, including indoors. There is also a multi-sport division for those who want to combine different sports (including cycling swimming, paddle sports, cross-country and downhill skiing, skateboarding, and more; see below.) Participation is mostly* based on the “honor system,” but there is a highly recommended - and very popular - Private Strava Club to bring everyone together. You can also sync your Strava account with your RunSignUp page so that all your activities automatically post here to RunSignUp.

* All participants in the top ten on the leaderboard - at any point during the whole month - MUST provide a high level of transparency. Additionally, ALL runs completed on a treadmill must be verified with a photo of the screen at the conclusion of the run. (Measuring distances on a treadmill with a non-synced GPS watch has proven to be an issue in the past.)

Go at your own pace, as often or as long as you want, wherever you live, anywhere on the planet! 

Guidelines:

• Running Division: You must complete all 267 miles on foot: This includes Walking, Hiking, Snowshoeing, and Treadmill, whether indoors or outdoors, covering 267 miles (430km) in 31 days. This is the Running Division, in which ONLY these bipedal activities may be counted. Also Note: In the Strava app, always log any of these activities as "Running" so that they appear on the club leaderboard.

NOTE: Elliptical is NOT allowed in the Running Division. 

• Multi-Sport division: MANY sports may be included: running, cycling, and swimming, and ALSO: All outdoor paddle and rowing sports*, plus ice-skating, rollerblading, skateboarding, and cross-country skiing are also allowed in the multi-sport category, and all they all count one-for-one. Others have a mileage conversion to "equate" them with running:

• Cycling: 3 miles cycling = 1 mile running. If you are cycling indoors, please make it realistic: Indoor bike rides are capped at an average speed of no more than 16MPH / 25.75KPH.

• Swimming: 1 mile swimming = 2 miles running.

• Elliptical: you must go 2 miles - with some intensity, NOT in the easiest setting - to log 1 mile in the RunSignUp system. (Elliptical is only allowed in the Multi-Sport division, NOT in the Running division.)

• Indoor rowing or paddling: you must go 1.5 miles - with some intensity, NOT in the easiest setting - to log 1 mile in the RunSignUp system. 

• Strength training: 1 hour of strength training equates to 4 miles of running.

• Yoga and other types of fitness classes count as 3 miles for a one-hour class.

• Downhill skiing or snowboarding: 1150 feet of vert = one mile, thus 10,000 feet of vert equals the 8.67-mile daily requirement. (A total of 307,050 for 267 miles!)

SWAG & AWARDS:

Unless they opt for "No Swag," participants will receive a BADWATER 267 VR tech shirt, BADWATER buff, and BADWATER sunglasses in a custom Badwater box. For those who log the necessary miles within the RunSignUp system, a BADWATER 267 VR Medal will also be awarded. (Medals are not sent just for participating; they are sent to those who cover the distance AND log all the necessary miles with the RunSignUp system.)

ALL of these items will be shipped approximately 45 days after BADWATER 267 VR concludes.

This is not a traditional ultra, nor a run-of-the-mill virtual – Badwater events are NEVER traditional – it’s the BADWATER 267 VR – an authentic and original BADWATER event – and we hope you will join us!

POLICIES:

There are NO refunds after December 30. There are also no credits or transfers.

See the event webpage for all the info.

name: Badwater Presents 40/40 NOW: Creating Balance in an Ultra World
description:
40/40 NOW, presented by AdventureCORPS: May 13 - June 21, 2026

 

Creating Balance in an Ultra World

 

We invite you to join us for a very special, first of its kind, 40-Day Life Adventure!

 

40/40 NOW is a 40-day program which can serve many purposes:

-              Cross-Training for Sport, and for Life

-              Celebrate the Summer Solstice as your Best Self

-              For Ultra Athletes: Sharpen your Body and Mind for the Summer Racing Season

 

40 / 40 NOW is open to anyone and everyone! (While we are the people behind the world-wide series of BADWATER® Ultramarathons, this opportunity is for anybody looking to head into summer as their very best self.)

 

Duration: 40 Days, from Wednesday, May 13 through Sunday, June 21.  

(The 2026 summer solstice is on Sunday, June 21, 2026 at 1:24 AM.)

 

Why 40 Days? 30 Days Creates a Habit, but a 40 Day Effort is a Spiritual Odyssey.

 

What Is the 40/40 Path? How does it work? What's involved? 

 

The core of this challenge is completing 40 minutes of intentional movement activities in the AM, and 40 minutes in the PM.        

-              One must be strength and/or flexibility oriented. Think weightlifting, yoga, stretch class, dance class, or martial arts. (This can be done at a gym or fitness studio, but also on your own at home, following DVDs or YouTube classes.)

 

-              The other 40-minute activity will be cardio-oriented. Think running, walking, hiking, bicycling, skating, or swimming. (For participants who already run or bike well over 40 minutes per day, we recommend pursuing a different sport for this 40-minute cardio activity.)

 

Additionally, each participant will check-In daily in the Strava Club: Given that participants will be all over the world, each morning (Pacific Time) we will post a “Daily Check-In!” reminder in the Strava Club: Every participant will comment to tell us what they did – and perhaps learned – that day after their PM activity. Accountability makes it real! Teamwork makes the dream work!

 

40/40 participants will also pursue ten different four-day personal challenges, and take “brain breaks” every Sunday: 

-              10 Personal Challenges: One will be announced every Four Days

-              Screen-Free Sundays: No digital noise for 8 hours: You pick the timeframe, as long as it's during waking hours. (If work or childcare means you need your phone close, keep the ringer on for notifications, or have a family member or friend be in charge of your phone. Or if you must be on your phone, just don’t scroll any social media.)

-              Also every Sunday: Pause and Celebrate!  This is the opposite of a To Do List, this is a Done List: Write it and celebrate all you’ve achieved today, or in the past four days, or in the past week!

Every day each participant will receive an email which contains:

-              An inspiring quote

-              A simple but powerful nutrition tip and/or recipe

-              A link to an inspiring online or social media talk

-              Also, every four days, the email will announce the next of the ten 4-Day Challenges

 

The 40/40 participants will receive a printed interactive guidebook containing: 

-              “The Power and Meaning of 40”

-              “The Power and Meaning of the Summer Solstice”

-              Recommended Reading List: 40 Books that could Change Your Life

-              Hints at the ten Four-Day Challenges (actual Challenge details will come by email, so there’s no “planning ahead” – part of the challenge is the surprise!)

-              40-Day Calendar to track your progress: May 13-June 21, 2026

 

 

HOW WILL 40/40 NOW PARTICIPANTS INTERACT?

                  For camaraderie and to share insights and inspirations, a special, private Strava Club will bring everyone together on an ongoing, daily basis.

 

WHAT HAPPENS ON DAY 1?

• You will study the 40 / 40 NOW Guidebook

• You will write a note to yourself about what you hope to gain from this, how you feel your life is now (where are you happy or unhappy, how you want to become a better version of yourself.) You will put this is an envelope and set it aside for 40 days.

• You will begin! – Your AM and PM 40-minute activities, and the first of the four-day personal challenges.

 

WHAT HAPPENS ON DAY 40? THE END IS JUST THE BEGINNING > COMING TOGETHER ON THE SUMMER SOLSTICE

 

With the arrival of the Summer Solstice, we will celebrate and “seal” this experience in several ways:

 

• First, you will read your Day 1 Challenged note to yourself. Whether you share about this in the Strava Club is entirely up to you; no pressure to “over share”!

• We will send out a few simple Rituals to Celebrate the Summer Solstice; choose one or more!

• You will post your final AM and PM activities to the Strava Club and log them in your printed 40 / 40 NOW Guidebook.

• Zoom Call: We will all come together for a 40-minute video chat via  Zoom; this will take place at 900am, Pacific Time. (There will be participants all over the world, but this time works best for those in the Western Hemisphere and Europe.)

 

FINALLY, some  Mementos will be sent to each participant after  40/40 NOW concludes:

40/40 NOW Keychain (Very high quality, meant to last!)

40/40 NOW T-shirt

40/40 NOW Decal

Delivered in a Custom 40/40 NOW Box

name: Badwater Salton Sea
description:
The BADWATER® ultra running experience returns to the Anza-Borrego Desert and Palomar Mountain when the thirteenth BADWATER SALTON SEA race takes place on April 18-19, 2026.

 

This remarkable event challenges teams of two or three ultrarunners – running together as duos or trios for the duration, NOT in a relay – to tackle an unimaginable traverse of Southern California deserts and mountains. The  route covers 81 miles (130km) from Salton City (elevation 234 feet / 71m below sea level) to Palomar Mountain, the almost tallest mountain in San Diego County (elevation 5500 feet / 1676m.)* Eight of the 81 race miles pass through Anza-Borrego State Park on a single track trail from Borrego Springs to Ranchita, creating a race route which is a mix of road and trail. There is a total elevation gain of over 9000 feet (2740m).

The twelve previous editions were received with wide acclaim. The thirteenth edition – with a limit of 100 runners – is scheduled for April 18-19 (Saturday-Sunday), 2026.

 

Badwater Salton is a Badwater 135 Official Preferred Qualifying Race and the first winning team across the line earns Titanium Ticket guaranteed entry to the following year's Badwater 135 (assuming all qualifying stardards are met and their winning time is below 18 hours.)

RACE DIFFICULTY

This is an extremely difficult race held in extreme conditions: Veterans of this event routinely state that it is as hard as any of the toughest 100 milers they have done.

The extreme weather changes - from 100+F / 38+C during the day, often with a sand storm, to freezing temperates with very wet fog at night - along with the extreme challenge of the two major mountain ascents - combine to make this an extremely difficult race.

It is critical to train properly for the heat and to train effectively for very steep desert single-track trail section of the race which is done in maximum heat and without the support crew nearby. Additionally, the single track trail is VERY steep and surprises runners every year with both its steepness, rugged terrain, and intense heat. Knowledge of maintaining proper electrolyte balance is also critical. Study the relevant articles at Badwater University closely, as well as race reports from former competitors.

QUALIFYING REQUIREMENTS

2027 Entry Requirements: All applicants must  have completed at least one difficult 100-175 mile ultramarathon in the eleven months prior to the race, and entry may be denied to those without sufficient endurance credentials. Proof of qualification must be included within the entry application OR by email at least 60 days prior to the race, unless other arrangements are made. (Veteran Badwater Salton Sea and Badwater 135 finishers may enter with a 50-mile qualifying event from the previous 12 months.)

2026 Entry Requirements: All applicants must have completed at least one difficult 50-mile or longer ultramarathon in the 12 months prior to the race, and entry may be denied to those without sufficient endurance credentials. Proof of qualification must be included within the entry application OR by email at least 60 days prior to the race, unless other arrangements are made. 

TEAM FORMAT

Unique to Badwater® Salton Sea is a “Team Ultra Racing” format: All race entrants must enter and race as teams of two or three runners (all male, all female, or co-ed divisions), remaining together for the duration – NOT in a relay format – and sharing just one support vehicle with at least two crew members.

We encourage each runner to select teammates with compatible running style and pace, and with whom he or she would really like to share this experience!

Divisions are offered for All Male, All Female, and Mixed (for 3x teams, 2 men and 1 woman, or 1 man and 2 women, are considered equal).

Some teams have come together in the past through the wonders of the internet, for example through our Facebook Event Page for each year’s event, or just through personal social media (and real world!) connections!

It is very important to pick good teammates to have an ideal experience at this race, and to have the highest likelihood of the whole team finishing together, intact, which SHOULD BE the goal of every team in the race. Here is what we suggest:

– Invite runners that you have run with a lot, and find you have compatible speeds, styles (pacing, how much time you spend getting aid, etc.), and temperament (sense of humour, how much you like to talk versus staying quiet or listening to music, etc.). Those could be runners in your club or with whom you train a lot. But that could also be runners who don’t live near you, but you only see at races.

– Think about all the races you do. Aren’t there others who consistently finish right near you in many races? Since you are already running about the same speed, why not work together instead of against each other? 

– What about fellow runners that you are mentoring, whether “formally” or just in a friendly way? Why not help another runner have an amazing experience, with you playing the role of “grizzled old veteran” or Jedi of ultra running? There is no Luke Skywalker without Obi-Wan Kenobi, after all.

Anyway, those are a few ideas for not only picking good teammates, but also for having an exemplary experience, something that will really be transcendent, and meaningful, and will resonate far and beyond after the race is over and you’ve – hopefully – gone home with your buckles.

REFUND POLICY

Generally speaking, it is our expectation that registered teams will not withdraw from this event. Instead, if one runner has to withdraw from the race, he or she will be replaced with a new teammate, at the discretion of the remaining runner(s) on the team. There are no transfers of registration, nor roll-overs to the next year. Entry fee refunds, less 25%, will be offered until 60 days prior to the event. After that, there are no refunds, nor roll-overs or credits.

ALL TEAMMATES MUST ENTER ON THE SAME WEEK

Please submit all registrations for all teammates within the same week, or preferably within a few days. No runner or team is considered fully registered until ALL runners on the team are registered and paid in full. Runners who register, but don’t have a full team registered within two weeks, may be dropped from the roster and issued a refund, less 25%.

EVENT CANCELLATION

If the event is canceled due to pandemic, hurricane, community disaster, or other force majeure, neither refunds nor credits will be given.

ROUTE APPROVALS

Although we anticipate using the same or nearly the same route each year, the final, exact route is subject to approval from various government agencies and is always subject to change due to various factors beyond our control.

MORE INFORMATION

Visit our Badwater.com website for more information!

Proof of qualification must be included within the entry application OR by email at least 60 days prior to the race, unless other arrangements are made. 

TEAM FORMAT

Unique to Badwater® Salton Sea is a “Team Ultra Racing” format: All race entrants must enter and race as teams of two or three runners (all male, all female, or co-ed divisions), remaining together for the duration – NOT in a relay format – and sharing just one support vehicle with at least two crew members.

We encourage each runner to select teammates with compatible running style and pace, and with whom he or she would really like to share this experience!

Divisions are offered for All Male, All Female, and Mixed (for 3x teams, 2 men and 1 woman, or 1 man and 2 women, are considered equal).

Some teams have come together in the past through the wonders of the internet, for example through our Facebook Event Page for each year’s event, or just through personal social media (and real world!) connections!

It is very important to pick good teammates to have an ideal experience at this race, and to have the highest likelihood of the whole team finishing together, intact, which SHOULD BE the goal of every team in the race. Here is what we suggest:

– Invite runners that you have run with a lot, and find you have compatible speeds, styles (pacing, how much time you spend getting aid, etc.), and temperament (sense of humour, how much you like to talk versus staying quiet or listening to music, etc.). Those could be runners in your club or with whom you train a lot. But that could also be runners who don’t live near you, but you only see at races.

– Think about all the races you do. Aren’t there others who consistently finish right near you in many races? Since you are already running about the same speed, why not work together instead of against each other? 

– What about fellow runners that you are mentoring, whether “formally” or just in a friendly way? Why not help another runner have an amazing experience, with you playing the role of “grizzled old veteran” or Jedi of ultra running? There is no Luke Skywalker without Obi-Wan Kenobi, after all.

Anyway, those are a few ideas for not only picking good teammates, but also for having an exemplary experience, something that will really be transcendent, and meaningful, and will resonate far and beyond after the race is over and you’ve – hopefully – gone home with your buckles.

REFUND POLICY

Generally speaking, it is our expectation that registered teams will not withdraw from this event. Instead, if one runner has to withdraw from the race, he or she will be replaced with a new teammate, at the discretion of the remaining runner(s) on the team. There are no transfers of registration, nor roll-overs to the next year. Entry fee refunds, less 25%, will be offered until 60 days prior to the event. After that, there are no refunds, nor roll-overs or credits.

ALL TEAMMATES MUST ENTER ON THE SAME WEEK

Please submit all registrations for all teammates within the same week, or preferably within a few days. No runner or team is considered fully registered until ALL runners on the team are registered and paid in full. Runners who register, but don’t have a full team registered within two weeks, may be dropped from the roster and issued a refund, less 25%.

EVENT CANCELLATION

If the event is canceled due to pandemic, hurricane, community disaster, or other force majeure, neither refunds nor credits will be given.

ROUTE APPROVALS

Although we anticipate using the same or nearly the same route each year, the final, exact route is subject to approval from various government agencies and is always subject to change due to various factors beyond our control.

MORE INFORMATION

Visit our Badwater.com website for more information!

name: Bayside Saved by the Bell 5K, 10K & Half Marathon
description:
September 19, 2026 · 7:00 a.m. PST · 6846 Owensmouth Ave, Canoga Park, CA

Get ready to dash through time in The Bayside Dash, a 90s high school sitcom-themed race packed with retro vibes, school spirit, and Slater-strength energy.

Presented by Jed & Ted’s Excellent Races

Whether you’re more Morris or Turtle, this race lets you channel your inner Bayside Tiger and crush your course with a smile.

  • Friends Forever 5K 🎶 Named after Zack Attack’s legendary ballad—because you don’t leave your squad behind on race day.
  • Time Out 10K✋ Inspired by Morris himself—freeze time, catch your breath, and own the course.
  • Hall Pass Half Marathon🎓 Go the distance like you’ve got a free pass to run the school (and the streets of Canoga Park).
  • The Multiverse Transfer Student Challenge (Virtual) 🌀 “Transfer Students” from any timeline can choose any distance and still earn their medal.

Expect high school pep rally energy, ‘Saved by the Bell’ moments, throwback tunes, and surprise “pop quizzes” of encouragement along the course. Costumes encouraged—go full Bayside or show off your best 90s teen energy.

This is a Jed & Ted’s Excellent Race—fun, fast, and full of nostalgia.

Sign up now. No hall pass required.

 

 

**Parody Disclaimer**  
This race is a fan-made parody event inspired by 90s pop culture and is not affiliated with or endorsed by any official trademark holders.

name: Bedrock Valley Gravel Ride
description:
BEDROCK VALLEY GRAVEL RIDE

A Gravel Ride experience you don't want to miss. Choose your ride experience around Diamond Valley Lake. This is truly a historic ride in an ancient place. This area's heritage begins during the Ice Age where the most concentrated amount of Mastodons once roam the earth. The remains of hundreds of Mastodons and other prehistoric dinosaurs were discovered in the bedrock of where the lake now rests.

BEDROCK VALLEY GRAVEL RIDE is the first Gravel Bike race that takes you around the Lake. Ride Gravel/Mountain/E-Bike

GRAVEL ROCK RIDE 36K takes you ONE LOOP around beautiful Diamond Valley Lake. Great for your first Gravel/Off-Road Ride

GRAVEL ROCK RIDE 72K takes you TWO LOOPS around beautiful Diamond Valley Lake. Test your skills and make it a double.

GRAVEL ROCK RIDE 108K takes you THREE LOOPS around beautiful Diamond Valley Lake. Find your limits and test your endurance.

GRAVEL YOUTH 10K is a fun and flat fun ride for the spirited rider/beginner. An out and back course that gets you stoked!

NEW! GRAVEL KID'S 3k fun ride. Parents ride with your kids and get them on the dirt. For Kid's 10 and under.

TEAM CHALLENGE enjoy the ride with friends and complete laps as a team in the 72k and 108k.

name: Bedrock Valley Trail Runs
description:
BEDROCK VALLEY TRAIL RUNS

The Bedrock Valley Trail Runs is a NEW trail running experience you don't want to miss. We offer something for the whole family to enjoy. Choose from the beautiful  Bedrock Valley Trail Marathon, Trail Half Marathon, 15k, 5k, Stroller 5k and bring the kids for the the 1 Mile Kid's Fun Run around Diamond Valley Lake. This is truly a historic run in an ancient place. This area's heritage begins during the Ice Age where the most concentrated amount of Mastodons once roam the earth. The remains of hundreds of Mastodons and other prehistoric dinosaurs were discovered in the bedrock of where the lake now rests.

TRAIL MARATHON is a great introduction into trail marathons. A relatively flat loop around the lake ending with some beautiful single track with small climbs. Ideal for all running levels.

TRAIL HALF MARATHON is a beautiful out and back section along the lake bed and perfect for accomplishing your first half marathon.

15K course challenges the runner with a little of everything: flat, fast, climbing, descending on the famous Wildflower single track trail.

NEW! 10K is a fast out and back with views of the lake.

name: Beginner Sailing: March 28 & 29
description:
Two-day adult sailing classes are offered most weekends from 9 am to 4 pm at Fiddler's Cove Marina. Classes are open to all eligible MWR patrons and sponsored guests. Minimum age requirement is 16 years or older with a parent or guardian.

Class fees per person vary by military affiliation and rank. Dependent fees are calculated at the sponsoring active duty or retiree rate. Pre-registration is required as classes can fill up quickly.

Registration includes boat rental, instruction, and textbooks. Students per boat will be kept to the minimum amount possible in order to maximize learning potential and will range from one to four. Number of students per boat is dependent on the boat size, sailing conditions and the skills being developed in the class. On completion of the course, participants receive a Navy Sailing Qualification Card.

A valid California Boater Card and/or a course completion certificate is required before attending the first class. This is a free California Safety class required for all boat owners 16 years and older. California Boater Cards and/or course completion certificates will be checked at the start of the first class. A free online course is offered through https://www.boatus.org/california/.   Once the course is complete and an application has been filled out through California State Parks then a card will be sent in the mail to your address. A digital card will be emailed at the completion of the course and is a valid representation of a California Boater Card for this course.

Once you sign-up please stop by Fiddlers Cove Marina boathouse to pick up your study materials. Some preliminary reading will be given before the start of the course.

Please note: closed-toe shoes are required aboard all Navy MWR boats. Sunscreen, sunglasses, and hats are strongly recommended. The class will be held rain or shine, so please dress accordingly for weather conditions.

name: Bell Gardens 5K
description: Bell Gardens 5K course is designed to provide fast times, and it’s ideal for spectators. This is a two-loop course that covers flat wide public streets of Bell Gardens. Participants will start at Veterans park at the corner of Perry and Suva, head east towards Scout Street, then back to complete the loop on Florence Place. Making a turn on Perry then onto lap 2. A water station will be available at the start of the second loop. The Kid's 1/2 mile is out and back on Suva Street. The road will be completely closed to traffic.

name: Bidwell Classic 5K, 10k and Half Marathon March 7th, 2026
description:
Join us for the Bidwell Classic 5K, 10k and Half Marathon. 

 

Celebrating 50 years of running in Bidwell Park in Chico CA this race has become a chico tradition for so many! We with 3 distances offered we are pleased to host the Bidwell Classic again in 2026! 

We are excited to offer a cash purse again for the top male and female in each event! 

 

BENEFITS STUDENT ATHLETES

A substantial portion of the race entry fees go to the local high school cross country running programs. When you participate in the Bidwell Classic, you are supporting local student athletes. If you would like to make an additional donation to the schools, please do so on the donation portion of the registration. Thank you so much for supporting this race and our local youth runners!

 

Online registration closes at 8:00am on Friday March 6th, 2026.  
In person registration will be available during packet pickup.
No in person registration will be available on race day.

name: Big Bear Turkey Trot
description:
The 12th Annual Big Bear Turkey Trot
✨ What’s New This Year
📍 A new home in the Moonridge Corridor, starting and finishing at Dank Donuts.
🌲 A fresh route incluing the new Rathbun Creek Trail, and a memorable lap through the Moonridge Zoo 🦓🦙🦅.
🏃 A paved 3-mile run through the pines that’s approachable for everyone!
🎶 Danksgiving Celebration party at the finish line featuring live holiday music and adult beverages 🍹

 
🗓️ Event Schedule

8:00 AM - Registration & check-in opens
9:25 AM - Holiday Warmup Yoga 🧘 with Colin Schour
9:30 AM - 3-Mile Turkey Trot 🦃
10:00 AM - Danksgiving Party 🎶🍩🥂 with live music & adult beverages
10:30 AM - Awards 🏆 & Costume Contest 🎭
 
💸 Registration
Adults: $40
Youth (under 18): $25
Kids Run: Free
Locals: $5 discount with ID at packet pickup
No refunds (rain, shine, or snow—it’s all part of the fun).
 
🎁 Included with Entry:

🎄 A holiday finisher ornament
🧘 A lighthearted yoga warm-up
🎭 A lively costume contest
🥧 Race timing and awards eligibility (elite wave start available for those who's costume is considered worthy). 
🎶🍹 The Danksgiving party at the finish line
 
📦 Packet Pickup

🗓️ Monday, Nov 24 – Wednesday, Nov 26 (4–7 PM): The Yellow Post, 546 Pine Knot Blvd
🦃 Race Morning, Nov 27 (8–9 AM): Dank Donuts, 42612 Moonridge Rd Big Bear Lake, CA
 
 
🙋 FAQs

Strollers & kids? Strollers are welcome, and the kids under 5 are free.
Refunds? Nope. The Turkey Trot happens in any weather.
Local discount? Show ID for $5 off.
What’s included? Ornaments, yoga, pie, costumes, music, and memories.
 
🎤 Closing Note

The Big Bear Turkey Trot has always been about more than miles—it’s a morning of laughter, costumes, pie, and community. This year, we’ll gather in Moonridge, run the trail, visit the zoo, and then celebrate together at Danksgiving. We’ll see you out there. 🦃✨

name: Big River Adventure
description:
Welcome to the 26th annual Big River Adventure!

Join us for a unique race experience where you can choose your adventure to run, swim, walk, or paddle your way through the scenic beauty of Mendocino County's Big River.

For the past 26 years, Cancer Resource Centers of Mendocino County has been bringing our community together for this special fundraising event. While the activities may change from year to year, our mission remains steadfast: to honor and remember those impacted by cancer, and to raise vital funds to support free services for individuals facing cancer in Mendocino County.

Starting at the Big River boat launch, participants will embark on a journey filled with stunning views and the shared goal of making a difference in the lives of others.

Don't miss out on this unforgettable adventure! Register now and be part of something truly meaningful.

To keep this family-friendly event affordable and accessible to our community, we will not be providing t-shirts this year.

Here is a link to a trail map

•             5k runners will run east on the haul road to the 5k turn around.

•             10k runners dash east on the haul road to the 10K turn around (10K map).

•             5k "Fun" Walkers will follow the 5k runners route.

•             Kiddie run will begin at the boat launch

•             Swimmers will dive in at the boat lunch and swim east up Big River

•             Paddlers will begin at the boat launch and paddle east up Big River  *Please note you must bring your own vessel.

There are multiple race age divisions. Note: Participants between the ages of 6 and 17 may enter any race division at a discounted rate of $20 at signup.

Race Contact Info

Phone / Teléfono: (707) 937-3833

E-mail / Correo electrónico: info@crcmendocino.org

name: Bike Hut Classic
description: Climb Tunitas Creek Road in Half Moon Bay from the Bike Hut to Skyline while supporting Abundant Grace Coastside Worker in addressing the homeless crisis! This gorgeous and challenging climb begins by rolling through a couple miles of Coastal farms and scenic countryside before starting the ascent through the Redwoods with switchbacks and stunning forest views. Please join us for this 8.3 mile climb with 1900 feet of elevation gain... a special DIY ride that's helping the Coastside community!

name: Bike The Coast
description:
Experience gorgeous riding along pristine beaches, historic Pacific Coast Highway, iconic beach landmarks and unique, Southern California weather with the annual Bike The Coast Bike Tour.   Select from distances of 25 mile, 50 mile, and 100 mile rides and then come out and ride along with 2000 other enthusiast along some of Southern California's best-known cities and roadways.  When you finish, meet us back at  the Oceanside pier to celebrate with your selection of food options, a lively beer garden, great music and new friends.

This is a truly bucket list event if you are an avid rider who enjoys getting some exercise, having fun, and experience great November weather.  This is a 'rules of the road' ride so come prepared to obey all traffic laws.

name: Bizz Johnson
description:
Set PRs and qualify for the Boston Marathon on this fast, downhill course! Total net downhill loss for the marathon is 929 feet making it the PERFECT course to qualify on! Per official B.A.A. confirmation, there will be no time penalties assessed for this course.

All races in 2026 will be Sunday, October 11. The marathon and 50K start at 8:00 AM at Mason Station Trailhead on McCoy Road with an out-and-back before jumping onto the Bizz Johnson Trail at Mason Station where the races travel through scenic Lassen National Forest. The first few miles of the course climb approximately 280 feet through the forest to Westwood Junction, then it’s downhill to the finish at Susanville, with a 1300-foot descent over the final 20 miles. The trail follows the route of the old Fernley and Lassen Branch Line of the Southern Pacific Railroad, built in 1914.

Roughly two-thirds of the way through the race, the trail enters the Susan River Canyon. Here, you’ll pass orange cliffs and cross the river ten times on picturesque wooden railroad bridges. About four miles from the finish, you’ll pass through two former railroad tunnels, 800 feet and 450 feet in length.

The Express Half Marathon starts at at 9:00 AM at Goumaz Campground which is Mile 14 of the full marathon route. After a short up-and-back, the Express Half Marathon flies down the Bizz Johnson to the finish.

Starting at Devil's Corral, the new Express 10K on Sunday does the last 6.2 miles of the full marathon. This course promises to be a fast, fun race. 

For all four events, you will be bused to a remote start.

PACKET PICKUP

  • Saturday Noon - 6 PM (50K, Marathon, Express Half Marathon, Express 10K): Susanville Historic Train Depot, 601 Richmond Road
  • Sunday Morning 6 AM - 7AM (Marathon and 50K), 7AM - 8 AM (Express Half Marathon and Express 10K): Susanville Historic Train Depot, 601 Richmond Road

PLEASE visit our website for maps, schedules, and all the important details!!

name: Bizz Johnson's Southside Scramble
description:
Are you ready to SCRAMBLE? This amazing new trail race showcases the best of the Susan River Canyon! Runners will head up the Bizz Johnson Trail from Hobo Camp for the first half and return via the beautiful and flowy singletrack on the Southside trail across the river. The Southside Scramble has 3 different distances to choose from, a 22K, a 14K, and a 7K. All races start and end at the Hobo Camp Day Use Area. On ODD years, we will run a reversed course! For 2025, all races go out the Southside Trail and back on the Bizz Johnson Trail. 

For the Dirty Devil's 22K, runners start on the Fire Road above the Hobo Camp Day Use Area and take the "outbound" portion of the Bizz Johnson Trail approximately 6 miles all the way to Devil's Corral.  From Devil's Corral, runners turn and drop down to the Susan River, crossing over a seasonal foot bridge, and enter the stunningly beautiful Southside trail with its rockslides, vista points, and flowy single track all the way back to Hobo Camp.

The Tunnel's Blast 14K starts on the Fire Road above the Hobo Camp Day Use Area and takes the "outbound" portion of the Bizz Johnson Trail approximately 4 miles to the entrance to the first railroad tunnel. Before heading into the darkness of the tunnel, runners will veer off onto singletrack, where they climb over the top of the tunnel to reach the Southside Trail. From there, they will enjoy the stunningly beautiful Southside trail with its rockslides, vista points, and flowy single track all the way back to Hobo Camp

The "Hobo's Special" 7K starts on the Fire Road above the Hobo Camp Day Use Area and heads approximately 2 miles up to the Twin Bridges Access connector to the Southside Trail. You'll get just enough of the Bizz Johnson's steady climb to excite your senses for the fast, flowy Southside's single-track return.

Finishers:

At Hobo Camp Day Use Area, participants can enjoy a fun finish line party with food and beverages.  All finishers will receive a custom medal and a custom beach towel just in time for a cool dip in the Susan River! Overall awards will be given to 1st through 3rd finishers (M/F/NB). Age group awards will be given to 1st-3rd AG in 10-year age groups.  

Start Times:

7:30 Dirty Devil's 22K

7:45 Tunnel's Blast 14K

8:00 Hobo Special 7K

Aid Stations:

Aid stations will serve fruit and salty snacks, Heed electrolyte, and water.  This is a cup-less race so runners should have their own hydration systems. Hydrapak is our cupless racing partner and runners will be provided with a collapsible cup at packet pickup.

Aid Station #1 is located on the Bizz Johnson Trail at the lower end of the lower tunnel at Mile 3.8. This aid station serves both the 22K and the 14K. 

Aid Station #2 is located on the Bizz Johnson Trail at the Devil's Corral at the Southside trail turnoff at mile 5.94. 22K 

Aid Station #3 is located on the Southside Trail just above the Twin Bridges access trail. This is approximately 2 miles from the finish. This aid station serves all three race distances.

For ODD years, with the reversed course, the Aid Station distances are slightly different. Additionally, the Twin Bridges Aid Station reverts to just hydration.

This race is Trail-Sisters Approved. There will be equal space on the start line for women and women's hygiene products at all aid stations and the finish line.

Event Parking:

Carpooling is HIGHLY encouraged as parking at Hobo Camp is very limited.  

Here are your options:

1. Hobo Camp - Most parking is on the middle and upper levels. There will be volunteers helping you park very tightly. There is also some parallel parking along the entrance road to Hobo Camp after the gate. This parking must only be on the uphill side of the road and you must be pointed in the direction to LEAVE Hobo Camp. There is NO parking on the Fire Roads.

2. There is some parking at Miller Road at the Bizz Johnson Trail (You must not park blocking the Bizz Johnson Trail). This is a short walk of about .25 mile from the start line.

3. There is a LOT of parking at the Bizz Johnson Trailhead across from the Susanville Historic Train Depot at 601 Richmond Road. This is about .75 mi from the start line. This is a flat, easy walk. One option would be to bring your bicycle and ride to the start. It is a flat, easy, short ride. There will be a place at the finish line to lock your bike and leave your keys with the Race Director.

Packet Pickup:

Packet Pickup will be at the Susanville Historic Train Depot at 601 Richmond Road on Friday, June 21st from 3 PM until 6 PM.  Late Registration will be available on Friday at packet pickup.

Race Day morning packet pickup will be available at the Hobo Camp Day Use Area (Finish Line Area) beginning at 6 AM. There will be limited race day registration from 6 - 6:45 AM (22K), 6 - 7:15 AM (14K), and 6 - 7:30 AM (7K).

Post-Race Activities

The Finish Line is approximately .1 mile from the Start Line. Feel free to bring a picnic lunch and EZ-up and hang out on the grass watching the other finishers. We will have hotdogs, watermelon, water, sodas, and non-alcoholic brews from Athletic Brewing Company for runners. If your family wants to join you, there are several newer charcoal BBQs in the day use area. The river has excellent access at the Day Use area so cooling off is a MUST!

This race is capped at  150 runners total for all 3 events!

Aid Station #1 is located on the Bizz Johnson Trail at the lower end of the lower tunnel at Mile 3.8. This aid station serves both the 22K and the 14K. 

Aid Station #2 is located on the Bizz Johnson Trail at the Devil's Corral at the Southside trail turnoff at mile 5.94. 22K 

Aid Station #3 is located on the Southside Trail just above the Twin Bridges access trail. This is approximately 2 miles from the finish. This aid station serves all three race distances.

For ODD years, with the reversed course, the Aid Station distances are slightly different. Additionally, the Twin Bridges Aid Station reverts to just hydration.

This race is Trail-Sisters Approved. There will be equal space on the start line for women and women's hygiene products at all aid stations and the finish line.

Event Parking:

Carpooling is HIGHLY encouraged as parking at Hobo Camp is very limited.  

Here are your options:

1. Hobo Camp - Most parking is on the middle and upper levels. There will be volunteers helping you park very tightly. There is also some parallel parking along the entrance road to Hobo Camp after the gate. This parking must only be on the uphill side of the road and you must be pointed in the direction to LEAVE Hobo Camp. There is NO parking on the Fire Roads.

2. There is some parking at Miller Road at the Bizz Johnson Trail (You must not park blocking the Bizz Johnson Trail). This is a short walk of about .25 mile from the start line.

3. There is a LOT of parking at the Bizz Johnson Trailhead across from the Susanville Historic Train Depot at 601 Richmond Road. This is about .75 mi from the start line. This is a flat, easy walk. One option would be to bring your bicycle and ride to the start. It is a flat, easy, short ride. There will be a place at the finish line to lock your bike and leave your keys with the Race Director.

Packet Pickup:

Packet Pickup will be at the Susanville Historic Train Depot at 601 Richmond Road on Friday, June 21st from 3 PM until 6 PM.  Late Registration will be available on Friday at packet pickup.

Race Day morning packet pickup will be available at the Hobo Camp Day Use Area (Finish Line Area) beginning at 6 AM. There will be limited race day registration from 6 - 6:45 AM (22K), 6 - 7:15 AM (14K), and 6 - 7:30 AM (7K).

Post-Race Activities

The Finish Line is approximately .1 mile from the Start Line. Feel free to bring a picnic lunch and EZ-up and hang out on the grass watching the other finishers. We will have hotdogs, watermelon, water, sodas, and non-alcoholic brews from Athletic Brewing Company for runners. If your family wants to join you, there are several newer charcoal BBQs in the day use area. The river has excellent access at the Day Use area so cooling off is a MUST!

This race is capped at  150 runners total for all 3 events!

name: Bizz Johnson's Southside Scramble
description:
Are you ready to SCRAMBLE? This amazing new trail race showcases the best of the Susan River Canyon! Runners will head up the Bizz Johnson Trail from Hobo Camp for the first half and return via the beautiful and flowy singletrack on the Southside trail across the river. The Southside Scramble has 3 different distances to choose from, a 22K, a 14K, and a 7K. All races start and end at the Hobo Camp Day Use Area. On ODD years, we will run a reversed course! For 2025, all races go out the Southside Trail and back on the Bizz Johnson Trail. 

For the Dirty Devil's 22K, runners start on the Fire Road above the Hobo Camp Day Use Area and take the "outbound" portion of the Bizz Johnson Trail approximately 6 miles all the way to Devil's Corral.  From Devil's Corral, runners turn and drop down to the Susan River, crossing over a seasonal foot bridge, and enter the stunningly beautiful Southside trail with its rockslides, vista points, and flowy single track all the way back to Hobo Camp.

The Tunnel's Blast 14K starts on the Fire Road above the Hobo Camp Day Use Area and takes the "outbound" portion of the Bizz Johnson Trail approximately 4 miles to the entrance to the first railroad tunnel. Before heading into the darkness of the tunnel, runners will veer off onto singletrack, where they climb over the top of the tunnel to reach the Southside Trail. From there, they will enjoy the stunningly beautiful Southside trail with its rockslides, vista points, and flowy single track all the way back to Hobo Camp

The "Hobo's Special" 7K starts on the Fire Road above the Hobo Camp Day Use Area and heads approximately 2 miles up to the Twin Bridges Access connector to the Southside Trail. You'll get just enough of the Bizz Johnson's steady climb to excite your senses for the fast, flowy Southside's single-track return.

Finishers:

At Hobo Camp Day Use Area, participants can enjoy a fun finish line party with food and beverages.  All finishers will receive a custom medal and a custom beach towel just in time for a cool dip in the Susan River! name: Blazin' Eagles 5K Fun Run/Walk
description:

name: Blossom Bike Ride
description:
The 36th Annual Blossom Bike Ride will take place on March 7, 2026. We are currently working on the routes for this year.  As the mileage gets longer, the route provides more of a challenge. Our 7 mile family ride takes you along the rails to trails pathway through Reedley. The 20 mile route offers more scenic landscapes north east of town for your viewing pleasure. If you are looking for a little more challenge, you might want to try our 40 mile route. This will get you started on the right course of mileage for the year. If you are looking for the longer ride, we offer the 60 mile route with some climbing. This route will take you into the foot hills east of Reedley.

Let's get ready to Ride!

 
These are ride times:
  • 60 Mile 7:00am
  • 40 Mile 8:30am
  • 20 Mile 9:30am
  • 7 Mile Family ride 10:30
 
Ride begins at:

     Reedley College
     995 N. Reed
     Reedley, 93654


This year our registration and ride take off will be at parking lot B which is different from the past rides.

 
Please allow yourself to arrive at least half an hour before ride so that you can check in at registration desk and receive your bib and T-shirt if you signed up for one. We will NOT be checking in riders more than 35 minutes before scheduled ride.  
 
Typical weather should be a beautiful low 70's that day. 
 
See you Saturday!

name: Blue Moon 5K. 10K. Half Marathon by Califlow Runs
description:
🌕 Blue Moon Run (Morning Race)
5K • 10K • Half Marathon
Sunday, May 31, 2026 | Long Beach, CA

This run really is once in a blue moon — literally.

Join us on the morning of the actual Blue Moon for a rare and memorable coastal run designed to celebrate movement, timing, and being present for moments that don’t come around often. Whether you’re chasing miles, memories, or just the magic of a truly unique day, this is one you’ll want to say you were part of.

Expect ocean views, high vibes, and that unmistakable CaliFlow energy — all under the glow of a moon that only shows up every few years. 💙🌕

 
🔵 Fun Blue Moon Facts
A Blue Moon happens when there are two full moons in one month
It occurs only every 2–3 years, which is why we say “once in a blue moon”
The moon isn’t actually blue — but the moment is still rare and special
This is one of those runs people remember and say: “I was there for that.”
 
🌊 Race Highlights
🌕 Professionally chip-timed for accurate results
📸 Free race-day photos & downloadable finish-line pics
🎖️ Finisher medals for all participants
🏆 Overall & Age Group Awards
🌊 Flat, fast, scenic beach course
🥤 Water stations & restrooms along the route
🎶 Finish-line music, snacks, and photo moments to celebrate your miles

 
🌺 Why CaliFlow Runs?
At CaliFlow Runs, we believe running should be inclusive, affordable, and fun. We host 50+ events each year to create experiences where everyone — of every pace and background — feels welcome.

Our races are known for professional execution, free photos, great vibes, and a strong sense of community — without the big-race price tag. Whether you’re racing the clock or soaking in the moment, you belong here.

 
👟 Who Can Participate?
Everyone!
Runners • Walkers • Strollers • All paces welcome

Come as you are. Leave with rare miles and a great story. 💙

 
⏰ Bib Pick-Up & Start Times
📍 Location: 5100 E Ocean Blvd, Long Beach, CA 90803 (Granada Beach)

Bib Pick-Up:
🕕 6:15 AM – 7:15 AM at the Race Ready Athletics Tent

Start Times:
• Half Marathon: 7:00 AM
• 5K & 10K: 7:15 AM

 
🚗 Parking Info
Street parking available (check posted signs for street sweeping).
Paid beach lot parking is $2.00 per hour via Passport app or on-site machine.
Arrive early for best access near the start line.

 
🏅 Awards & Medals
🏅 All finishers receive a custom Once in a Blue Moon medal
🏆 Overall & Age Group Awards in each distance

 

If it’s not CaliFlow, it’s just an average race. 💙

name: BMR Sacramento Black History Month Family 5k Walk/Run! We're creating GENERATIONAL HEALTH!
description:
Black Men Run Sacramento presents our 4th Annual Black History Month Family 5k Run/Walk!

OUR MISSION: The Black History Month Family 5k Walk/Run encourages healthy lifestyles within the Black community by promoting physical activity like running and walking while fostering connections with BIPOC organizations dedicated to improving health outcomes. This event helps creates a new standard for generations to follow. This is Generational Health!

We welcome walkers and runners to choose whichever distance works for you and your family! Net proceeds go to the Capitol City Black Nurses Association. The first 200 registrants will receive a medal!*  The race starts and ends at REI Sacramento. 

*As of 7:10PM, February 9th, medals are no longer available. No worries, there will be plenty of raffle prizes and giveaways! All attendees will receive a free BMR branded canvas tote bag, compliments of REI! (while supplies last).

IF YOU AREN'T IN THE SACRAMENTO AREA OR CANNOT ATTEND IN PERSON, WE ENCOURGE YOU TO RUN/WALK THIS EVENT VIRTUALLY TO SUPPORT THE AMAZING HEALTH EQUITY WORK OF THE CAPITOL CITY BLACK NURSES ASSOCIATION. PLEASE POST YOUR PICS ON YOUR SOCIAL MEDIA WITH THESE HASHTAGS:  #BMRSACRAMENTO #CCBNA #BLACKHISTORYMONTH #RUNFORAHMAUD

name: Boogie Nights 5K & 10K
description:

June 27, 2026 · 8:00 p.m. PST · 6846 Owensmouth Ave, Canoga Park, CA

Join us for Boogie Nights 5K & 10K After Dark — a disco-drenched nighttime run through the Valley where polyester reigns, vibes are high, and everybody’s a star at the finish line.

name: Bowman Run with the Bulls presented by Hotel Vista Sierra
description:
Join us for the annual Bowman Run with the Bulls 5K Run/Walk presented by Hotel Vista Sierra!
Lace up your shoes and be part of this fun community tradition that welcomes runners and walkers of all ages. The course winds through the heart of Auburn, The Endurance Capital of the World.

The race starts and finishes at Railhead Park, with all proceeds supporting continued improvements to Bowman Charter School’s large gymnasium -- a space that brings our students and community together. 

🏅 Registration Details

  • $40 for kids (13 and under)
  • $45 for general registration
  • $50 same-day registration (shirt not guaranteed)
  • Family Discount: Register 3 or more and receive $3 off each runner!
  • Register by March 22 to guarantee your cotton T-shirt.

🌟 Special recognition for Bowman families: Register for the race by March 22 and include a $50 or more donation at checkout, and your family name will be proudly featured on the race T-shirt.

🏆 Class Challenge: Join a Bowman class team and help your class earn a special reward for the most participants and fundraising!

❤️ Can't join in person? You (or grandparents and other family members) can sign up to participate virtually or support the cause with a donation—every contribution helps Bowman students go the distance! Please note: virtual registration is purely for fun and does not include a bib, swag or award. You may not register for the virtual event and participate in person at the race.

🏃‍♂️ Race Highlights

  • Race bibs and chip timing sponsored by Hotel Vista Sierra
  • Packet pickup hosted by Auburn Running Company on Friday, April 10
  • Finisher's medals provided to all kids, made possible by Auburn Clay Arts
  • Water aid station sponsored by Synergy Real Estate Partners
  • Professional digital race photos sponsored by Sacfit Ultra Runners
  • Age-group awards or prizes will be presented for both kids and adults

Come out and celebrate fitness, community, and school spirit -- Run with the Bulls!

This event is an annual fundraiser organized by Bowman Charter PTO.

name: Break the Chains: A Walk for Cult Recovery - 2026 International Cult Awareness Month
description:
This isn’t just a walk—it’s a movement.

Join us for Break the Chains: A Walk for Cult Recovery, a powerful virtual walk/run honoring the courage, resilience, and strength it takes to break free from coercive control and cultic abuse.

Whether you’re walking in honor of a survivor, raising awareness in your community, or celebrating your own journey of freedom—every step you take helps shed light on the realities of cultic abuse and the healing that follows.

Over the course of six weeks (one week before August, throughout International Cult Awareness Month (ICAM), and one week after), we’ll walk together—virtually but united. Each week, participants will receive empowering content including survivor stories, educational tools, inspiring challenges, and calls to action.

💥 Your registration includes:

  •  A digital race bib to print and wear proudly
  •  Weekly themed content to keep you motivated and learning
  •  A downloadable chain-breaking progress tracker
  •  Optional access to exclusive campaign merch
  •  A certificate of completion to honor your commitment

No matter where you are in the world, you can help raise awareness, honor survivors, and be part of breaking the cycle.

  • All paces and mobility devices welcome (walking, rolling, treadmill, etc.)
  • No GPS tracking or time submission required
  • Content and activities will be screen-reader accessible and inclusive in language and design

How far is the race? That's up to you and your capabilities. Take it as far as you'd like! Here are some suggestions:

  • 4 Miles for 4 Weeks of Awareness - A short but powerful tribute to each week of Cult Awareness Month.
  • 10 Miles to Represent the Average Years in a Cult - Or choose a number that reflects your story—or that of someone you walk for.
  • 26.2 Miles (Marathon of Liberation) - For those who want to take on a bold challenge in honor of long-term recovery.
  • Freedom Your Way – Custom Race - Set your own distance, pace, and purpose. Every step counts.

Walk with us. Learn with us. Break the chains.

Hosted by The Freedom Train Project, Incorporated, a nonprofit dedicated to helping survivors recover from coercive control and cultic abuse, this virtual walk/run is more than just an event—it’s a movement for awareness, healing, and hope.

name: Breezin’ Through Beaumont
description:
On Saturday, May 16, 2026, the City of Beaumont will celebrate the return of Breezin’ Through Beaumont. This event consists of a 5k road race. Everyone is encouraged to come out and watch this exciting event. 

The race will begin in front of the Beaumont Civic Center, located at: 550 E. Sixth St., Beaumont, CA 92223. and continue along the islands of Palm Avenue to 13th Street before returning southbound to 8th Street where the race will wind around Stewart Park before finishing back at the Civic Center. Whether you are an experienced runner or an avid walker, everyone who is interested is encouraged to participate.

Event Times

  • 6:30 a.m. - Registration and bag pickup 
  • 8:00 a.m. - Race starts 
    • Expected to maintain a 15-minute mile pace 
  • 9:00 a.m. - Awards Ceremony

The awards ceremony is expected to take place at 9am on the front steps of the Civic Center. The top three male and female finishers in each age division will be awarded medals. Overall male and female winners will receive trophies. 

Registration Information

  • Preregistration (Open until April 30) - $30
    • Pre-registration guaranteed a race shirt.
  • Race Day Registration - $50

  • All sales are final. No refunds.

Current Divisions by Age

  • 7 - 9 
  • 10 - 12 
  • 13 - 15
  • 16 - 19

Bib Pick-up Information

  • Pick-up on race day at the Beaumont Civic Center beginning at 6:30 a.m. 
  • Runners can pick up their race bibs and t-shirts ahead of race day on May 11 – 14 from 1pm to 5pm at the Albert A. Chatigny Sr. Community Recreation Center, located at 1310 Oak Valley Parkway. 

Road Closures
During the events, there will be rolling street closures and no-parking zones throughout the course. The areas most affected within the city will be along:

  • 6th Street

name: Brian Waterbury Memorial Rock to Pier Run
description:
Run the Coast. Honor a Legacy. Experience the Central Coast at its Best!

Join us on Saturday, July 18, 2026, for the 56th annual Brian Waterbury Memorial Rock to Pier Fun Run and the 12th annual Rock’n Around the Pier Half Marathon, starting at 8:00 AM.

Set against the stunning backdrop of the Central Coast, both events begin at Morro Rock and take runners along the shoreline for an unforgettable beach-running experience.

Event Options
Rock to Pier Fun Run (6 miles)
Run from Morro Rock to the iconic Cayucos Pier, finishing right at the pier. This beach run is open to all ages and abilities—perfect for seasoned runners and first-timers alike.

Rock’n Around the Pier Half Marathon
A challenging and scenic out-and-back course starting at Morro Rock, heading to the Cayucos Pier, and returning south. At mile 10.5, runners will detour through Cloisters Park before finishing back at Morro Rock.
Course closes at 12:00 PM.

Race Day Details
Both events start at 8:00 AM

Water/Aid Stations throughout course!

Expect wet shoes—this is a true beach run!
Post-race breakfast and awards at Morro Rock
Bus transportation provided from Cayucos Pier back to Morro Rock for Rock to Pier participants
Parking is limited in Cayucos; ample parking available at Morro Rock (arrive early!)

Extras & Notes
Limited shirt sizes available (some sizes sold out)
Dogs are not allowed on the course due to Snowy Plover nesting season

Come celebrate tradition, community, and coastal beauty in one of California’s most unique running events. Whether you’re racing for a personal best or soaking in the scenery, this is a run you won’t forget!
