name: Bruin Run/Walk 5K
description:
Bruin Run/Walk is excited to present the 26th annual 5K at UCLA, benefiting The Painted Turtle. This year's theme is SLUMBER PARTY RUN! Make sure to show up in your best pajamas, and we highly recommend bringing a stuffed Teddy Bear or other plushie along for the ride! As one of twelve committees within UCLA’s USAC Student Wellness Commission (SWC), Bruin Run/Walk organizes one of the largest student-run events on campus each year.

​

The Bruin Run/Walk 5K supports the The Painted Turtle, a camp in Lake Hughes, California for children with chronic illnesses and their families. The 5k event brings together nearly 1000 students, UCLA faculty, and members of the greater LA community in support of this meaningful cause.

​

For 25 years, Bruin Run/Walk has been a proud UCLA tradition, raising over $75,000 for our beneficiary! This event is made possible by a dedicated team of UCLA undergraduate students working closely with The Painted Turtle.

name: BURRITO 12K RUN - BAKERSFIELD
description:
Reyes Running events present this very unique event, BURRITO FUN RUN! Participants get to choose the distance they want to participate in 12K, 5k or 2 MILE WALK!...and YES, course will take participants to the famous BURRITO HILL at Yokuts Park AND there will also be some delicious BURRITOS for all participants at the finish line! 12K is perfect for anyone getting ready for a Spring half marathon/marathon! For sure you don't want to miss this friendly, family running event!

 A few reasons:

Authentic delicious BURRITOS
Hot chocolate
Unique medal
EXTRA medal (Reyes Running Series)
Age group awards (12K)
Athena/Clydesdale group awards
Kids races
12k Run, 5K Run/Walk or 2 mile walk
Great running course
Music
Fun! 5K is a run/walk fun event. Top 10 male/female in the 5K get awards, but NO age group awards for this event.

name: Buzz Marathon #26
description:
WHAT'S THE BUZZ?

The Buzz Marathon is a Boston qualifying race, hosted at Camp Roberts California National Guard Installation. This annual event includes; A full marathon, half-marathon, 10K, 5k, and a kids 1-mile run. Proceeds of this event help fund the Paso Robles Veterans of Foreign Wars (VFW) with their mission of supporting Veterans and veteran services. The VFW  provides services to support the wellbeing of Veterans and their families. The goal of the VFW is to connect veterans to resources, support them with VA Claim connections through the VA, and continue to build comraderies. 

Boston Qualifier: USATF #CA24001TEB 

 

CAMP ROBERTS ENTRY REQUIREMENTS:

All participants and visitors must comply with base access protocols

Drivers are required to provide:

  • Real ID (or valid government-issued ID)
  • Current vehicle registration and proof of insurance
  • ALL VEHICHLES ARE SUBJECT TO SEARCH AND SEIZURE

All other visitors or passengers (ages 16 and above) are also required to provide a Real ID or government-issued identification.

 

COURSE DESCRIPTION

Runners will start at the heart of the Camp Roberts instillation, heading northeast through diverse terrain and varying elevations. Along the way, participants will take in breathtaking scenic views, with chances to spot local wildlife such as elk, deer, and the elusive kit fox.

The course also offers a unique blend of natural beauty and history, featuring glimpses of California wildflowers and historic military landmarks that highlight the rich heritage of Camp Roberts.

 

AID STATIONS

Aid stations are positioned approximately every two miles, with additional placements at key turns to help guide runners along the correct route.

Stations are located at the following mile markers:

  • 1.6
  • 3.6
  • 5.1
  • 6.55 (Half Marathon Turnaround)
  • 8.0
  • 9.9
  • 12.0
  • 13.12 (Full Marathon Turnaround)


Each station is stocked with water, Powerade, bananas, oranges, energy gels, and latrines.


 

PARKING

Parking on Convoy Parking Lot on California Blvd and Montana Blvd. Short walk to the start/finish line.

 

AWARDS

All participants will receive a T-shirt and a finisher medal. Awards ceremony will be held at noon, where we’ll present a plaque to the overall first-place male and female in each race.

 

PACKET PICKUP

The Camp Roberts MWR will be hosting packet pickup at the Phoenix Recreation Center (Building 6083), located approximately 75 yards from the Start/Finish line at the corner of Arizona and California Blvd.

Packet pickup and security clearance will be available:

  • Tuesday to Friday, March 17th – 20th, 9:00 AM – 3:00 PM
  • Race Day – Saturday, March 21st, 6:00 AM - 8:00 AM

Participants are strongly encouraged to check in early during the Tuesday–Friday window to complete security clearance and avoid race-day delays.

On site reg available for $20 extra 3/17 - 3/20 10AM-4PM

name: Buzz Marathon #26
description:
WHAT'S THE BUZZ?

The Buzz Marathon is a Boston qualifying race, hosted at Camp Roberts California National Guard Installation. This annual event includes; A full marathon, half-marathon, 10K, 5k, and a kids 1-mile run. Proceeds of this event help fund the Paso Robles Veterans of Foreign Wars (VFW) with their mission of supporting Veterans and veteran services. The VFW  provides services to support the wellbeing of Veterans and their families. The goal of the VFW is to connect veterans to resources, support them with VA Claim connections through the VA, and continue to build comraderies. 

Boston Qualifier: USATF #CA24001TEB 

 

CAMP ROBERTS ENTRY REQUIREMENTS:

All participants and visitors must comply with base access protocols

Drivers are required to provide:

  • Real ID (or valid government-issued ID)
  • Current vehicle registration and proof of insurance
  • ALL VEHICHLES ARE SUBJECT TO SEARCH AND SEIZURE

All other visitors or passengers (ages 16 and above) are also required to provide a Real ID or government-issued identification.

 

COURSE DESCRIPTION

Runners will start at the heart of the Camp Roberts instillation, heading northeast through diverse terrain and varying elevations. Along the way, participants will take in breathtaking scenic views, with chances to spot local wildlife such as elk, deer, and the elusive kit fox.

The course also offers a unique blend of natural beauty and history, featuring glimpses of California wildflowers and historic military landmarks that highlight the rich heritage of Camp Roberts.

 

AID STATIONS

Aid stations are positioned approximately every two miles, with additional placements at key turns to help guide runners along the correct route.

Stations are located at the following mile markers:

  • 1.6
  • 3.6
  • 5.1
  • 6.55 (Half Marathon Turnaround)
  • 8.0
  • 9.9
  • 12.0
  • 13.12 (Full Marathon Turnaround)


Each station is stocked with water, Powerade, bananas, oranges, energy gels, and latrines.


 

PARKING

Parking on Convoy Parking Lot on California Blvd and Montana Blvd. Short walk to the start/finish line.

 

AWARDS

All participants will receive a T-shirt and a finisher medal. Awards ceremony will be held at noon, where we’ll present a plaque to the overall first-place male and female in each race.

name: Camp Turkey Terror: After Dark- Friday the 13th  Turkey Trot: 5K. 10K. Half Marathon by Califlow Runs
description:
This a 2026 Event

🦃 Camp Turkey Terror – Where the Turkeys Fight Back
🌲 Friday the 13th 
5K | 10K | Half Marathon
📍 5400 E Ocean Blvd, Long Beach, CA 90803
📅 Friday, November 13, 2026
🕓 Check-In begins : 4:00 PM to 6:30 PM
Start Times | Half: 5:00 PM | 10K & 5K: 6:30 PM

 
💀 About the Event
Welcome to Camp Turkey Terror — where the tables have turned and the turkeys are taking revenge. 🦃🔥
It’s Friday the 13th, and under the harvest moon, the woods come alive with feathers, fog, and just a hint of chaos.

Join us for the final chapter in the Camp CaliFlow Trilogy, a fall night of fun, fright, and fearless miles. Whether you’re running from guilt, running for the pie, or just running for the glow, this one’s for you.

Because at Camp Turkey Terror… the turkeys fight back.

 
🌊 What to Expect
USATF-Certified Course 🏁
Professional Chip Timing ⏱️
Free Race-Day Photos by Nina & Dre 📸
Finisher Medals for All Participants 🏅
Overall & Age Group Awards 🥇
3 On-Course Water Stations (one at each turnaround)
Finish-Line Feast & Campfire Festival 🔥
Costume Contest – Pilgrims, Pumpkins & Poultry Welcome 🦃🎃
DJ, Lights & Glow Effects for that signature CaliFlow After-Dark magic
All paces welcome — runners, walkers, and leftovers alike!
 
🌕 Course Info
The course begins beneath the glowing CaliFlow arch near Belmont Pier, tracing the flat, scenic Long Beach path under the light of the harvest moon.

As you make your way through the fog, you’ll pass a few iconic “Camp Turkey Terror” checkpoints:
🔥 The Final Feast Turnaround
🍂 Stuffing Station 13
🥧 Pie or Die Water Stop

Half Marathon: 3 × 4.36-mile loops
10K: 2 × 5K out-and-backs
5K: 1 loop

Each turnaround features a full water station, friendly “camp counselors,” and plenty of autumn spirit to keep you moving before the turkeys catch up.

 
🍁 The Vibe – Totally Camp CaliFlow
Think Thanksgiving meets slasher flick, but with way better lighting and medals you’ll actually want to show off.

Expect glowing campfires, pumpkin decor, moody fog, and more laughs than screams as you cross the finish line at our “Campfire Feast” celebration.

Because at CaliFlow Runs, we don’t fear the chaos — we run through it.
And this time… the turkeys are watching. 👀

✨ Not just a race. Join the movement.

name: Campus Life 5k - The FROZEN 5k!
description:
Join us for our 12th Annual Campus Life Frozen 5k + Kids' Fun Run on Saturday, May 9, 2026 at Woodward Park. This event is for the whole family to enjoy! For those who want or need, we are still offering a virtual race option. There will be BREAKFAST, COLD BREW from Lanna Coffee, and ACAI BOWLS from TOWER BLENDZ! If this is the only reason you show up, we understand! 

This FROZEN 5k benefits Fresno/Madera Youth For Christ and the mentoring work it does with over a thousand students each year. 

 

Pricing:
Campus Life 5k: $45 $40 SPECIAL PRICING 
Virtual Campus Life 5k: $45 $40 SPECIAL PRICING 
Kids Fun Run (recommended for kids aged 2-7): $25 $20 SPECIAL PRICING 
*Shirts are only guaranteed for registrations by 4/23

 

ADDITIONAL TOP FINISHER PRIZE LEVELS!
Top 3 (Men)
Top 3 (Women)
1st Place (11 years and under)
1st Place (12-18 years)

 

Campus Life interacts with students daily to help them “give life to their story”. Find out more about YFC at www.yfcnow.org.

 

Sponsorships are available for the Campus Life 5k. 

 

IMPORTANT DATES

Campus Life 5k & Kid's Fun Run 
Saturday, May 9th, 2026
Location: Woodward Park (Mountain View Shelter): 7775 N Friant Rd, Fresno, CA 93720
7:30am: Kids Fun Run

Friday, May 8th
3:00pm - 6:00pm

8681 N Chestnut Ave Clovis, CA  93619

EVENT DETAILS

Please note that it costs $5 to park if you would like to park on Woodward Park's property. You can pay at one of the many kiosks located around the park. 

All 5k participants receive:

  • Race shirt! (Unisex and youth sizes available)

  • FREE ACAI BOWLS FROM TOWER BLENDZ!

name: Catalina Island Half-Marathon & 10K
description:
Experience the ultimate California trail half-marathon, an adventure that will test your limits while rewarding you with awe-inspiring beauty. Starting in the charming town of Avalon, the race kicks off with a scenic run past the historic Wrigley Mansion. From there, you’ll journey into Catalina Island’s rugged Interior, tackling challenging climbs that lead to breathtaking peaks.

At the summit, take in sweeping views of the Pacific Ocean, where, on a clear day, you might catch a glimpse of two other Channel Islands. The journey continues with a thrilling descent through the serene Wrigley Memorial, winding your way back into the heart of Avalon.

For runners looking for a shorter, yet equally stunning course, the 10K route offers a picturesque tour through Avalon’s scenic hillsides, capturing the island’s unique charm and natural beauty. Whether you’re taking on the half-marathon or the 10K, this race is a perfect blend of challenge, adventure, and unforgettable views.

name: CELEBRATE LIFE RUN
description:
Description: Join two-time world champion triathlete, Siri Lindley, as she celebrates her 6th year cancer-free, officially being cured of Acute Myeloid Leukemia! Siri and her wife, Bek Keat, created this annual run to honor life and make a difference ...not just for people, but for horses too!
Your tax deductible race fee will feed a horse for a week!
This event honors all life, remembers those we've lost, and embodies the resilience of the human spirit.
Race Date: February 21, 2026

Start Time: 9AM (Day of registration opens at 8AM)
Details: The CELEBRATE LIFE RUN will begin and end at Believe Ranch and Rescue where Siri and Bek rescue abused, neglected and slaughter bound horses.
You'll be able to meet Siri, Bek and their beautiful rescue horses! Enjoy horse rides, local artisan pop ups with coffee, baked goods, wine & spirits, arts and crafts! 

Race Fees:
$40 through 8/31 
$50 through 12/31
$60 through 2/20
$70 on race day
(Processing fees included)
Virtual:
$40 through 12/31
$50 through 2/21
(Processing fees included) 

Finisher medals for all participants!

Awards for top finishers and spot prizes from Rudy Project, HyperIce and F2C.

Course Description: Beautiful, picturesque Santa Ynez countryside.
Event begins and ends at Believe Ranch and Rescue, Santa Ynez, CA.
5K Map: Coming soon
 
Swag: Finisher medals included. For those attending the race in person, short sleeve dry fit tech shirts are available for purchase through this registration process that will be picked up on race day.
Virtual runners can purchase shirts here:  https://www.bonfire.com/celebrateliferun2026/
Beneficiary: 100% of proceeds will be allocated to Believe Ranch and Rescue to help save lives.
Any and all additional donations are tax deductible, 501c Believe Ranch and Rescue.

Weather Policy: Event will take place rain or shine.
 
Event Contact: info@siriandbek.com

name: Cerro Gordo Silver Run
description:
Saturday. May 23, 2026 | Start Time: 8:00 AM | Check-in by 6:30 AM
(Camping & lodging info at the bottom of this description)

Check out the video recap from this past year for more context!

Are you tough enough to race up a mountain road built for mule trains and silver barons?

Join us for a legendary race in the Eastern Sierra - an 8-mile uphill battle climbing 4,600 vertical feet to the historic ghost town of Cerro Gordo, once the richest silver mine in California.

This is not your average run.
This is a gut-check. A pilgrimage. A challenge against time, gravity, and yourself.

The infamous Cerro Gordo Road was carved out in 1865 to shuttle silver down from the mountains. Now, once a year, runners race back up - chasing glory, chasing ghosts, and chasing history.

When you summit the town, the day’s just beginning. Cross the finish line and celebrate with:
– A giant mountaintop BBQ
– Live music and games
– Self-guided exploration of the abandoned town
– And a well-earned sense of triumph.

What’s included:
- Aid stations every mile stocked with fuel and encouragement
- A limited-edition Silver Run 2026 shirt and finishers medal
- Shuttle vans for the ride back down
- Eternal bragging rights: the winner’s name is engraved in silver and enshrined in Cerro Gordo’s history

Last year’s winning time: 1:14:04 by Jacob Banta
Think you’ve got what it takes to beat it?

There’s no time limit. Whether you finish in 1 hour or 5, this mountain has room for all. We’ve had teenagers run with their parents. We’ve had an 81-year-old cross the finish line. All are welcome - as long as you're willing to dig deep and climb.

Check out the 2025 race results:
https://my.raceresult.com/341872/results

Don’t miss the most epic footrace in California.
This is all happening: Saturday. May 23, 2026 
Come run for the silver.

Camping & Lodging

Our neighbor is providing camping spots available in Keeler, CA, less than 1/4 mile from the starting line, available for $20/spot. These will have restrooms available at the campground area. This is by far the cheapest and closest accommodation option. 

Otherwise, Lone Pine, CA is 15 miles from the starting line and has a wide variety of hotels, motels, RV parks, and more. 

Another option is BLM Land camping. There is a lot of BLM land around and you can camp there for free for up to 14 days. Google "BLM camping" for more information. 

There will be multiple parking lots available in Keeler, CA the day of the race to leave your cars. There will be volunteers on site to direct you to these day of the race. After the race, you will be brought down by shuttle bus, back to these parking lots.

name: Champion Mine Trail Race
description:
Challenge Yourself and Enjoy the Great Outdoors

Join the Sierra TrailBlazers Running Club and Bear Yuba Land Trust for the inaugural Champion Mine Trail Race!

Get ready to travel to a must-see destination race in Northern California. Explore some of Nevada City’s most exciting trails with this brand-new half-marathon (13.1 miles) event. The course winds through towering pines, crosses a historic swinging bridge, and challenges runners with a series of rewarding climbs. With multiple aid stations, historical landmarks, and a newly constructed trail section offering varied terrain, this course rivals some of the best trail races in Northern California.

Runners will enjoy breathtaking views along the Tribute Trail and Deer Creek, combined with a beautiful variety of landscapes throughout the race. Best of all, the adventure begins right on Nevada City’s historic Broad Street — a truly unforgettable starting line!

The Champion Mine Trail Run offers a dynamic mix of pavement, gravel, and single-track trails, making it a must-do event for any trail enthusiast.

name: Cherry Pickin 5k WAVE RACE
description:
Cherry Pickin’ 5K Wave Race                             

At Leona Valley Elementary

Saturday, May 23, 2026 

The 5K WAVE RACE! This is a handicapped race based on Age-Graded tables.
If you are a good runner for your age or gender, you could WIN this race! Your start time will depend on your age and gender per the table found in the link below.
Custom medals will be given to the top 150 overall finishers – not based on age divisions. There are no age group divisions since the start of the race is handicapped by age and gender.
Up and Down 5k Course - Uphill first half, super fun downhill coming back!
All entries get a t-shirt – while supplies last. 

There will also be a "Family Fun Run Wave."  If you would like to just come out and run, jog or walk and not worry about time or placing you may opt for the Family Fun Run Wave, starting at 8:00 am. You will not be timed and you will not earn a finish placing.

This event is a fundraiser for the West Antelope Valley Education Foundation - WAVE. They provide funding for extracurricular opportunities such as field trips, clubs, sports, etc for the students of the Westside Union School District.

name: Chester 4th of July Fun Run
description:
One mile route down historic Chester Main Street!

The Almanor Recreation and Park District’s 45th annual Chester 4th of July Fun Run will take place at 9 a.m. on Saturday, July 4, 2026. The one mile run/walk will start on the Collins Pine lawn located at 500 Main Street and proceed down Chester’s historic Main Street to the finish at the Bidwell House located at 1 Main Street.

Participants will receive a commemorative T-shirt (first 400 registrants) and enjoy refreshments at the finish line. After the event, there will be a 4th of July Craft Fair at Chester Park from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. and a 4th of July Parade starting at 11 a.m. on Main Street. The Craft Fair is sponsored by the Chester Elks and the Parade is sponsored by the Lake Almanor Area Chamber of Commerce.

The one mile route down Main Street is open to participants of all ages and abilities, and adds to the excitement of the 4th of July celebration in town. The Fun Run is ARPD's largest fundraising event and all proceeds benefit District programs and events, as well as capital improvement projects, with an emphasis on recreation, parks and trails.

This year’s platinum event sponsors include Chase International Lake Almanor Brokers, Chester Car Wash, Collins Companies, Howard Construction, Knotty Pine Resort, Plumas Bank, Slusher Plumbing and Seneca Healthcare District.

Gold sponsors are Ayoob’s Intermountain Hardware, Buffalo Chips Pizza, Holiday Market and Lake Almanor Ace Hardware.

Silver sponsor is Kehr-O’Brien Coldwell Banker Real Estate.

Bronze sponsors are Berkshire Hathaway Lake Almanor Real Estate, Cal-Sierra Title, Gather Home, Timber House and  the Bidwell House B&B. Thanks to all our sponsors for their contributions!

Please join us this year for a great time and be sure to wear your favorite costume or sport your 4th of July colors and bling. Spectators are also welcome. Thanks for your support!

name: Chico Air Museum RUN THE RUNWAY! 5K and One Mile Run/Walk
description:
Do you feel the need?  The need for speed?!   If you do then this timed 1 mile run on the main runway at the Chico Regional Airport is the event for you. Or, if you want a longer race, choose the 5K option with the first mile on the runway.

The Chico Air Museum is a 501(c)(3) non-profit aviation and space museum located at the Chico Regional Airport. The museum is open to the public Thursdays-Sundays and charges no admission. Numerous aircraft and historical exhibits are on display, both indoors and outdoors. Volunteer docents are available to provide tours and explain the rich aviation history of Chico and Northern California.

RUN THE RUNWAY! is a timed mile and 5K for runners, joggers, and walkers which takes place on Runway 31R at the Chico Regional Airport. This is a rare and unique opportunity to run on an actual aircraft runway. Overall and age group medals will be awarded. The race ends at the Chico Air Museum which will be open to visitors following the race. Museum admission is always free.

Please come out and enjoy this special event. Thank you for supporting the Chico Air Museum.

Please Note: Runners who register after March 20th are not guaranteed a shirt. Please register in advance. There will be no race day registration.

name: Child Abuse / Foster Care Awareness 5k Run/Walk
description:
The Social Work Student organizations, Phi Alpha Honors Society, and Title IV-E program at California State University, Fresno are hosting a Child Abuse/Foster Care Awareness 5K Run/Walk, which will not only raise awareness about child abuse and Foster Care but also incorporate a wellness component for families. This dual-purpose event aims to both advocate for child safety and foster care, raising awareness of the need to support the well-being of families, caregivers, and foster youth. By promoting self-care and providing resources for mental and physical well-being, this event seeks to increase family and individual well-being. Proceeds will support next year's event to make this an annual event. 

Special pricing for children 9 and under of $25.00 - Discount applied during check-out.

name: Chingona Fest
description:
This event is a fundraiser for Chingonas on the Run and an opportunity to bring our community together through running and camping.

 Chingonas on the Run: Camp & Loop 

Where miles, mountains, and mujeres meet.

Join us for a weekend that’s more than just miles — it’s a celebration of grit, comunidad, and the kind of campfire connections that linger long after the headlamps switch off.

On Sunday, June 28, 2026, you’ll take on a 6-hour challenge to complete as many loops as your legs (and ganas) can handle within the 6-hour timeframe. Each loop is 4.16 miles with 728 ft of gain, winding through sweet single track trails in the heart of the Angeles National Forest, summiting Mount Hillyer each time you circle. The loop starts and finishes at basecamp where our aid station will be ready to keep you fueled, hydrated, and cheered on — every lap, every time. Click here to view route.

Note the cut-off to start the last loop is 11:45 AM. Chingonas have the option to set out for one last loop by 11:45 AM or hang out at basecamp to ring their cowbell to welcome the remaining finishers. As a reminder you are encouraged to run at your own pace and ability. We are here to support you on any goal you set for yourself within the 6-hour time frame.

 

 The Flow

Saturday, June 27, 2026:
Camp check-in opens 2:00 PM – 4:00 PM (no late arrivals). Find your spot, pitch your tent, settle in under the pines. Your campground fee is included in your registration, so all you need is your gear and your ganas — and if you don’t have gear, no problem! Email us and we’ll connect you with resources to borrow what you need.

Sunday, June 28, 2026:
The loop begins at 7:00 AM, weaving through that sweet single track with your Chingona crew towards Mount Hillyer. Each loop starts and ends at our basecamp aid station, stocked with snacks, hydration, and all the encouragement you need to keep going, loop after loop. Run your heart out until the clock strikes 1:00 PM — see how many summits you can bag before the final bell rings.

When the loops are done, it’s time for a post-run celebration. Gather for a hearty lunch meal, swap stories, laugh under the pines, and soak up that Chingona magic. You’ll walk away with a finisher’s medal and a keepsake to remember every brave mile and every unstoppable smile.

Closing ceremony will end at 5:30 PM, runners will be able to clean-up and depart between 5:30 PM - 8:00 PM (Note: Sunset is at 8:07PM).

 

 What’s Included

Trail Aid: Aid station at the start/finish of each 4.16-mile loop fully stocked with food, snacks, hydration, and high-fives.

Food & Fuel: Grab-and-go breakfast Sunday morning, dinner Saturday night, a hearty post-run lunch Sunday evening and grab-and-go refreshments throughout the event.

Welcome Goodie Bag: Festival Swag

Finish Line Love: A finisher’s medal — because your miles deserve to be remembered.

Photos: FREE event photos by a professional photographer.

Post-Run Celebration: Stick around for post-run celebration activities — laughter, storytelling, and community under the pines.

Campground Fee: Included in your registration — one less thing to worry about.

Parking Pass: Included in your registration.

Need Gear? No gear, no problem — email us and we’ll connect you to resources to borrow camping gear. We’ve got you, amiga.

 

 This is for You

Bring your miles, your messy, your brave. Bring your tent, your trail shoes, your hunger for connection and your wild, resilient heart. No gear, no problem — email us and we’ll connect you to resources to borrow camping gear. We’ve got you, amiga. This is where Chingonas lift each other up — loop by loop, mile by mile, under the endless Angeles sky.

This event is for women and those whose identity aligns with womanhood — trans, non-binary, and gender-expansive folks are warmly welcome. To honor this safe space, this event is closed to cis men.

description:
🌶️🏃‍♂️ Run Against All Odds: Cinco de Mayo Run! 🌟

This Cinco de Mayo, challenge yourself and celebrate resilience, community, and culture with the Cinco de Mayo Run Against All Odds! Whether you’re running for fun or for fitness, this event is all about pushing limits and embracing the spirit of overcoming obstacles—just like the holiday itself! 

Overview:
Run will sell-out QUICK! We will close off waves the moment they fill up. If waves are sold out, you can sign-up for the virtual run option or wait list.
This is a smaller, private group run with a cap per wave.
All paces and ages (under 18 with guardian) are welcome - Run or Walk!  
There's no equipment or setup, this is a pure run with our coordinators to support you in a warm, stress-free setting!
When you sign-up, we give you the support you need to help you achieve your goals and fitness. We also invite you to be part of our local run clubs that supports your fitness journey. 
Timing:
- Timing is Optional: You may track your time on an app (Strava, RunKeeper, Nike Run, etc) and submit your times with our easy form to be posted online. Or you can ask our coordinators to help keep track of your time. 
- No timing chips (This is a stress free run to support you in achieving your goals)!
What You Get (Swag Bag):
- Running T-Shirt (Shipped to the address you register with - US only)
- Finisher's Towel or Giveaway
- Finisher's Medal! 
- Digital Training Pack 
- Online Results & Certificate of Completion
- Invitation to Join one of our Local Running Clubs
- We now have Technical Running Shirts (Optional). These lightweight, moisture wicking shirts can be upgraded for just $5 more. 
Packet Pickup:
No hassle of picking up packets required!
-Swag shipped direct to your address (Please make sure you provide your full, correct US mailing address including apartment number and check spelling)
- Race bibs are provided on race day
When will I get my Swag?
You will get your shirt at your mailing address the week of your race.
Race Updates:
We will email you a final update the Wednesday before the race with final details and course maps.
Do you accept last minute registrations? (For those signing up 2 weeks before the race)
Yes, but please note that it takes time for us to ship your shirt. Your shirt will likely arrive after the run. You can wear any shirt you find appropriate to run the race! 
 
Wave Times: (Email Us Your Desired Wave Time: info@thebestraces.com)
(Waves filled on a First Come, First Serve Basis)

Wave B: 8:00AM

https://www.thebestraces.com/faq/

Virtual runs can be done any time and place of your choosing using any tracking device (optional). After you finish, you can submit your results to info@thebestraces.com to receive your medal!

Sign-up for more races and get a discount! 

Sponsorships & Promoting your Business:

If you're looking to become a sponsor, we'd love showcase your business!
https://www.thebestraces.com/events
 

Team Glo Volunteers:

If you're interested in helping put on runs for the Community and helping people achieve their goals, we invite you to join our team of volunteers, fill out the form here: https://www.thebestraces.com/volunteer-form/
 

Be part of the Journey!

Our Charity Initiatives. Find out more @ www.thebestracesjourney.com
Keep running. Every mile you log after the race, we'll donate $1 to one of the charities we work with! (Note that Fundraising is Optional)

name: CINCO DE MILE 5 QUE- FRESNO 5K
description:
Come and celebrate “5 de Mayo” at this UNIQUE EVENT! Join your fellow taco loving participants and run this SCENIC COURSE out and back along Woodward park. Course is on a bike paved trail and some dirt road/trail! As you cross the finish line, you will be greeted by a post-run FIESTA like none other!  MUSIC ENTERTAINMENT before, during, and after your run, followed by a FOLKLORICO DANCE demonstration. Whether running or supporting a runner, everyone is welcome to celebrate running, food, and community. For sure, a FUN event you don't want to miss! 

Our 5K is a 20-point CENTRAL VALLEY RUNNER OF THE YEAR event. 

All participants receive:

  • FREE TACOS for ALL participants!!
  • MEXICAN “AGUAS FRESCAS”
  • SHIRT  
  • UNIQUE MEDAL 
  • AGE GROUP UNIQUE AWARDS
  • EXTRA/ADDITIONAL MEDAL!!  Reyes Running Series! Collect all of them! 
  • 20 PT RUNNER OF THE YEAR SERIES EVENT (5 mile race)
  • DANCE ENTERTAINMENT (FOLKLORICO/ZUMBA)
  • ATHENA/CLYDESDALE AGE GROUP CATEGORIES
  • KIDS RACES INCLUDING A 10 METER "RUN" FOR KIDS UNDER 1 YEAR OLD
  • GREAT, RUNNING COURSE (WIDE OPEN, OUT AND BACK, DIRT TRAIL)
  • DJ, MUSIC, FUN!!

SPECIAL AWARDS FOR THE FOLLOWING: 

  • LATIN DANCE COMPETITION (Cumbia, salsa, merengue...)
  • BEST COSTUME COMPETITION  for 5 de Mayo!
  • CLYDESDALE (MEN- 225LBS)  AND ATHENA (WOMEN-185LBS) AGE GROUP CATEGORIES 

6:00PM    CINCO DE MILE 5 QUE RUN/WALK AND 2 MILE WALK 

5:45PM    KIDS RACES

                                        AWARDS

TOP 3 AGE GROUP CATEGORIES 5 QUE RUN AND ATHENA/CLYDESDALE GROUP CATEGORIES. NO AWARDS FOR 2 MILE WALK.   

                                        KIDS RACES!!!!

5:45PM- 400 meters (7–10-year-old)                   5:52PM-  50 meters (1–2-year-old) 

5:47PM- 200 meters (5-6 year-old)                       5:55PM-  10 meters (under 1 year-old)

5:49PM-  100 meters (3–4-year-old)

UNIQUE AWARDS FOR TOP 3  (BOYS/GIRS) ON EACH KIDS RACE!! ALL KIDS GET A SHIRT/MEDAL!!

Walking Registration & Packet Pickup:  THURSDAY, 04/30TH/25 (4:30-6:30 PM). FLEET FEET, Fresno. 

Race Day Registration & Packet Pickup:  FRIDAY, 05/01/25 (4:00-5:45 PM) GROUP ACTIVITY AREA                                

Information:  camposlove2run@yahoo.com           Race Director:  Jesus Campos 

Bakersfield runners, join us SUNDAY, MAY 3RD!  Bakersfield Race: bakersfield5que.com

(Distances are accurately measured using a Rolatape® surveyor's measuring wheel.)

description:
Come join us at the 3rd Annual City of Artesia 5K Run/Walk! The goal of our event is to promote health and fitness in the Artesia Community! We invite you to run or walk our event, meet new friends, and enjoy our Health & Wellness expo afterwards, featuring food truck, vendors, giveaways, and more! Event is rain or shine!

Race Bib Pickup: Participants will be able to pick up their race bibs early on Thursday, November 19 and Friday November 20 at the Albert O. Little Community Center at Artesia Park (18750 Clarkdale Ave.) during the hours of 5pm-8pm. Bibs can also be picked up the day of the race before 6:30am!

name: Clovis Memorial Run
description: This event honors our Military Servicemen and Servicewomen who made the ultimate sacrifice to secure our freedom. We also celebrate Active Service-members and their families for devoting their time and talents to our great nation. This event has something for every ability level: a timed 5K run or walk, a 2-mile walk, a kid’s ½ mile run, and a ½ mile Senior Walk and Roll. There is also a large resource fair with over 20 community organizations providing information on health and wellness for veterans, seniors, and families. Registration includes a hot pancake breakfast, event t-shirt, and beautiful patriotic medal for all event finishers.

name: Coffee Lovers Run 5K/10K/13.1 LOS ANGELES
description:
☕️For all the Coffee Lovers, this run is for you!

You’ll love the shirt we send you. Set a goal, bring a friend, and join this super fun 5K/10K/13.1 Half-Marathon!

 

Overview:

Run will sell-out QUICK! We will close off waves the moment they fill up. If waves are sold out, you can sign-up for the virtual run option or wait list.

This is a smaller, private group run with a cap per wave.
All paces and ages (under 18 with guardian) are welcome - Run or Walk!  
There's no equipment or setup, this is a pure run with our coordinators to support you in a warm, stress-free setting!
When you sign-up, we give you the support you need to help you achieve your goals and fitness. We also invite you to be part of our local run clubs that supports your fitness journey. 
Timing:
- Timing is Optional: You may track your time on an app (Strava, RunKeeper, Nike Run, etc) and submit your times with our easy form to be posted online. Or you can ask our coordinators to help keep track of your time. 
- No timing chips (This is a stress free run to support you in achieving your goals)!
What You Get (Swag Bag):
- Running T-Shirt (Shipped to the address you register with - US only)
- Finisher's Towel or Giveaway
- Finisher's Medal! 
- Digital Training Pack 
- Online Results & Certificate of Completion
- Invitation to Join one of our Local Running Clubs
- We now have Technical Running Shirts (Optional). These lightweight, moisture wicking shirts can be upgraded for just $5 more. 
Packet Pickup:
No hassle of picking up packets required!
-Swag shipped direct to your address (Please make sure you provide your full, correct US mailing address including apartment number and check spelling)
- Race bibs are provided on race day
When will I get my Swag?
You will get your shirt at your mailing address the week of your race.
Race Updates:
We will email you a final update the Wednesday before the race with final details and course maps.
Do you accept last minute registrations? (For those signing up 2 weeks before the race)
Yes, but please note that it takes time for us to ship your shirt. Your shirt will likely arrive after the run. You can wear any shirt you find appropriate to run the race! 
 
Wave Times: (Email Us Your Desired Wave Time: info@thebestraces.com)
(Waves filled on a First Come, First Serve Basis)
Wave A: 7:30AM
Wave B: 8:00AM
Wave C: 8:30AM
Late runners can run upon arrival (Please note our coordinators stay 3 hours after the first wave)
Are there any other Questions we missed?
https://www.thebestraces.com/faq/
Virtual Run Option:
- Our Virtual Run uniquely offers a Training Pack with Digital Tools to support your run. 
Virtual runs can be done any time and place of your choosing using any tracking device (optional). After you finish, you can submit your results to info@thebestraces.com to receive your medal! 
Race Bundle:
Sign-up for more races and get a discount! 

Sponsorships & Promoting your Business:

If you're looking to become a sponsor, we'd love showcase your business!
https://www.thebestraces.com/events
 

Team Glo Volunteers:

If you're interested in helping put on runs for the Community and helping people achieve their goals, we invite you to join our team of volunteers, fill out the form here: https://www.thebestraces.com/volunteer-form/
 

Be part of the Journey!

Our Charity Initiatives. Find out more @ www.thebestracesjourney.com
Keep running. Every mile you log after the race, we'll donate $1 to one of the charities we work with! (Note that Fundraising is Optional)

name: Compton Run Club- Connecting Compton Relay Race
description:
Event Overview:

The Connecting Compton Relay is a community-based, 13.45-mile (slightly over half- marathon distance) 4-member team relay race. Each member will carry and pass on batons to their teammate at designated exchange zones across Compton. The event brings together runners of all levels — from first-timers to seasoned athletes — to experience the power of teamwork, community pride, and fitness while exploring the heart of Compton. This is an unsanctioned race with no street closures. Each participant should have experience running/walking on sidewalks and streets through traffic, including at intersections.

Event Details:

Date: Saturday, February 28, 2026

Time: 6:30 AM meeting time - 7 AM race start

Start/Finish Location: Compton VFW parking area- 303 E Palmer St, Compton, Ca 90221

Parking: Street Parking 

Distance: 13.45 Miles (Slightly over Half Marathon Distance)

Format: 4-Person Team Relay (Women, Men, Co-ed) 

Registration:

Total team cost is $128.20. The team captain should register the entire team with the signup link above. At packet pickup, the team captain is required to bring waivers for the rest of the team. 

Race Concept & Course:

Participants will run a looped route that highlights many areas in Compton. Each leg will begin and end at a relay exchange zone staffed by volunteers. The course will emphasize safety, visibility, and community engagement.

  • Leg 1: VFW → North on Alameda → Left on El Segundo → Left on Central (Approximately 3.21 miles)

https://www.strava.com/routes/3453480572785629852

Exchange to Leg 2 at Centennial High School (2606 N Central Ave, Compton, Ca 90221- Front of School- Checkpoint 1) 

  • Leg 2: Centennial High School → Continue on Central → Left on Alondra (Approximately 3.16 miles)

https://www.strava.com/routes/3453465976112979924

Exchange to Leg 3 at Compton High School (Alondra side of School, Oleander/Alondra- Checkpoint 2)

  • Leg 3: Compton High School → Continue on Alondra (Approximately 3.45 miles)

https://www.strava.com/routes/3453466161731343848

Exchange to Leg 4 at McDonald's- (7357 Alondra Blvd, Paramount, Ca 90723- Alondra/Garfield- Checkpoint 3)

  • Leg 4: McDonald's → Left on Garfield → Left on Somerset/Compton Blvd (Approximately 3.65 miles)

https://www.strava.com/routes/3453466161737421288

Finish back at VFW


Event Goals:

  • Promote Health & Wellness: Encourage physical activity and teamwork within the community.
  • Highlight the City of Compton: Showcase local parks, schools, and neighborhoods in a positive light.
  • Foster Community Pride: Unite residents, organizations, and small businesses through a signature citywide event.

Race Packet Pickup:

Race packet pickup on the following day and time:

  • Saturday, February 21, 2026, from 10:00 am - 1pm- At Compton Airport- 901 W Alondra Blvd. Compton, CA 90220
  • Thursday, February 26, 2026, from 6pm-8pm- Centennial High School- 2606 N Central Ave
    Compton, CA 90221 (Behind the school at track area) (Track Thursdays) 

Participant Information:

  • Team Size: 4 members per team
  • Categories: Men's, Women's, and Co-ed 
  • Co-ed teams should include 2 women and 2 men 

Registration Includes:

  • Custom race bib & baton
  • T-shirt 
  • Finisher medal for each participant
  • Photos from the race
  • Post-race refreshments and music• Access to the "Finish Line Celebration Zone" at VFW

Post Race: 

Post-race food and music at the VFW to celebrate the event. 

Please Note:

The 4th leg for each team should wear the bib for time-tracking purposes. 

Full Route on Strava:

https://www.strava.com/routes/3453482244785098600

name: Concord California Turkey Trot 5K
description:
Diablo Valley Federal Credit Union (DVFCU) is pleased to welcome you to our information page about the Concord Turkey Trot, a 5K run/walk benefiting Loaves and Fishes of Contra Costa.

The event will take place at Newhall Park on Thanksgiving, Thursday, November 26, 2026, at 8 AM.  For the safety and enjoyment of all participants, registration for this event is capped at a TBD number of participants.  Everyone participating in the 5K run/walk course must have a paid registration, with the exception of children 2 years old and under, who will be in a stroller for the duration of the event. 

The course includes varied terrain, including grass fields, park pathways, and city streets. Those participating with strollers or pets will be asked to enter at the back of the start area so as not to impede those wishing to race for time. All 5K Run/Walk Participants will receive a tech t-shirt and a medal!

The race will take place rain or shine.  Once your registration has been paid, there are no refunds. This includes inclement weather or any other reason, such as injuries, illness, or personal emergencies.

name: Corona 5000
description:
From 1913-1916, the roar of engines and the thrill of speeds approaching 100 mph electrified Grand Boulevard in Corona, as up to 100,000 spectators cheered during the legendary Corona Road Races. This perfect circle in the heart of “Circle City” was the stage for automotive history. Now, 110 years later, Grand Boulevard is set to pulse with excitement once again!

Join us for the Inaugural Corona 5000, a vibrant 5K run and walk that revives the spirit of this historic course. Lace up your shoes and be part of a new legacy, racing or strolling the iconic loop of Grand Boulevard. 

This is a Race For the Ages, all ages. 

Don’t miss your chance to make history in Corona’s Circle City!

name: Coronado Rotary Low Tide Ride & Stride
description:
Celebrate the 29th Anniversary of the Low Tide Ride & Stride with a our 5K Course during the lowest tide of the month on the beach from North Beach down to the end of the Shores and back. Kick off summer with this fun, family-friendly, 5K chip-timed race. Run! Walk! Bike! Stroll! This Coronado signature event takes place along one of the top 10 beaches in the world and provides much needed funds with Local Military and First Responders being the primary beneficiaries. Drop your beach chair in Sunset Park along with your reusable water bottle. After the race, kick back and enjoy LIVE MUSIC, grab a snack, visit local vendors' booths, and more.                                                  

WHY THE 5K COURSE?

If you have participated in past Low Tide Ride & Stride events, you may have noticed military and civilian volunteers lining the beach along the State Park and Navy Base. They were protecting the Least Tern’s nesting grounds. You see, the Least Terns are an endangered species and their numbers continue to dwindle. Even the military must limit their training on the beach during nesting season March – September. According to the Audubon Society, since 1970 we have lost half of all bird populations globally. By keeping the course of the race off of the Amphibious Base, Rotary is protecting critical nesting grounds for the Least Tern and Snowy Plover. We are excited for race course -- less hassle, family friendly, and fun at Sunset Park!  We can’t think of a better way to bike, run, walk and celebrate the beginning of summer than the Low Tide Ride & Stride!. 

For any questions please contact the event organizer at info@lowtideride.com or call (734) 945-6443.

name: Corporal Javier Bejar Memorial Run     Reedley Police Department
description:
Join us as we honor the life and legacy of Corporal Javier Bejar, a Reedley Police Officer, Marine Corps veteran, and beloved member of our community who made the ultimate sacrifice in the line of duty.

This memorial run is more than a race—it’s a tribute to courage, service, and community. Every stride taken represents our gratitude for Corporal Bejar’s dedication and the enduring impact he left behind.

All participants will receive a commemorative race shirt and finisher’s medal, designed to celebrate his life and sacrifice. Whether you run, walk, or cheer from the sidelines, your presence helps keep his memory alive and supports the values he stood for: honor, commitment, and service.

Together, let’s run in remembrance and unity.

 

NOTE: Only the first 350 Runners are guaranteed a medal.

Any participant registered after 02/01/2026 is NOT guaranteed a shirt. 

 

Packet Pickup & Schedule

Friday, February 20th: Packet Pickup from 3:00pm - 6:00pm

Location: Reedley PD - Annex Building 843 G Street, Reedley, CA

Race Day Schedule (Saturday, February 21st):

6:00am Late Packet Pickup 

7:00am Ceremony

7:20am 10K Walk Start

7:45am 5K Run/Walk & 10K Run Start

name: Courage Triathlon
description:
Welcome to the 11th Annual Courage Triathlon! This year, we're expanding!

To support and celebrate the ongoing expansion efforts of Courage Worldwide, we're broadening our horizons and expanding our annual event to include virtual registrations! While you still have the option to join us in person to run, bike, and kayak to support Courage Worldwide's efforts, you can also now join us from wherever you live, expanding our net of support child survivors of sex trafficking.

 

When you register as a participant, you'll have the ability to submit your own times and distances for the activities you choose to complete! Want to run five miles to show your support? Log it! Are you hoping to paddleboard for two hours around your local marina? We'd love to hear about it! Interested in supporting our work but not so much in doing a full triathlon? Take a walk around your cul-de-sac, post a photo on Instagram, and tag us! This year, we want to see evidence of support for child survivors all across the country.

 

Participate with us in any way, big or small, to support us in providing residential housing and therapeutic services for child survivors of sex trafficking.

name: COVINA FUN RUN XXIX
description:
Join Us for the 2026 Covina Fun Run!
The Covina Rotary Club is proud to sponsor the 2026 Covina Fun Run at District Field Covina on April 25, 2026! In partnership with Covina-Valley Unified School District, Charter Oak Unified School District, and valued sponsors, our dedicated committee members are volunteering their time to create a fun, family-friendly, and health-conscious event that brings our community together.

How You Can Make a Difference
Since 1923, the Covina Rotary Club has been committed to serving and uplifting our community. Proceeds from this event directly support local youth programs, veterans, and other vital initiatives. Would you consider making a donation to help us achieve our mission? Every contribution—big or small—makes an impact, helping to fund teacher mini grants, youth programs, and other community-driven efforts.

Join Us!
Be part of something special—run, walk, sponsor, or donate to help make a lasting difference in Covina. Together, we can strengthen our schools, support our teachers, and promote health and wellness in our community.

Covina Rotary Charities is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization.

name: Cowboy 5K
description:
Saddle up for the Cowboy 5K, a Western-themed community race taking place on Saturday, March 7 at the Clovis Old Town Trail in Clovis, California.

Designed for runners, walkers, families, and first-timers alike, the Cowboy 5K brings together fitness, fun, and a touch of Western spirit in a welcoming and inclusive environment. Whether you’re chasing a personal best, enjoying a relaxed walk, or simply looking for a great way to start your Saturday morning, this event is for you.

Participants can choose between a timed 5K run or a 2-mile walk/run, making the event accessible to all fitness levels and ages. The course follows the Clovis Old Town Trail, offering a scenic, flat, and well-marked route through one of Clovis’s most recognizable areas. Volunteers and course support will be on hand to ensure a safe and enjoyable experience from start to finish.

Western attire is encouraged (but never required). Bandanas, hats, and a little cowboy flair are welcome—just be sure to pair them with comfortable running shoes.

All registered participants will receive a custom event t-shirt, a finisher medal, and post-race refreshments. Awards will be given to top finishers in the 5K, along with fun recognition for best Western-themed attire.

name: Crescent Moon Chase – 5K, 10K, 10-Miler, Half Marathon
description:
We're racing for the moon!

Race Details

Start Location: Claremont Beach, 5400 E Ocean Ave, Long Beach, CA 90803
Parking: Parking in the lot is $2/hour and starts at 8am, if you are running the Half/10m you can use the Passport app to pay for parking. Street parking is free.

Event Schedule

Saturday
1-3:00pm – Early bib pick-up on the 2nd floor at Sports Basement Long Beach (store discount sent via email the week of the event)
2100 N Bellflower Blvd, Long Beach, CA 90815

Sunday
6:20am – Bib pick-up opens 
7:00am – Half marathon & 10m start
7:30am – 5k & 10k start
7:35am – Registration & start line close
10:20am – Course closes (3 hours, 20 minutes for the Half and 10m)

Early start of 6:30am may be pre-arranged for half marathoners, email your request to events@hightideruns.com. All early starters will not be eligible for awards.

Out and Back Courses

5k & 10k: The 5k route is used for the 5k (one lap) and 10k (two laps) – 5k route
10m: The 5m route is used for the 10m (two laps) – 5m route
Half: The 5m route is run twice and the 5k route is run once for the Half – 5m route and 5k route

More about the Course

The beach path is an open course, so you will encounter others using it. When we start the race, please stay on the right side of the beach path. The right side is for pedestrians and the left side is for cyclists.

On-Course Support
A fully stocked water station is located along the course. The finish line will also have an aid station stocked with water, electrolytes, gels, and fruit snacks. We have a first aid kit at each station and all High Tides Crew Members have received CPR training. The turns are clearly marked with chalk, a runner turn sign, and a flag

Final Details

Bib: Please wear your race bib on the front of your shirt so we can track your time and send your pics!
Gear Check: You may leave personal items with staff at the registration tent. Please bring your own bag.
Medals: All finishers earn a race medal. 1st place medals are given to the overall 1st male and female in each distance
Results & Photos: An email with race results and photos will be sent the day after the race and earlier on Instagram. Race photos are free!

Join Us Again: Did you have a blast running with us at our low-pressure, high vibes race? We have themed races throughout the year in Long Beach, the San Fernando Valley, Orange County, and San Diego. Register for multiple races at a time to earn a discount. Check our full schedule.

Have Another Question? Check our FAQ page, it's probably answered there!

name: Crown City Classic 12K & 5K
description:
The Most Patriotic Race on The West Coast!

 

We’re thrilled to celebrate the 53rd year of the Crown City Classic 12K & 5K Run along the stunning Coronado Bay! Kick off your 4th of July festivities with a 12K (7.4 miles) or 5K (3.1 miles) run, and don’t forget that in 2026 our Crown City Kids Half Mile—open to racers 12 and under—will return to inspire the next generation of runners! Both courses start and finish in Tidelands Park, treating participants to picturesque views of the Coronado Bridge as they make their way along Glorietta Boulevard. 

 

The Perks of Participating:
  • Kick-start your 4th of July weekend!
  • Exclusive 2026 Event Tee
  • Commemorative Finisher Medal
  • Live Finisher Results
  • Access to Crown City Classic Expo
  • Overall and Age Group Awards

name: CSDR's 7th Annual Cub 5k Run/Walk hosted by the PE Department
description:
Spring Break is around the corner!  Start off your fun break by challenging yourself to do the Cub 5k Run/Walk! 

Community members, families, and non-CSDR students ages 13+ will register and pay the $10 race sign-up fee (per person). CSDR staff, students, and volunteers are free and do NOT need to register. All are encouraged to donate to help support our PE Department.  Proceeds will go towards the purchase of new PE equipment.  Our goal this year is to raise $1,000!

Here is how it works:

FOR FAMILIES of CSDR Students;

1. Register to secure your spot. Click on the Sign Up button.

2. Feeling generous? Make a donation to the CSDR Physical Education Department. Click on the "Donate" button at the top right of this screen.

3. Run/walk the distance with your family/co-workers/classmates on the CSDR campus.

4. There will be post-race activities in the Cave gym for the finishers from 11:00 am to 12:00 pm. Snacks and drinks will be provided at the pool pavilion during the run/walk event.

name: Cycle Through the Vineyards
description:
CYCLE THROUGH THE VINEYARDS 2025

 

Temecula Sunrise Rotary (a 501c3 nonprofit) is again celebrating Spring in the beautiful Temecula Valley Wine Country on Sunday May 3rd with our annual CYCLE THROUGH THE VINEYARDS 2026! And for our past participants, 2026 brings exciting changes! For the first time LORIMAR Vineyards will be our host venue for the start/finish, post-ride celebration and raffle! And we are again excited to award a raffle grand prize drawing of an AVENTON E-BIKE from AVENTON BIKES! And our local AVENTON dealer Bicycle Warehouse of Temecula has upgraded the ebike and warranty coverage to bring the value of this ebike to over $2,500!  Secondly, we will again offer a shorter scenic guided tour route of 13 miles for our intermediate riders. While there is no way to totally avoid the challenges of the vineyards naturally hilly terrain, the shorter route is designed to better accomodate some of our intermediate level participants. 

Lorimar Winery is a popular local winery known for its daily live entertainment and is nestled amongst the gentle vine covered rolling hills in the heart of Temecula Wine Country. They will be offering discounts on their wines (both flights and bottles) and food for our ride participants! We are confident that our riders and guests will find LORIMAR Winery a great venue to hold our post ride “happy hour”! This year we will also be celebrating AMERICA 250 and have a fun filled experience planned for our participants! We are truly fortunate to have such a picturesque location for our Cycle Through the Vineyards this year.

We are truly fortunate to have such a picturesque location for our Cycle Through the Vineyards this year.

name: Dashing for Donuts 5K Fun Run and 1 mile Kids Race
description:
I will be holding the fourth annual, Dashing for Donuts 5K and kids 1 mile fun run on June 7th! We will be running the same course as last year. It will be held on the El Dorado Trail from the new bridge at Missouri Flat Road. It is an out and back race. Once you're finished, you get a donut and a medal. The 5K race will happen first and then we will have the kids 1 mile race.  

All proceeds from the race will go to the National Ovarian Cancer Coalition, (NOCC) -Team Teal. I am a 16 year survivor of ovarian cancer and a team member of NOCC - Team Teal. NOCC helps all women diagnosed with ovarian cancer and educates along with supporting them.  

Packet pick-up will be at Kaia Fit, 4615 Missouri Flat Road #5, 4 pm to 5:30 pm on Friday, June 5th or 8:30 am to 10 am on Saturday, June 6th. You may also pick-up the morning of the race at the race location. 

The last day to register and guarantee your shirt size is: May 31st.

Dogs are allowed on the course but you will have to start in the back. Thank you for your support! 

Packet Pickup will be outside Kaia Fit in Placerville. 4615 Missouri Flat Road, Placerville.

Friday, June 5th, 4 pm - 5:30 pm.

Saturday, June 6th, 8:30 am - 10:00 am.

Sunday, June 7th; Race Day, 7:30 am by start line. The timer used is the one that is used by our Cross Country Finals. No chip needed.

Race Day will be great! Every participant will get a donut when finished along with cold water. Awards will be for the top three women, top three men, top three girls, and top three boys. There will also be age group awards for 1st-3rd place, 10 year increments.

Race Day:

8:00 am 5k starts

9:00 am Awards for 5k

9:05 am 1 mile kids run begins with awards immediately after it is completed.

name: Davis Moonlight Run
description:
Event Day:

Saturday night, July 18, 2026

Four Events:

  • 5K, 10K, 10 Mile, 2K (approx. 1.25 miles)

Registration Opens:

March 2nd - Deal Days will run from March 2 to March 13, 2026

Event Details:

The Davis Moonlight Run will take place at Schilling Robotics, 201 Cousteau Place in Davis. The event begins at 7:50 pm with the 10 Mile and 10K, followed by the 5K and 2K at 8:00 pm. Courses are flat and travel along city streets as well as Davis' well-loved greenbelts. 10K, 10 Mile and 5K participants with an estimated finish greater than 45:00 are strongly encouraged to wear a headlamp or bring a flashlight for visibility along the course(s) in the dark. At the finish line, participants will be greeted with a heavyweight finisher medal (yes, it's cow-themed) and live music. Post-race activities include refreshments (including pizza by the slice, available for purchase), complimentary sno-cones, beer samples (21+) and awards distribution (for age group and our unique special divisions; see below for more details).  A dri-blend short sleeved race t-shirt is included with each entry; we also offer the ability to upgrade to a tank top (men's and women's sizing; 100% polyester fabric). Please note that dogs are not permitted in this race due to our race insurance, unless they are service animals. Wheelchairs and pushed wheelchairs for disabled athletes are permitted. 

Your entry to the Davis Moonlight Run includes the following*:

  • T-shirt included in entry (option to opt-out and save $5)
  • Finisher's medal
  • Age Group awards 
  • Special Division eligibility
  • Post-race music, suds, and snacks
  • Finish under the stars! 

*One complimentary beer to those 21+. Sno cones available for everyone including those who do not consume alcohol or who are designated driver. Additional beers available for donation. 

2026 Start Times


6:30 PM – Race Night Registration Opens
7:50 PM – 10 Mile and 10K Start
8:00 PM – 5K and 2K Start
10:00 PM – Cut Off For Course Support
10:15 PM – Finish Line Breakdown

Note: at this time of the year it gets dark at approximately 8:40 pm.
Start times are subject to change. Last updated 12/17/25.

Packet Pick Up

Bib and T-shirt pick up is held on race night starting at 6:30pm. Arrive an hour prior to your race start to have sufficient time to pick up, warm up, use restrooms, etc. Remember, hydrate all day so that you are well-hydrated for your run/walk.

Beneficiary: Cancer Champions

A Change of Pace is proud to announce our continued relationship with Cancer Champions as our ongoing charitable partner. Cancer Champions is a 501(c)(3) non-profit dedicated to supporting cancer survivors through custom fitness, nutrition, and mindset programming tailored to the unique needs of those battling or recovering from cancer treatment. Donations to Cancer Champions enable the organization to provide survivors with expert guidance to complement traditional cancer treatment. A Change of Pace and Cancer Champions both believe in the powerful and proven benefits of exercise, and we are very happy to be able to deepen our relationship in the name of health, fitness, and quality of life.

Location & Parking

All races start and finish at the same location, at Schilling Robotics, 201 Cousteau Place, Davis, CA 95618. Parking (free) is available in the adjacent business parks off Cousteau Place on the east side of Cousteau. 

Course Maps

Scroll to the bottom of this page to view course maps. Aid stations along the routes (denoted by a W on the map) will offer water and Gatorade. Please carry fluids with you if you are accustomed to drinking them more frequently during your training.

Please note: Our race insurance for this event does not permit dogs, except for service animals. If your dog is a service animal, they are welcome to join you. Otherwise, dogs unfortunately should not be brought on the race course. They are welcome to spectate with you if they are leashed, comfortable in crowds and non-reactive to other dogs. 

Post-Race

After the event, each participant will be invited to enjoy one complimentary beer (ages 21+, please bring ID if you appear under age 30), a sno-cone, plus light refreshments. 

Overall and Age Group Divisions and Awards:

Awards will be presented to the top three overall finishers per gender (male, female, nonbinary) for each the 2K, 5K, 10K, and Ten Mile.  No overall or age group awards for participants who decline to give a gender or age. Overall awards for all distances are based on gun time. Age group awards will be based on net time.  Gun time is the elapsed time from the sound of the horn to when a participant crosses the finish line. Net time is the elapsed time from when the participant crossed the start line timing mats to when they cross the finish line.

  • Age Groups for the 5K and 10K are: 9 and Under, 10-12, 13-15, 16-19, 20-24, 25-29, […], 75-79, 80-84, 85+. Note: will extend to 85-89, 90+ if participants in these categories.
  • Age Groups for the Ten Mile are: 15 and Under, 16-19, 20-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59, 60-69, 70+.
  • Age Groups for the 2K are: 6 and Under, 7-9, 10-12, 13-17, 18-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59, 60-69, 70+.

Special Divisions (5K, 10K, 10 Mile)

- Cancer Survivor
- Davis Resident
- Woodland Resident
- Sacramento Resident
- College Student 
  • Any 2 or 4 year undergraduate, graduate, professional, or technical degree school/program is considered eligible
  • Open to those who are currently enrolled in a program (e.g. summer school) or who will be enrolled in a program for Fall 2025
- Adaptive Division for Athletes With Disabilities
  • The Davis Moo-nlight Races encourages participation in the event by athletes with disabilities.
  • We will recognize the top 3 athletes in the adaptive division, by gender, with a special prize. 
Notes:
  • It is not possible to enter more than one special division. If you are eligible for more than one division, you will need to pick one.
  • Awards are not mailed. Check race results before you leave the event. Scan the QR code on your race bib with your phone or use one of the available chromebooks to check results.

6:30 PM – Race Night Registration Opens

name: Davis Stampede
description:
The Davis Stampede takes place each year in February, and includes 5K, 10K and Half Marathon routes. We also offer a family friendly 2K (1.24 mile) fun run/walk division that is perfect for younger athletes, families, and walkers. Starting and finishing at Davis’ Playfields Park, the Davis Stampede is a great way to kick off 2026 with a commitment to fitness. Courses are mostly flat and take runners and walkers through east and south Davis’s greenbelts and neighborhood streets. Race amenities include finisher’s medals, half marathon pace groups, t-shirts, a post-race expo, and course water stations stocked with water and electrolyte replacement along the course.

 

Registration for the 43rd Davis Stampede opened on October 1, 2025

Please register early! The Half Marathon often sells out or comes close to it.

 

Start Times:

8:00 a.m. - Half Marathon and 10K
8:10 a.m. - 5K
9:00 a.m. - 2K 
last updated 9/2025; subject to change

Entry Includes:

Blend performance short sleeved t-shirt, finisher medal, chip timing, eligibility for division awards. Option to upgrade to a long sleeve technical (100% polyester) shirt for $8; available while supplies last. You also may opt out of the short sleeve t-shirt and save $5. 

Packet Pick Up:

You can pick up your packet (bib and shirt) on Saturday, February 21 from 1pm to 4pm at Playfields Park (race venue). We allow you to pick up for friends, and ID is not required.  You can also pick up on race day (Feb. 22) starting at 6:30 a.m. If picking up on race day, we suggest arriving at least one hour prior to your race start. We encourage all participants to have their QR code available on their phone for fast check-in. You can find this in your confirmation email. 

Safety pins will be available at registration. On race morning, please pin your race bib to the clothing on the FRONT of your body so that it is visible to timing officials, course monitors, and race photographers. 

Overall and Age Group Awards:

Overall awards will be presented to the top male, female and nonbinary finishers based on gun time. Age group awards will be determined by net time and will be awarded to the top three male, female, and nonbinary registrants per age group. Registrants may decline to state their gender and / or age, however, those entrants will not be eligible for age group or overall awards or results ranking in those categories.  Award pick up is available on race day; unclaimed awards are not mailed. Awards also presented to the top three finishers in each special division. See section below for more detailed information on age groups and special divisions. 

Participate Virtually:

Those who are unable to attend on event day or who would prefer to participate on their own schedule may register as a virtual participant. Virtual packets will be mailed on or about 2/25/26 and will include a bib, finisher medal for the division you designate upon entry, and t-shirt (if selected). Virtual participants are welcome to pick up their packets at the Saturday Packet Pick Up if preferred. The deadline to sign up as a Virtual Participant is Thursday, February 19. The last day to request a switch from an in-person division to the virtual division (in cases of injury, change of plans, illness, etc.) is February 21 at 11:59 pm and this may be done via email.  Virtual participants may upload their results online by following these steps: (1) search name in upper right-hand corner; (2) next to name, click 'edit time'; (3) input your finish time in the format of HH:MM:SS and provide other requested information. Times may be submitted from February 21 through March 22 (link will be available on Feb. 21), although you may complete your run/walk any time that works for you after time of registration. Submitting a time is optional and not required. There are no age group or overall awards for the virtual divisions.  

Half Marathon:


Half Marathon course cut-off time is 3.5 hours or 11:30 a.m. Those on a pace to finish after this time will be offered a ride back to the finish line.

Minimum age to participate in the Half Marathon is 15. Consideration will be made on a case by case basis for youth 14 and under to participate in the Half Marathon who are sufficiently trained; must be accompanied by an adult (who must be registered). Send your request to acopfoundation@gmail.com by February 12th.

Water/fluid stations will be located approximately every two miles and will offer water and electrolyte replacement. Please carry nutrition or salt with you should it be a part of your training/racing regimen. 

Strollers, Wagons, and Wheels:

Wheelchair entrants may participate in all divisions. Racing wheelchairs should start at the front and coordinate with event official; pushed or casual wheelchair entrants should start toward the back. Pushed wheelchairs should start towards the back. Adaptive Divisions in the 5K, 10K, and Half Marathon.  Please note: half marathon has approximately 1/4 mile on crushed gravel by Barovetto Park plus about 1 mile on trail (service road around Wildhorse Golf Course). 5K or 10K entrants wishing to push a stroller MUST start toward the back of the pack at the starting line, no exceptions.  In the 2K, strollers and wagons (for children) and wheelchairs are permitted. Wagons must have seatbelts if children are inside them. Those with  strollers should line up behind the runners who are participating without a stroller. It is not suggested that children under age 11 run unaccompanied in the 2K. 

Timing:

Because this even utilizes chip timing for all events, we remind participants that there is no need to crowd the start line when the race starts; your time does not start until you physically cross the mats at the starting line. All age group awards and results placements, except for the top overall finishers (i.e. first 3 per gender across the finish line), are determined by chip/net time.

Guides/Support Runners for Adaptive Entrants:

If you are a sighted guide for a visually impaired participant, or a support runner/walker for an entrant in an adaptive category, please do not enter the adaptive division. Support Runners (including sighted guides) must be registered for the event either as a standard paid entrant or as a support runner. To register for the support runner/walker category, select "Support Runner" choice at registration (end of list). Those registering as a support runner will not be eligible for age group awards nor be ranked by age.   In the case that support runners  wish to receive the full race experience (eligible for awards, ranked by age division, etc) in that case they should register for the distance they are going to run/walk (Half Marathon, 5K, etc) instead of as a Support Runner, but be sure to not enter an Adaptive Division. Email acopfoundation@gmail.com with any questions prior to registering.  

Notes:
- We suggest that support runners/walkers and guides wear high visibility clothing or a vest indicating that they are a guide or a support runner. However, it is not required. 
- Please do not register as a Support Runner if you do not already have an athlete you are paired with. At this time we do not have a matching program, but will post if there are adaptive entrants seeking support runners.
- Please email us at acopfoundation@gmail.com with any questions. 

Beneficiary 

The event will benefit Cancer Champions. Read more about their mission at https://cancerchampions.org.  

Volunteers

Volunteers are needed to help with a variety of tasks on race day, as well as at Packet Pick Up. Sign up on the volunteer tab. For more information about the opportunities we have available for interested volunteers, or to sign up as a group, please see the volunteer tab on our website here. 

Refund Policy & Race Rules:

Entries are non-refundable and non-transferable to other events in the case of illness, injury, or change of plans; event happens rain or shine. You must be registered for the distance for which you intend to participate.  We reserve the right to postpone, delay, reschedule, or cancel the event if unforeseen condition occur that would compromise the ability for the event to be held in a manner that is safe for athletes, volunteers, staff, law enforcement, and the community. Should the event be postponed, rescheduled, or canceled, refunds will NOT be offered. Read complete details here: https://runsignup.com/Race/28183/RefundPolicy

Because this even utilizes chip timing for all events, we remind participants that there is no need to crowd the start line when the race starts; your time does not start until you physically cross the mats at the starting line. All age group awards and results placements, except for the top overall finishers (i.e. first 3 per gender across the finish line), are determined by chip/net time.

Guides/Support Runners for Adaptive Entrants:

If you are a sighted guide for a visually impaired participant, or a support runner/walker for an entrant in an adaptive category, please do not enter the adaptive division. Support Runners (including sighted guides) must be registered for the event either as a standard paid entrant or as a support runner. To register for the support runner/walker category, select "Support Runner" choice at registration (end of list). Those registering as a support runner will not be eligible for age group awards nor be ranked by age.   In the case that support runners  wish to receive the full race experience (eligible for awards, ranked by age division, etc) in that case they should register for the distance they are going to run/walk (Half Marathon, 5K, etc) instead of as a Support Runner, but be sure to not enter an Adaptive Division. Email acopfoundation@gmail.com with any questions prior to registering.  

Notes:
- We suggest that support runners/walkers and guides wear high visibility clothing or a vest indicating that they are a guide or a support runner. However, it is not required. 
- Please do not register as a Support Runner if you do not already have an athlete you are paired with. At this time we do not have a matching program, but will post if there are adaptive entrants seeking support runners.
- Please email us at acopfoundation@gmail.com with any questions. 

Beneficiary 

The event will benefit Cancer Champions. Read more about their mission at https://cancerchampions.org.  

Volunteers

Volunteers are needed to help with a variety of tasks on race day, as well as at Packet Pick Up. Sign up on the volunteer tab. For more information about the opportunities we have available for interested volunteers, or to sign up as a group, please see the volunteer tab on our website here. 

Refund Policy & Race Rules:

Entries are non-refundable and non-transferable to other events in the case of illness, injury, or change of plans; event happens rain or shine. You must be registered for the distance for which you intend to participate.  We reserve the right to postpone, delay, reschedule, or cancel the event if unforeseen condition occur that would compromise the ability for the event to be held in a manner that is safe for athletes, volunteers, staff, law enforcement, and the community. Should the event be postponed, rescheduled, or canceled, refunds will NOT be offered. Read complete details here: https://runsignup.com/Race/28183/RefundPolicy

name: Davis Stampede Vendor Registration
description:
This is a vendor registration page for the 2025 Davis Stampede, taking place on Sunday, February 23, 2025 at Playfields Park. Vendor booths are 10' by 10'. Tents, tables, tablecloths and other items to be supplied by vendor. A site map and one-sheet will be emailed out on approximately February 18.

Expected Participation:

Approximately 500 half marathoners and 1,800 2K/5K/10K participants.
