description:
About our Event...

 

The Zeta Zeta chapter of Kappa Delta at California State University, San Bernardino, is excited to host our 16th Annual Shamrock 5K Walk/Run on Saturday, March 14, 2025!

The Shamrock Project is a national Kappa Delta initiative supported by collegians and alumnae to raise funds for both national and local child abuse prevention organizations. Our goal for this year’s event is to raise $20,000 to support the prevention of child abuse.

 

Eighty percent (80%) of the funds raised will stay in the San Bernardino community, supporting the incredible work of Children’s Fund.
Twenty percent (20%) will be donated to Prevent Child Abuse America (PCAA), helping to create a safer future for children nationwide.
By participating in this event, you are making a meaningful difference in the lives of children in our community and beyond.

 

Registration...

Registration fee: $45 per runner.
CSUSB single registration: $40 for CSUSB students, faculty, and staff (requires CSUSB email).

Groups of 5 or more: $40 per runner - All members must register at the same time to receive the discount (Single Transaction). 

Additional fees: Applied to the registration fee.
Day-of-race registration: $50 for all participants (CSUSB-affiliated or not).

Medals will be given out to runners once they complete the race. 

 

The day of...

Check-In Details

Time: Begins at 8:00 AM
Race Start: 9:00 AM
Location: Check-in tables will be set up north of Parking Lot G, near the tennis courts.

 

Parking Information
At California State University, San Bernardino, parking permits are required at all times (24/7). Guests have two options to purchase a $10.00 daily parking permit:

 

ParkMobile App:
Download the app on your mobile device.
Enter the code 7001 to purchase your permit.

 

Blue Parking Permit Dispensers:
Dispensers are located in the following areas:
Parking Lot D
Parking Lot N

 

Once you have purchased your parking permit, please park in Parking Lot G, located on the east side of the campus.

Important: Failure to purchase a parking permit may result in a parking ticket. Your parking permit is virtual, meaning your license plate will serve as your permit. There is no need to display or print a physical permit.

 


Community Event

After the race, join us for a community event on PE Lawn 1 with food, games, and music from 9:00 AM to 11:00 AM.

All are welcome—bring your friends and family for a fun-filled morning!
Supporting a Great Cause
 We are proud to host this event to raise funds for Prevent Child Abuse America (PCAA) and Children’s Fund. Your participation makes a significant impact on the lives of children in our community and across the nation. Together, we can help prevent child abuse and provide much-needed resources to children in need.  

 

Contact Information
If you have any questions, please reach out to the event coordinator, Alyssa Houghton, at kdzzcommunityservice@gmail.com.

We appreciate your support and can’t wait to see you at the event!

name: Kaweah Lake Bottom Trail Run
description:
Get ready to join the fun as we roll out the Second Annual Kaweah Lake Bottom Trail Run - a fun and scenic adventure along the empty Kaweah Lake Bottom! After an incredible sold-out inaugural race (two weeks early!), we're thrilled to welcome back our runners for another unforgettable day on the trails.

Enjoy breathtaking views, perfect fall weather (God willing), and a friendly community atmosphere as you take on either the 5K or 10K course. Whether you're chasing a new PR or just out to enjoy nature with friends, this event is all about having fun, great company, and a little bit of post-race celebration!

Delicious post-race food, music, and fellowship await at the finish line - all while supporting a good cause. Spots will be limited again this year, so mark your calendar, signups open May 14, 2026. This year will be even better than last year.

All proceeds to benefit St. Anthony Retreat & Conference Center. St. Anthony is a peaceful and naturally beautiful setting for individual and group retreats, as well as both religious and secular conferences and gatherings. St. Anthony Retreat Center provides meeting space, dining and overnight accommodations for up to 100 guests. St. Anthony Retreat Center is located adjacent to the newly built Santa Teresita Youth Conference Center. For more information about St. Anthony's and Santa Teresita Youth and Conference Centers please visit their website at stanthonyretreat.org  

Parking is limited so try to CARPOOL if possible.

All Finishers Receive: 

  • Lake Bottom Finisher Tee
  • Custom Wood Medal 
  • FREE Race Photos
  • Finish Line Snacks 
  • Chip timing with live results

name: Kayak, Koffee and Hike
description:
KAYAKE, KOFFEE & HIKE

Sunday, March 29, 0830 AM, FREE

Guided kayaking tour along the point loma inlet in the Morning followed by coffee, snacks and hiking in the afternoon in Cabrillo National Monument. let's enjoy what San Diego has to offer by exploring its rugged coastline by sea and land. We should see seabirds, sealions and seals on this trip. hiking in the afternoon. 

please be prepared with a sunhat, light jacket, change of clothes for this moderately strenuous outing.

name: Kerman Almond Festival Scholarship Fun Run/Walk
description:

name: Keyesville Classic 5k
description:
🏃‍♂️ Keyesville Classic 5K — 1st Annual Trail Run
The 1st Annual Keyesville Classic 5K brings runners of all ages and abilities to the rugged hills of the Southern Sierra Nevada for a true California trail-running experience. Set just outside Lake Isabella, CA, this event blends natural beauty, rolling terrain, and community energy into one unforgettable race day.

This is not a road race. Expect dirt trails, elevation changes, wide-open views, and a course that rewards grit and steady pacing. Whether you’re a seasoned trail runner, a first-time 5K participant, or a family looking to experience an outdoor challenge together, the Keyesville Classic 5K delivers a course that is approachable—but never boring.

The 5K is part of the broader Keyesville Classic weekend, a long-running celebration of endurance sports, outdoor lifestyle, and community connection. Runners will be welcomed into the same atmosphere that has made the Keyesville Classic a staple event in Kern County for decades.

Who It’s For
Trail runners & road runners looking for something different
Beginners tackling their first 5K
Competitive runners chasing podium spots
Families, friends, and outdoor enthusiasts
Come run where mountains meet history—and help launch the first year of what’s set to become a new annual tradition.

Run wild. Run local. Run the Keyesville Classic.

description:

name: Kit Carson Park
description:
Kit Carson Park in Escondido is a 285-acre urban park with a great mix of open fields, winding paths, shaded areas, and water features—an ideal setting for orienteering. The varied terrain creates fun navigation challenges while still being approachable for first-timers. Whether you’re brand new to orienteering or a seasoned navigator, this event offers something for everyone. Beginners will find welcoming courses and helpful guidance, while experienced orienteers can enjoy longer, more technical route choices.

Come explore one of North County San Diego’s favorite parks, sharpen your navigation skills, and enjoy a day outdoors with the San Diego Orienteering community!

Event Team:

  • Event Director: Sergri Vinnichenko
  • Course Setter: Elena Vinnichenko
  • Visit the Volunteer page to learn how to help with the event.
    • See "Volunteer" at the top right of the page. 🔝
    • Volunteers get up to a $20 credit for a race to cover their registration fee.
    • Volunteer roles explained in detail

Format: Traditional 

Map:  scale  1:7500  |  2m contours

Courses: Beginner, Intermediate, and Advanced

​Starts: 10am to 11am

Time Limit: Two and half hours. All competitors must return to HQ and download by 1:30pm so we know you are safe. If you don't check in before leaving, volunteers will search the course to ensure you are not lost. Please check in before you leave.

Scoring: Electronic punching will be offered. All participants must bring, rent, or purchase one. Controls will be AIR+ enabled. 

E-Punches: Rental electronic punches will be available for $5. Alternatively, you can purchase your own e-punch at our gear store for delivery to the event (use "000000" when registering).

Clinics:  An introductory clinic will be offered at 9:45 am. An experienced orienteerer will teach you the basics.

Registration: All participants must pre-register. All standard SDO registration policies apply.

Fees:

  • $20 for adults, $10 for juniors (under 21)
  • $5 early bird discount through midnight, Saturday, Jan 31st.

Closes: Registration will close at 10 am on Friday, Feb 20th, or when we reach our limit

Entry Limit: This event is limited to 100 participants. See the "Find a Participant" tab to see the registration list.

 

HQ Location:  33°04'27.3"N 117°03'45.9"W  - "Tree Lake Picnic area #2"

Parking: There is ample parking at the park.

name: Kiwanis El Segundo PTA Run for Education 5K/10K
description:
Register before price increase at midnight April 13, 2026 

Pre-Race Day Packet Pickup: Thursday April 23rd 5-8pm, Friday April 24th 11am-7pm 

Online Registration Closes at 8pm on Friday, April 24th.  
Race Morning Packet Pick Up and In-Person registration will open at 6:30am on April 25th.
  • 5K Run/Walk is an easy-to-moderate hill course loop through local neighborhoods on closed streets. The 10K Run essentially runs the 5K loop twice.
  • 1K Fun Run for kids ages 6 to 10. 1/2K Fun Run for kids ages 2 to 5. All youth, 10 and under, registered for the 5K receive a free Fun Run entry.
  • Event includes large Post Race Finish Line Expo.
  • USA Track and Field (USATF) Sanctioned Event (26-33-160500) with Certified Courses (CA21007TEB and CA21021TEB).
  • Chip timing. Mile markers. Multiple water stations.
  • This event is a USATF Southern California Association (SCA) 2026 Road Running Grand Prix Series Event.
  • Proceeds benefit the El Segundo Unified Schools, supporting students pre-K-12th grade. 
  • Start/finish: El Segundo High School, 640 Main St, El Segundo, CA 90245. 
  • All 5K, 10K, and Fun Run participants receive custom die cast finisher medals.
  • All registrants receive custom race t-shirt (while supplies last) and goodie bag.
  • Awards: Top 3 Overall Male and Female 5K and 10K Winner Trophies; Medals for Top 3 in each age category: 0-8, 9-10, 11-12, 13-14, 15-17, (0-12 and 13-17 for 10K), 18-23, 24-29, 30-34, 35-39, 40-44, 45-49, 50-54, 55-59, 60-64, 65-69, 70-74, 75-79, 80 plus.  Team type winners each receive special medals.

name: L.A. CADA Dream Run 5K
description:
The L.A. CADA Dream Run 5K is more than a race, it’s a commitment to a world where people achieve optimum health and wellness through unrestricted access to healthcare and recovery services. This community-driven event supports our Youth Scholarship Fund, helping remove barriers so young people can access education, leadership, and life-changing opportunities.

Rooted in L.A. CADA’s mission to save lives, unite families, inspire hope, and uplift communities, the Dream Run directly invests in our Youth & Family Services Department, which serves adolescents ages 12–17 facing substance use and mental health challenges. Through school-based prevention, early intervention, outpatient and intensive outpatient services, and comprehensive mental health support, we meet youth where they are, before challenges become crises.

Our work extends beyond youth to families and communities through education, family workshops, prevention coalitions, and youth leadership initiatives like Jóvenes Speak Up, which empowers young people to become peer advocates and community leaders. Every step taken during the Dream Run 5K represents compassion, perseverance, and respect in action. Together, we are building healthier families, stronger communities, and brighter futures - one stride at a time.

name: La Jolla Cove Swim
description:
Iconic Open Water Swim held in La Jolla, California the first Sunday after Labor almost every year since 1916. 

There are four swim events available on race day. 

  • 250 Meter kids race "Garibaldi Grommets"
  • 1 Mile "Sea Lions"
  • 3 Mile "Leopard Sharks"
  • 4 Mile "Whole Enchilada" Swimmers compete in both the 1 mile & 3 mile events  - there is about an hour between the 2 swims.

All swimmers receive an event t-shirt. All finishers receive a finisher's medal. There are Age Group Medals awarded that follow U.S. Masters Swimming age brackets. For the kids race it is by individual year. 8 year olds will only be competing with 8 years etc up through 12 years of age.

name: La Jolla Half Marathon & 5K
description:
The La Jolla Half Marathon is one of America's most picturesque and beautiful point-to-point races. Starting at the Del Mar Fairgrounds, the course follows a scenic coastal route before reaching the challenging climb to the summit of Torrey Pines State Park. The course then rolls atop Torrey Pines mesa, continues down through residential La Jolla Shores, and finishes at La Jolla Cove.

For those interested in a shorter option, the La Jolla Shores 5K offers a mostly downhill course and features some of the most scenic views of the last 3.1 miles of the half marathon course.

name: Lace Up For Learning
description:
Lace Up For Learning is a nonprofit that was started in 2024 by five 8th grade friends who believe in the value of community, the importance of education, and the power of running. 

The mission behind this annual event is to raise money for under resourced classrooms across the greater Sacramento area. In the first two years, participants, donors, and sponsors raised more than $30,000 -- reaching thousands of students, K-12. 

The 5k and 10k courses run on the beautiful, flat paved Parkway Trails in Folsom. The Kids Fun Run includes obstacle elements and takes place on a large grass field. Participants of all levels are welcome - from serious runners to community supporters pushing strollers or walking their dogs.

We look forward to meeting you on race day - and we appreciate your support for our mission.

name: Laguna Hills Memorial Day Half Marathon, 5K & 10K
description:
Join us on Memorial Day to celebrate all of the great Americans and their families and supporters who have earned the right to be honored and cherished on Memorial Day each year.  The event will have three timed-races on May 26, 2025. The Half Marathon is on a picturesque and challenging course that showcases the beauty of Laguna Hills and the surrounding cities.   The 5k and 10k runs will tour the streets of Laguna Hills, and offers a distance and challenge for runners of all ages and abilities.  Children can be a part of the event by registering for the Kids Run.

*** ALL RACES START AT 7 AM ***

name: Lake Hodges Trail Duathlon
description:
THE LAKE HODGES TRAIL DUATHLON RUN | BIKE | RUN

TRAIL DUATHLON Run | Bike | Run is our one of a kind experience during our annual Lake Hodges Trail Fest. Challenge yourself and compete as and INDIVIDUAL or bring friends along for the challenge and compete as a TEAM.

We are a CUPLESS race series. Please make sure to bring some form of hydration vessel for your event. There will be no cups at aid stations.

name: Lake Hodges Trail Festival
description:
THE LAKE HODGES TRAIL RUNS & TRAIL DUATHLON- RUN | BIKE | RUN

is an annual trail running experience you don't want to miss. We offer something for the whole family to enjoy. Choose from the Lake Hodges 50K, 15K, 10k, 5k, and bring the kids for the the 1 Mile Kid's Fun Run!

 50K is a great introduction into ultra marathons, ideal for all running levels.

NEW! 25K is a great day on the trails, ideal for all running levels.

 15K is a beautiful courses for exploring new trails and accomplishing race goals.

 10K course challenges the runner with a 1,000ft gain but with a beautiful reward of the view from the summit of Bernardo Mountain Peak.

 5K is an old favorite with a new twist, exploring the lakes shore. Great for a quick run or walk.

 Stroller Trail 5K a new way to run on the trails with your little one.

The Kid’s 1 Mile Fun Run is open to children 10 and younger. This is a non-timed run. All kids receive a finisher’s medal and other treats.

 Trail Duathlon- Run | Bike | Run is our one of a kind experience to a weekend of racing. Challenge yourself and compete as and INDIVIDUAL or bring friends along for the challenge and compete as a TEAM.

We are a CUPLESS race series. Please make sure to bring some form of hydration vessel to carry hydration for your event. There will not be cups provided at aid stations.

name: Lake Sonoma 100K, 50K, TS Half Marathon
description:
Join us in Healdsburg, California, on April 11th 2026 for the TERREX Lake Sonoma 100K, 50K, and Trail Sisters Half Marathon! We are excited to have adidas TERREX back as our presenting partner!

We are stoked to team up with Mountain Outpost to bring you full livestream coverage, athlete panels, interviews, and commentary from special guests!

Lake Sonoma 100K

The 100K course will start with a climb up Pritchett Peak with a water only stop at the top. Once you reach the summit you’ll head back down toward the Lake Sonoma Visitors Center and then up to the hill to South Lake Trailhead where you’ll embark on an out and back of the original old school LS course and then back down the hill to the finish. It’s the same great Lake Sonoma Relentless experience, only this time with a big climb to kick it all off!

Lake Sonoma 50K

It’s not worth it unless you have to work for it! The 50k start is located in the green space next to the Lake Sonoma Visitor Center (you can’t miss it). After a short road section to get the field spread out  the course then continues onto beautiful rolling single track trails. You will continue past South Lake, Island View, Warm Springs Creek, Wulfow, Liberty Glen and the Bummer aid stations, finally crossing the scenic lake bridge. Remember to save some juice for the last few miles, as you have a screaming downhill towards the finish. The race starts at 7:30am.

Don’t forget to enjoy the views! … and be sure to take a dip in the water to cool off. (but don’t drink!)

Trail Sisters Women's Half Marathon

The Trail Sisters (TS) Half Marathon is a women’s only event. It was created to foster encouragement and camaraderie amongst all abilities and experience levels. This out and back course starts with steep trail ascent to South Lake Trailhead, but also provides a speedy descent to the finish. True to its label, you can expect relentless rolling hills that will challenge your mind and body. description:

We are stoked to team up with Mountain Outpost to bring you full livestream coverage, athlete panels, interviews, and commentary from special guests!

Lake Sonoma 100K

The 100K course will start with a climb up Pritchett Peak with a water only stop at the top. Once you reach the summit you’ll head back down toward the Lake Sonoma Visitors Center and then up to the hill to South Lake Trailhead where you’ll embark on an out and back of the original old school LS course and then back down the hill to the finish. name: Lakewood Run
description:
Join us for the exhilarating Lakewood Run “Powered By Heart, Fueled By Community” 5K Walk/Run, 5K Ruck, and 10K Run! The Lakewood Run returns on Saturday, March 7, 2026!  This event is a celebration of physical fitness, community spirit, and personal determination. Whether you are a seasoned runner, a passionate walker, or a dedicated rucker, there’s something for everyone in this inclusive event. 

There will be delicious food, refreshments, live music, and race results, including a medal ceremony. Also, stick around and visit all our amazing vendors for a chance to participate in an opportunity drawing with great prizes! The Lakewood Run brings together runners, walkers, ruckers, and neighbors for a morning that’s more than just miles—it’s about heart.

 The Lakewood Run is presented by the Lakewood Sheriff’s Station and Soroptimist Int’l of Lakewood/Long Beach. Proceeds from the race benefit both charity organizations.

name: LASAA Mug Run - Altadena Forever Run
description:
LASAA’s mission is to organize athletic events for our members, which include Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department employees and law enforcement officers. We aim to promote health, fitness, and camaraderie among our members.

The Mug Run series began in 1993. At that time, it was a small event with an average of just 10 runners per race, primarily attended by law enforcement personnel. Over the years, participation has grown significantly, expanding to welcome members of the public. Today, more than 300 runners join us, and the Mug Run continues to foster friendly competition and positive engagement between law enforcement and the community.

Each year, LASAA partners with Sheriff’s stations across the county to host a series of Mug Runs. Each station brings its own spirit, culture, and traditions to the event. This year, Altadena Station is dedicating their Mug Run to commemorating the two-year anniversary of the Altadena Eaton Fire.

One year after the fire blackened the ridges above our town, the inaugural Altadena Forever Run stands as a symbol of resilience and recovery. It honors those who were affected, those who responded, and those who continue working to rebuild and strengthen our community.

The Altadena Forever Run welcomes everyone. Your participation, sponsorship, and presence demonstrate solidarity, remembrance, and hope. Proceeds from this event will be directed to the Altadena Station Unit Fund to support community-benefit initiatives connected to the Eaton Fire Survivors organization, as well as programs supported by the Altadena Sheriff’s Support Group. LASAA’s part in the Mug Run series is to create meaningful, community-focused fitness events and transfer the proceeds to the station hosting the run. Altadena Station manages how this support is directed locally.

Packet Pickup Location: Grocery Outlet Parking Lot Altadena

2270 Lake Ave, Altadena, CA 91001

Days: TBD

Hours: TBD

Race start time is 8AM, January 10th.

description:
Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department is hosting a 5K suicide awareness and prevention walk/run.  Our mission is to bring law enforcement personnel, family, and friends together and raise awareness of the support and resources that are available to those who struggle with suicidal thoughts.  It is important to break the stigma so that people do not suffer in silence and get the support they deserve because we are "Better together"! The event will highlight resources for law enforcement personnel and activities for participants to enjoy in the company of family and friends.

event T-Shirt,

name: Leprechaun Chase – 5K, 10K, 10-Miler, Half Marathon
description:
Let's celebrate St. Patricks Day together, chasing rainbows and pots of gold!

Race Details

Start Location: Alamitos Beach, 780 E Shoreline Dr. Long Beach, CA
Parking: Parking in the lot is $2/hour and starts at 8am, if you are running the Half/10m you can use the Passport app to pay for parking. Street parking is free.

Event Schedule

Friday
4-6:00pm – Early bib pick-up on the 2nd floor at Sports Basement Long Beach (store discount sent via email the week of the event)

Saturday
6:20am – Bib pick-up opens 
7:00am – Half marathon & 10m start
7:30am – 5k & 10k start
7:35am – Registration & start line close
10:20am – Course closes (3 hours, 20 minutes for the Half and 10m)

Early start of 6:30am may be pre-arranged for half marathoners and 10-milers only, email your request to events@hightideruns.com. All early starters will not be eligible for awards.

Out and Back Courses

5k & 10k: The 5k route is used for the 5k (one lap) and 10k (two laps) – 5k route
10m: The 5m route is used for the 10m (two laps) – 5m route
Half: The 5m route is run twice and the 5k route is run once for the Half – 5m route and 5k route

More about the Course

The beach path is an open course, so you will encounter others using it. When we start the race, please stay on the right side of the beach path. The right side is for pedestrians and the left side is for cyclists.

On-Course Support: A fully stocked water station is located along the course. The finish line will also have an aid station stocked with water, electrolytes, gels, and fruit snacks. We have a first aid kit at each station and all High Tides Crew Members have received CPR training. The turns are clearly marked with chalk, a runner turn sign, and a flag

Final Details

Bib: Please wear your race bib on the front of your shirt so we can track your time and send your pics!
Gear Check: You may leave personal items with staff at the registration tent. Please bring your own bag.
Medals: All finishers earn a race medal. 1st place medals are given to the overall 1st male and female in each distance
Results & Photos: An email with race results and photos will be sent the day after the race and earlier on Instagram. Race photos are free!

name: Liberty Bell 5k fun run
description:
Welcome to the 1st annual Liberty High School Band 5k.  The Liberty High School Band is excited to host this event as it will directly benefit the marching band, jazz band, concert programs, winter percussion and winter guard programs.

IN PERSON AND VIRTUAL RACE OPTIONS

This site is not accepting payment.  Please go to 

https://libertybell5kfunrun.itsyourrace.com/event.aspx?id=16236

for registration for this event. 

This years event will be both in person and/or a virtual run! For the in person, the race will begin at Veterans Park and participants will run on the Marsh creek Trail through Creekside Park and beyond for an out and back.  The race will commence at 7:30am and will be handing out medals the finish line. For the virtual run, you can run whenever and where ever you want beginning Thursday July 4th through Sunday July 14th.  All participants will receive a 2024 first annual commemorative t-shirt and medal participating!

Packet pick up is scheduled for Wednesday, July 3rd from 3:00-7:00pm at Fleet Feet, located at 6061 Lone Tree Way in Brentwood. ***Please note, VIRTUAL RACERS WILL NEED TO PICK UP THEIR SHIRT AND MEDAL AT PACKET PICK UP AS WE ARE UNABLE TO SHIP OUT RACE SAWG.  

This race is open to any and all who want to participate, as long as they are human.  For the safety of all participants, NO ANIMALS are allowed on the course.  Strollers are welcome when pushed by an adult.  Bring the family, young and old and run or walk with us! We can't wait to see you out there. 

Race Fees:
Children ages 3 and under are welcome to participate, no registration necessary.

Kids One Mile 
Kids under 12
January 1st - April 30th- $20
May 1st - July 3rd - $25
July 4th - $30
 
5k Dates and Fees
January 1st - April 30th
Ages 4-9 - $15
Ages 10-18 - $20
Ages 19 and up - $35

May 1st - July 3nd
Ages 4-9 - $20

Ages 19 and up - $40

Race Day Registration - July 4th
Ages 4-9 - $25

Ages 19 and up - $50


If you register on or after June 1st, you WILL NOT be asked for a t-shirt size.  You will be able to select a t-shirt from a variety of sizes at packet pick-up or on race day.  
Course Information:
For the safety of our runners DOGS ARE NOT ALLOWED ON THE COURSE.
Strollers are allowed on the course if they are pushed by an adult.

name: Liberty Celebration Swim
description:
Coronado’s Liberty Celebration Swim (formerly 4th of July Rough Water Swim) has been an iconic way to celebrate our Nation’s Independence. The swim takes place in beautiful Glorietta Bay Park (Open Water) . The event has a distance for every swimmer and experience level. The venue has iconic back drops of the famous Coronado Bridge. The course is nested in the southwest corner Glorietta Bay Park, with low wave/wake and current impacts, making this race experience fun and competitive for all athletic levels and is a perfect race for swimmers new to the open water scene. 

All participants receive a finisher medal, souvenir swim cap and race t-shirt!

name: Lighthouse Fun Run & Family Day
description:
Family Fun Day!

Find your fast feet – the 12th Annual Lighthouse 5K Benefit Fun Run and Family Fun Day is kicking off! This year’s scenic site? The gently rolling hills and tidy trails of Ancient Peaks Margarita Vineyards. Start at the stunning Ancient Peaks Barn and wind your way around the vines of this beautiful venue. Ideal for runners trying to set a quick trail time, or for wandering walkers taking in the views. 

Kids can run like rabbits as they race the half-mile or the 100-yard dash (6 and under), and jump for joy in the bounce house.

Stay to enjoy Kiwanis’ always perfect pancake breakfast, listen to music from DJ Trent, visit our vendor booths, and paint your heart out with the HiYa Rock Project, too! 

This event benefits Lighthouse Atascadero – a valuable program dedicated to serving the needs of our youth by building a safe and healthy community through Awareness, Prevention, Intervention and Education.

name: Logix Love Run Westlake
description:
The Logix Love Run supports Senior Concerns' Meals On Wheels Program. 

One of Conejo Valley's oldest and largest races is celebrating 32 years and over 1.6 Million Meals Delivered.

 

Event Date 
Sunday, June 7th, 2026

 

Awesome Race Swag for All Participants

- Custom Finisher's Medal

- Custom Love Run Shirt (Super Soft Shirt)

- Age Group Awards (for 5K and 10K)

- Pancake Breakfast

- Mimosa Garden (1 Mimosa Included Must be 21+ and Show ID)

- Free Photos

- Age Based Pricing for Kids Age 8 and Under in the 1 Mile (Registration Starts at $30)


Race Start Times 

10K - 7:00 AM

5K -  7:20 AM

1-Mile -  9:00 AM

Virtual - Anytime
 

Packet Pick-Up
We highly recommend that pre-registered participants (those that have signed up online before race day) pick up your packet on Saturday, June 6th from 11:30am - 4:30pm at Road Runner Sports (1714 Newbury Rd, Newbury Park, CA 91320). 

We do offer race morning packet pick-up beginning at 6:00AM. Please arrive AT LEAST 30 MINUTES PRIOR TO YOUR EVENT START TIME. Expect lines on race morning pick up.  You can pick up someone else's packet if you have a copy of their ID.
 
Race Location
2829 Townsgate Rd
Westlake Village, CA 91361
(between Westlake Blvd and Lakeview Canyon)

 

Your Participation Directly Supports Local Seniors in Need
Don’t miss out! Joining the race and fundraising is a wonderful way to give back and make an impact in seniors' lives.

description:
🌸 Bloom & Zoom
Long Beach Mother’s Day Run
5K • 10K • Half Marathon
📅 Sunday, May 10, 2026
📍 5400 E Ocean Blvd, Long Beach, CA

 
💐 Event Description
This Mother's Day, trade the brunch table for the finish line and celebrate with miles that bloom!
The Long Beach Mother's Day Run – Bloom & Zoom honors moms, caregivers, and all who uplift us—with ocean views, finish-line flowers, and CaliFlow’s signature energy. Whether you’re running hard or walking easy, this day is about movement, memories, and love.

Perfect for:

💖 First-time walkers
👟 Runners chasing PRs
👩‍👧 Stroller moms & multi-gen families
🌼 Anyone who wants to show up with heart

🏅 Finisher medals for everyone
🏆 Overall & age group awards

🌊 Scenic, flat out-and-back course along the beach path

Everyone!

name: Lookin' for a Cure Palo Alto
description:
Description

Join Us in the Pursuit of a Cure at the Lookin' For A Cure Palo Alto 5K!


Every year, Lookin' For A Cure 5k events light up cities across the United States. These events are not just about running, they are about igniting awareness, and unity in the fight against Ocular Melanoma. By participating, you're not only support groundbreaking research but also bringing together individuals affected by Ocular Melanoma.We are Lookin' For a Cure" in Palo Alto. Join A Cure in Sight on Saturday July 11th, 7AM-11AM at: 2452 Watson Ct. Palo Alto, CA US 94020. Help raise awareness and support the fight against Ocular Melanoma, the most common eye cancer in adults in the United States.  

A Partnership for Progress


A Cure In Sight collaborates with leading research facilities and dedicated physicians that specialize in Ocular Melanoma treatment. Together, we channel the net proceeds from these events into ongoing research projects and patient support programs. Your involvement directly contributes to advancing the quest for a cure. Walk shoulder-to-shoulder with Ocular Melanoma survivors, their families, and the medical professionals who care for them at the Byers Eye Institute at Stanford University School of Medicine. 

All ages are welcome to attend. Come run, walk, or stay in one place and play games at the Fourth Annual Lookin' for a Cure 5K at Stanford, hosted by A Cure in Sight and the Byers Eye Institute at Stanford.  Set up your team, invite your friends and family, start your fundraiser and you are off to the finish line. Proceeds from this event will support the Stanford Ocular Oncology Program. Stanford is a national leader in providing state-of-the-art care for ocular melanoma patients of all ages and has pioneered groundbreaking research advances. Prithvi Mruthyunjaya, MD, MHS, professor of ophthalmology who anchors the ocular tumor service at Stanford is also working hard at Stanford to bring this event to fruition.

The race also aims to spread the word about the importance of early detection by getting regular dilated eye exams. Ocular melanoma makes up approximately 5 percent of melanomas in the United States. It is estimated that between 6-8 people per million will be diagnosed annually in the Western world. 

Read more about the work Stanford is doing around ocular melanoma here.

Event Details

Packet pick up will be held at Road Runner Sports San Carlos located at: 1125 Industrial Rd, San Carlos, CA 94070. Details will be available soon. 

Race Swag

  • Guaranteed T-shirt, If Registered by June 27th.
  • Finisher Medal
  • Food & Drink
  • Course Aid Station
  • Commemorative Race Bib
  • Free Downloadable Photos
  • Official Finishers Time With Age Group Placements

Race day schedule

  • Registration 7 AM
  • Race start 8 AM
  • Announcements Awards 9:30 am

Free parking is available in the Byers Eye Institute parking lot on the corner of Embarcadero Rd. and Bayshore Rd.

name: Loop the Lagoon
description:
Fleet Feet is pleased to announce registration for Loop The Lagoon 2026 is now open!

Join us for a fun filled day with friends, family and school mates all while raising money for YOUR Vacaville School!!

All participants will receive a medal and are guaranteed the brand new Loop Tech Hat with their registration as long as they register by April 16, 2026. If not, any excess hats will only be available on race day after the race.
​

Packet pickup will be on 4/24/26 from 12pm - 6pm at Fleet Feet Vacaville located at 354 Merchant St, Vacaville, CA 95688. There will be race day packet pick up from 6:30-7:30 AM at Lagoon Valley park (Kids fun run packets available until 8:30 AM).  We highly encourage you to pick up your packet on Friday to minimize lines and for you to get your FREE parking pass!

RACE START TIMES
5K &10K Tower Challenge - 8:00 AM
2 Mile Untimed walk - 8:05AM
1/2 Mile Kids Fun Run - 9:00AM
1 Mile Kids Fun Run - 9:15AM

The 5K Run/Walk & 10K Tower Run will be at 8:00 a.m.  All runners will be lined up according to their pace. The lineup will be clearly marked by pace time. The main staging area for all race-day activities is at Lagoon Valley Park, 4627 Pena Adobe Rd., Vacaville, California.


Other race-day activities include community booths, kids zone with a petting zoo, music and other fun activities for the entire family.

Loop The Lagoon is a collaboration between Vacaville Public Education Foundation (VPEF) and Fleet Feet Vacaville who have joined together to raise awareness and support for children and our schools in Vacaville. 

Thank you for getting out and exercising and remember supporting this event raising money for YOUR Vacaville school!

name: Los Angeles Sunset Trail Relay | 5K & Kid Run
description:
For more Information go to: https://lasunsetrelay.com/

 

Get ready for an unforgettable evening of trail running at the Los Angeles Sunset Trail Relay & 5K! This race brings together adventure, teamwork, and breathtaking views in one epic event. As the sun sets over the city, you'll traverse scenic trails, soak in stunning skyline views, and take on a thrilling course through the heart of Griffith Park.

🏃 10 Mile Relay – Teams of 4! Gather your crew, with each runner completing the same scenic loop before passing the baton. It's the perfect mix of teamwork, strategy, and fun!

 

🏃 5K Solo Race! A thoughtfully designed route that balances challenge and enjoyment — perfect for experienced trail runners and those new to the sport.

 

Whether you're racing with a team of four or taking on the 5K solo, this event is the perfect way to push your limits, connect with fellow runners, and embrace the magic of trail running under the evening sky. With well-stocked aid stations, an enthusiastic volunteer crew, and an electrifying atmosphere, you'll have everything you need to make this race one to remember.

So grab your teammates, lace up your trail shoes, and join us for an incredible night of running, camaraderie, and unforgettable moments! Register now and experience the Los Angeles Sunset Trail Relay & 5K like never before!

 

Each Participant receives:

  • Scenic, and well marked courses

  • Panoramic views of Griffith Park, the LA River, and Glendale.

  • Ultra-soft, ultra-comfy premium gender-specific short sleeve T-shirt featuring the names of every team at the event!* 

  • Unique Finisher’s medal for all participants

  • Live Music

  • Prizes from our sponsors awarded to the top 3 teams (Relay Only).

  • Exclusive Captain, and Anchor Badge for Last Leg Runners (Relay only)

  • Special Award for Overall and Age Grade Division Winners (5K only)

  • Special Trophy for the team with the Most Spirited Name (Relay Only)

  • Free Downloadable Race Photos from our professional photography team

  • Chip time results

  • Course Aid Stations with medical staff

  • Food Truck

  • Custom Bibs

  • Enthusiastic Volunteer Support

  • Finish Line Fruit, Snacks, Refreshments, and Full Body Wipes

  • Flexible deferral and transfer options

  • Access to the exclusive Los Angeles Sunset Trail Run sale at Fleet Feet Burbank

  • Lifelong memories with friends!

 
*Must register by August 31, 2026 to have your team name printed on the back.

Awards

WHAT IS A VIRTUAL RACE REGISTRATION? A virtual race is a race that can be run (or walked) from any location you choose. You can run, jog, or walk on the road, on the trail, on the treadmill, at the gym or on the track (or even at another race). You get to run your own race, at your own pace, and time it yourself. Run on your own, or with friends! Your race bib, shirt and medal will be shipped directly to you. And your registration fee and fundraising efforts will go directly to help support victims of crime through our survivors hope fund. Register Today!

$40.00 Pre Registration | $50.00 Day of Registration -- Includes Shirt, Medal, Goody Bag to First 500 Pre Registered, Food ,Drinks, and Entertainment

name: LSA's Run Home 2026
description:
This is a fundraiser for Life Services Alternatives which provides homes and services for the I/DD community in the Bay Area.

 

Please register to race and donate, or just donate!

 

Life Services Alternatives Run Home

Life Services Alternatives celebrates 22 years after opening their first home with a Live Race Event

  • Race Distances -- 5K, 10K

  • Virtual Run Distances - 5k, 10k - for those who are unable to join on race day.

 

Register early before price goes up and to secure your T-shirt (Shirt sizes subject to availability).  Take advantage of $5 early bird special discount until June 3rd. 

 

Register for LSA's Run Home Here!

Life Services Alternatives, Inc sponsors this race and is the beneficiary. All participants are encouraged to donate and or raise funds for the Life Services Alternatives cause. If you are not a runner or are unable to run you are still available to donate to Life Services Alternatives!

 

About Life Services Alternatives

Life Services Alternatives provides exceptional community living and programs for adults with developmental disabilities. 
 
In our county, there is a housing shortage for adults with development disabilities. In the past 4 years, over 40 programs have closed due staffing issues, low government rates and the high cost of living in the Silicon Valley. A high percentage of adults with developmental disabilities live at home with their parents. Unfortunately, parents age, have health issues, or they can no longer care for their adult child. Parents worry about who will take care of their adult child when they no longer can.
 
Life Services Alternatives helps to alleviate those worries. We opened our first three homes in 2004 in Santa Clara. It was a goal of Life Services Alternatives to establish homes where residents could grow and thrive in a non-institutional setting.  We currently have 15 licensed homes throughout Santa Clara County (San Jose, Campbell, Santa Clara and Morgan Hill) that are home to men and women who are developmentally disabled. Our residents’ range in age from 20 to 80 years old with a wide range of disabilities. 16th home is in the process of renovation and retrofitting to meet the community home standards. Five of our fifteen homes are for individuals who have special health care needs and intensive support needs. Our remaining nine homes, are home to residents who need 24-hour a day, non-medical care and supervision. It is Life Services Alternatives goal to continue to open new homes in our county where residents can live their best possible lives. Your support is needed to reach our goal. Your donation is greatly appreciated and will help change the lives of a developmentally disabled adult.

This is a fundraiser for Life Services Alternatives which provides homes and services for the I/DD community in the Bay Area.

 

Please register to race and donate, or just donate!

 

Life Services Alternatives Run Home

Life Services Alternatives celebrates 22 years after opening their first home with a Live Race Event

  • Race Distances -- 5K, 10K

  • Virtual Run Distances - 5k, 10k - for those who are unable to join on race day.

 

Register early before price goes up and to secure your T-shirt (Shirt sizes subject to availability).  Take advantage of $5 early bird special discount until June 3rd. 

 

Register for LSA's Run Home Here!

Life Services Alternatives, Inc sponsors this race and is the beneficiary. All participants are encouraged to donate and or raise funds for the Life Services Alternatives cause. If you are not a runner or are unable to run you are still available to donate to Life Services Alternatives!

 

About Life Services Alternatives

Life Services Alternatives provides exceptional community living and programs for adults with developmental disabilities. 
 
In our county, there is a housing shortage for adults with development disabilities. In the past 4 years, over 40 programs have closed due staffing issues, low government rates and the high cost of living in the Silicon Valley. A high percentage of adults with developmental disabilities live at home with their parents. Unfortunately, parents age, have health issues, or they can no longer care for their adult child. Parents worry about who will take care of their adult child when they no longer can.
 
Life Services Alternatives helps to alleviate those worries. We opened our first three homes in 2004 in Santa Clara. It was a goal of Life Services Alternatives to establish homes where residents could grow and thrive in a non-institutional setting.  We currently have 15 licensed homes throughout Santa Clara County (San Jose, Campbell, Santa Clara and Morgan Hill) that are home to men and women who are developmentally disabled. Our residents’ range in age from 20 to 80 years old with a wide range of disabilities. 16th home is in the process of renovation and retrofitting to meet the community home standards. Five of our fifteen homes are for individuals who have special health care needs and intensive support needs. Our remaining nine homes, are home to residents who need 24-hour a day, non-medical care and supervision. It is Life Services Alternatives goal to continue to open new homes in our county where residents can live their best possible lives. Your support is needed to reach our goal. Your donation is greatly appreciated and will help change the lives of a developmentally disabled adult.

name: LUCHA RUN
description:

name: Make a Move for Water Presented by CLEAN International
description:
What:   Make a Move for Water this March! Help to provide and protect water worldwide. 
Where: Your own community! 
When:  March 1-31, 2026
Why?: Millions of people lack access to clean water. These people are spending their days walking long, dangerous distances to collect unclean water. Together, we can end this walk for water!
Can my club or business be an event sponsor? Yes! We customize sponsorship opportunities and would love to talk with you! Please contact us today at 1-833-246-8166 or engage@cleaninternational.org.

name: Make Scents: Do it yourself perfume workshop
description: Discover the art of fragrance. In this hands-on perfume lab. You will mix and match oils, florals, and aromatics to create a scent that's all you. No experts, no rules just creativity and a little nose for adventure.

name: Mammoth Bar Trail Runs
description:
"Standard distance. Mammoth vert."

Mammoth Bar Trail Runs take place on the single-track and double-track trails of Mammoth Bar OHV Area in Auburn State Recreation Area, in the Endurance Capital of Auburn, California.

Mammoth Bar is known for its steep climbs and descents, as well as it's beautiful American River Canyon views.

These are not your average courses. You get more vert per dollar! Yay!

name: Mammoth Bar Trail Runs
description:
"Standard distance. Mammoth vert."

Mammoth Bar Trail Runs take place on the single-track and double-track trails of Mammoth Bar OHV Area in Auburn State Recreation Area, in the Endurance Capital of Auburn, California.

Mammoth Bar is known for its steep climbs and descents, as well as it's beautiful American River Canyon views.

These are not your average courses. You get more vert per dollar! Yay!

name: Mammoth BUFF - Beer Mile Run
description:
In honor of what once was Oktoberfest’s Bier Run, we now host our own beer run to keep the party going. Participate in the run AND the ride to be entered into the BUFF Category for Mammoth TUFF. Scored as an Omnium on time.

Date
Friday, September 18, 2026

Time
3pm-4:15pm: Pick up bib and swag in The Village at Mammoth
4:30PM: Race begins

Race Entry Fee
$30

All participants will receive three beers/water for the run.

Distance
3 laps of Lincoln House building in the Village
Distance: 3 x 0.3 mile

Layout
Race brief @ 4:30pm
All runners start together @ 4:35 

Format
Back by popular demand are 12-oz beers and traditional format of:
Drink 12oz beer, Run 0.3mi, Drink 12oz beer, Run 0.3mi, Drink 12oz beer, Run 0.3mi, Finish!
You must run all three laps and drink 3x12oz beers to get a finishing time within 25minutes of the timing start. 
Sober? No problem! We will have 12-oz sparkling water cans available for you.

Awards
1st place, BUFFEST WOMAN & MAN, will each receive a special gift.
Finishing times will be calculated into the BUFF Category omnium for awards on Sunday, Sept 20th.

name: March for Marrow California
description:
We invite patients and their friends and families throughout the state of California to be with us in-person or virtually for our 16th Annual March for Marrow at the iconic Shoreline Village, in Long Beach, CA. We will run or walk along the beautiful shore and FUNDRAISE for the Aplastic Anemia and MDS International Foundation, Inc. (AAMDSIF).

AAMDSIF provides education, support, and hope for patients living with aplastic anemia, myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS), paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH) and related bone marrow failure diseases.

name: Mardi Gras Run - Run for the Beads - 5K, 10K, & Half Marathon by Califlow Runs
description:
🎭 Run for the Beads: Mardi Gras 5K • 10K • Half Marathon
📍 5100 E Ocean Blvd, Long Beach, CA 90803 – Granada Beach
📅 Sunday, February 22nd
✨ Let the Good Times Run! 

 
💜 Event Overview


Get ready to let the good times roll at the Run for the Beads!
This Mardi Gras-themed celebration brings the color, energy, and spirit of the season straight to the beach. Whether you’re chasing a new PR or just running (or walking!) for the fun of it, you’ll enjoy a vibrant course, festive music, and beads galore!

So grab your friends, dress in purple, green, and gold, and join us for miles of smiles, energy, and coastal charm.

 
💚 Event Highlights
🎷 Beads & Bling: Snag your Mardi Gras beads as you dash along the course!
🎶 Finish Line Festival: Celebrate your finish with live music, festive treats, and of course — King Cake!
📸 Epic Photo Ops: Pose with colorful backdrops featuring crowns, masks, and beads for your perfect race-day shot.
🎊 Festive Atmosphere: Music, decorations, and energy that make every mile feel like a parade!
🏅 Finisher Medals: Every participant earns a  finisher medal!

💧 Bead & Water Stations: Stay hydrated and keep the beads flowing every 2 miles!
🎭 Costume Contest: Show your Mardi Gras flair — prizes for Most Festive, Best Group, and Wildest Spirit!

 
💛 CaliFlow Experience


🌊 Professional Chip Timing – Accurate results for all distances
🎶 Live DJ & Finish Line Festival – Music, celebration, and good vibes
📷 Free Race Day Photos – Capture your Mardi Gras magic
🥇 Overall & Age Group Awards – Celebrate your speed (and style!)
👟 Stroller & Walker Friendly – Everyone’s welcome to roll, run, or stroll
🏁 Fully Marked Coastal Course – Flat, fast, and full of fun energy

 
🕕 Bib Pick-Up & Start Times
📦 Bib Pick-Up: 6:00 AM to  7:35 AM (Race Ready Athletics Tent)
🏁 Half Marathon Start: 7:00 AM
🏁 5K & 10K Start: 7:30 AM
⚠️ No late starts — make sure you’re ready to roll when the beads start flying!

  
🚗 Event Day Parking Information
🅿️ Beach lot parking available – rates  $2:00 Per Hour
💳 Pay at the machine or use Passport APP

 
☀️ Weather & Safety
This is a RAIN or SHINE event — because Mardi Gras doesn’t cancel for clouds!
(Only postponed for tidal waves, tsunamis, or zombie parades 🧟‍♀️🎭 — we’ll notify you by email if that happens.)

 
🎉 Join the Movement
Tag your moments with @CaliFlowRuns and #CaliFlowRuns for a chance to be featured!
Follow us for weekly giveaways and #FreeEntryFriday fun.

 
🎭✨ Run. Revel. Repeat.
Let the beads fly and the good times roll — only with CaliFlow Runs!

name: Martha's Village & Kitchen 20th Annual Thanksgiving Day 5K
description:
The Martha’s Village & Kitchen Thanksgiving Day 5K is an annual, family friendly run and walk held in Palm Desert, California and this year we are celebrating 20 years of giving back!

This beloved Thanksgiving tradition brings more than 5,000 participants, spectators, and volunteers together to raise awareness and critical funds in support of Martha’s Village & Kitchen and our mission to end hunger and homelessness in the Coachella Valley.

Race day is a full celebration featuring a live DJ and stage, trophy presentations, and a high energy finish line experience. Register as an individual, start a team, or join an existing team and get ready to run or walk for a cause!

Do not forget to capture the moment! Share your race day photos and videos and tag @MarthasVillage or use #MVK5K on Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok!

name: Matcha for Miles
description:
Spring energy. Good movement. Matcha magic.
This is your feel-good run to start the season right.

Matcha for Miles is our newest wellness event— a blend of community-powered energy and feel-good miles. Think: your favorite Saturday morning routine, but leveled up with DJ beats, friends, and a whole community moving together.

Whether you’re an elite runner, not-so-elite runner, stroller-pushing hero, or maybe you're in need of a hot-girl walk (yes diva!)… this morning is for you!

Happening two weeks before the California Classic Half Marathon, it’s the perfect shakeout for your race— or a chance to simply show up for yourself and feel good while we dive into spring.

Bring your people. Bring your energy. Bring your matcha sweet-tooth.

Spring is in the air, and there’s no better time to celebrate wellness, movement, and community— one mile (and matcha) at a time.

Let’s run, walk, vibe, and sip!

name: Me AND Mom 5k
description:
About the Campaign

Join us for the 2nd Annual Love & Time, Me AND Mom 5K Walk/Run at Liberty Station, where together we can champion women’s mental well-being in a vibrant, supportive community!

 

Bring your family and friends and be part of an uplifting day filled with purpose and connection. Every dollar raised directly supports free mental health services for women facing complicated pregnancies. We can’t wait to walk, run, and celebrate with you!

We’re thrilled to welcome children and furry friends! (Please help us keep the park clean by picking up after your pets.) Every participant will receive an exclusive event T-shirt and a finisher’s medal to celebrate their achievement—plus, special medals await our top three finishers!

Bib and T-shirt pickup is scheduled for April 24th from 3:00 PM to 7:00 PM at Road Runner Sports, 5549 Copley Dr., San Diego, CA 92111. During this time, participants will receive their official race bibs and event T-shirts. Please bring a valid photo ID or your registration confirmation for verification at pickup.

If you are unable to attend the scheduled pickup, you may collect your bib and T-shirt on race day. Early check-in will be available starting at 7:00 AM sharp at the event site. To avoid delays, we recommend arriving early and having your identification or registration confirmation ready. 

- Experience our scenic two-lap course around Liberty Station Park, beginning and ending at the lively NTC Park.

- Enjoy convenient open parking for all participants.

- Get energized by live DJ music throughout the event!

- Kids can dive into face painting, a bouncy house, and creative arts and crafts—fun for all ages!

- Refresh with complimentary water and snacks waiting for you at the finish line.

Don’t miss our vibrant vendor exhibits—discover resources, interactive experiences, and expert guidance to empower your self-care and mental well-being. There’s something inspiring for everyone!

Sponsorship opportunities are available. For more information, please contact Yvonne @ yvonne.meneses@meandmom.org

name: Mean Girls 5K, 10K & Half Marathon
description:
On Mean Girls Day, October 3rd, 2026 he asked you what day it was. You said it’s October 3rd.

Now lace up and run.

Welcome to The Mean Girls 5K, 10K and Half Marathon, a pink powered comedy fueled tribute to the most quotable high school ever. This event transforms the LA River Path into North Shore High where every runner is either trying to make fetch happen or survive gym class without being personally victimized by Regina George.

Presented by Jed and Ted’s Excellent Races.

Wear pink if it’s Wednesday. Wear sweatpants only if it’s Saturday. Do not wear army pants and flip flops unless you want everyone else to buy army pants and flip flops.

This is your chance to run like you’re late for Calc, dodge Regina’s bus, and earn a medal pretty enough for the Spring Fling Court.

Choose your challenge:

  • The Burn Book 5K - A fast and funny out and back perfect for anyone who wants to run, walk, gossip, or talk about how butter is a carb.
  • The Glen Coco 10K - Six point two miles of pure candy cane energy. You go Glen Coco. Treat yourself and your friends. None for Gretchen Wieners.
  • The Full Plastics Half Marathon - Thirteen point one miles of pure drama control. Stay hydrated. Stay cute. Try not to start a three way call attack. Cross the finish feeling like the new Spring Fling Queen.
  • The Multiverse Lunch Table Dash (Virtual) - Run from anywhere. Work. School. Your bedroom. Africa.

Costumes Welcome

  • Pink everything
  • Plastics energy
  • Mathletes jackets
  • Mrs. Norbury teacher vibes
  • Kevin G rap battle looks
  • Mouse ears because duh you’re a mouse

Community Vibe

This race is all about fun, connection, silliness, and giving runners a day they’ll talk about in group chats all year. No cliques here. Everyone can sit with us.

 

Parody Note
This event is a fan made parody inspired by early 2000s teen pop culture and is not affiliated with or endorsed by any official rights holders.

Welcome to The Mean Girls 5K, 10K and Half Marathon, a pink powered comedy fueled tribute to the most quotable high school ever. This event transforms the LA River Path into North Shore High where every runner is either trying to make fetch happen or survive gym class without being personally victimized by Regina George.

Presented by Jed and Ted’s Excellent Races.

Wear pink if it’s Wednesday. Wear sweatpants only if it’s Saturday. Do not wear army pants and flip flops unless you want everyone else to buy army pants and flip flops.

This is your chance to run like you’re late for Calc, dodge Regina’s bus, and earn a medal pretty enough for the Spring Fling Court.

Choose your challenge:

  • The Burn Book 5K - A fast and funny out and back perfect for anyone who wants to run, walk, gossip, or talk about how butter is a carb.
  • The Glen Coco 10K - Six point two miles of pure candy cane energy. You go Glen Coco. Treat yourself and your friends. None for Gretchen Wieners.
  • The Full Plastics Half Marathon - Thirteen point one miles of pure drama control. Stay hydrated. Stay cute. Try not to start a three way call attack. Cross the finish feeling like the new Spring Fling Queen.
  • The Multiverse Lunch Table Dash (Virtual) - Run from anywhere. Work. School. Your bedroom. Africa.

Costumes Welcome

  • Pink everything
  • Plastics energy
  • Mathletes jackets
  • Mrs. Norbury teacher vibes
  • Kevin G rap battle looks
  • Mouse ears because duh you’re a mouse

Community Vibe

This race is all about fun, connection, silliness, and giving runners a day they’ll talk about in group chats all year. No cliques here. Everyone can sit with us.

 

Parody Note
This event is a fan made parody inspired by early 2000s teen pop culture and is not affiliated with or endorsed by any official rights holders.

name: Meet at: Beetlejuice Musical
description:
He earned his stripes on Broadway… now the ghost-with-the-most is coming to San Diego. 

It’s showtime! Based on Tim Burton’s dearly beloved film, this hilarious musical tells the story of Lydia Deetz, a strange and unusual teenager whose whole life changes when she meets a recently deceased couple and a demon with a thing for stripes. With an irreverent book, an astonishing set, and a score that’s out of this Netherworld, BEETLEJUICE is “SCREAMINGLY GOOD FUN!” (Variety). And under its uproarious surface (six feet under, to be exact), it’s a remarkably touching show about family, love, and making the most of every Day-O!

name: Meet at: Brewery Festival at North Park
description:
Be a VIP at North Park’s Festival of Beers with early access to unlimited 2 oz pour samples and live music! Enjoy special brews from local breweries and in and out privileges.

The festival ends at 4 pm.

For ages 21+ only. 

This is a meet at event, no transportation will be provided.

name: Meet at: Mission Bay Bike Loop
description:
Cruise a scenic 3-mile loop around Mission Bay’s breezy and ocean vibes. This is a beginner friendly ride and all about fun! 

Please No E-bikes and please bring your own bikes and helmets. We will not provide those. 

For ages 16 and up.

name: Meet at: Savannah Bananas Game
description:
Watch as the Savannah Bananas put on a wildly entertaining, circus-like baseball show packed with dancing players, outrageous stunts, nonstop fan interaction, and unexpected twists that turn America’s pastime into a high-energy party.

 

This special ticket to sit on the Western Metal Supply Company building includes an all-inclusive Ballpark menu and drinks. 

Tickets for ages 3 and up.

name: Meet at: The Love Story Musical
description:
Based on the best-selling book, The Notebook Musical, tells a tale of two lovers who come from different worlds but share a lifetime of love.

Seats are located in the Balcony Section, Rows 2 and 3. For ages 10 and up.

name: Meet at: Up & Close with the Wild
description:
Behind the scenes experience where curiosity has no age limit. Learning, exploring and going a little wild. Come see where the magic happens.

The tour is 90 minutes long.

All adults and children of all ages attending MUST purchase the Behind the Scenes ticket. Ages 0-15 must be accompanied by a paid adult. Maximum of 2 children age 0-15 per adult in a party. Electric Safari Cart takes guests to off-exhibit, behind the scenes places. 

Tickets must be picked at Q-Zone.

name: Meet at: Whale Watching Tour
description:
3.5 hour cruise to see whales, dolphins, sea lions, and the beautiful San Diego harbor! January is peak sighting season for Gray Whales and Humpback Whales while they migrate along the California Coast. Whale watching ships have a 360-degree viewing open-air observation deck and spacious indoor and outdoor seating. 

The ship boards at 9:00 am and departs for the cruise at 9:30 am (you must be boarded at this time or the boat will leave without you). The cruise will return to the dock at 1:00 pm.

Please arrive early to make sure you have time to park and check-in prior to the boat's departure.

name: Memorial Day 5K, 10K & Kids 1 Mile Run/Walk
description:
This favorite Memorial Day running event takes place near the beautiful Diamond Valley Lake in Hemet, CA. This flat, out, and back course is perfect for your next PR or for those just starting their journey. Runners and walkers of all experience levels are invited to come out and enjoy the Memorial Day festivities! With a 5K Run/Walk (3.1 miles),10K Run/Walk (6.2 miles), and our iconic Kid’s Run (1 Mile), there is something for everyone!

Why Run The Memorial Day 5K, 5 Mile, 10K & Kids 1 Mile Run?

  • Flat & Fast Course in Hemet, CA 
  • Awesome and well-designed race bibs, shirts & medals
  • 10 minutes from Southern California Wineries
  • Lots of excitement in Old Town and Temecula’s Premier Mall
  • Locally owned & locally produced – Memorial Day 5K, 10K & Kids 1 Mile Race is a homegrown race!

Included in your registration:

  • Technical fabric, men’s and women’s race shirts
  • Custom finisher’s medal
  • Chip Timing
  • Support stations 
  • Post-race refreshments
  • Finish line expo

 

Race Start Times:

10K: 7:30 AM

5K: 7:45 AM 

Kids 1 Mile: 9:00 AM

name: Memorial Day Run 5K/10K/13.1 LOS ANGELES
description:
Honor, Remember, and Run for Freedom This Memorial Day, join us for the Memorial Day Freedom Run - a special event that combines a run with the powerful spirit of remembrance.  Whether you're running solo or with friends and family, this event honors the brave men and women who have sacrificed for our freedom.
Every mile you complete is a tribute to their courage and service.  With scenic routes, motivating challenges, and a community united in purpose, the Memorial Day Freedom Run is more than just a race - it's a meaningful way to pay respect while staying active. 
Sign up today to celebrate freedom, remember our heroes, and run for a cause that matters.  Together, we can make this Memorial Day unforgettable.

Overview:
Run will sell-out QUICK! We will close off waves the moment they fill up. If waves are sold out, you can sign-up for the virtual run option or wait list.
This is a smaller, private group run with a cap per wave.
All paces and ages (under 18 with guardian) are welcome - Run or Walk!  
There's no equipment or setup, this is a pure run with our coordinators to support you in a warm, stress-free setting!
When you sign-up, we give you the support you need to help you achieve your goals and fitness. We also invite you to be part of our local run clubs that supports your fitness journey. 
Timing:
- Timing is Optional: You may track your time on an app (Strava, RunKeeper, Nike Run, etc) and submit your times with our easy form to be posted online. Or you can ask our coordinators to help keep track of your time. 
- No timing chips (This is a stress free run to support you in achieving your goals)!
What You Get (Swag Bag):
- Running T-Shirt (Shipped to the address you register with - US only)
- Finisher's Towel or Giveaway
- Finisher's Medal! 
- Digital Training Pack 
- Online Results & Certificate of Completion
- Invitation to Join one of our Local Running Clubs
- We now have Technical Running Shirts (Optional). These lightweight, moisture wicking shirts can be upgraded for just $5 more. 
Packet Pickup:
No hassle of picking up packets required!
-Swag shipped direct to your address (Please make sure you provide your full, correct US mailing address including apartment number and check spelling)
- Race bibs are provided on race day
When will I get my Swag?
You will get your shirt at your mailing address the week of your race.
Race Updates:
We will email you a final update the Wednesday before the race with final details and course maps.
Do you accept last minute registrations? (For those signing up 2 weeks before the race)
Yes, but please note that it takes time for us to ship your shirt. Your shirt will likely arrive after the run. You can wear any shirt you find appropriate to run the race! 
 
Wave Times: (Email Us Your Desired Wave Time: info@thebestraces.com)
(Waves filled on a First Come, First Serve Basis)
Wave A: 7:30AM
Wave B: 8:00AM
Wave C: 8:30AM
Late runners can run upon arrival (Please note our coordinators stay 3 hours after the first wave)
Are there any other Questions we missed?
https://www.thebestraces.com/faq/
Virtual Run Option:
- Our Virtual Run uniquely offers a Training Pack with Digital Tools to support your run. 
Virtual runs can be done any time and place of your choosing using any tracking device (optional). After you finish, you can submit your results to info@thebestraces.com to receive your medal! 
Race Bundle:
Sign-up for more races and get a discount! 

Sponsorships & Promoting your Business:

If you're looking to become a sponsor, we'd love showcase your business!
https://www.thebestraces.com/events
 

Team Glo Volunteers:

If you're interested in helping put on runs for the Community and helping people achieve their goals, we invite you to join our team of volunteers, fill out the form here: https://www.thebestraces.com/volunteer-form/
 

Be part of the Journey!

Our Charity Initiatives. Find out more @ www.thebestracesjourney.com
Keep running. Every mile you log after the race, we'll donate $1 to one of the charities we work with! (Note that Fundraising is Optional)

name: Menlo Park Kids Triathlon
description: The Menlo Park Kids Triathlon (“MPKT”) is a triathlon specifically for kids ages from 4 to 17 years old. A triathlon is a race that consists of a combination of three sports: swimming, cycling, and running. The kids start the race with swimming at the Burgess Pool in waves (triathlon speak for groups) of 20 to 25  kids. From the swim, they run to the transition area to put on their helmets, shoes, and anything else they need. They then mount their bikes and head out to the bike course. When the kids are done with the bike, they head back to transition to put their bike away, and head to run round Burgess Park. They finish the race in the park by crossing through the finishing chute!

name: Merced River Canyon Run - Burma Grade and McCabe Flat
description:
Mariposa county's classic Merced River Canyon Race returns this year with two options for runners.  

McCabe Flat Flat out. This 5 mile race is from the Briceburg bridge to McCabe Flat campground and back (2.5 each way).  As the name suggests this race is about as flat as a race in the foothills can be. This race can be done at any pace but some will choose to try and set a record on the flattest footrace in the county. 

Burma Grade. This 9 mile race starts at the river level and climbs up the mighty Burma Grade (4.5 each way). This race offers the most elevation of any foot race in the county and leaves the racers with an amazing sense of accomplishment.  

Both races are on hardpacked unpaved roads and offer amazing scenery in the Merced River Canyon.

Note on location and directions, please take highway 140 to get to Briceburg. While there are other ways to get here, they are not recommend, especially not on race day.

name: Merry Miles-  5K, 10K,  and Half Marathon by Califlow Runs
description:
🎅 Merry Miles 5K. 10K. Half Marathon
📅 Saturday, December 6, 2026
📍 5400 E Ocean Blvd Long Beach, CA 90803

 

This festive coastal run is all about holiday spirit, good vibes, and giving back — plus, we’re collecting donations for the Long Beach Animal Shelter to help local pets in need. 🐾
Bring a toy, treat, blanket, or bag of food from their wish list (posted at check-in) and help spread pawsitive cheer to our four-legged friends waiting for their forever homes.

 
🏃‍♀️ Event Highlights
✨ Professional chip timing on a flat, fast course
📸 Elfie Stations & finish-line photo ops galore
🏅  Finsher Medals for All - Overall and Age Group Awards
🎅 Costumes encouraged! Dress festive, funny, or fabulously extra 

🎅 Costume Contest with Prizes
🍪 Holiday treats & hot cocoa at the finish-line festival
🎶 DJ Claus spinning holiday remixes all morning

 
🕒 Schedule of Events
Bib Pick-Up: 6:00 AM – 8:00 AM at the Race Ready Athletics Tent
Half Marathon Start: 7:00 AM
5K & 10K Start: 8:00 AM
🏆 Awards: 9:30 AM

All finishers receive a medal, free race-day photos, and yummy holiday snacks — whether you’ve been naughty, nice, or somewhere in between.

 
💝 Why We Run
Because giving back feels even better than crossing the finish line.
Your donations to the Long Beach Animal Shelter help keep rescue pets warm, fed, and full of holiday hope. Every mile = a tail wag of gratitude. 🐾

 
💬 Why CaliFlow Runs
CaliFlow Runs creates inclusive, affordable, and high-vibe races that bring runners and walkers of all paces together. We keep it low-key, coastal, and full of good energy — because fitness and fun should always go hand in hand.

 
🚗 Parking
$2.00 per hour in the beach lot or Street Parking is FREE

name: Michael Bazan Jimenez & Noah Lichwa Memorial Fun Run/Walk
description:
The 3rd Annual Michael Bazan Jimenez & Noah Lichwa Memorial Fun Run will be a fundraiser taking place on Winters Youth Day, April 25th, 2026 to help raise money for the Noah Lichwa & Michael Bazan Jimenez Memorial Scholarships. On June 9th 2022, we tragically lost two young men which effected our community deeply. We are bringing back this Youth Day Fun Run not only to raise money to benefit students at the local high school, but also to remember and honor the boys we lost that day. This will be a 5K fun run/walk, on April 25th, 2026 and starting at 7:00 AM. All funds raised will be given to the Scholarship and awarded at the Winters High School Senior Night. If you can't register on line, in person registration will take place on Friday April 24th from 5:00 to 7:00 PM at the Winters Community Center. All participants that register by Thursday April 2nd will be guaranteed a commemorative Noah Lichwa and Michael Bazan Jimenez Memorial Fun Run t-shirt. Participants who register after that will only receive t-shirts as supplies last, on a first come first serve basis. 

 

Race Day Schedule:

7:00-Shirt Pick Up and Late Registration

7:30 Announcements

8:00- Race Starts

name: Midway Shelter Winter Run / Walk ~ 5k, 10k and Kids Run
description:
General Info - December 5th, 2026


Join us for the annual Midway Shelter winter run. Event takes place at the Harbor Bay Ferry Terminal in Alameda on Bay Farm Island and supports a great cause. 


The run will take you along the beautiful shoreline of Bay Farm Island and is a flat out and back with views of San Francisco and the Alameda Main Island. the first half is on the Harbor Bay Road with closed lanes for runners and the return is on the trails


The Kids run for 12 and under will be a 1/2 mile course. Kids run will start at 9:45am and will follow a circular loop out and back on the shoreline trail. There is plenty of parking at the Ferry terminal and we will have snacks and drinks when the race is over. 


Packet Pick up and Race Schedule:

  • December 4th and 5th, 2026: 10:00am - 5:00pm Lauren's Closet 1420 Park St / Alameda, Ca. 94501
  • December 6th: 
    • 7:30am ~ raceday registration opens
      8:30am ~ 10k starts
      8:45am ~ 5k starts
      9:45am ~ kids 1/2 mile run starts
      10:00am ~ 5k and 10k awards
       

Midway Shelter provides emergency shelter to homeless women and children and is operated through a partnership with Alameda Homeless Network and Building Futures – learn more about our work by checking out our two websites, below!

Founded in 1989, Midway Shelter of Alameda provides a safe and supportive environment for women and children experiencing  homelessness. By pledging any dollar amount, in addition to your registration, you can support the Midway Shelter provide a safe place for women and their children. Your donation is tax deductible as the Alameda Homeless Network operates as a 501(c)3 Tax ID number 94-3078153)

 

http://midwayshelter.org/donate.htm
www.bfwc.org

name: MIGUEL REYES ELITE/FUN 5K Run/Walk
description:
11TH YEAR ANNIVERSARY FOR OUR MIGUEL REYES ELITE/OPEN 5K!! COME AND JOIN US AT THIS FUN, COMPETITIVE race in memory of a great person, runner and friend Miguel Reyes from Fresno, who passed away in 2015. Join his family, co-workers and friends participate in this 5K Run/Walk! This local race is considered "THE FASTEST, MOST COMPETITIVE RACE IN THE CENTRAL VALLEY".  We've had several Olympians who have joined us in the past and this year we are again expecting it to be a great running event. 

RACE AMENITIES:

  • $16,000 CASH AWARDS for top finishers (top 5 male/female overall, master runners, breaking course records...)
  • 30 pt Central Valley Runner of the Year event!
  • DRI FIT SINGLET SHIRT (Must be registered before July 15th)
  • UNIQUE MEDALS
  • FREE TACOS and Mexican "AGUAS FRESCAS", ICE CREAM!
  • ATHENA (>185lbs) & CLYDESDALE (>225lbs) CATEGORIES
  • TROPHY AWARDS FOR AGE GROUP CATEGORIES
  • PINT GLASSES (must be registered by 07/15)
  • CHIP TIMING EVENT
  • CIF HS CROSS COUNTRY CERTIFIED COURSE!
  • KIDS RACES including a 10 meter "run" for kids under 1 year old
  • $300 cash award for team with most participants 
  • Extra medal for those doing Reyes Running series 
  • MUSIC, RAFFLES, FUN!!
  •                                                                          $16,000 CASH AWARDS!!!

TOP 5 OVERALL (MEN/WOMEN)
     1st ($2000)
     2nd ($1500)
     3rd ($1000)
     4th ($850)
     5th ($500)

Top 5 overall excluded from age group divisions

MILE MARK CHALLEGE!

$500 for the FIRST MALE/FEMALE to pass the MILE MARK!

BONUS COURSE RECORD!

$2,000 for the FIRST MALE/FEMALE to break our COURSE RECORDS: 14:06 Evert Silva (2024), 16:05 Alma Delia Cortes (2022)

EXTRA BONUS TIME!

$1,000 for the FIRST MALE to break 14:00 and FIRST FEMALE to break 16:00. 

TOP 3 MALE/FEMALE MASTERS  (40+ YRS OLD)

1ST- $500

2ND- $250

3RD- $100 

$500 BONUS for first male/female MASTER (40+ yr old) to break our meet records of 15:42 (Juan Luis Barrios, 2023) and 17:26 (Argentina Valdepenas, 2024)!! 

Top 3 masters excluded from age group divisions. Top 3 masters are eligible for overall awards!

TOP 3 AGE GROUP (men & women)
 Very unique TROPHIES!! (<29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59, 60-69, 70+) MS, HS, COLLEGE.

Top 3 Clydesdale (man >225lbs) and Athena (woman >185 lbs) get UNIQUE TROPHIES!

Students (Middle/High School/College) are NOT eligible for cash awards!

Kids Races!!!! 8:00 am - ages 7-10 years, 400 meters. 8:05 am - ages 4-5 years, 200 meters.
                    8:10 am ages 3-4 years, 100 meters. 8:15 am - ages 1-2 years, 50 meters 8:20 am
                    under 1 year, 10 meters. All kids get medals, shirt and tacos!!

TOP 3 KIDS ON EACH RACE (BOYS/GIRLS) GET TROPHIES!

Packet Pickup:
Friday, July 24th (3:00-5:00pm). 
Fleet Feet, 9447 North Ft. Washington Road #106, Fresno.
Race Day Registration & Packet Pickup: Mt. View Shelter Woodward Park, beginning
at 5:45 am until 6:45am.
