name: Penn Valley Daffodil Race
description:
The Daffodil race has been a staple for the Nevada County community for many, many years. Offering a 5K and a 10K, the routes travel through the quaint little town of Penn Valley and across the green rolling hills on country roads. The 5K travels along the edge of Western Gateway Park, past the dog park, and finally to the park and ride for a quick turnaround for a return to the finish. The 10K begins the same as the 5K, but will take a detour through the park before heading to the park and ride. During the return, the 10K turns right and weaves through the rural countryside of Penn Valley before racing back to the finish. 

Penn Valley is known for its daffodils and green grass, and if the timing is right, runners will get to see both. April lends towards cooler temps, so runners can experience energy from the springtime air and community. How could anyone say no? 

The Penn Valley Chamber will be serving a pancake breakfast for a small cost and the Penn Valley Lions will be the course marshals on the road. Sierra TrailBlazers are organizing and handling entries, bibs, t-shirts, and awards for the day. A wonderful community project to help all of you get out to have a wonderful spring running experience.

name: Pi Day Run
description:
The goal of our events is to get people outside, moving and having fun.  Running, Math and Pie enthusiasts come together at the Pi Day Run featuring run/walk distances of 2Mi, Pi (3.14) Miles, and 2Pi (6.28) Miles.  We invite Science, Technology, Engineering, and Math students or clubs to have a booth/display to be voted on by the participants.  Cash prizes will be awarded to 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place booths as voted for by our participants. Proceeds benefit a scholarship fund at CSU Fresno for STEM Majors.

  • 2Mi, 1Pi, and 2Pi distance run/walk
  • T-Shirt
  • Medal
  • Fruit Pi (several flavors)
  • Costume contest
  • STEM Fair

name: Pier to Cove Swim
description:
Swim 1.5 miles from Scripps Pier to La Jolla Cove. This is an organized and timed event with awards to the top finishers.  It is an open water event and the conditions and temperature add to the challenge.  San Diego Lifeguards will oversee the safety of all participants.  At the finish, you will be greeted by LJCSC volunteers, awards for top finishers, breakfast, and participant swag. 

EVENT INFORMATION

Registration 7:30-8:30 AM at La Jolla Shores

NOTE: Registration Location: La Jolla Shores Beach, Kellogg Park, North End
(North side of parking lot; near north end bathrooms; setup on grass). Swimmers will walk from there to the Pier, about ¼ mile away.

The swim will start on the north side of Scripps Pier at 9:00 AM.

Swimmer safety is our first priority. San Diego Lifeguards will watch over swimmers from a boat, jet skis, and paddleboards.

"Beach" REGISTRATION and PRE-REGISTERED CHECK-IN is 7:30 - 8:30 AM

NOTE: REGISTRATION LOCATION:
LA JOLLA SHORES KELLOGG PARK NORTH END
(North end of main parking lot)

There is a large free parking lot at the registration area and parking is plentiful, especially if you arrive early. You can also carpool, UBER, LYFT, or have someone drop you off.

If you need a ride from La Jolla Cove to Registration , we will offer limited, free shuttle service from the Cove starting at 7:15 AM until around 8:15 AM. Shuttle service is not guaranteed, especially if you arrive late.

Restroom facilities are available next to the registration area at the North end of the Shores.

Restrooms and showers (cold) are also available at La Jolla Cove.

Swimmers may leave their swim bags at registration with event volunteers, and the bags will be taken to La Jolla Cove where you can pick them up at the end of your swim. They will be watched, but do not leave valuable or fragile items in bags.
*The La Jolla Cove Swim Club is not responsible for loss.

Electronic Timing will be provided.

*There is a 90 minute time limit for this swim. After 90 minutes, lifeguards will remove any remaining swimmers from the water.

Registration Categories:

"Regulation" is according to USMS rules. Neoprene swim caps are acceptable.

“Non-Regulation”: Swimmers may wear wetsuits, rash guards, fins, or masks and snorkels, etc.

Awards to the 1st place Overall male and female “Regulation” swimmers.
Awards to the 1st place "Regulation" male and female finishers in each age group.

We encourage young swimmers, but safety is our prime concern. Parental approval is required for swimmers younger than 18. The recommended minimum age for this swim is 16. Younger swimmers will be considered if they have an acceptable swimming resume. Approval is at the discretion of the Event Director.

Prior to registering swimmers younger than 18, please send an email to lajollacoveswimclub@gmail.com and include a list of their open water swimming experience. Approval will be at the discretion of the event director. If approved, the swimmer may register on-line.

An event swag will be guaranteed for the first 250 registered swimmers.

This event is for experienced ocean swimmers who are prepared for a swim of 1.5 miles in open ocean, “rough water” conditions. The San Diego City Lifeguards will provide safety support, but we cannot guarantee the safety of swimmers, especially for those who are unprepared.

name: Pincushion Hill Climb
description:
1 mile. Straight up. This will be a chip timed hill climb starting at the San Joaquin River Trailhead in the South Finegold picnic area (Millerton Lk SRA; end of Sky Harbor Rd) and finishing at the top of Pincushion Mountain. There will be a special prize for the Top 3 Male and Female finishers, age groups winners will receive awards as well as Clydesdale/Athena division winners. All runners will receive a custom finisher award and event shirt. 

Pincushion Hill Climb: Mountain Goat Edition! The Mountain Goat race is for those who like to go the extra mile or miles. Your first run up will be timed and scored for the regular event then you have until 12pm (4hrs total) to complete as many trips up to Pincushion Peak as possible. Your first trip down you must take the long way (just over 1.5 miles) after that you may descend the same route you take to the top. You must complete at least 2 trips to the top in order to be considered a Mountain Goat. You will receive a special finishers award and the top Male & Female runners will receive an additional award.

Your first run up will be timed and scored for the regular event then you have until 12pm (4hrs total) to complete as many trips up to Pincushion Peak as possible. Your first trip down you must take the long way (just over 1.5 miles) after that you may descend the same route you take to the top. You will receive a special finishers award and the top Male & Female runners will receive an additional award.

name: Pleasanton Run for Education
description:
Race Day is April 19, 2026

Registration opens January 20

The Pleasanton Run for Education is an event designed for the entire community. The 14th Annual event will offers four distances: a 2 Mile, a 5K (3.1 mile) Run or Walk, 10K (6.2 Mile) Run, and a Kids' 1/4 Mile Challenge (3-10 years).  The 2 Mile, 5K  are stroller and walker-friendly events. The 10K is geared towards runners, is stroller-friendly, and entrants have 1 hour 45 minutes to complete the course).

Race Information

DATE –  April 19, 2026 

 

LOCATION - Pleasanton Middle School, Pleasanton, CA 94566

 

START TIMES  - 10K - 8 am; 5K/2 Mile - 8:10/15 am; Kids Challenge - 9:20 am
Note: Late starts are not permitted as roadways must reopen to traffic promptly. Please arrive at the start/finish area at least one hour early to ensure you do not miss the start. Allow additional time for parking and walking to the site from the various downtown options. No parking will be allowed at Pleasanton Middle School or Hearst Elementary school

 

2 Mile, 5K, 10K & ENTRY INCLUDES

Race entry includes a short sleeve performance blend t-shirt (cotton/polyester blend), race timing (5K/10K), commemorative bib number, eligibility for age group and overall awards (5K/10K), finisher medal, and post-race refreshments. All ages are welcome to participate in these three divisions; there is no minimum age. Option to upgrade to a technical race t-shirt (tri-blend poly/cotton/rayon jersey) available in men's  sizing for $10.00. One may opt-out of the t-shirt and save $5.00.

Age divisions for awards for the 5K will be: 7 and Under, 8-9, 10-11, 12-13, 14-15, 16-19, 20-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59, 60-69, 70-79, 80+. Age divisions for the 10K will be 11 and Under, 12-15, 16-19, 20-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59, 60-69, 70+.

The top three finishers per gender (male, female, nonbinary) will be awarded a medal to commemorate their top finish in their age division. Age group awards will be based on net (elapsed) time. Overall winners (top finisher per gender across the finish line) will be recognized based on Gun Time. The 2 Mile will not be timed and no awards will be presented.

 
KIDS' CHALLENGE ENTRY INCLUDES

The Kids' Challenge is a 1/4 mile fun run (no times or places kept) for children ages 3 to 10. Entry includes a short sleeve t-shirt, commemorative bib number, finisher medal, and post-race refreshments.  Start Time: 9:20 am.

SNOOZE FOR SCHOOLS
For those with schedule conflicts or who prefer to participate on their own time, this category offers members of the community the chance to support the event without attending on race day. This includes a T-shirt (but can be opted out of to save $5). Note: shirts are not mailed. You may pick up your shirt(s) at Packet Pick Up on Saturday, April 18. This category is a great option for people who wish to support PPIE without any running or walking involved!


PLEASANTON UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT EMPLOYEES

All staff employed by the PUSD are offered a reduced-rate entry. Those registering with PUSD pricing ("PUSD 5K," "PUSD 10K," or "PUSD 2 Mile" categories) must show their PUSD ID Badge at Packet Pick Up to receive bib and t-shirt. The PUSD Staff discount is available through Thursday, April 16th at 11:59 pm. Please note: the discount is offered to the person employed only, not family members of the PUSD employee  

PACKET PICK UP

Race packet pick up will be held on Saturday, April 18th at Pleasanton Middle School (PMS) from 11:00am to 3:00pm. You can also pick up packet on event day at Pleasanton Middle School near start/finish line starting from 6:30 am onwards. Plan on arriving at registration 75 minutes early if picking up your bib (or registering) on event day (allow additional time for parking). ID is not required to pick up packets and you may pick up for friends or family. The race packet will include your bib number and t-shirt.

 

FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

 

Q: Are dogs permitted?
A: Dogs are not permitted on the Pleasanton Middle School, with an exception only for service dogs.

 

Q: Can I push my infant in a stroller in the 5K? 
A: Yes.

 

Q: My 9 year old wants to run the 5K. Do I need to register to run alongside them?
A: Yes, all participants on the 2 Mile, 5K, and 10K courses must be officially registered. Additionally, we do not advise that children 11 or younger participate in the 2 Mile, 5K, or 10K without adult supervision. 

 

Q: Can I walk the 2 Mile?
A: Yes, the 2 Mile and 5K are walker-friendly. The 10K is designated as a run and has a 1 hour 45 minute cut-off time. 

 

Q: Does the race entry include a shirt?
A: Yes, all entries include a unisex (men's/youth) short sleeve performance blend t-shirt (cotton/poly blend). You may opt out of the t-shirt and save $5.00 on your entry. You may also upgrade to a technical (poly/cotton/rayon jersey blend) short-sleeve t-shirt (men's sizing) for an additional $10.00; available while sizes last. 

 

Q: I cannot attend the Packet Pick Up on Saturday. May I pick up at another time?
A: We offer race morning pick up near the start/finish at Pleasanton Middle School for those who cannot attend on Saturday. You may also have a friend or family member pick up for you on Saturday during the Packet Pick Up. 

 

Q: I cannot remember if I registered. Is there a way to look this up? 
Yes - use the participant look-up here.

 

Q: Where can I look up past race results?
View past results here (scroll to bottom on mobile; view list in right-hand column on desktop)

 

Q: I registered for the event but can no longer make it due to illness/scheduling conflict. May I obtain a refund? 
A: All entries are non refundable. You are welcome to pick up your shirt at packet pick up, or, you may gift your entry to a friend or family member.  To gift your entry, follow these steps: (1) obtain the first and last name plus email address of the person you wish to gift your entry to (2) email this information to our timing company with your request  no later than Tuesday, April 14th (3) upon receipt, they will respond and transfer your entry to the new participant. The new participant will receive an email indicating you have gifted your entry and they will be prompted to follow steps online to become officially registered.

description:
Free Community Event • 5K
📍 5100 E Ocean Blvd, Granada Beach (Rosie’s Dog Beach), Long Beach, CA 90803

Get ready for good energy, ocean breezes, and a little bit of Long Beach weirdness.

Popsicle Dash is not just a run — it’s a whole mood. This free 5K community event celebrates movement, sunshine, and the laid-back, colorful spirit of Long Beach. Walk, jog, or run — all paces welcome.

FREE Popsicles at the finish line

 
🏁 Event Perks
🌊 Flat, fast beach path with ocean views
⏱ Professionally chip-timed event with live results
🏅 Finisher medals for all participants
🥇 Overall awards for top 3 male & female finishers
🏆 Age group awards (top 3 in each 10-year bracket)
🍧 Popsicles at the finish line
📷 Free race photos
🍼 Stroller- and walker-friendly


 
🔥 🏖 “Most Extra Costume Contest”  🏖 🔥


Any costume. Any vibe. You choose.

Show up in your wildest, weirdest, most over-the-top look. Think:
🏄‍♂️ Hawaiian shirts & beach party vibes
🌈 Neon retro fits
🦩 Flamingos, inflatables, or totally random accessories
🎶 90s LBC throwback looks

🏆 Winners crowned post-run — plus ultimate bragging rights for being the most extra.

 
📍 Check-In & Start Time
🕕 Check-In Opens: 6:30 AM
📍 5100 E Ocean blvd Long Beach, CA 90803 (Granada Beach)
🏁 5K Start: 8:00AM

 
🚗 Parking Information
✅ Free street parking available
🅿️ Beach lot parking: $2.00 per hour (pay at the machine)

 
🫶 Safety First
We prioritize participant safety at every event:
💧 Water stations on course
🚑 Medical staff  at the finish

 
🎉 Ready to Run, Chill & Cool Off?
Bring your friends, your family, your pup, and your best summer energy.
Run the miles. Earn the popsicle.

name: Pre Reg 2027 Heroes 4 Hearing 5K
description:
This is the registration page for 2027 - if you are looking for info on the Aug 16th 2026- please go to 

https://runsignup.com/Race/CA/FountainValley/Heroes4Hearing

 

Place

Shoreline Aquatic Park
200 Aquarium Way, Long Beach, CA 90802

HearAid Foundation presents our 6th Annual Heroes for Hearing 5K Fundraiser.

Be inspired by heroes overcoming their hearing loss. Run with heroes who bring the gift of hearing. Become a hero.
  
 
Join us on Sunday, August 15th, 2027 in Long Beach, California (or virtually) as we celebrate our recipients and those who helped give the gift of hearing! Let’s run and walk together so we can keep on giving this precious gift. 

Join us for an exhilarating run along the marina and water front in Long Beach, California. Whether you're up for a 5k or the Kids Run, this event promises a memorable experience amidst the natural beauty of the sea.

Event Details:

Bib Pickup: Starts at 7 am
Race Start Times:
5k: 8 am Kids Dash: 9:15 am

Course Description:

Course Time Limit: 1 hours and 45 minutes. You must cross the finish line by 9:45 a.m.

What You Get:

All participants will receive a finisher's medal, finish line treats, and free downloadable race photos.
Race results will be posted on our website within 12 hours of the race.

Gear Check: Personal items can be stored with our staff .

Water Station on the course, with water and electrolyte beverages.

Race Photos: Our course photographer will capture your journey, and you can download your photos for free within 24 hours of the event.

Results: Published on RunSignup within 2 hours of the race.

Refund and Deferral Policy:

Unfortunately, we do not offer refunds, please purchase the inexpensive insurance if you think there is a chance you might need to back out and will want a refund instead of considering it a donation to the charity. 


Who Can Register:

Everyone is welcome! Our races are open to participants of all ages, abilities, and races. Whether you're an experienced runner, a casual jogger, or a first-time walker, you're invited to join us. Parents can bring their children and strollers, as we believe in creating an inclusive and welcoming atmosphere for all. Come and be a part of this fun and rewarding race experience!

We look forward to seeing you adjacent to the aquarium for a day of fitness, fun, and camaraderie. Get ready to lace up your running shoes and create lasting memories in this beautiful setting!

name: Pre Reg 2027 Torrance Memorial Medical Center, BRA Run, Los Angeles
description:
Day of Event

Our 14th Annual 5K & 13K are held on a fully paved course next to the sand in Playa Del Rey on August 30th, 2026

6:00am: Parking Lots Open (LA County charges $13, bring cash). The line backs up so arrive early. 

7:00am: Registration and Vendor Booths Open

7:05am: Warm up for Bike Tour

7:10am: Bike Tour Starts 

7:30am: Costume Contests

7:40am: Warm Up for 5/13k

8:06am: National Anthem 🇺🇸

8:10am: 13K start (2 hour time limit, 15 min per mile pace or faster)

8:30am: 5K start

10:00am: Kids Run starts (time is approximate and depends on when the last 13K walkers are off so kids can run clear)

10:10am: Awards Ceremony

Share your photos on social media! We are @brarunla and @runmercury and our official hashtag is #brarunla. We will be resharing your posts whenever we can.


Charity

In its 14th year, The BRA Run supports Evelyn’s BFF, a charity that helps breast cancer survivors get back to their new normal while supporting counseling, reconstruction, and other items that people are often not able to get covered by their insurance. Most of our grant recipients have bills going into 6 figures! This event is the biggest fundraiser for this all volunteer organization and determines how many people they can help this year.

Evelyn, the founder of the Evelyn's Breast Friends Forever (BFF), a 501(c)3 non-profit public benefit charity foundation, started this event in 2013 and in her honor we have a 5K and a 13K at the BRA Run. We have the unusual distance of 13K because women have a 1 in 8 risk (or 13%) of having breast cancer in their life. A 13K is also slightly more than 8 miles.

Join us for Evelyn's party so we all can help other breast cancer survivors and their families. Our event spreads awareness of breast cancer reconstruction to the community by encouraging men and women to run and walk in their BRA (Breast Reconstruction Awareness) in honor and in memory of those who have been diagnosed with breast cancer.

Donate to Evelyn's BFF.

Costume Contest

Dress up in celebration of the BRA Run! Our participants get creative with their attire and we have awards to celebrate. Wear a decorated bra (sports bra, lacy bra, nursing bra, any type of bra) or dress up your shirt! You can wear the bra on its own or over a shirt. Looking for ideas? Here are some of last year's costumes.

Winners will be announced in the following categories:

Female Individual: Best Decorated Bra
Male Individual: Best Decorated Bra
Team*: Best Dressed

*Teams must have 5 or more people to enter the team competitions.

Make it a Virtual Run/Walk

Can't make it in person but want to be a part of the event and support breast cancer survivors? Sign up for the virtual run and we will mail you a bib, shirt and medal.

Beach to City Challenge

Want to nab an additional medal? Take part in the Beach to City Challenge with the Greta Garbo medal!

Greta Garbo, the cinematic legend and breast cancer survivor, called Culver City home, so we celebrate her with a special medal. If you run both the BRA Run and Screenland 5k (in Culver City) back-to-back, you can claim this bonus bling!

If you ran Screenland 5k 2025 and BRA Run 2025, you can claim your medal at BRA Run 2025
If you run BRA Run 2025 and Screenland 5k 2026, you can claim your medal at Screenland 5k 2026

You can only claim the bonus medal once a year.

Sign up for Screenland 5k 2025 to ensure your Greta Garbo medal. If you register for Screenland 5k at the BRA Run finish line, you'll get a discount on registration.

A list of those who qualify for the medal will be published on the BRA Run website in August before the event. Check to make sure your name is on it!

Thank you so much to ©Harriet Brown Inc. for working with us to bring you the iconic images of the great Greta Garbo that are used in our challenge medals.

name: Pre Reg 2027 Wrigley River Run & Tadpole Trot Presented by Long Beach Clinical Trials
description:
This page is for the 2027 Event, for the event on June 6th, 2026 please visit www.wrigleyriverrun.com for full event information.

The start/finish, expo area and bib pick up will be located in the parking lot of Westland Real Estate Group/Long Beach Beer Lab, at 520 W Willow St, Long Beach, CA 90806.

There is special pricing of only $10 for youth 17 & under who want to do the 5k or the 10k.

The Half Combo is a total of 13.1 miles and includes a 5k and 10 Mile Entry. You will receive a half marathon time as well as a time in each event. You will also receive a bonus medal. There are no age group awards for the Half Combo.

If you have a group of 6 or more contact us about your options for a group discount.

The Wrigley River Run is the Long Beach Neighborhood Foundation’s signature event and is designed to promote community involvement, education, tolerance, and a healthy non-violent lifestyle.  All funds generated from the event are used to benefit youth organizations in Long Beach and the surrounding communities.

name: Pre Registration 2026 - Beverly Hills Run of the Stars
description:
This is the page for the 2026 event! (If you are looking for the event held on Oct 19th, 2025, please click here https://runsignup.com/Race/CA/BeverlyHills/STARS5K) 

 

Lace up and run through the flat, scenic streets of Beverly Hills at this year’s 5K on October 18th, 2026!

 

Run or Walk on your own or on a team!

Can’t make it in person? Join our Virtual Challenge and complete your 5K from anywhere in the world.

We’re also hosting a 1K “Stars of Tomorrow” Kids Race held at the same location right after the 5K- perfect for young runners ready to shine! (Note: All ages are welcome to participate in the 5k but only those under-10 can registers for the 1k.)

 

This event supports NOT TODAY CANCER and their mission to find a CURE for devastating childhood cancers. 
 
Despite childhood cancer rates being on the rise, a desperately small amount of US Federal Funding for Cancer Research goes to children. 
 
When Mason was 9 years old he was diagnosed with T-Cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL).  His cancer was treated with chemotherapies that have been in use for decades, because there is a devastating lack of funding for new treatments with better outcomes!  
For two years, Mason and his family used the slogan “Not Today Cancer'“ as their mantra and when he died from the disease, the journey continued and this local non-profit was founded in Mason's honor. Scientists are close to a cure to help children like Mason and you can help! 
 
NOT TODAY CANCER 

 

Packet Pick Up, where you can get your shirt and bib, on Saturday, the day before the race. Time and Location TBD. 

If you are having someone else pick up your bib, shirt, and bag, they will need two things. A printed copy of your ID and a printed signed copy of the waiver. You can download and print the waiver here.  No bibs will be given out without this. The lawyers and our insurance company require us to be strict on this, sorry for the inconvenience.

If you are unable to join us the day before, you can pick up your bib and shirt on race day in the festival area but get there early and be prepared to wait in line on race day.
*Reminder: Please wear your bib on the front of your clothes so that your photos can be tagged and so we know you are with the event.*

DAY OF RACE INFO: https://www.nottodaycancer.care/ntc-run

RACE PARKING:  TBD

Race Day Schedule:

TBD

name: Pre-Registration 2026 Plymouth Rock n Run
description:
Please visit https://runsignup.com/Race/CA/Anaheim/PlymouthRocknRun to sign up for the 2025 Plymouth Rock n Run or to view results or photos. This site is only for 2026 early registration. 

 

Get ready to lace up your running shoes and join the fun at the most exciting event in Anaheim, CA!

It's all happening on Thanksgiving Day, at  La Palma Ave, right in the heart of beautiful Yorba Regional Park. We've got a fantastic day of activities and races planned for you, so let's dive into all the exhilarating details:

Event Highlights:

🏃‍♂️ USATF-Certified Courses: We've got both 5k and 10k courses that'll take you on a thrilling journey along La Palma Ave and the enchanting Santa Ana River Trail, all while you soak in the natural beauty of Yorba Regional Park.

⏱️ Chip Timing: For those competitive spirits, we've got chip timing for the 5k and 10k run/walk events. Race against the clock and challenge yourself to a new personal best!

👦👧 Kids' Fun Run: Calling all young runners! We've got a Kids 1k fun run for those aged 10 and under, and even a 100-yard tot trot for the little ones aged 4 and under. It's a blast for the whole family!

🥇 Awesome Awards: The top male and female finishers in both the 5k and 10k races will receive special awards. Plus, medals three deep for top runners in 18 different age categories. Everyone's a winner!

🏅 Custom Finisher Medals: You won't want to miss our custom-designed diecast finisher medals for all 5k/10k and kids run/trot participants. It's a race souvenir you'll cherish!

👕 Stylish Shirts: Participants in the 5k and 10k get cool shirts in adult unisex, women's, and youth sizes. Show off your accomplishment in style!

👫 Team Spirit: Gather your friends and form a team of 8 or more – you'll enjoy fantastic discounts! There are also team competitions with awards for the biggest, fastest, and highest fundraising teams.

🎉 Finish-Line Festival: The fun doesn't end at the finish line! Join us at the finish-line festival for a costume contest, live music, delicious food, freebies, and tons of entertainment for adults and kids of all ages. It's a celebration like no other!

PACKET PICK-UP 
Multiple options are planned for the Saturday, Tuesday and Wednesday leading up to the race day. Check out the bib pick up tab for the latest details as they are confirmed and follow us on social media for the fastest updates.


LOCATION/PARKING 
The event staging area is located at the west end of Yorba Regional Park (7300 E La Palma, Anaheim Hills, CA 92807), just past the softball fields near the 5k/10k start line. 

Parking is available inside Yorba Regional Park. Payment of $5 per car may be required Enter the park off La Palma from eastbound or westbound lanes starting at 6:00 AM until approximately 6:45 AM, when the eastbound lanes along the park will be closed for the start of the 10k race. Thereafter, access to the park will be via westbound La Palma only when the course is clear of runners. 

Additional parking is available in the following areas: 1) Paved/gravel lots adjacent to softball fields at the west end of Yorba Regional Park (very limited capacity); 2) residential areas directly across from the park; 3) residential areas west of Fairmont Blvd off Hondo Dr; and 3) on the street and in church parking lots off of the Fairmont Connector between Esperanza and Fairmont Blvd. 

We expect heavy traffic on race day morning; carpooling and early arrival is strongly recommended!

PRELIMINARY RACE DAY SCHEDULE - SUBJECT TO CHANGE
6:00 AM - Late registration/packet pick-up 
7:00 AM - 10k start 
8:00 AM - 5k start
8:40 AM - 5k & 10k overall winners announced*

name: Pre-Registration Screenland 5K 2027
description:
This is only the Early Registration page for the 2027 event, please go to

https://runsignup.com/Race/CA/CulverCity/Screenland5K  or https://www.screenland5k.com for more information about our event on March 1st, 2026 and to sign up.

Follow the yellow brick road with Dorothy, Toto and the Munchkins pursued by the Wicked Witch of the West, experiencing legendary movie and television experiences. Finish on the red carpet with Scarlett O'Hara, Rhett Butler and paparazzi at our start studded Annual family fun 5K adventure in the Heart of Screenland.

All participants will receive commemorative bib, official time, medal and shirt and on course support and entertainment, entrance into the post race party and free downloadable event photos among many other perks.

Beach to City Challenge

Screenland 5K + BRA Run = Bonus bling featuring the fabulous Greta Garbo! 

This cinematic legend and breast cancer survivor called Culver City home, so we are celebrating her with the Beach to City Challenge! 

You must do both events back to back. You can do the 5K at Screenland and then either the 5K or the 13K at the BRA Run and you will be able to claim the bonus medal at the finish line festival of the BRA Run in August at Dockweiler Beach .  If you missed Screenland in the spring, you can start the challenge at BRA Run in August and finish it at Screenland the following year.

We update the list of those who are qualified on the BRA Run website in August, before that event. You can check there to make sure we have you on the list after you register.

Sign up for both events at the same time or register for the BRA Run at the finish line festival after the Screenland 5K, and get a discount on registration.

More info about the BRA Run 5k & 13K  at www.BRArunLA.com.

name: Project Youth OC - 2026 OC Marathon
description:
Join Us for the 2026 OC Marathon and Support Project Youth OC!

Since 2004, Project Youth OC has proudly partnered with the OC Marathon as an official Charity Partner. This year, we are celebrating 22 years of impact - and reaching a major milestone.

In 2026, Project Youth OC will surpass $1 million raised through our partnership with the OC Marathon.

Our Road to a Million campaign represents more than a number.  It reflects decades of community support, thousands of runners and fundraisers, and countless young lives impacted at critical turning points.

The OC Marathon offers something for everyone:

  • 5K Walk/Run: Saturday, May 2, 2026, at the OC Fairgrounds.
  • Marathon & Half Marathon: Sunday, May 3, 2026, starting at Fashion Island and finishing at the OC Fairgrounds.

When you join our team, you’ll help empower youth and strengthen families across Orange County. 

Every dollar raised through peer-to-peer fundraising goes directly toward life-changing mentorship, education, and support services for over 1,500 youth and their families each year.

Together, we can run, walk, and fundraise for a brighter future!

name: PSL Evolve Harvest 5K Walk/Run
description:
Get ready to move with purpose at the beautiful California Citrus State Historic Park! Enjoy the fresh air, scenic trails, and a taste of local citrus as you experience this one-of-a-kind setting during the PSL Evolve Harvest 5K Walk/Run. This event brings together health, wellness, and community impact in one powerful day. Whether you're a seasoned runner or a casual walker, this 5K welcomes participants of all paces and fitness levels to rise to the challenge and evolve together.

Join us as we run, walk, and stride toward optimal health and greater impact. Every mile tells a story, and every dollar raised brings us one step closer to changing someone's narrative through meaningful community outreach.

Celebrate your accomplishment at the finish line with a PSL Evolve finisher medal, a healthy post-race lunch, fresh orange tastings, and live music to keep the energy high. Come be part of the movement as we maximize every moment with momentum!

Bib / T-Shirt / Parking Pass Pickup:

Date: March 6, 2026

Time: 1:00 PM – 6:00 PM

Location: California Citrus State Historic Park, 9400 Dufferin Ave, Riverside, CA 92503

**Same-day bib pick-up will be available at 7:00 a.m on March 7th. To ensure a smooth check-in process on race day, we encourage bib pick up on Friday, March 6th.**

Event Schedule:

7:00 AM – 7:30 AM: 5K Walk/Run Check-in
7:30 AM – 7:45 AM: Activity led by Coach Christy
7:45 AM – 8:00 AM: Stretch led by Coach Mike
8:10 AM – 9:40 AM: Harvest 5K Walk/Run
9:00 AM – 10:00 AM: Orange Tasting & Hydration 
10:00 AM – 10:30 AM: Post-Race Lunch
10:00 AM – 11:30 AM: Soulful live entertainment at the outdoor amphitheatre 

Additional Information:

Vegan and Vegetarian lunch options will be available. 

Pets are welcome! Please keep them on a leash at all times and bring bags to clean up after them. Since children and families will be present, we ask that your pets be well-behaved and comfortable around people.

Children are welcome to participate if registered. Each registration includes a bib, finisher medal, T-shirt, wrist band, and lunch. Unregistered children may walk with a parent, but will not receive race items.

name: PSYKO FIT HYROX LITE
description:
ROX LITE
Your first step into the HYROX arena

Ready to have some fun and test what your training can really do?

ROX LITE is a HYROX-style event built for our gym community—same race-day energy, scaled to be accessible, safe, and seriously fun. Whether you’re brand new to competition or sharpening your edge for an upcoming HYROX, this is your chance to show up, push hard, and celebrate your fitness.

The ROX LITE Workout

  • Ski Erg – 500 meters
  • Sled Push & Pull – 50 meters total
  • Burpee to Plate Jump – 40 reps
  • Rower – 500 meters
  • Farmer Carry – 100 meters (24 kg × 2 for men / 16 kg × 2 for women)
  • Sandbag Reverse Lunges – 50 total
  • Wall Balls – 50 reps

 
Important Event Info
Our events use a wave start format to keep things moving smoothly.

You’ll choose a start time when you register
Athletes are released in waves at that time
Arrive at least 30 minutes early for course walkthrough and warm-up
Late arrivals will be placed in the next available wave
Wave sizes are limited, so early registration is strongly encouraged
 
What to Expect on Race Day
Clearly marked stations and smooth transitions
Coaches and volunteers at every station to guide standards and rep counts
Electrolytes and water on-site to keep you fueled
Electric energy and a supportive community cheering you on
 
Why You Should Do This
Celebrate your training in a fun, safe, and structured environment
Build confidence for your next HYROX or competitive event
Create a performance you’ll be proud of
Race day photos live forever—make yours count

Spots are limited!

Claim your wave and register early.

name: Rabbit Run 10K, 5K, Kid's 1-mile
description:
Rabbit Run is a flat and fast course along a dedicated run/bike path. The course runs along the beautiful Maria Ygnacio Creek and Obern Bike Paths which are paved with no vehicle traffic. Free parking is available along Gwyne Ave. Packet Pickup is located near the Start Line (865 Gwyne Ave, Santa Barbara) from 7-9 AM on race morning. The 10K starts at 9:00 AM, 5K at 9:10 AM, and the Kid's 1-mile (Family Fun Run, non-competitive) at 10:00 AM. Water Stations will be placed at approximately every 1.5 mile mark. There will be plenty of "nutrition" after the race.  The Awards Ceremony is also near the Start Line at 10:30AM.  Awards are issued to the top 3 runners in both the Men's and Women's categories for all Age Groups in 5-year increments for both the 5K and 10K.

name: Race for Open Space
description:
Big Sur Land Trust's 2026 Race for Open Space is a one-day trail running event dedicated to fostering an appreciation of natural spaces in Monterey County and celebrating the health benefits of time spent in nature. This annual event invites runners and hikers of all ages to find wonder among Monterey County’s most iconic landscapes. This time of year will provide participants with sweeping views of green ridge lines punctuated by colorful wildflowers.

Centered around Palo Corona Regional Park, participants are invited to choose their adventure by registering for a 5K, 12K, 25K, or 35K+ trail run. Each course promises a spectacular journey through sections of the Palo Corona Backcountry, normally closed to the public. A one-mile Fun-Run will be offered for individuals of all ages and abilities.

Race for Open Space’s technical partner, Inside Trail Running, will oversee the start/finish line, trail-marking, aid stations, and participant timing/results. All activities will be offered in compliance with public health and safety guidelines. Our community is deeply passionate about our mission to inspire love of land across generations, conservation of our unique Monterey County landscapes, and access to outdoor experiences for all. 

On the day of the event, community partners and businesses such as Alvarado Street Brewery will help participants celebrate crossing the finish line with beer, food, and interactive tabling displays.

name: Race2Unravel
description:
Join us in Gilroy, California on Saturday, August 22, 2026, for the Race2Unravel — a powerful day of ACTION in the fight against childhood cancer.

This inspiring community event features a 5K, 10K, and our new 5K Ruck Division — because every step forward fuels critical pediatric cancer research. Whether you run, ruck, sponsor, or donate, you are helping fund innovative research and honoring the children who inspire us: those still fighting, those we’ve lost, and the future we refuse to give up on.

And for our youngest supporters, we've added a Kids Fun Run at the end of the event - an opportunity for children to get involved and feel the spirit of the day. 

Move with purpose. Show up with heart. Race2Unravel...until there is a cure!

 

About Rucking: 
Rucking is a physical activity that involves walking with a weighted backpack, often referred to as a ruck. It combines the benefits of strength training and cardio, making it an effective workout for building endurance and muscle. Weight requirements are 30 lbs for men and 20 lbs for women, and rucksacks will be weighed prior to the start.


About the Course: 
The route begins at Christmas Hill Park (Ranch Side) and winds through parts of the Uvas Creek Levee Park Preserve, following the Uvas Creek Levee Trail. The course is mainly flat and fully paved, offering a scenic run through one of Gilroy’s most beautiful natural areas.

To ensure a smooth and confident experience for all participants, there will be prominent course signage and clearly marked turnaround points. 

 

 

IMPORTANT DETAILS: 

  • Registration Deadline for T-shirt is July 31st
  • No Pets Allowed
  • This is a Cupless Race - Please bring your own water bottle. 
  • Strollers are allowed but please start toward the back and give the right of way on the narrower portions of the course. 
  • Regular Registration Ends Friday, August 21st @ 3pm; Same day registration available until 7:30AM sharp on Saturday, August 22nd. 
  • Medals will be presented to the top three male and top three female finishers in the 5K, 10K, and 5K Ruck divisions. Participants in the Kids Fun Run will also receive a commemorative medal.

And for our youngest supporters, we've added a Kids Fun Run at the end of the event - an opportunity for children to get involved and feel the spirit of the day. 

Move with purpose. Show up with heart. Race2Unravel...until there is a cure!

 

About Rucking: 
Rucking is a physical activity that involves walking with a weighted backpack, often referred to as a ruck. It combines the benefits of strength training and cardio, making it an effective workout for building endurance and muscle. Weight requirements are 30 lbs for men and 20 lbs for women, and rucksacks will be weighed prior to the start.


About the Course: 
The route begins at Christmas Hill Park (Ranch Side) and winds through parts of the Uvas Creek Levee Park Preserve, following the Uvas Creek Levee Trail. The course is mainly flat and fully paved, offering a scenic run through one of Gilroy’s most beautiful natural areas.

To ensure a smooth and confident experience for all participants, there will be prominent course signage and clearly marked turnaround points. 

 

 

IMPORTANT DETAILS: 

  • Registration Deadline for T-shirt is July 31st
  • No Pets Allowed
  • This is a Cupless Race - Please bring your own water bottle. 
  • Strollers are allowed but please start toward the back and give the right of way on the narrower portions of the course. 
  • Regular Registration Ends Friday, August 21st @ 3pm; Same day registration available until 7:30AM sharp on Saturday, August 22nd. 
  • Medals will be presented to the top three male and top three female finishers in the 5K, 10K, and 5K Ruck divisions. Participants in the Kids Fun Run will also receive a commemorative medal.

name: Ramona Family Adventure Race
description:
Registration closes 4/8/26 at noon!

The next San Diego Adventure Racing event returns to Ramona for another super beginner-friendly Adventure Race for newbies and families that involves both hiking and biking (mountain bikes or gravel bikes).  Navigation will be with the maps provided at the start line, but still no GPS allowed.  Compasses encouraged.  Two courses will be available:

  1. 10 and Under (with parental assist) - geocache style (2-4 hours)
  2. Family / Adults - punched passport style (4-6 hours)

The start line location will be at Ramona Oaks Park, in Ramona, CA.  Please register EACH person coming so that we have enough maps, snacks, and kiddo awards.

Timeline

Saturday, Ramona Oaks Park:

  • 7:30am: Arrival and drop off bikes
  • 8:00am: Adult course start
  • 8:30am: Navigation clinic for Children/Family course
  • 9:00am: Children's Geocache course starts
  • 12:00pm: Lunch available
  • 1:00pm: End of all races and Awards

GEAR

  1. BYOB (Bring Your Own Bike)
  2. Food and water - 0.5L per person per hour, minimum, and snacks, especially for the kiddos (snacks will also be available at Start/Finish)
  3. Compass, of any type really - at least to help with coarse direction and not end up too disoriented.

COURSE ESTIMATES

 Remember that a majority of the miles are on bike, not on foot:

  • Geocache style course: 1-4 miles
  • Punch style course: 10-20 miles

All checkpoints are optional.

SPONSORS

Women of AR sponsors this event!  Dana Borie and Chelsea McBride are both Women of AR Ambassadors, seeking to grow the sport by including all types of people!

name: Ramona Wine Country 5K
description:
Be sure to grab your family, friends, coworkers and come join us for one of the most fun filled events in Southern California, the Ramona Wine Country 5k. It takes place at the breathtaking Backcountry Gardens and is part trails with a splash of mud run plus a healthy dose of Mother Nature’s obstacles mixed in for fun. You’ll also find some hills, streams, boulders and much more. Not your average 5K! Everyone can do it as long as you have the drive and determination to keep going, not quit and in the words of Joe Dirt, “keep on keepin’ on." 

It’s a 1.5 mile two loop course. If two loops are too many, feel free to enjoy the single loop option. 

Oh, and don’t miss out on the Charity Solo & Team Beer Mile after the 5K is finished. All you gotta do is drink 4 beers and run 4 x400 meters Fastest individual or 2-4 person team earns the bragging rights.  

Once the fitness is over, you’ve gotta then join us across the road at the award winning Ramona Ranch Winery for a FREE wine tasting, share stores and food for purchase from Farmhouse 78. If you didn’t know, Ramona Ranch is also San Diego’s only Certified Sustainable Vineyard and Winery.  

REGISTRATION INCLUDES;
- FREE Ramona Ranch wine tasting
- Finisher’s medal
- Race swag
- Ramona Radio playing tunes
- Food for purchase from Farmhouse 78
- FREE Parking 

A portion of the proceeds help support the life changing OPERATION REBOUND – FRONTLINE TO FINISH LINE: CAF’s Operation Rebound® program strengthens the mental and physical well-being of veterans, military personnel and first responders with permanent physical injuries by providing them opportunities to use sports and fitness to re-integrate into our communities and by empowering them through sports.

name: REACH Foundation Shamrock 'n Run
description:
The REACH Foundation’s favorite tradition continues! The Shamrock ’n Run 5K & 2K is once again bringing the Placentia-Yorba Linda community together for a festive, fun-filled day in support of our students.

Since 2012, thousands of families have participated in this beloved community event—running, walking, and celebrating together—while helping raise critical funds that directly support enrichment programs and events for PYLUSD students. It’s more than a race; it’s a celebration of community, school spirit, and giving back.

Performance Medals

Medals are awarded for 1st, 2nd and 3rd for both genders in Overall and by Age Divisions.

  • Overall
  • Ages 1-8, 9-10, 11-12, 13-15, 16-18, 19-24, 25-29, 30-34, 35-39- 40-44, 45-49, 50-54, 55-59, 60-64 and 65-99

We’re excited to welcome our four-legged friends, too! 🐾 For participants planning to run or walk the 5K or 2K with their dogs, please review the Yorba Regional Park guidelines below to help ensure a safe and enjoyable experience for everyone:

  • Dogs must be on a leash at all times while in the park
  • Leashes must be no longer than 6 feet
  • Leashes must be physical leashes (no e-collars)
  • Participants must carry doggie bags and clean up after their pets
  • Dogs should be well-socialized and comfortable in a busy race environment with runners, walkers, and spectators


Thank you for helping us keep Shamrock ’n Run safe, welcoming, and fun for all—two-legged and four-legged alike. We can’t wait to celebrate with you! 🍀

The REACH Foundation Team

name: Red Hills Ramble
description:
Strap on your adventure hats and smear on that sunscreen, folks, because the Red Hills Ramble is back, and it's sassier, sweatier, and more rock-strewn than ever! (Seriously, we keep throwing the rocks away and they just find their way back to the trail). Nestled in the breathtaking Sierra Nevada foothills—just a stone's throw (or a rock trip) from Oakdale—this isn't your co-worker’s Sunday morning stroll. It's a springtime extravaganza where the only thing more abundant than the elevation changes are the chances to laugh in the face of adversity.


Here in the Red Hills, every little rock seems to have a vendetta against your ankles, and the sun blazes with the intensity of a thousand fiery tacos. Our trails are peppered with technical single tracks, mischievous rocks of all sizes, and fire roads that will have your calves singing odes to endurance. And then there's El Guapo—the hill so steep it's got its own fan club. Conquer it a you will be officially required to humble brag about your achievement for many, many months. And what can we say about the view from the top? Let's just say it's the kind of breathtaking scene that'll make you forget the electrolites you just lost.
Forget the "grab your swag and bolt" routine; at the Red Hills Ramble, your race swag isn't just a memento—it's a potential bandage for the battle scars you'll wear with pride. So, bring your lawn chairs, because we're turning the finish line into a fiesta of food, drinks, and maybe a beer (or two). With distances of 10K, 15K, and 30K, there's a challenge for every level of misery.

El Guapo is calling, and those trails aren't going to run themselves. name: Red Hills Ramble
description:
Strap on your adventure hats and smear on that sunscreen, folks, because the Red Hills Ramble is back, and it's sassier, sweatier, and more rock-strewn than ever! (Seriously, we keep throwing the rocks away and they just find their way back to the trail). Nestled in the breathtaking Sierra Nevada foothills—just a stone's throw (or a rock trip) from Oakdale—this isn't your co-worker’s Sunday morning stroll. It's a springtime extravaganza where the only thing more abundant than the elevation changes are the chances to laugh in the face of adversity.


Here in the Red Hills, every little rock seems to have a vendetta against your ankles, and the sun blazes with the intensity of a thousand fiery tacos. Our trails are peppered with technical single tracks, mischievous rocks of all sizes, and fire roads that will have your calves singing odes to endurance. And then there's El Guapo—the hill so steep it's got its own fan club. Conquer it a you will be officially required to humble brag about your achievement for many, many months. And what can we say about the view from the top? Let's just say it's the kind of breathtaking scene that'll make you forget the electrolites you just lost.
Forget the "grab your swag and bolt" routine; at the Red Hills Ramble, your race swag isn't just a memento—it's a potential bandage for the battle scars you'll wear with pride. So, bring your lawn chairs, because we're turning the finish line into a fiesta of food, drinks, and maybe a beer (or two). With distances of 10K, 15K, and 30K, there's a challenge for every level of misery.

El Guapo is calling, and those trails aren't going to run themselves. Welcome to the greatest trail race in the universe—where the heat is hot, the hills are personal, and the finish line is just the beginning of the celebration. See you at the Red Hills Ramble, where we're all about making memories, nursing bruises, and living to tell the tale!

name: Redding Breakfast Lions Turtle Bay Run 2026
description:
Runners in this years  half marathon  will run along the Sacramento River and will be crossing three bridges: the Sundial Bridge, the Ribbon Bridge and the Diestelhorst Bridge. The runners will start out crossing the Turtle Bay Sundial Bridge, and go north on paved paths in park surroundings most of the way, until they reach the Ribbon Bridge where they cross the Sacramento River and go south until they reach Middle Creek trail, which is an out and back (2 miles), with a return to the River Trail. Once back on the River Trail the runners cross back on the Diestelhorst Bridge to the north side of the river. The runners then continue back to the Sundial Bridge where they cross back to the south side and the Start / Finish.

In addition to the half marathon there is a 10 K, which also goes along the Sacramento River, just less distance; and a 2 mile run / walk for younger and older, who do not want the longer distances. Having the multiple distance options makes it a very family friendly event.

The half marathon and the 10 K have been certified with the American Track and Field Association. For those of you who need a certified distance, this is another good reason to run this particular race.

A couple of years back we added electronic timing, through individual tracking on each runner's race bib.  Since everybody liked it, this will continue for all runners at any distance.

This year's race will maintain acknowledgement of  age division winners in 5 year increments starting at “under 15 years of age” . For the two mile run there will be three additional divisions starting at 5 years and under.

If you are a sponsor of the race you will get one free entry into the division of your choice. If you would like to become a sponsor please complete a sponsor form which can be found on our website at https://reddingbreakfastlionsclub.com/events-2/turtle-bay-run/

Swag bag and packet pick up will be at Fleet Feet, 1376 Hilltop Drive , Redding California, 96003 on Saturday October 3rd from 12 until 2 pm, or at the start / finish area on October 4th from 7:00 am until 8:30 am.

We will have the ability to enter school teams this year, where students can be entered by their school / coach at the cost of $10.00 for any distance. This is only for high school or younger and  no shirt is included. Please contact us on our website for a sign up form at: https://reddingbreakfastlionsclub.com/events-2/turtle-bay-run/

Forms and money must be in our hands by September 25th 2026 for student entries.

PLEASE NOTE : IF YOU SIGN UP AFTER September 11th 2026, YOU MAY NOT GET A SHIRT

name: Reentry Resource Center’s Rise Up and Run 5K
description:
The County of Santa Clara Reentry Resource Center and its partners are hosting a 5K run/walk to raise money to support the immediate needs of justice-involved people (clothing, food, hygiene, transportation, etc.). The in-person 5K will take place on Saturday, October 18th at Hellyer County Park with a race start time of 9:00AM. Participants who choose the virtual option can run or walk the race on the day and time of their choice between October 18, 2025, and November 1, 2025. Runners will receive a Rise Up and Run race shirt and medal. 

 

Packet pickup information will be coming soon.  

 

Help support this effort by registering for the race, sponsoring other participants to run or donating to buy new clothes for those reentering our community from jail or prison. Many of these individuals have no clean clothes in which to start their reentry journey.  

 

Here are some ways you can help:

  • Register and run the race!
  • Sponsor a race registration for an individual or a family.
  • Donate monetarily to buy new clothes for individuals released from custody.
  • Buy or donate new clothes for reentry clients leaving custody.

 

Every day at the County of Santa Clara Reentry Resource Center we see clients ready to make dramatic changes in their lives. But having a felony record can be almost as restrictive as being incarcerated. Access to jobs, housing, and other opportunities becomes incredibly limited due to employment and housing restrictions and social stigma. 

 

Yet despite these challenges, we see clients determined to clear those hurdles. They are taking college credit classes, working their way up from minimum wage jobs to management positions and union apprenticeships and some are entering peer mentoring and counseling professions to help those who are following in their footsteps. 

You can help support individuals who are just starting this journey to change their lives and share their talents with our community. Each person you help to rise up makes our community stronger. 

 

If you would like more information about the County of Santa Clara Reentry Resource Center, please visit www.sccreentry.org or email Juan Guevara at juan.guevara@ceo.sccgov.org.

 

We look forward to partnering with you for social change.

name: Reno to the Redwoods
description:
Experience an epic challenge...

By participating in Reno to the Redwoods, all challengers support women with cancer in Santa Cruz County through WomenCARE.  WomenCARE offers a safe haven where women with any type of cancer find mutual support, shared experiences, and open hearts. We provide cancer advocacy, resources, education, and support to women, their families and friends, and healthcare practitioners at each stage of the journey: diagnosis, healing, surviving or dying.
Virtually take the 300 mile route from Reno, Nevada around Lake Tahoe, through the mountains and valleys to the Redwoods in Santa Cruz, California, OR take the 180 mile route from Reno to the River (San Joaquin River in Stockton!). Make no mistake, this virtual challenge will test you!  But you can use whatever exercise you prefer (run, bike, swim, walk, row, fitness center machines, other, or a combination of any) to complete the challenge, further your fitness goals, and raise money for WomenCARE. And we will motivate you along the way! 
As you are increasing fitness and feeling great, You Are Making A Real Impact!  We have set our initial goal to raise $10,000 in donations to support WomenCARE! 
All challengers receive a limited edition Move Out Against Cancer, Reno to the Redwoods T-Shirt and a complimentary decal, as well as have access to Live Map Tracking of your progress.
 
Live Map Progress Tracking!
You will be able to see your progress along the route as you enter your mileage.  Our live map tracking feature will even allow you to see where your fellow challengers are on the map compared to you - now that's some motivation! 
 
You've Got This!

Take on as few as 14-20 miles per week (2-3 miles per day). Add all your activity miles together. If you keep track of all the miles from steps you take on a normal day, be sure to add this. Those steps add up! You can set your goal to move as few as 20 miles per week or challenge yourself to cover as many as you can - be sure to pace yourself! We will help you total up your distance and track your progress with our online platform.
 
These challenges are simple:
1. Do what you want to do, when you want to do it, from wherever you are!
2. Connect and track your progress on our race page and connect on our Facebook group!
3. Get your limited edition Reno To The Redwoods Challenge T-Shirt and your decal!
 

Spread the Word!

IMPORTANT ITEMS TO NOTE:
YOUR REGISTRATION FEES cover event design, production, marketing, T-shirts, decals, and INCLUDE A $35 DONATION TO WOMENCARE.  Using the donate button provides the opportunity to give additional support to WomenCARE. 100% of your donations go directly to WomenCARE.
This fundraiser does not ask that you recruit donations or pledges - however - the more participants we have, the more funds we raise!
We encourage you to invite your friends to participate with you! Form a team!
Post information about the challenge to your social media accounts and invite friends and acquaintances to participate.
THE MORE PARTICIPANTS WE HAVE, THE MORE FUNDS WE RAISE!

Important Dates:

March 15: Registration begins

April 1: Challenge begins and you may start logging your miles!

April 17: Registration deadline if you would like a t-shirt

May 18-June 11: Tee shirt pickup for local particpants at WomenCARE office during office hours, Monday-Thursday, 1pm-5pm.

July 1st: Challenge ends

July 7th: Last date to log your miles

 

JOIN US!

name: Ride 4A Reason 2026
description:
Ride 4 A Reason has 3 different routes for cyclists of every level and experience, and there's always a virtual option for those that prefer to ride with us in spirit! 

110 Miles - Ride all the way from Oakland to Sacramento!  The century ride begins at Oakland Technical High School and passes through beautiful bay area communities on the way to Sacramento. 

68 Miles - Start in Suisun City and enjoy some of the most delightful miles of R4R.  This route begins at the Suisun City train depot, and riders can choose a shuttle bus from Oakland Tech (leaves at 8 AM) or take the train/drive a car to the Suisun City train station. 

45 Miles - Our most family friendly route starts in Vacaville and has less than 600 ft of elevation gain, making it a perfect ride for anyone who is newer to long-distance cycling. This route begins at a park in Vacaville, and riders can take a shuttle bus that leaves at 8 AM from Oakland Tech to the ride start.

All rides end in Sacramento at the State Capitol with a catered lunch and a rally to celebrate the riders and highlight the need for more education funding.  Riders can choose to reserve a seat on the shuttle bus back to Oakland Tech or take Amtrak back to Oakland/Jack London Square.

name: Ride Santa Barbara 100
description:
Ride Santa Barbara returns for its 15th year!

RideSB100 offers four distinct courses to suit a range of cycling abilities – each course offering a world-class Santa Barbara cycling experience! 🚵🏻‍♂️

All courses start along the beach and follow the beautiful Santa Barbara beachfront before turning inland to experience all Santa Barbara has to offer. Cyclists will wind through some of the most exclusive neighborhoods in the country; experience the rolling foothills lined with citrus and avocado orchards and climb some of the most famous mountains in the country, all while experiencing some of the most beautiful views in southern California.

 

All cyclists will receive:

  • Official 2026 RideSB100 t-shirt
  • Official 2026 RideSB100 water bottle
  • Official RideSB100 drawstring bag with sponsor goodies
  • Fully supported aid stations
  • Mechanical support
  • Finish Line Festival with lots of food and beer
  • All Gibraltar Challenge finishers will receive a coin at the top of the hill.
  • Age group medals for Gibraltar Challenge
  • Option to buy event Jersey
  • And more!

All riders will receive an overall chip time and riders who participate in the Gibraltar Challenge will be ranked for the King and Queen of the Mountain (KOM/QOM) Jersey awards! 

 

RIDES*

 

100 mile

  • Over 9,700′ of climbing | Start Time: 7:00 AM
  • Recommended for experienced cyclists only 
  • Tackle a challenging ride that begins at Chase Palm Park, rolls through Carpinteria, and continues into the scenic Lake Casitas region. Climb Toro Canyon and Ladera Lane before testing your legs on the Gibraltar Climb Challenge, a timed 6.1-mile ascent with an 8% grade and over 2,500 ft of elevation gain. Descend, then join the 100KM Coastal Route along Cathedral Oaks through Isla Vista and past UCSB, finishing back at Chase Palm Park.
  • Includes a timed hill climb segment up the famous Gibraltar Road  – with a KOM/QOM jersey awarded to the 1st place winners in each age group!
  • For more information, go to ridesb100.com/100-mile/


100 KM + Climb 

  • Over 6,600 ft. of climbing | Start Time: 7:30 AM
  • Recommended for experienced cyclists only 
  • Covering 64 miles of Santa Barbara’s most stunning terrain, this route begins at Chase Palm Park and heads south along the coast to Carpinteria. Tackle the Toro Canyon Climb (5.3% grade) and the steep Ladera Lane (10.9% grade), then test your mettle on the Gibraltar Climb: a 6.1-mile ascent with an 8% grade and a 2,551 ft elevation gain. After summiting Gibraltar, descend via the technical Painted Cave route, continue west along Riberia Drive through the serene Hope Ranch community, and return to a well-earned finish at Chase Palm Park.
  • Includes a timed hill climb segment up the famous Gibraltar Road  – with a KOM/QOM jersey awarded to the 1st place winners in each age group!
  • For more information, go to ridesb100.com/100km-climb/

 

100 KM Coastal Route 

  • 4,000 ft. of climbing | Start Time: 7:30 AM
  • Recommended for intermediate to experienced cyclists only
  • Covering 64 miles of Santa Barbara’s finest scenery, this route begins at Chase Palm Park and heads south along the coast to Carpinteria. Challenge yourself on the Toro Canyon Climb (5.3% grade) and steep Ladera Lane (10.9% grade), then descend toward the historic Old Mission Santa Barbara. From there, ride west through Isla Vista, take in breathtaking coastal views at Goleta Beach, pass the University of California, Santa Barbara, and finish back at Chase Palm Park.
  • For more information, go to ridesb100.com/100km-coastal/

 

34 miles 

  • Over 2,200 ft. of climbing | Start Time: 8:30 AM
  • Beginner to intermediate level cyclists 
  • Enjoy a stunning start along the coastline from Chase Palm Park before heading inland to San Ysidro Road. Tackle a gentle ascent on Mountain Drive (max 5.1% grade), then roll past the historic Old Mission Santa Barbara. Continue west along Riberia Drive through the serene Hope Ranch community and finish back at Chase Palm Park. Perfect for those seeking Santa Barbara’s natural charm with just the right amount of challenge.
  • For more information, go to ridesb100.com/34-mile/

*Event details and courses are subject to change. 

 

Charity

Ride to benefit MOVE Santa Barbara County! Help us raise needed donations and awareness for the great work they’re doing in Santa Barbara County. The mission of MOVE is to advocate for equitable county-wide infrastructure for walking, bicycling, and public transit and to empower and educate communities to choose active and sustainable forms of transportation. 

 

Refund Policy

All entry fees are NON-REFUNDABLE, no exceptions. Once we receive and accept your entry, you will not receive a refund if you cannot participate. You may do a one-time entry transfer to another event, person or year for $15.

For more information, visit our website ridesb100.com or e-mail our team at info@ridesb100.com.

 

Follow us on Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter! 

Subscribe to our e-newsletter! 📧

name: Ring Out the Old – 5K, 10K, Half Marathon
description:
Join us for the celebratory Ring out the Old race and let's kick 2026 to the curb together!

Race Details

Location: Woodley Park, 6076 Woodley Ave, Encino, CA
Parking: Free parking in the lot; more is available on Woodley Ave

Event Schedule

6:20am – Bib pick-up opens
7:00am – Half marathon & 10k start
7:30am – 5k start
7:35am – Registration & start line close
10:20am – Course closes (3 hours, 20 minutes for the Half and 10k)

Early start of 6:30am may be pre-arranged for half marathoners, email your request to events@hightideruns.com. All early starters will not be eligible for awards.

Courses (rain routes)

5k route: Runners do one loops around the lake – route here
10k route: Runners do two loops around the lake with a little extra – route here
Half Marathon: Route is around the park, done twice and then one of the 10k route loops – route here

More about the Course
The race routes go across the grass, under the road through a tunnel, and enter the Lake Balboa Park area. Route will be finalized week of race, rain-pending

Our courses are on open paths so please be considerate of other park users!

On-Course Support
Multiple water stations are located along the routes. The finish line will also have an aid station stocked with water, electrolytes, and other snacks. We have a first aid kit at each station and all High Tides Crew Members have received CPR training. The turns are clearly marked with chalk and runner turn signs

Final Details

Bib: Please wear your race bib on the front of your shirt so we can track your time and send your pics!
Gear Check: You may leave personal items with staff at the registration tent. Please bring your own bag.
Medals: All runners receive a finishing medal. 1st place medals are given to the overall 1st male and female in each distance
Results & Photos: An email with race results and photos will be sent the day after the race and earlier on Instagram. Race photos are free!

Join Us Again: Did you have a blast running with us at our low-pressure, high vibes race? We have themed races throughout the year in Long Beach, Santa Monica, San Diego, the San Fernando Valley, and Orange County. Register for multiple races at a time to earn a discount. Check our full schedule

name: Riverpark 5k Summer Series
description:
Join us for the 2nd Annual Riverpark 5k Summer Series!  This is a run/walk event, with the course being located on a bike path and sidewalk.  5k event starts at 6:00pm each week, and Free Kids 1k is at 5:45pm.  The starting and ending point is located at Windrow Park.  Each race is limited to first 150 registrants!

T-Shirts will be for sale at the event, or online for $20 or FREE T-shirt by registering for at least 2 of the 3 races. 

As this is a series, awards will be given to the top 3 in each age category at the conclusion of Week 3 (7/24) at Window Park.

Choose to participate with us for 1, 2, or all 3 weeks!  Plus, there is a discount for registering for all 3 races (full series)!  Each finisher in the Kids 1k races receives a finisher medal!  100% of the proceeds go towards Rio Mesa Cross Country and Track teams.

Course map is located here.

Check-in for bibs will be located in the park starting at 5:00pm each week.

Series Points for Riverpark 5k:

Age Group Points are given based on what place you get in your age group each week (please note age is based on your age on the last day of the series). If you don't place in the top 9 in your age group, you get 1 point for participating each week. Age groups are: 1-12, 13-19, 20-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59, 60-69, 70+.

1st Place - 10 Points

2nd Place - 8 Points

3rd Place - 7 Points

4th Place - 6 Points

5th Place - 5 Points

6th Place - 4 Points

7th Place - 3 Points

8th Place - 2 Points

9th or greater Place - 1 Point

For all inquiries, please email rapidorunning@gmail.com

name: ROARIN' THROUGH THE POCKET 5K
description:
A fun-filled 5K (3.1 Mile) course through the scenic "Greenbelt" park system within the Greenhaven/Pocket neighborhood!

Participants can choose from one of three categories to enter: Race / Run / Walk.

There will be monetary awards given out to the first-, second-, and third-place men's and women's finishers in the "Race" category.

This is a fundraiser for the Senator Lions Club organization in Sacramento.

Start Times:

Race = 8:00 a.m.

Run = 8:15 a.m.

Walk = 8:30 a.m.

name: Rock It in El Moro Canyon 6K & 10 Miler
description:
Run it, hike it, and rock it on the trails of beautiful El Moro Canyon. Treat yourself to a 6K or 10 mile run or hike with challenging climbs, descents and beautiful views of the Pacific Ocean. There's nothing like reaching the finish line on a course like this! Your memories will live on through the race photos included in registration, the shirt you'll proudly wear, and your finisher medal.  Course maps are here

Races subject to weather conditions and may be rescheduled due to rain or other event and venue restrictions. Participants will be automatically transferred to the new date, and no refunds will be given.  Please note that parking at California State Parks is $15 per vehicle, payable to the park attendant on site.  Carpool if you can!

Crystal Cove State Park - Moro Canyon lot parking opens at 6:00am.  Packet pick up opens at 6:45am in the lower Moro Canyon parking lot. 8471 N Coast Hwy, Laguna Beach, CA 92651

name: Rock It in El Moro Canyon 6K & 10 Miler
description:
Run it, hike it, and rock it on the trails of beautiful El Moro Canyon. Treat yourself to a 6K or 10 mile run or hike with challenging climbs, descents and beautiful views of the Pacific Ocean. There's nothing like reaching the finish line on a course like this! Your memories will live on through the race photos included in registration, the shirt you'll proudly wear, and your finisher medal.  Course maps are here

name: Romantic Movie Night
description: Enjoy an incredible throwback romantic movie with someone you love but pay attention so you can answer the movie trivia throughout the night! We will provide snacks and beverages for your enjoyment.

name: Rotary Club of Fillmore 5/10K Run/Walk- Fillmore, California
description:
Rotary Club of Fillmore, The Rotary Club of Fillmore Community Foundation and FHS Cross-Country Team (Harrier's Club) are proud sponsors of the 5k/10k Run and Fitness Walk. All registered participants before May 10 receive a t-shirt. Registrations after May 10 are not guaranteed a shirt.
 

Race Times:

Fun Run: 7:30 a.m.

5k/10k: 8:00 a.m.

Medals

NEW 2026- Participation Medals for all finishers.

Top 3 finishers in each male and female age division: 0-9, 10-14, 15-19, 20-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59, 60-69, 70+

Top male and female finisher in the 5k and 10k will receive a gift certificate for running swag.

Packet Pickup

May 15th- Early Bird Pick Up- Information and location will be sent out 1-2 weeks before the race.

May 16th- Race Day Pick up- Starts at 6:30AM at the finish line.

Course Descriptions

Fun Run: 1k starting at the 5k/10k line and looping around the City of Fillmore fire station through the bike paths.

10k: Start at the City of Fillmore City Fire Station and travel North into the back roads where you will enjoy a nice climb up into the avocado ranches, circle back and down the hill to run until you enter the Fillmore bike path that runs along the Sespe River, then travel along the bike path, and finish back at the fire station.

5k: Start at the City of Fillmore City Fire Station and run through North Fillmore until you enter the Fillmore bike path that runs along the Santa Clarita. You will then travel along the bike path that runs along the Sespe River, then travel along the bike path, and finish back at the fire station.

Team Challenge

Earn money for your Club/Organization/Charity

1st Place- $150.00 for the 5/10k

2nd Place-$100.00 for the 5/10k

Most Participants-$50.00

Guidelines: 1. Participate in the Rotary Club of Fillmore 5/10K Run/Walk.  2. Minimum Team- 5 Members   3. Discounted Registration Fee of $30.00 through May 14th.

Earn money for your Club/Organization/Charity

name: Rotary Rainbow Run - 5k  & 1k
description:
Join us for the Third Annual Rotary Rainbow Run - 5k or 1k (Fun Run) on June 7th, 2025. The Rotary Rainbow Run is sponsored by the San Juan Bautista Rotary Club and all proceeds will benefit the San Benito County Esperanza Center  as well as local scholarship and grants.  San Juan Bautista is a small California Mission town just off Hwy 101 approximately 50 miles south of San Jose.  The Rainbow Run races will start and finish on the old El Camino Real (The Alameda) with the course taking participants through the historic downtown, friendly neighborhoods, rural countryside, and the California State Park and Mission Plaza.

Show your community pride by dressing up in a fun and colorful costume! The 5K will be timed with awards, as well as Best Costume prizes will be awarded to the best dressed runner and four legged participant.

Team themes are encouraged. Please keep costumes family friendly. Come join the fun! 

2025 Rotary Rainbow Run Start Times: Run Day: June 7th, 2025

9:00am - 1K Rainbow Fun Run

9:30am - 5K Rainbow Run

2025 Prices: 

1k Fun Run-$15 

5K - $35

Fees include a dri-tech tshirt & finisher medal

name: Ruff Run California
description:
Join Us here for our annual obstacle run designed for people and their pups! Over 20 obstacles and growing every year- this course will test your training, your bond and your willingness to just let loose and have great time! This 20 acre course is more than just getting dirty!!! Our obstacles range from mud and water to thinking and strategy to test your bond with your pup!! Are you a team??Every year we add more challenges!  After party with music, games and vendors! Come spend the day in the beautiful high desert at 4200 ft above sea level! 

Follow our Facebook page Ruff Run California for all the info and details as well as pics from the last event!

name: Ruff Run presented by Paws of Coronado
description:
Calling all dogs (and their humans)! The Ruff Run presented by Paws of Coronado is a 5K run/walk celebrating our furry friends. Come on out to Tidelands Park on Saturday, March 7th for some tail-wagging fun! 

 

Run For A Cause

Help support the vision on Paws of Coronado for every animal to have a safe and loving forever home.

 Make an additional donation with your registration to help provide PAWS of Coronado with the instant ability to fund essential medical care, finance emergency surgeries, provide behavioral support, and make vital improvements to the shelter facility! To learn more about how your donation aids PAWS of Coronado, go to pawsofcoronado.org/. 

 

Participant Perks:

  • Official Ruff Run Dog Water Bowl
  • Exclusive Doggie Finisher Medal (can also be used as dog tag!)
  • T-shirt for Your Human!
  • Doggie Bag (Swag Bag)
  • Live Finish Results and Rankings
  • Overall & Age Group Awards
 Important Note: Our furry friends must be social and on a non-retractable leash during the run! For the safety of all dogs and humans alike!

 

Event Details

  • Run or walk a 5K with your favorite furry friend; starting/finishing at Tidelands Park on Coronado Island
  • 1.5 mile course for walkers and dogs of any ability
  • 1 aid stations available for both humans and dogs
  • Awards: all runners will be timed. Overall and age group division awards are reserved for participants who run with the dog. 

 

RACE WEEKEND AT A GLANCE:

  • 7:00am  Race Day Registration and Check-in at Coronado Tidelands Park 2000 Mullinex Dr, Coronado, CA 92118
  • 8:00am  5K & 1.5 Mile Start
  • 9:15am  Awards Presentation
  • 9:30am  Event Concludes

*Subject to Change

name: Run Back to the 80s
description:
Get ready to run back in time with the Totally Rad 5K! 

Dust off your neon gear, throw on your leg warmers, and lace up those classic sneakers because it's time to hit the pavement with an epic 80s throwback twist! Whether you're a seasoned runner or just in it for the vibe, this 5K or 2 Mile Walk will take you on a totally tubular journey through the past.

 

From funky tunes blasting in your ears to the retro swag waiting for you at the finish line, this race is all about fun, fitness, and fabulous 80s fashion! Don't forget to bring your A-game for the best-dressed 80s costume contest—prizes await the most radical outfits! 

 

Join us for a morning of high-energy fun, unforgettable memories, and a celebration of all things 80s. Whether you're running, walking, or dancing to the finish line, you're guaranteed to have a blast! 

 

So, what are you waiting for? It's time to channel your inner 80s icon and race into a neon-colored future. Register today—this event will sell out faster than you can say "I love the 80s!"

 

A portion of the proceeds from this event will be donated to the Ronald McDonald House Central Valley.

name: Run Big Kern
description: Kern River Conservancy's Charity 6K/11K Run at historic Kernville and Whiskey Flat trail is a community-driven event dedicated to raising funds to support the Kern River Conservancy's mission of keeping the Kern River clean and protected. Runners and outdoor enthusiasts of all levels come together to enjoy a scenic course through the historic Keysville area while contributing to conservation efforts. Proceeds from the race go directly toward trash cleanups, habitat restoration, and public education programs that promote responsible recreation along the Kern River. This event not only raises awareness about environmental stewardship on the Kern River, but also fosters a strong sense of community involvement in preserving one of California’s most cherished natural resources.

name: Run by the Sea
description:
Run by the Sea returns to lovely Wilder Ranch State Park on Sunday, October 4th! This unique Half Marathon, 12K run, and 4K run/walk meanders along the gorgeous coastal bluffs of California's Central Coast in Santa Cruz and consists mostly of flat, packed dirt trails. Participants will enjoy scenic coastal views while passing along the bluffs and Wilder Ranch park trails. Get ready to take in the natural beauty of the Monterey Bay, the serene flats of Wilder Ranch's meadows, and maybe even catch a glimpse of some dolphins - no other race is quite like it!

Now in its 10th year, Run by the Sea is organized by the Santa Cruz Track Club and benefits the track club's youth program, Bike Santa Cruz County, and Santa Cruz Mountain Trail Stewards.
