name: The Rabbit Run 5k & OC Challenge Wild Hare 5k IRVINE
description:
IRVINE JEFFREY TRAILS . Race start /finish Jeffrey Trail Middle School

SATURDAY, April 4, 2025

RACE DAY SCHEDULE: 

  • 8:00 AM : The OC CHALLENGE WILD HARE 5K : Competitive race with age division
  • 8:35 am Top 3 Overall Awards 
  • 8:40 am Awards Ceremony for the Wild Hare
  • 8:55 am  THE BUNNY DASH kid's race    (200 yards- 5& under, 400 yards- 6 to 7, 1/2 mile- 8 and above)
  • 9:00 AM  THE RABBIT RUN 5k  All finishers get medals and a special EASTER PRIZE BAG when they finish.( You may use the bag to hide the prizes anywhere in the park or school to give your kids an Easter Hunt experience afterward)
 It's an EGGcellent RUN.  DO both 5ks.  Get two bibs and two Finisher Medals.  One Shirt

Chip timed by ITZ ABOUT TIME. If doing both.  Wear only the one bib each time you run and receive a different medal each run.  

Easter-themed goodie bags and BLING! Awesome soft, fully designed custom shirts. A finisher medal that opens!  An Easter bag full of prizes at the finish! Selfie Pictures with the Easter Bunny! 

BIB PICK IS RACE DAY ONLY . There is no early packet pick up for this race . 

Participants can pick up the day of event. Registration will open at 6:30 am on race morning and continue until the 9am race start. 

COURSE: It is out and back with a twist on a picturesque, landscaped running path.  You will be sharing the route with cyclists, other runners, and dog walkers.  If pushing a stroller, stay to the right.  .  Special appearance of the Easter bunny for great selfie photos!!  Run fast, or enjoy this event with friends &  family! Make your Easter have a healthy kick to it! 

PARKING: At 155 Visions Jeffrey Trail Middle School

And , what better to Spring into SPRING, than to run a Spring race with flower names for street names!

RESTROOMS will be located inside the school buildings to the SOUTH and NORTH of the expo area.  Follow the signs.

PROCEEDS from this event to benefit the formation of Ware in the World Foundation. Proceeds will be going to Miss Pam's Ranch, a working ranch that teaches troubled youth to ride, do chores, build esteem,  and set goals. Miss Pam RUNS her ranch from a wheelchair. We are still trying to raise funds to repair the travel chair we gifted her last year.   Plus, many other projects.  We are earning money to put on a Ware in The World 5k in Tanzania, Africa to inspire a village of youth to aspire in running.

name: The Rebel Run – 5K, 10K, 10M, and Half Marathon
description:
Join us for an out of this world run!

Details
Start Location: Alamitos Beach, 780 E Shoreline Dr. Long Beach, CA
Parking: Parking in the lot is $2/hour and starts at 8am, if you are running the Half/10m you can use the Passport app to pay for parking. Street parking is free.

Event Schedule
6:20am – Bib pick-up opens
7:00am – Half marathon & 10m start
7:30am – 5k & 10k start
7:35am – Registration & start line close
10:20am – Course closes (3 hours, 20 minutes for the Half and 10m)

Early start of 6:30am may be pre-arranged for half marathoners and 10-milers only, email your request to events@hightideruns.com. All early starters will not be eligible for awards.

Out and Back Course
5k & 10k: The 5k route is used for the 5k (one lap) and 10k (two laps) – 5k route
10m: The 5m route is used for the 10m (two laps) – 5m route
Half: The 5m route is run twice and the 5k route is run once for the Half – 5m route and 5k route

More about the Course
The beach path is an open course, so you will encounter others using it. When we start the race, please stay on the right side of the beach path. The right side is for pedestrians and the left side is for cyclists.

On-Course Support: A fully stocked water station is located along the course. The finish line will also have an aid station stocked with water, electrolytes, gels, and fruit snacks. We have a first aid kit at each station and all High Tides Crew Members have received CPR training. The turns are clearly marked with chalk, a runner turn sign, and a flag

Final Details

Bib: Please wear your race bib on the front of your shirt so we can track your time and send your pics!
Gear Check: You may leave personal items with staff at the registration tent. Please bring your own bag.
Awards: All finishers earn a medal. 1st place medals are given to the overall 1st male and female in each distance.
Results & Photos: An email with race results and photos will be sent the day after the race and earlier on Instagram. Race photos are free!

Join Us Again: Did you have a blast running with us at our low-pressure, high vibes race? We have themed races throughout the year in Long Beach, the San Fernando Valley, Orange County, and San Diego. Register for multiple races at a time to earn a discount. Check our full schedule.

Have Another Question? Check our FAQ page, it's probably answered there!

name: The Riverside County K9 Run & Walk With the Animals Experience
description:
This Riverside County event features two distinct course experiences, designed intentionally for safety, flow, and participation.

🏁 The Riverside K9 Run Experience (5K)
The 5K Run & Walk is a longer distance course open to participants with or without dogs and is best suited for high-energy dogs and participants looking for more of a challenge. Educational signage along the route highlights shelter facts, stories, and initiatives, creating a meaningful Learn While You Run/Walk experience.

🐕 Mary S. Roberts "Walk With Animals" Experience (2.5K)
The Walk With the Animals follows a separate 1.5-mile, dog-friendly course, created specifically for the safety and comfort of dogs and walkers. Participation in this walk recommends a personal dog or an on-site day foster provided by Mary S. Roberts Pet Adoption Center. This ensures a controlled, positive environment for all animals involved.

 
🎉 Finish Line Festival & 🍺Beer Garden
After completing either course, participants are invited to enjoy a festival-style finish line experience featuring food trucks, vendors, live entertainment, K9 demonstrations, and adoption opportunities.

Guests 21+ can also access the on-site Beer Garden, offering top-quality draft beer from local and national breweries. The beer garden includes shelter trivia and interactive activations, allowing guests to engage with the mission while enjoying the celebration.

A portion of all proceeds from the event directly supports Mary S. Roberts Pet Adoption Center, helping provide food, medical care, and resources for animals in our community.

After completing either course, participants are invited to enjoy a festival-style finish line experience featuring food trucks, vendors, live entertainment, K9 demonstrations, and adoption opportunities.

A portion of all proceeds from the event directly supports Mary S. Roberts Pet Adoption Center, helping provide food, medical care, and resources for animals in our community.

name: The Rocky Hill Triathlon
description:
The Rocky Hill Triathlon returns for the 11th year in Exeter, California! We are the best kept secret in the Central Valley with a course that is challenging and showcases the foothills of the Sierra Nevada mountain range. Our fun course will help push you to new limits and you can earn some of the best swag to prove it! We will be offering two different distances on race day. The Short Course will have a 400 yard swim, 12.5 mile bike & 3.1 mile run. The Long Course will have an 800 yard swim, 24.8 mile bike & 6.2 mile run. New this year is the 10k course which is challenging with two climbs over Rocky Hill. Or choose the 5k which is less challenging

We are USAT sanctioned

Events

-Short Course
-Long Course
-10k
-5k


Why the Rocky Hill Triathlon?

  • Scenic Ride and Run into the foothills

  • FREE Race Photos

  • FREE Beer Ticket to VIP Pizza

  • Rocky Hill Trucker Hat (Triathlon)

  • All Finishers get a Pullover Hoodie

  • Towel (Triathlon)

  • Polar Cycling Water Bottle (Triathlon)

  • Finisher Medal

  • Epic Finish with Music

Age Group Awards

10 Year Age Group Awards for Male and Female short distance, long distance, 5k, and 10k 

Artletic Apparel Kits Available

Artletic has designed custom kits available during registration. A portion of sales will be donated to the Rocky Hill Triathlon
Artletic Store: https://runsignup.com/Race/Store/CA/Exeter/RockyHillTriathlon2023

Who we Support

The Rocky Hill Triathlon has invested more funds back into the Exeter community than any event. Since day one the board and race director have elected to volunteer their services unpaid. A large portion of your registration will used to benefit a park or project in the city of Exeter

name: The RODEO RUN 5K/10K
description:
The RODEO RUN at Huntington Beach State Park 

                       Bringing the WILD WEST Alive!                           

The Cowboy Western-Themed Running Experience 

                                                                      Sunday, March 15, 2026 Huntington State Beach

Western Music. Live horses. Line dance instructors. Cowboy or cowgirl it up!  We are celebrating everything WESTERN.  It’s not just a run, it is the cowboy round-up of the year.  Learn to rope station, and try your turn at 2 stepping.  Best-themed WESTERN wear event shirts.  Custom cast finisher medal that turns into a belt buckle! NEW MEDAL DESIGN each year!  Line dance warm-up area.   5K /10K age division awards.  Top three overall custom awards.  RFID CHIP TIMED by Itz About Time. There is a Wild West in all of us. An extraordinary Caren Ware Event.

Race Start Time  

  • 6:30 am Registration Opens/ EXPO begins. Same day packet pick-up and same-day registration sign-ups.
  • 8:00 am Little Cowpoke Dash (200 and 400 yards)  or 1 Mile Kid's Fun Run
  • 7:30 to 8:30 WILD WEST entertainment and LINE DANCING
  • 8:30 am 5K/10K Start
  • 9:30 am 5k awards
  • 9:45 am 10k Awards

Race Location:  Huntington State Beach, CA. (lot 10. Corner. This is the EAST entrance off of Beach Blvd. and Pacific Coast Hwy. to the Left.  Lot 10. 

  • 21601 Pacific Coast Hwy, Huntington Beach, CA 92646 is the google address.  But enter in the GATE on the corner of PCH and Beach Blvd at 6:30am.  To the EAST.  If you enter to the WEST you are heading into the City of Huntington  Beach lot.  The first lot on the left is the race! Early entry at 6am is at the Main gate on Magnolia and PCH. 
  • After the race, enjoy the fun amenities of Pacific City.  Limited spaces for metered parking on the street.  Parking in Pacific City.  State Park charges $15 for parking so Carpool!  or parking on the metered streets or in Pacific City Parking structure (use the 3/4 or a mile to the race as a warm up for the parking structure)

 Perfect selfie moments! ‘Corral’ camaraderie! Awards are 3 deep in 5-year age spans.  Plus top overall male and female trophies.

Early Packet Pick up: TBD

RACE DAY SIGN UPS are available at RACE SITE  from 6:30 am to 8:15 am.  And RACE DAY PICK-UP AVAILABLE. 
Walk-up registration is welcome on race day. One person may pick up for other participants. Strollers and dogs on leases are allowed.

Registration Fee includes a Western-themed event shirt, a running bib, and the Best BELT BUCKLE  custom cast FINISHER MEDAL ever!  

AWARDS:

There are “In It To Win It” age categories 3 deep with 5-year age spans:
1-10, 11-14, 15-19, 20-24, 25-29, 30-34, 35-39 40-44, 45-49, 50-54,55-59 60-64, 65-69, 70-74, 75-79 and 80-84, 85 & plus.

Presented at 9:30 5K and 9:50 am 10K

PARKING: State Park charges $15 to enter, but you will get to park front row, right next to the event.  Carpool.  Limited meter parking on the street.  Arrive early. Or park at Pacific City and enjoy shops and a bite to eat afterward!

Course: Definitely flat and fast on the paved running path with views of the beach and the sounds of the surf crashing. Great atmosphere. 

PLEASE NOTE: The course IS open to the public and will be shared with CYCLISTS and other runners and dog walkers.

You choose your course tactics. Race…Jog…Stroll…or Roll. Families can bring strollers but agree to use them at their own risk.  Water at the 1 mile/2 mile and turn arounds for the 10K.  

The Cause: Caren Ware Events are the something for EVERYBODY and EVERY BODY races.  Our desire is to host enriching fun, healthy, outdoor options for your lives and, in turn, gift life-enhancing opportunities to others.  Activity helps health. It heals.  It makes life interesting. This is your opportunity to literally RUN a ranch. We are asking for additional donations to support MISS PAM’s Ranch; a ranch that has changed countless lives by a woman in a wheelchair. Do something real and really needed. Miss Pam’s ranch needs wheelchair accessibility. We are going to SPECIALLY BUY HER AN accessible restroom trailer for the ranch.  We can free up funds for ramps with your donations and help feed the animals on the ranch. Pick a project and fall in love with the great combination of kids and livestock. Caren Ware Events is forming the Ware in the World Foundation, which connects cultures through outdoor activities.  Providing hope, happiness, and enhanced life experiences.

Rain or Shine. 

BE Active. BE healthy. Saddle up and enjoy!

name: The Sasquatch Scramble 5K/10K/Enigmatic 11 Miler (LIVE or VIRTUAL)!
description:
The Sasquatch Scramble 5K/10K/Half RETURNS on Sun, 5/10/26 to the trails of the Presidio in San Francisco!

Where: Ecology Trail Head @ the end of Barnard Avenue, San Francisco, CA, 94129 (or ANYWHERE for Virtual)
When: Sunday, 5/10/26. The 10K starts at 8AM. The 5K starts at 8:05AM. The Half Marathomn starts at 8:10AM.
Course Maps: TBD

The Swag:

All participants (Live or Virtual) receive...

  • An AWESOME race woodallion from Aravaipa Artwork
  • A SWEET Sasquatch Scramble lifestyle tee
  • A Sasquatch Scramble beer sampler stein
  • Pre-race  bib & shirt pickup and BREWFEST at A Runner's Mind (3575 Sacramento St) on Friday, 5/8 from 5-8PM!
  • Post run beverages (bubbly water & soft drinks) & pre-packaged snacks including Jambar and Bellwether Farms yogurt.

Pre-Race Bib & Shirt Pickup (& BREWFEST) at A Runner's Mind SF on Fri, 5/8 from 5-8PM!

All scramblers are cordially invited to a festive pre-race BREWFEST with brews from Standard Deviant Brewing and a bib/shirt pickup event at A Runner's Mind SF (3575 Sacramento St) on Fri, 5/8 between 5-8PM! 

*NOTE-If you cannot attend this event, you can claim your bib/shirt on race morning between 6:30-8AM.

PLEASE NOTE WE CANNOT SUPPORT REFUNDS, TRANSFERS, AND/OR CREDITS.

In the event of race cancellation due to wildfires, hazardous air quality, hazardous weather conditions, natural disasters, COVID and/or other global pandemics, or any 'act of God' (force majeure) that is beyond our control, we cannot support refunds, transfers, and/or credits. Please note this has only happened ONCE due to COVID in 2020, but anything is possible. Please make sure you are comfortable with these potential risks before you sign up. 

In the event of race cancellation due to any of the aforementioned, we will ship all race swag/items to participants and provide direction around navigating the course(s) on your own. We'll also provide direction around submitting your result. 

We also cannot support refunds, transfers, and/or race credits if you get injured in the days/week(s) leading up to race day, if your schedule changes in the days/week(s) leading up to race day, if a work trip comes up that makes it impossible for you to attend on race day, and/or any other professional or personal matter that arises making it difficult for you to attend in person on race day.

In the event of any of the aforementioned, we will ship all race swag/items to said participants and provide direction around navigating the course(s) on your own. We'll also provide direction around submitting your result.

name: The Terminator 2 Trot: 5K, 10K & Half Marathon
description:
Presented by Jed & Ted’s Excellent Races.

On March 14, 2026, at 7:00 a.m. PST, relive one of the most legendary action sequences in film history as you race along the Los Angeles River, the iconic chase scene location from Terminator 2: Judgment Day! Kicking off near Canoga Park High School, this event features 5K, 10K, and Half Marathon distances on a fast, flat course through the heart of the Valley.

As the sequel to our inaugural race, Beyond the Streets, it’s only fitting that we pay homage to one of The Valley's greatest sequels of all time. Just like T2, this race is bigger, bolder, and totally unstoppable.

Whether you're here to run, jog, or outrun the T-1000, this race is your chance to be a part of history. Hasta la vista, baby...see you at the start line!

Choose your challenge:

  • The Hasta La Vista 5K
  • The Judgment Day 10K
  • The Skynet Half Marathon
  • The Multiverse Judgment Dash (Virtual)

Expect high-energy music, 80s and 90s throwbacks, themed signage, and a cheering crowd. Costumes welcome.

This is a Jed & Ted’s Excellent Race...fun, fast, and full of heart.

 

 

Parody Note
This event is a fan-made parody inspired by classic pop culture. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by any official rights holders. It’s all for fun and good vibes.

name: The TRON Night Run: Neon Grid 5K & 10K & Half Marathon
description:
Date & Time:
Saturday, August 15, 2026
8:00 PM – 11:00 PM

Location:
L.A. River Path – 6846 Owensmouth Ave., Canoga Park, CA 91303

Event Description:

Glow hard or go home.
Join us for The TRON Night Run, a neon-lit night race inspired by digital dreams and grid-style glory. Runners will blaze through a looped nighttime course along the L.A. River, lit up with LED vibes and TRON-inspired energy. Whether you're taking on the 5K or 10K, come dressed to impress in your brightest gear and light up the grid!

✨ Glow swag
🏅 Custom finisher medals
📸 Epic photo ops

Distances:

TRON 5K
TRON 10K

Start Time:
All distances begin together at 8:00 PM.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

🌀 Multiverse Option (Virtual Runners Welcome)
Can’t make it to the Grid? Log in from your timeline.

Our TRON Run: Neon Grid race is open to all warriors of the digital frontier—wherever you’re plugged in. Whether you’re pounding the pavement in Tokyo, biking the lightcycle trail in Boise, or navigating a treadmill in your garage, the mainframe still counts your steps.

Choose the Multiverse Option during registration and select your distance (5K, 10K, or Half Marathon).

Run anytime between August 16–18
Track your run on any device or app (Strava, Garmin, smartwatch, or just a well-timed selfie—we’re cool)
Submit your proof and shipping info
We’ll transmit your finisher’s medal straight from the Grid
You don’t need to be in Canoga Park to feel the pulse of the neon.

 

 

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

🚨 Parody Disclaimer
This race is a fan-made parody event created with love by Jed & Ted’s Excellent Races. We are not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by any of the original creators, studios, or rights holders referenced in our race themes. All names, references, and characters are used for humorous and transformative purposes under fair use. We're just fans… who like to run in costume.

name: The Valley Race – 5k, 10k, and Half Marathon
description:
High Tide Runs has made it to The Valley! THE Valley. The one and only The Valley. Now...let's represent the 818 with an amazing event of community and running!

Race Details
Location: Woodley Park, 6076 Woodley Ave, Encino, CA
Parking: Free parking in the lot; more is available on Woodley Ave


Event Schedule
6:20am – Bib pick-up opens
7:00am – Half marathon & 10k start
7:30am – 5k start
7:35am – Registration & start line close
10:20am – Course closes (3 hours, 20 minutes for the Half)

Early start of 6:30am may be pre-arranged for half marathoners, email your request to events@hightideruns.com. All early starters will not be eligible for awards.

Courses
5k route: Runners do one loop – route here
10k route: Runners do two loops - route here
Half Marathon: Runners do two loops plus the 10k route – route here

More about the Course
The race routes go across the grass, under the road through a tunnel, and enter the park. The 5k loops the lake and returns. The 10k and half head to the other side of the park, going under the bridge, and then journey back along a different path.

Our courses are on open paths so please be considerate of other park users!

On-Course Support
Multiple water stations are located along the routes. The finish line will also have an aid station stocked with water, electrolytes, and other snacks. We have a first aid kit at each station and all High Tides Crew Members have received CPR training. The turns are clearly marked with chalk and runner turn signs

Final Details

Bib: Please wear your race bib on the front of your shirt so we can track your time and send your pics!
Gear Check: You may leave personal items with staff at the registration tent. Please bring your own bag.
Awards: All finishers earn a race medal. 1st place medals are given to the overall 1st male and female in each distance.
Results & Photos: An email with race results and photos will be sent the day after the race and earlier on Instagram. Race photos are free!

Join Us Again: Did you have a blast running with us at our low-pressure, high vibes race? We have themed races throughout the year in Long Beach, the San Fernando Valley, San Diego, and Orange County. Register for multiple races at a time to earn a discount. Check our full schedule

name: The Village's Sixth Annual Miles for Mamas Walk/Run-Santa Monica
description:
Join us for The Village's SIXTH Annual Miles for Mamas Walk/Run! 

Join our main event location in Santa Monica, California, OR participate on your own with friends in your own community by registering virtually.

All proceeds help new and expecting moms with limited means!  Ask your friends and family to sponsor your race.   Prizes for the top fundraising individuals will be awarded at the finish line.  

Run or walk-you choose!  A one mile walk in solidarity or a an unofficial 5k-we've mapped out the route for you!

Set up your fundraising goal now (we suggest $300) and create a unique URL to send to everyone you know.

Let them know you are WALKING THE WALK for moms in need.

Santa Monica event begins and ends at North Street Playground off of Highway 1! (West side of the highway)

Virtual event begins wherever you are!

More details will be provided closer to the event via email.  We can't wait to to walk the walk for moms in need with you!

name: The Water Run
description:
The Water Run
📍 Los Alamos Hills Sports Park, Soccer Field #6
📅 March 21st, 2026

Get ready for a family-friendly day of fun, fitness, and fundraising—all led by kids with a heart for clean water! This event supports Living Water International, with 100% of donations going directly to building wells.

🏃‍♂️ Kids Race – Kids run loops around the football field trying to outrun the "Water Man"! The last three runners standing earn prizes and finisher medals.

👟 Family 5K Walk/Run – 16 laps around the football field. Not officially timed, but medals go to 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place finishers (men and women). We will have a water station at the start/finish for all of our runners!

💧 How It Works – One donation per family is your ticket to race. All donations go directly to Living Water International through our campaign page. Plus, kids can ask family and friends to sponsor their run to help us hit our fundraising goal.

Let’s race for clean water—and make every lap count!

name: Third Annual SCTC 5K Turkey Trot
description:
Thanksgivings Day Turkey Trot! 5K run! 

 

Please join us 11/26/2026 8:45 AM for the third annual Santa Clarita Track Club's Turkey Trot. 

The Santa Clarita Track Club invites community members of all ages to run, walk, or jog in our third annual Thanksgiving Day ‘Turkey Trot’ event benefiting the club’s Cross Country and Track & Field programs.

At the event, participants will run a 5k cross country course through the Santa Clarita Central Park through the hills overlooking the Santa Clarita Valley, 

We've added a 10 & Under 1K run around fields 9 & 10,  (8:15 am) 

The 1K event begins at 8:15 a.m. on Thanksgiving Day, Thursday, Nov. 26, 2026
The 5K event begins at 8:30 a.m. on Thanksgiving Day, Thursday, Nov. 26, 2026.

Registration takes here online place or at the race start, (An entry fee of $35.00 per runner.)

For more information about the third annual Thanksgiving Day ‘Turkey Trot’ event please contact coach Elaine Bingham at (661) 373-6897 Email coachelaine@runstorm.org

name: THOUSAND FLAGS FUN RUN
description: Join this family-friendly 5K and run through Bakersfield Breakfast Rotary’s annual Thousand Flags Memorial Day weekend display. This awe-inspiring annual event showcases over 1,000 American flags on display at The Park at River Walk to honor those we have lost. There will be a 5K course and a one-mile memorial walk. The 5K course winds its way through the scenic flag adorned park and down the multi-use trail adjacent to the park, and is suitable for both runners and walkers. Proceeds will support the Thousand Flags event and other Bakersfield Breakfast Rotary community projects. The events will be timed and awards will be given for the top three 5K finishers in each category. Register by May 3rd, 2026 to ensure you receive a Thousand Flags T-shirt. All veterans participating in the event will be recognized with a complimentary Thousand Flags pin.

name: Thrive San Diego Half Marathon & 5K
description:
The Kaiser Permanente Thrive Half Marathon & 5K returns for its 10th year!

We’re excited to THRIVE with you on Saturday, November 14, 2026! More than just a race, it’s an invitation for the entire San Diego community to “Thrive” together—staying active, eating healthy, living well, and giving back. All courses start and finish at Ski Beach in Mission Bay, offering fast, flat stretches with beautiful Mission Bay views and refreshing ocean breezes.

 
Half Marathon: 
  • Start Time: 7:15AM
  • Experience 13.1 miles of scenic San Diego beauty on a loop course that starts on Ingraham Street, winds along Mission Bay, and finishes at Ski Beach. Enjoy fast, flat stretches, picturesque bay views, and refreshing ocean breezes as you chase your personal best.
  • Go to thrivehalfmarathon.com/halfmarathon/ for more information.

 

Half Marathon Relay:
  • Start Time: 7:15AM
  • Take on the Half Marathon Relay with a partner and split the challenge of 13.1 miles! Each runner will cover approximately 6.5 miles before handing off the "baton" to your teammate at Telecote Shores. This scenic route along Crown Point starts on Ingraham St and finishes at Ski Beach in Mission Bay, featuring fast, flat stretches, breathtaking bay views, and refreshing ocean breezes.
  • For more information go to thrivehalfmarathon.com/halfmarathon-relay/.
 
5K:
  • Start Time: 7:30AM
  • The 5K is a scenic loop route along Crown Point that starts on Ingraham St and finishes at Ski Beach in Mission Bay.
  • For more information go to thrivehalfmarathon.com/5k/.
 
Entry Includes:
  • Official Thrive Short Sleeve Tech Tee
  • Racer Bib
  • Finisher Medal Unique to Each Distance
  • Chip Race Timing
  • Live Finish Results and Rankings
  • Award Winner Prizes
  • Overall & Age Group Awards
  • Access to Thrive Expo
 

Virtual Runners:
  • For runners who can’t make it to San Diego but still want to participate and benefit Make-A-Wish San Diego! Complete your distance anytime during race week and post your results to the virtual leaderboard.
  • For more information go to thrivehalfmarathon.com/virtual-runners/

 

Charity:

Run to benefit Make-A-Wish® San Diego! Join us in granting wishes for children diagnosed with critical illnesses. Donate today to show your support for Make-A-Wish® San Diego on Race Day.

 

For more information on Make-A-Wish San Diego, visit thrivehalfmarathon.com/charity/.

All courses start and finish at Ski Beach in Mission Bay, offering fast, flat stretches with beautiful Mission Bay views and refreshing ocean breezes.

 
Half Marathon: 
  • Start Time: 7:15AM
  • Experience 13.1 miles of scenic San Diego beauty on a loop course that starts on Ingraham Street, winds along Mission Bay, and finishes at Ski Beach. Enjoy fast, flat stretches, picturesque bay views, and refreshing ocean breezes as you chase your personal best.
  • Go to thrivehalfmarathon.com/halfmarathon/ for more information.

 

Half Marathon Relay:
  • Start Time: 7:15AM
  • Take on the Half Marathon Relay with a partner and split the challenge of 13.1 miles! Each runner will cover approximately 6.5 miles before handing off the "baton" to your teammate at Telecote Shores. This scenic route along Crown Point starts on Ingraham St and finishes at Ski Beach in Mission Bay, featuring fast, flat stretches, breathtaking bay views, and refreshing ocean breezes.
  • For more information go to thrivehalfmarathon.com/halfmarathon-relay/.
 
5K:
  • Start Time: 7:30AM
  • The 5K is a scenic loop route along Crown Point that starts on Ingraham St and finishes at Ski Beach in Mission Bay.
  • For more information go to thrivehalfmarathon.com/5k/.
 
Entry Includes:
  • Official Thrive Short Sleeve Tech Tee
  • Racer Bib
  • Finisher Medal Unique to Each Distance
  • Chip Race Timing
  • Live Finish Results and Rankings
  • Award Winner Prizes
  • Overall & Age Group Awards
  • Access to Thrive Expo
 

Virtual Runners:
  • For runners who can’t make it to San Diego but still want to participate and benefit Make-A-Wish San Diego! Complete your distance anytime during race week and post your results to the virtual leaderboard.
  • For more information go to thrivehalfmarathon.com/virtual-runners/

 

Charity:

Run to benefit Make-A-Wish® San Diego! Join us in granting wishes for children diagnosed with critical illnesses. Donate today to show your support for Make-A-Wish® San Diego on Race Day.

 

For more information on Make-A-Wish San Diego, visit thrivehalfmarathon.com/charity/.

name: Torrance Memorial Medical Center, BRA Run, Los Angeles
description:
Day of Event Schedule

Our 14th Annual 5K & 13K are held on a fully paved course next to the sand in Playa Del Rey on August 30th, 2026

5:15am: Parking Lots Open (LA County charges $13, bring cash). The line backs up so arrive early. 

6:15am: Registration and Vendor Booths Open

6:30am: Bike Tour Starts 

7:05am: Costume Contests

7:16am: National Anthem 🇺🇸

7:30am: 13K start (2 hour time limit, 15 min per mile pace or faster)

7:50am: 5K start

9:30am: Kids Run starts (time is approximate and depends on when the last 13K walkers are clear of the kids run course)

9:45am: Awards Ceremony

Share your photos on social media! We are @brarunla and @runmercury and our official hashtag is #brarunla. We will be resharing your posts all week post-race!


Charity

In its 14th year, The BRA Run supports Evelyn’s BFF, a charity that helps breast cancer survivors get back to their new normal while supporting counseling, reconstruction, and other items that people are often not able to get covered by their insurance. Most of our grant recipients have bills going into 6 figures! This event is the biggest fundraiser for this all volunteer organization and determines how many people they can help this year.

Evelyn, the founder of the Evelyn's Breast Friends Forever (BFF), a 501(c)3 non-profit public benefit charity foundation, started this event in 2013 and in her honor we have a 5K and a 13K at the BRA Run.

Join us for Evelyn's party so we all can help other breast cancer survivors and their families. Our event spreads awareness of breast cancer reconstruction to the community by encouraging men and women to run and walk in their BRA (Breast Reconstruction Awareness) in honor and in memory of those who have been diagnosed with breast cancer.

Donate to Evelyn's BFF.

Make it a Virtual Run/Walk

Can't make it in person but want to be a part of the event and support breast cancer survivors? Sign up for the virtual run and we will mail you a bib, shirt and medal.


Location

12000 Vista Del Mar
Dockweiler Beach
Playa Del Rey, CA US 90293

name: Totally 80's Fast Times in Huntington Beach 5K, 10K, & Half Marathon
description:
Fast Times in HB 80s Run 🎸
Totally Rad. Totally Fast. Totally 80s!
📍 Huntington Beach, CA — Lot 25

Dust off your leg warmers, pump up the boombox, and get ready to run it back to the 80s! Step into a time machine and experience Fast Times in HB — a totally tubular 5K, 10K, and Half Marathon where the vibes are high, the outfits are wild, and the music is loud!

Whether you're rocking neon spandex, channeling your inner Ferris Bueller, or just here for fast times and good vibes, this is the ultimate throwback running party. 🏁✨

 
🎭 Costume Contest
Go all-in on your best 80s look — sweatbands, tracksuits, tutus, and leg warmers are highly encouraged! 🕶️
🏆 The most outrageous, nostalgic, and creative outfits will win epic prizes.

 
🎸 80s Beach Party After the Run
The fun doesn’t stop at the finish line — join us for a totally rad post-race party featuring:
✅ Live DJ spinning the best 80s hits
✅ Local vendors + exclusive race swag
✅ Photo ops with 80s props 🚗
✅ Delicious post-run snacks to refuel

 

📍 Race Day Pickup
Available starting at 6:30 AM at the event site.
💡 Save time by grabbing your packet early — lines can get long on race day!

 📼 Why Run Fast Times?
✔ Flat & scenic oceanfront course
✔ Chip Timing - 80s finisher medal 🏅
✔ Low-key, high-energy community vibes
✔ All paces welcome — flashback fun for everyone!

name: Trail Work Series presented by Runners for Public Lands, Coyote Two Moon Trail Races, and the Los Padres Forest Association
description:
Runners for Public Lands (RPL) envisions a world in which everyone has access to healthy, clean, and runnable environments. We are a 501(c)(3) nonprofit that empowers runners to engage in climate action, protect public lands, and expand access to nature for all people. 

We are excited to partner with the United States Forest Service (USFS), Los Padres Forest Association, and Coyote Two Moon to present the 2026 Trail Work Series in Ventura County. This brings our local community of runners together to learn about and care for the living landscapes we run with. Through repetitive, hands-on service events, we can share ecological values and create strong connections that inspire runners to care for the people and places they love. 

This 2026 Ventura Trail Work Series will include 3 independent trail work events, each event will be approved, permitted, and insured by the USFS, led by the Los Padres Forest Association trail work leaders, and managed by Runners for Public Lands Staff and volunteers.  Participants are not required to attend all events but can earn prizes/incentives from our brand coalition sponsors including nomadix, Keen, Teva, Altra and GU for attending multiple events. 

Registration opens on February 6 for the first event of the season on Saturday, February 21st. Registration for the second event opens on February 8th, and one month out for the March event. Please note that the days and times of all events are subject to change based on the discretion of the USFS, current conditions and weather. We will keep everyone informed through the Runners for Public Lands Ventura Strava Club and direct emails to registrants.

name: Tri Santa Cruz
description:
Come play at  of one of the most fun and scenic events on the west coast. This race has a sprint and international (Olympic) distance triathlon, with relays, aquathalon and aquabike categories for both races. Clydesdale and Athena triathlon categories are available.

 

There is a special, non-competitive Family & Friends wave for people who are new to triathlon or just want to race with family and friends regardless of age or gender. 

 

Special youth pricing is available for youth 12-17 and seniors 70+ for all individual distances.  Contact us for a discount for an all youth/senior relay team.

 

Triathlon club disounts available.  If your Tri Club does not have a code, have a club officer contact us.

 

Sheltered swim and flat bike and run course make this a perfect place for your first race or a PR. Voted one of the best late season triathlons in the country. The bike ride is a totally closed course and both the bike and run courses follow the coastline to create one of the most scenic races around! (Pending approval of the 2025 bike course)

 

Stick around and play for a day at the famous Santa Cruz Beach Boardwalk or visit the Surfer Museum or National Marine Sanctuary Center.

 

Participants will receive a finisher medal and custom t-shirt as part of their registration, plus a post race lunch and awards.

name: Tri to Inspire
description:
Tri to Inspire, formerly the DJFE Triathlon Race Series, was created to introduce the sport of triathlon to the Sonoma County community in a welcoming, inclusive way. This short-distance event is open to all abilities and is ideal for first-time triathletes and families looking to experience a fun, supportive race environment together.

Athletes may choose between two distance options. The Mini Sprint includes a 100-yard pool swim, a 3-mile bike, and a 1-mile run. The Sprint distance features a 400-yard pool swim, a 9-mile bike, and a 3.1-mile run. Tri to Inspire is a non-competitive, untimed event designed to help participants complete their first triathlon—or simply enjoy the experience without pressure. More experienced athletes are also encouraged to participate and will find a positive, community-focused atmosphere. The race begins with a pool swim at the Finley Aquatic Center, followed by a flat, family- and beginner-friendly bike and run course along the Santa Rosa Creek Trail.

Each athlete’s registration includes a custom finisher medal, swim cap, and athlete goody bag. Proceeds benefit Inspiration Sports Foundation, a local 501(c)(3) nonprofit supporting youth in Sonoma County through sports camps and fitness-based programs.

name: TriFind Race Director Summit
description:
The Future of Multisport Starts Here

The TriFind Multisport Race Director Conference brings together the industry’s most influential race directors and brand partners for an afternoon of insight, collaboration, and recognition.

With representatives from 1,600+ multisport races invited, this gathering is designed to deliver real data, actionable strategy, and meaningful connections that shape the future of endurance racing.

Who’s Invited

  • 900+ NGB races
  • 600+ Non-NGB races
  • Leading brands and sponsors seeking 2027 partnerships
  • Industry media and nonprofit leaders

Important Registration Information

This registration is intended for race directors attending the TriFind Race Director Summit.

Sponsors and brand partners are warmly invited to participate, but must register through the 2026 Optimism Cal Tri Newport Dunes race registration at the sponsor rate. 

This ensures sponsors receive the appropriate race weekend access, exposure, and activation opportunities, while allowing the summit sessions to remain focused on race director collaboration.

What You’ll Experience

2026 State of the Sport
A comprehensive look at participation trends, athlete behavior, and market outlook.

Actionable Research & Insights
Channel and consumer research presentations you can apply immediately to grow and strengthen your races.

Brand & Sponsor Engagement
Connect with companies actively seeking race partnerships and activation opportunities for 2027.

Race Director Awards
Honoring excellence and leadership in the industry, including:

  • Most Innovative Race
  • Most Collaborative Organization
  • Additional peer-recognized honors

Hosted & Emceed By
Bob Babbitt — Breakfast With Bob, the voice of endurance sports.

Registration & Giving Back

Introductory Registration: $100
100% of proceeds benefit the Challenged Athletes Foundation (CAF)

Your registration directly supports athletes with physical challenges, reinforcing the multisport community’s commitment to inclusion and impact.

Conference Hotel & Room Block

A limited block of hotel rooms is available at a discounted rate for attendees.

We strongly recommend booking early, as availability is limited and rooms are expected to sell out.

🔗 Reserve your discounted room here.

Exclusive Race Director Benefit

Registered race directors are invited to compete at no cost in the
 2026 Optimism Cal Tri Newport Dunes
 📅 November 1, 2026

The longest-running triathlon in the world operating continuously from the same venue - a chance to race, connect, and celebrate the sport alongside your peers.

Why Attend

  • Gain clarity on where the sport is headed
  • Learn what’s working and what’s next
  • Build relationships that power future races
  • Be recognized for the work you do
  • Give back to a cause that strengthens our community

Secure Your Spot

Limited capacity. Early registration recommended.

name: Tulare Santa Fe Trail-A-Thon 5k
description:
Get ready to join the community for the 23rd annual Tulare Santa Fe Trail-A-Thon 5k, hosted by the Tulare Sunrise Rotary Club! This fun and impactful event supports the club’s High School Scholarship Program, which in 2024 awarded a $5,000 4 year college and a $1,500 trade school scholarship to two Tulare High School seniors. 

Event Details:

Date & Location: The race begins and ends at Live Oak Park, Tulare, offering a scenic route and plenty of space to enjoy the day.

 

Time: Onsite registration and bib pickup will run from 8:00 am to 8:45 am, with the race starting promptly at 9am.

 

Registration: This year we are charging a registration fee of $15 per participant. This fee helps cover the costs of the finisher and winner medals and the timing system costs. We will also accept donations this year.

Awards and Prizes:

Finisher Medal: All finishers will receive a commemorative medal and lanyard and Rotary participant pin.

 

Age Group Awards: Medals will be awarded to top finishers in each age group: 9 & Under, 10-14, 15-19, 20-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59, 60+ (Male and Female).

 

Fastest Runner Awards: The top male and female runners will each receive a special trophy and $100 gift card!


Sponsor Opportunities:

Want to help make a difference in the lives of local students? Consider becoming a sponsor! Contact Matthew Hamilton at matt@hamiltonmarketing or Petrus Tjandra at ptjandra@aol.com for more information.

 

Join us for a memorable morning on the Santa Fe Trail as we come together to support education and enjoy some friendly competition. See you on race day!

name: Tunnel to Towers 5K Run & Walk - Riverside County, CA
description:
What is a Tunnel to Towers Run & Walk?
The Tunnel to Towers Run & Walk Series was created to honor the heroic life and death of Stephen Siller, a New York City firefighter (FDNY) who lost his life on September 11, 2001 after strapping on his gear and running through the Brooklyn Battery Tunnel to the Twin Towers. Honor all of those who lost their lives on September 11, 2001 and support our first responders and military who make extraordinary sacrifices in the line of duty! For more information on the Tunnel to Towers Foundation, please visit www.t2t.org.

This will be our 2nd Annual Tunnel to Towers 5K Run & Walk in Riverside and we are excited to grow the community’s commitment to honor first responders, remember 9/11, and raise funds for the Tunnel to Towers Foundation. This event is put on in conjunction with CalFire, the Riverside County Sheriff's Department, and the Ben Clark Training Center.

How far is a Tunnel to Towers Run & Walk?
This is a 5K (3.1 miles). Anyone can run, walk, or experience this event

What is the address of the event?
Ben Clark Training Center 16902 Bundy Ave, Riverside, CA 92518

Where can I pick up my packet?
Packet pick up will  be available on the morning of the event (3/21/2026) at the Ben Clark Training Center beginning at 7am and at the Moreno Valley College of Public Safety in the afternoon on Friday, March 20th. Please check back for information on a  pre-event day packet pick up hours as the event date approaches!

Where can I pick up my packet?
Yes, T-shirts are guaranteed to all participants who register before March 1st, 2026

Can I register the day of the run?
Yes. Registration will open at 7am the morning of the run at the Ben Clark Training Center. You’ll save time and money if you register in advance. In addition, if you wait to register we may not have a shirt for you and we do not guarantee sizes for late registrants.

Is there parking available?
Yes. There is plenty of parking at the Ben Clark Training Center.

Do I have to wear my bib number?
Yes, please display your bib on the front of your outermost garment. The bib number is how we record the time. Those who run without a bib will be asked to leave the course and will not be allowed to finish.

I am a fast runner. Can I get a front line position?
Runners predicting a pace faster than 6 minute/mile will be seeded in the front corral (arrive early).

Will there be awards for running?
Award medals will be given to the top three men/women, boys/girls under 18, and the top 3 first responders running in their turnout gear.

Will water be available?
Yes, water will be available at the start line/finish line and at the crossover section of the course by miles 1 and 2.5

What can you bring to the event? Can I run with a stroller, backpack, wheelchair, roller blades, bicycle, etc?
Strollers and wheelchairs are permitted, but we ask that those with strollers start towards the back. Firefighter turnout gear and military backpacks are also permitted. Please leave all personal items and valuables in your vehicle. All items should be stored securely at the owner's risk. Tunnel to Towers Foundation will not be responsible for the loss of any items.

Does my registration fee count towards my fundraising goal?
Your registration fee does not count toward the fundraising goal.

Can someone else pick up my packet for me?
Yes, they can. They must present a copy of your registration receipt. And don't forget to thank them!

Can I still donate to a team and/or individual after the start of the race?
Yes. Donations will be accepted for 6 weeks after the event.

How can my company/organization sponsor this event?
Please send all sponsorship correspondence to riversiderun@t2t.org with your contact information and someone will be in touch with you within 24 hours.

I would like to donate goods or services to this event. How do I do that?
You can contact us at riversiderun@t2t.org We make every effort to keep costs down to allow us to give the most to the Tunnel to Towers Foundation’s programs.

As a participant, can I fundraise/encourage others to donate?
Yes! Once you are registered, you will be given directions to start your own fundraising page and you will be able to accept donations online. Do you want to donate cash/money? We can help you with that. Contact us at riversiderun@t2t.org and we can walk you through the process or you can send donations directly to: 

Tunnel to Towers Foundation
ATTN: Riverside 5K – Thomas Mazza
2361 Hylan Blvd.
Staten Island, NY 10306

Please  give us your information so we can add it to your fundraising page.

Where can I mail an OFFLINE donation (check made payable to Tunnel to Towers Foundation)?
Please mail any offline donations to:

Tunnel to Towers Foundation
ATTN: Riverside 5K – Thomas Mazza
2361 Hylan Blvd.
Staten Island, NY 10306

Can I transfer my registration to another participant?
Yes. See information above OR contact us at riversiderun@t2t.org and we will manually change it in our system.

Can I get a refund?
We do not provide refunds for the event regardless if you cannot make the date or the foundation needs to cancel the event for extenuating circumstances. Registration may be transferred to another person.

How can I volunteer?
It's simple, either register online or email us at riversiderun@t2t.org and we will reply within 24 hours. Volunteers are always needed for the day of festivities. Thank you!

Do registrants get receipts?
When you register online you should automatically receive a receipt via email. 

Is there a medical staff available on-site?
Yes, there will be an Emergency Medical Service team available on site. There is also radio communication available on the course to help communicate with the EMS.

Does Tunnel to Towers offer fundraising incentives?
Yes, we offer fundraising incentives each year; check out our latest in our Fundraising Guide.

name: Two Cities Marathon
description: In its 18th year and presented by CalViva Health, 2CM takes place in the central valley of California along the border of Fresno and Clovis. Our events offer scenic and truly flat PR courses for elite and beginners alike.  Unique features of our Boston qualifying marathon distance include the Boston Challenge and  an exciting Final Mile Competition in the full and half distances.

name: UCR Glow Run 2026
description:
You are personally invited to join us for our 4th Annual Health, Well-being, and Safety (HWS) Glow Run at UC Riverside. It is an exciting 5K that is open to the entire UCR community, as well as the local community.  This year, the event is led by The Well and R’ Healthy Campus.

-This 5K is officially timed; however, participants are welcome to either run or walk. 

-Registration is required before the event date to participate. 

  • $5- UCR Students
  • $15-UCR Staff and Faculty
  • $20-Community Members

Goals of Glow Run 2026:
  • Create a family-friendly environment to promote physical health and community
  • Encourage participants to learn about the benefits and resources related to physical health
  • Increase awareness and visibility of the HWS Division and its aligned mission to care for the health and well-being of the UCR and local community
  • Use funds from registration to support The Well department to expand and further the impact of their wellbeing strategies and services to the UCR community. 


Who Are We and What is Our Mission: 

  • Health, Well-being & Safety (HWS) is a UCR division made up of nine departments that are dedicated to listening, supporting, and providing UC Riverside students with helpful resources and services for your overall safety and well-being.
  • The Well Department advances health education and promotion at UCR by applying intentional, evidence-informed strategies that foster a culture of holistic well-being. We collaborate to create inclusive and innovative approaches that support the lifelong health of the UCR community.
  • R’ Healthy Campus: To embed health, equity, and sustainability into the daily learning and working experience at UCR—advancing the University’s mission by supporting inclusive programs, partnerships, and resources that help every member of our community thrive

 

Details: 

Thursday, April 23rd, 2026

  • Doors Open at 5:00 pm
  • Run/walk Starts and 6:00pm
  • Event Ends at 8:00pm 

UCR Rivera Lawn 

900 University Ave, Riverside, CA 92521


Registration Details: 

Your registration will include:

  • Bib for official timing
  • Ticket for Food and a drink
  • Participatory Medal

name: United Health Centers Foundation Fun Run
description:

name: USS Hornet Halloween 5k
description:
Event Details: October 30th.  Friday pre-halloween Evening Run 

We have partnered with the USS Hornet to bring back a super fun and unique race experience to Alameda. Our "day of the dead" Twilight Run we did a few years ago is back, just moving the date slightly to coincide with Halloween. The event will still benefit the USS Hornet Museum and will start at 6:30pm. Sunset is scheduled that evening for 6:12pm, so headlamps are recommended but we will have lights on the course. 

Costume highly recommended and encouraged! 

The run will take you for a scenic loop around Alameda Point, starting and finishing at the Pier. Runners will enjoy views of San Francisco, spirit alley and the estuary shoreline along the flat and fast 5k course. There will be our normal beer garden, food, music and Age Group awards

THERE IS NO KIDS RUN FOR 2026 - DUE TO TRAFFIC CONCERNS ON FRIDAY NIGHT.

There is plenty of parking at the Hornet and around Alameda Point. 

Event - Schedule 

  • Packet pick-up ~ Lauren's Closet: 1420 Park st: October 28th - 29th: 10:00am - 5:00pm
  • Race day Registration and Packet Pick-up ~ USS Hornet: 4:30pm
  • 5K run starts ~ 6:30pm 
  • 5K awards ~ 7:15pm
  • Expo and music ~ 6:00pm - 8:00pm

name: VALENCIA Trail Race
description:
Run the VALENCIA Trail Race, run the awesome trails and killer hills with breathtaking views of the Santa Clarita Valley in a 10K, Half Marathon, or 50K Ultra race. For runners who love to run great trails and want to accomplish a good challenge. Prepare to take on the Awesome Trail Challenge in Valencia, California. Southern California features a diverse range of nature and terrain, giving runners a wide variety of spectacular trails and running experiences. Located north of Los Angeles up against the California State park boundaries is Valencia, a suburban community that is surrounded by hills and mountains featuring awesome trails to be experienced.

Registration is now open with course distances for all types of runners to offer a variety of challenges. Experience a course that takes you up challenging hills to the peaks and along the ridgelines with panoramic views, then into the canyons and valleys for a truly awesome trail challenge.  Registration is available on VALENCIATrailRace.com or on the popular Active.com running network. 

Learn more at >> VALENCIATrailRace.com

name: VIRTUAL Race for Rewritten - An Annual Race for the Fatherless and Underserved
description:
Welcome to our VIRTUAL Race for ReWritten! VIRTUAL, simply, means your miles take place wherever you choose- a local park, a track, a treadmill, your neighborhood, wherever you're able to get those miles done. All you need to do is register and once you receive your race kit in the mail- throw on your race shirt anytime between June 12-21, 2026, find your route, track your miles, upload your time, then, put on your race medal for doing the hard work of completing those miles and supporting fatherless youth. More exciting details below!

About Race for ReWritten

We are thrilled to bring to you an opportunity to be a part of our Annual Race for ReWritten - Virtual Edition, happening wherever you are! An event that supports our efforts to bring Christ-centered, highly-relational, mentoring support to fatherless and underserved youth all across America. Join the movement, from June 12-21, 2026, that is bringing people together from all over the country. Whether you walk, run or roll, grab a friend or two, register and head out into your neighborhood, to your local park or anywhere else you can race to help us transform the lives of young people near and far. 

For over 14 years, ReWritten has been working to improve the quality of life for young people who are living with the burden of an absent father. A burden we believe no boy or girl should have to carry alone. A young person growing up without a father, is a young person at risk. To fill the void left by their fathers, youth will often turn to drugs to feel good, promiscuity to feel loved, and gangs to belong.

It, simply, doesn’t have to be this way.

That’s what this race is about.

This race will play an important role in the financial support of our impactful programs and services offered year round, in-person and virtually throughout the United States. Programs that provide much needed emotional and academic help to struggling young people hoping for real change. With your support, we can continue to make a real difference in the lives of young men and women at a time when they need it most.

We pray you will join us!

Race Details

2026 Race for ReWritten - June 12-21, 2026

Pricing
EARLY BIRD REGISTRATION- February 15, 2026, 12:00am PDT - March 31, 2026, 11:59pm PDT

5k $40.00 Race Fee

REGULAR REGISTRATION- April 1, 2026, 12:00am PDT - April 30, 2026, 11:59pm PDT 

5k $50.00 Race Fee

LATE REGISTRATION- May 1, 2026, 12:00am PDT - May 31, 2026, 11:59pm PDT 

5k $65.00 Race Fee

*PLEASE NOTE - All "Late Registration" participants are subject to receive standard (non-race/event) participation race swag bag, t-shirt and medal while supplies last.

**5k Child (12 and Under) Registration February 15, 2026 12:00 PDT - May 31, 2026 11:59 PDT - $25

Race Kit

In addition to an incredible opportunity to join a movement, early and regular race kit registration includes:

Swag Bag

2026 Race for ReWritten T-Shirt

Race Bib

Event Medal

Race Kit Disbursement and Shipment

Race Kit disbursement and shipments will begin the week of June 1, 2026.

Social Media

Post your pictures and share your race experience with us using #RaceforReWritten.

*Social media links are located in the banner above and at the bottom of this page.

name: Walk for Water 5K Los Angeles
description:
Walk Their Journey. Change Their Future.

Join us for a powerful and transformative experience at the Walk for Water 5K Charity Fundraiser, co-hosted by Pathway To Tomorrow and Drop of Water. This isn’t just a walk—it’s a step into the daily reality that millions of women and girls in Africa face just to access something as basic as water. 

Every day, women and girls spend 200 million hours hauling unclean water, often walking miles under a burning sun, along dangerous paths, carrying heavy containers. Every two minutes, a child dies from a water-borne disease, and 1.5 million children under five die annually in Africa from diarrhea caused by unsafe water. 

Ethiopia, Africa’s second most populous country, is in the grip of this devastating water crisis. Nearly half of its 125 million people lack access to clean water, according to UNICEF.

The situation is even worse in rural areas — where 80% of Ethiopians live and are hit hardest by this crisis, forcing women and girls to walk long distances just to find unclean water. Girls are expected to miss school to collect water for their families. Each journey robs a girl of her education, her safety, and her childhood. For far too many, these walks end in tragedies, like gender-based violence and death — not just exhaustion.

We walk not just for awareness—but for action.

This 5K fundraiser challenges participants to take 7,000 steps, representing the average distance many walk each day to collect water. As you walk, you’ll carry not just steps—but stories. Stories of resilience, hardship, and hope. You'll walk in solidarity with those who can’t just turn on a tap.

We’re asking each participant to go further by asking friends, family, and coworkers to sponsor their steps with a donation to the cause, or join their team to fundraise or walk alongside them!

Our goal? To raise $250,000 to fund 2 deep borehole wells and rural piping systems in up to 16 rural villages in Ethiopia. This will provide clean, safe, and sustainable drinking water for up to 16,000 people. 

Your steps can change a life. Your walk can build a well.

Register today. Walk their path. Bring water home.

The 5K route is along the Main Trail at Griffith Park - 4800 Crystal Springs Drive, Los Angeles, CA 90027

The course is flat, scenic and shaded, covering the perimeter of the golf course.

name: Waves & Whales 5K Trail Run
description:
The annual Waves & Whales 5K Trail Run‐Walk is held on the Mendocino Coast in Point Arena. Taking full advantage of the location, the run takes place on the Point Arena-Stornetta Unit of the California Coastal National Monument. The course begins behind City Hall in the conifer forest off Highway 1, makes its way to the coast where it follows the bluffs, and then winds back into the pine and cypress forest.

Proceeds from the Waves & Whales Trail Run support ACORN Partners in Education’s environmental stewardship program, Students Protecting the Coast, which engages youth in hands‐on learning with a focus on conservation and community outreach. Students Protecting the Coast began during the 2012‐13 school year as part of the local and national campaign to include the Point Arena‐Stornetta Lands in the California Coastal National Monument. Students continue to learn about our coastal landscape and are empowered to use their voice by sharing what they’ve learned with the community.

ACORN is committed to hosting a sustainable event that honors the natural landscape and educates the larger community. The Waves & Whales Trail Run promises to be a worthwhile coastal excursion—runners can expect a rejuvenating run surrounded by natural beauty and the knowledge that they are supporting the continued stewardship of this land by, and for, the next generation.

  • Hikers welcome.
  • Participants receive organic cotton t‐shirt and snacks. (Register early to ensure a t-shirt in your size.)
  • Age categories and awards. (Hand-made award medallions from Point Arena Tileworks.)

name: We Crawl this Town- 5k and Beer Mile Relay - Camarillo
description:
In partnership with Institution Ale Company from Camarillo CA, join us for this off the wall kind of run. 

Once again we will offer 2 events;

5K-(Family Friendly)
Starting with the widely popular beer send off toast (21+ runners only) you will embark on a fast and flat course starting and finishing from the brewery. Along the way you will run a significant portion of your race on the beautiful bike path over looking the Calleguas Creek before ultimately finish back at the brewery. Stick around and join us for beer sampling, discounted food and music.

Beer Mile Relay!- (Teams of 4 - All team member must be 21+)
Here teams go head to head in our one of a kind race format.

Runner#1- Drink 12 oz beer/ run 1 mile/ drink 12 oz beer/ pass baton

Runner#2- Drink 12 oz beer/ run 1 mile/ drink 12 oz beer/ pass baton

Runner#3- Drink 12 oz beer/ run 1 mile/ drink 12 oz beer/ pass baton

Runner#4- Drink 12 oz beer/ run 1 mile/ drink 12 oz beer/all team members cross the finish together.

name: We Crawl this Town- 5k and Beer Mile Relay - Camarillo
description:
In partnership with Institution Ale Company from Camarillo CA, join us for this off the wall kind of run. 

Once again we will offer 2 events;

5K-(Family Friendly)
Starting with the widely popular beer send off toast (21+ runners only) you will embark on a fast and flat course starting and finishing from the brewery. Along the way you will run a significant portion of your race on the beautiful bike path over looking the Calleguas Creek before ultimately finish back at the brewery. Stick around and join us for beer sampling, discounted food and music.

Here teams go head to head in our one of a kind race format.

Runner#1- Drink 12 oz beer/ run 1 mile/ drink 12 oz beer/ pass baton

Runner#2- Drink 12 oz beer/ run 1 mile/ drink 12 oz beer/ pass baton

Runner#3- Drink 12 oz beer/ run 1 mile/ drink 12 oz beer/ pass baton

Runner#4- Drink 12 oz beer/ run 1 mile/ drink 12 oz beer/all team members cross the finish together.

name: West Coast SUCK
description:
Created by Joe Decker, a Guinness World Record holder and accomplished Ultra Endurance Athlete, The SUCK is twelve hours of non-stop pushing your limits with a purpose behind every minute. Each overnight SUCK takes you through miles of dark trails, heavy carries, military style calisthenics, strongman work, and whatever curveballs Mother Nature feels like throwing your way.

Make no mistake, it is brutal. And that is exactly why it works. We are not out there to break you. We are out there to empower you. Sometime around 2 AM, when the world goes quiet and your excuses run out, you discover who you really are. You face the stuff you have been avoiding. And then you rise anyway. That feeling stays with you long after the sun comes up.

Come test yourself in one of the most extreme fitness challenges on the planet. Do the hard thing on purpose and walk away a different person.

And if you finish the entire event, you earn a one of a kind Challenge Coin. It cannot be bought. It cannot be gifted. You have to earn it the hard way. It puts your name on the short list of those who have stepped into the dark, fought through the doubt, and officially Embraced the SUCK. 

The SUCK - Mandatory Gear: 
• Ruck Sack / Backpack - I personally recommend a 60 liter / 3500 cubic inch
• CamelBak hydration plus pack - recommend 70 - 100 oz
• Guys 2 x 50lb sandbags
• Gals 2 x 35lb sandbags
• 2 x 5 gallon buckets
• Headlamp
• Duct tape
• Pliers
• Trail Shoes
• Work gloves
• Workout gear
• Warm/cold weather gear
• Plenty of food, water & electrolytes for the entire 12 hours, there are no aid stations
• Suggested - snake bit kit, poison ivy/oak remedy, first aid kit

NOTE: Gut Check Fitness, LLC policy is that there are NO REFUNDS and/or TRANSFERS. You are making a commitment to train, work hard, stay focused then to show up and 'Embrace the SUCK'. Please reach out if you are in need of a training program.

name: WICKED FAST MARATHON & HALF MARATHON SAN DIEGO
description:
Experience San Diego’s newest and fastest marathon!

The Wicked Fast Marathon & Half Marathon San Diego is San Diego’s premier speed course, featuring a net downhill drop of under 1,500 feet from start to finish — fully compliant for Boston Qualifying with zero penalties. Starting in the mountain town of Alpine, California, runners cruise through San Diego’s East County on a smooth, scenic rolling descent and finish in unforgettable style at Sycuan Casino Resort. With long, flowing downhills, gentle rollers, and fast pavement, this course is purpose-built for PRs, BQs, and breakthrough performances — delivering a stunning Southern California race experience that’s as beautiful as it is blazing fast.

name: Wild Flowers 10k
description:
Join us for the 2026 Wild Flowers 10K 🌸

Run in Auburn… Finish in Spain! 

Trip to Spain is from September 21st to September 28th, 2026 

Get ready for the most empowering girls’ day of the year! The Wild Flowers 10K is a joyful morning where besties, sisters, and mamas bloom together — running, walking, laughing, and celebrating every step.

🌸 From the stunning views of the scenic Auburn trails, you’ll experience a race filled with heart, sparkle, and pure women’s magic.

🌸 Every 10K finisher receives a beautiful Wild Flowers race tee as a symbol of your strength and sisterhood.

🌸 The magic doesn’t stop at the finish line. 4 finishers earn an all-expenses-paid trip to Spain to represent Auburn.

🌸 Four will be randomly chosen to enjoy a dreamy week in Spain at an exclusive women’s running camp in VIGO Galicia lead by our elite runner Aroa Sio! (Yes , you just have to finish the race )

🌸 Your journey starts at the Auburn … but it might just take you across the world.

Girl Time + Celebration ✨ 

After the race, join us in the pavilion for a warm, complimentary breakfast cooked by the Wild Runners crew.

Take photos, celebrate your shine, and enjoy a morning filled with love, friendship, and community.

Tell every wonder woman in your life 

🌸 This is her day to bloom grab your besties. Hold hands. Believe in your bloom. 

🌸 You don’t have to be the fastest — every woman has a chance to win big!

🌸 4 finishers earn an unforgettable trip to Spain, representing Auburn.

 

Packet Pick-up 

Friday, April 10th 2026: 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. (Wild Runners Auburn – 198 Sacramento Street)

Saturday, April11th 2026 (Race Day): Packet pickup opens at 7:15 a.m. (Starting Line)

Event Day Schedule 

Saturday, April, 11th 2026:  Packet pickup opens at 7:15 a.m. (Starting Line)

Wild Flowers 10K start at 8:30 a.m.

Awards 

Overall Awards: There will be a prize for the top 3 overall 10K winners.( only the winner gets the first ticket to Spain the other spots are via raffle )

 

10K Age Division Awards

Awards to the top three finishers in the following age groups:

18-24, 25-29, 30-34, 35-39, 40-44, 45-49, 50-54, 55-59, 60-64, 65-69, 70-74, and 75-over

Course Information 

Saturday, April 11th 2026: 8:30 am

Your journey begins at the beautiful Auburn Overlook, where the Wild Flowers 10K takes off into some of the most scenic trails in Northern California. This fun loop has a little bit of everything — smooth downhills, peaceful flats, and (because this is Auburn) a reminder that if you go down… you will go back up.

You’ll experience sections of gorgeous single-track, rolling stretches perfect for finding your rhythm, and viewpoints that will make you stop and say “wow” or at least pretend you’re stopping for the view and not to catch your breath.

We’ll have two fully stocked aid stations, a cheerful crew directing you every step of the way, and… breaking news…Sasquatch has officially confirmed his appearance. (He promised to cheer loudly, but we can’t guarantee he won’t photobomb.)

Get ready for fun, adventure, and the most unforgettable 10K you’ll ever run.

Course Preview Day

Join us for a course preview training run on March 28 at 8:00 AM, starting at Wild Runners Auburn (198 Sacramento St, Auburn, CA). We’ll explore the route together so you’ll know exactly what to expect on race day.

After the run, enjoy refreshments and food back at Wild Runners. Our sponsors will also be there with demo shoes, and 3 lucky runners will each win a free pair of shoes!

Parking Information 

Saturday, April, 11th 2026

You may park at Railhead Park, along nearby neighborhood streets (please do not block driveways or entrances), by the high school, or in the two public lots in Old Town Auburn.

Please note: parking in Old Town may require up to a 1-mile walk to the start.

Plan to arrive early to give yourself plenty of time.

RACE RULES

🌸 Friends may pick-up packets and register for you.

🌸 No entry refunds, transfers, or exchanges.

🌸 Due to course congestion, NO STROLLERS or ANIMALS are allowed on the course. 

🌸 No leg or foot casts allowed.

🌸 Per our official event rules and guidelines: Sale and/or transfer of race entry/bib is strictly prohibited and will result in the disqualification and/or banning of any individuals involved from future events. All entry fees are non-refundable and may not be deferred toward a future event.

🌸 Winners must show or get a passport within 30 days. If winners cannot attend the trip, a new winner will be randomly drawn from the finishers.

🌸 Elite runners are not eligible for the trip to Spain. This is an amateur run.

name: Wild for Moreland Community 5K (Run/Walk)
description: This is a Moreland Community Event run by the Moreland Education Foundation.  Our goal is to build community and to raise money to continue enhancing Art, Music, Sports and the education enrichment of the students in all seven schools in the Moreland School District.  Join this fun family event with your Moreland community and invite friends and relatives.  Enjoy a fun morning out, community booths, games, and food & a friendly competition among schools. Please wear your school colors to show your school pride! Note kids under 5 are free and don't need to register as they won't receive a bib,

name: Wild Rose Half Marathon & 5K
description:
Wild Rose Half Marathon & 5K
Saturday, May 16, 2026 – 8:30 AM
Pleasant Grove Bike Path, Roseville, CA (start/finish at Moksa Barrel House)

The brand new Wild Rose Half Marathon & 5K is blooming in Roseville this spring! Starting at Moksa Barrel House, runners will enjoy smooth paved trails, fresh air, and a new PR!

  • Half Marathon: A unique forked out-and-back on the Pleasant Grove Bike Path with less than 240ft of elevation gain. Flat, fast, and ideal for chasing a personal best.
  • 5K: A popsicle loop through William Hughes Park with just 40ft of elevation gain. Short, fun, and welcoming to runners of all levels.

All Half Marathon & 5K Runners will receive their choice of a Wild Rose technical shirt or BOCO running hat, a finishers medal, plus a drink ticket from Moksa Brewing Co. (21+). Walkers will receive a finishers medal and a drink ticket. After the race, stick around for raffle prizes from our sponsors.

Presented by Bad Luck Run Club

name: Wise Villa Wine Run 5K
description:
Like Running or Walking?  Love Wine?  This race is for you! 

Join us on Saturday, April 11, 2026 with start times at 8:30am and 10:30am (you will select your start time during registration) for an exciting annual event that features The Wise Villa Winery. Since their first vintage was released in 2009, Wise Villa has been a family owned and operated winery, estate vineyard, and Tuscan-style Gourmet Restaurant located in the heart of the Sierra Foothills Wine Appellation of Placer County. Their grapes are meticulously grown using organic and sustainable practices. During harvest they go a step further by triple sorting and implementing whole berry cold fermentation to retain a balanced wine with natural fresh fruit character. So, whether you are looking to run, walk or just enjoy the wonderful wine and camaraderie this race is a sure thing for a great time and an incredible experience!  This race is timed and scored by J3 Timing.  Results will be posted at www.J3Timing.com. 

Registration Includes:

  • T-shirt:  Super Soft Ring Spun Cotton t-shirt included! 
  • Wine Glass: Wise Villa Winery logo plastic tumbler!
  • Finisher Medal: Doubles as a Wine Stopper!
  • Race Bib: Chip timed 5k run/walk
  • Results Posted Online
  • ...and of course, a pour of wine!*

*Please note that the post race drink ticket is available race day only

* Runners who pick up their packets early on Thursday and Friday will receive a 15% discount on bottle purchases.

*Wise Villa Winery is a non-smoking property

Parking spaces are limited at the winery, so please car pool if possible.  We will have parking attendants directing traffic on race day, but please plan to arrive early for your wave in order to get a good parking space.

name: Women's History Month Virtual 5K with Foundation for Women Warriors
description:
Register today for Foundation for Women Warriors' Women’s History Month Virtual 5K. Registration is free!

 

Whether you plan to run, walk, hike, or bike – log your miles in honor of the trailblazing women who defied societal norms. We encourage you to participate in honor of a woman in history who inspires you and to share her story!

 

Rally your own team! Become a captain and recruit your running team. Captains get a free tote bag with teams of 4 or more. Look for this option in the registration portal to set up.

 

Don’t forget to post who you are running for and your results on social media! Tag us for a chance to win the various prizes below:

→ The first runner to post results will receive a FFWW tote bag.

→ The runner to post the fastest time will receive a $25 Starbucks gift card.

→  Become a team captain and receive a tote bag with teams of 4 or more.

→ The runner /captain to post a group photo with the most friends or family that participated will receive a $25 Starbucks gift card and FFWW magnets for everyone in their group.

→ All runners who tag us on social media will be entered in a giveaway! On April 1st, three lucky runners will be selected receive a $25 Starbucks gift card.

 

You can go a step further in supporting our woman veteran community by hosting your own 5K fundraiser through the registration portal with these easy steps:
1. Select the “Sign Up” button on this page.
2. Begin filling in the fields with your information.
3. Once you get to the donation page, click “Become a Fundraiser” and set your goal.
4. After you register, you have the option to share your fundraiser via Facebook and/or you can copy the link to share on your other socials. You will also be able to access your fundraiser via the link in your confirmation email.

 

COMPLETE YOUR RUN/WALK BY MARCH 31ST, REGISTER TODAY!

name: Woodbridge Village Association 50th Anniversary - Ralph J. Redington 5K/10K Run and Kids Run
description:
Race Registration:  All registration will be handled online for the race.  Please note the last day to register will be Friday, July 3rd by 12:00 p.m.  No registrations will be accepted on the day of the race or in person at the Woodbridge Community Center. 

Calling all runners! Compete with your neighbors and friends in the annual 4th of July race. The races will start by the North Lake Gazebo on Barranca Parkway.

Check-in time for the 5K and 10K Runs is 6:30 a.m. The 5K and 10K Runs will begin at 7:15 a.m. The Kids Run will begin at approximately 8:15 a.m.

The entry fee for early registration 5K/10K participants is $45 per person, including an official race T-shirt, or $40 without a T-shirt, up until Sunday, June 14th.  

The entry fee for all 5K/10K participants registering on Monday, June 15th through Friday, July 3rd at 12:00 p.m. is $60 per person, which includes an official race T-shirt, or $55 without a T-shirt.

The entry fee for the Kids Run is $20 per child, which includes a T-shirt, or $15 per child without the T-shirt, up until Friday, July 3rd at 12:00 p.m.

Please note: All registration is online only. There will be no in-person “cash” sign-up registrations prior to or on the day of the races. 

Early registration participants (registration completed by Sunday, June 14th) may pick up their run bib numbers and T-shirts on the special pick-up day of Friday, July 3rd, from 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m., at the Woodbridge Community Center (31 Creek Road) to avoid long lines on the day of the race.  If you registered after Sunday, June 14th, please pick up your run bib numbers and run T-shirts at the event on Barranca Parkway on Saturday, July 4th.

Awards will be presented to first-place finishers only in each age division for both men and women, and to the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place overall finishers in the Kids 1-mile run for boys and girls.

Official 50th Anniversary Run T-shirts are available for purchase standalone at the Association Office (31 Creek Road) for $10.

name: Wrigley River Run & Tadpole Trot
description:
Visit www.wrigleyriverrun.com for full event information.

The start/finish, expo area and bib pick up will be located in the parking lot of Westland Real Estate Group/Long Beach Beer Lab, at 520 W Willow St, Long Beach, CA 90806.

There is special pricing of only $10 for youth 17 & under who want to do the 5k or the 10k.

The Half Combo is a total of 13.1 miles and includes a 5k and 10 Mile Entry. You will receive a half marathon time as well as a time in each event. You will also receive a bonus medal. There are no age group awards for the Half Combo.

The Wrigley River Run is the Long Beach Neighborhood Foundation’s signature event and is designed to promote community involvement, education, tolerance, and a healthy non-violent lifestyle.  All funds generated from the event are used to benefit youth organizations in Long Beach and the surrounding communities.

name: YOLO Run
description:
You Only Live Once, so join us for the YOLO Run for a morning of sunshine that benefits children and families. UC Davis Children's Hospital and the NEC Society are teaming up on May 16th because it's Necrotizing Enterocolitis (NEC) Awareness Day. 

 

Join us on the football field on May 16, 2026, at the UC Davis Health Stadium in Davis, California! Choose your distance and get ready to start and finish your race in the Stadium at the second annual YOLO Run, presented by the NEC Society and UC Davis Children's Hospital.

 

NEC is an intestinal disease that can affect medically fragile infants during their first weeks and months of life. UC Davis Children's Hospital provides lifesaving care for babies at risk of NEC, and the NEC Society is the world's leading nonprofit advancing NEC research, education, and advocacy. Yolo County locals, Jennifer and Noah Canvasser, launched the NEC Society after tragically losing their son, Micah, to the disease. By teaming up with UC Davis Children's Hospital, the Canvasser family and NEC Society are building a world without NEC. Join us for the YOLO Run to support this work!

 

Interested in sponsoring the YOLO Run? Email Jennifer@NECsociety.org


Want to learn more about NEC? Check out NECsociety.org

 

Race Day Info

  • Race start time: 8:00 a.m.
  • Registration fee includes a YOLO Run finisher's medal and shirt. Entries received after May 2 may not receive desired shirt size. 
  • Bib pick up will open at 6:45 a.m. on race morning. Arrive no later than 7:30 a.m. to check-in. 
  • Parking is available on campus in lot adjacent to the stadium. 

 

Course Maps

  • Check out the YOLO Run 10K course
  • Check out the YOLO Run 5K course
  • Check out the YOLO Run 2K course 

 

Post-Race

  • 2025 YOLO Run photos by Facchino Photography available here
  • 2025 Race Results: View 2025 results here

name: Youth Splash and Dash
description:
The Youth Splash and Dash is our first  swim & run for kids ages 6-14. Come celebrate our first event with a full size finish line with snacks and finisher certificates and hang out with their friends. 

This would be an introductory event that would prepare the kids for their first triathlon/aquathlon.
The main goal is to wake up the outdoor spirit in our little athletes and walk them through the transition in this type of sport that is lately gaining in popularity.


Distances are short and intended simply to expose our youngest athletes to the basic elements of two legs of triathlon. 

The swim will take place in the Washington pool, which has 25 yard lanes. Ages 6-10 will do 4 lengths, and ages 11-14 will do 8 lengths. Volunteers will help count laps.

The transition from swim to run will take the youth to the picnic area before doing a loop around a nearby section of campus. The run course will be supported by cheering, excited volunteers. 11-14 year old will do two loops.

Note: triathletes usually swim and run in the same clothes! There will not be a changing area, but we will have an area for youth to put clothes on over their swimsuit if they aren't wearing a triathlon suit.

The 10K turns around at the Baker Beach aid station while the Half Marathoners head through Seacliff and continue along Coastal Trail to the turnaround at Lands End overlooking the historic Sutro Baths.
(Distances are accurately measured using a Rolatape® surveyor's measuring wheel.)
